notes: These vectors pin CBA dual-plane semantics. DataEvent vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_ref and never use preconditions. Control Move vectors use signed kind + payload + scope_ref + seal_basis and may use preconditions. Every cell write is receiver-projected from the registered reducer contract.

Seal delta entries reference only newly sealed control-plane event digests. Cumulative coverage is derived from predecessor_refs[] plus delta[]. DataEvent digests may appear in data_event_set_root / data_view_root observations, but those roots do not confer control-plane finality.
Cell ids follow ak:cell:ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n>:<subject>; subject placeholders use dot-safe strings to keep examples unambiguous.

vectors.name: data_event_accepts_without_seal_finality
vectors.description: A message DataEvent is locally accepted when signature, actor chain, seal_ref, auth_context, capability and data-plane Lattice validation pass. It does not wait for Seal coverage.

vectors.name: data_event_observation_does_not_seal
vectors.description: A Seal may observe DataEvents through data_event_set_root, but that observation is evidence, not control-plane finality.

vectors.name: control_move_requires_seal_basis_and_seal
vectors.description: A membership ban Control Move uses seal_basis for authorization and preconditions. It remains control_pending until covered by a valid Seal.

vectors.name: same_batch_does_not_advance_authorization_basis
vectors.description: An Event earlier in the same submit batch may resolve bytes and causal refs for later Events, but it cannot create a grant used by a later Event in the same batch.

vectors.name: data_plane_conflict_returns_bottom_without_winner
vectors.description: Concurrent incompatible writes to a data-plane cas_register cell return structured bottom. The reducer must not choose a winner by HLC, actor id, arrival order, or Seal observation order.

vectors.name: seal_delta_excludes_data_event_digest
vectors.description: A Seal delta contains newly sealed control-plane event digests only. Including a DataEvent digest in delta is a seal validation failure.

vectors.name: open_set_compaction_preserves_control_roots
vectors.description: A signed compaction Seal must be equivalent to the deterministic control view of its predecessors and preserve control_event_set_root, state_root and fault diagnostics.

vectors.name: seal_canonical_no_self_reference
vectors.description: Seal canonical bytes are computed from signed top-level body fields only. The Seal id and notary_signature are excluded from the transcript.

vectors.name: cas_mixed_basis
vectors.description: cas_register writes on a non-initial settled value require an explicit CBA basis; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.

expected.note: Per event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.3.1 the projector copies the whole-value head_eq into op.from, so the join sees the v1 -> v2 supersession chain and settles on v2 instead of bottom. The blind write above deliberately has no from: it forms a second chain head and the defensive join stays bottom.

vectors.name: auth_context_epoch_pinning_reject
vectors.description: Verifier evaluates key and credential epoch validity at the event seal_ref, not only against the current DID document.

vectors.name: seal_compaction_interval_enforced
vectors.description: Realm seal_compaction_max_interval_ms is a structural obligation: valid full-coverage compaction enables bootstrap, mismatched coverage rejects, and overdue compaction raises health alarms.

vectors.name: inclusion_list_obligation
vectors.description: A multi-signer notary Seal must discharge valid inclusion-list obligations by inclusion, signed reject, or pre-state verification failure proof.

vectors.name: notary_fault_equivocation_quarantine
vectors.description: Two different Seals signed by the same notary in the same slot authorize public equivocation evidence, quarantine the fork, and reject later Seals from that signer.

vectors.name: sealed_control_move_full_digest_collision
vectors.description: Two different canonical preimages recompute to the same event_id under one suite, and the colliding Control Move is already covered by an accepted Seal. Unlike notary equivocation, the sibling event_digest values are byte-identical, so no digest can name the winner.

vectors.name: open_set_concurrent_revocation_fail_closed
vectors.description: A DataEvent whose seal_ref is locally valid is re-evaluated against the joined multi-leaf control view when a concurrent revocation branch is observed.

cases.name: late_revocation_leaf_retroactive_removal
cases.description: Ordered sequence, not a single joined-view snapshot: E is first accepted and its reducer-projected write is materialized into data cell X under the initial joined view that has NOT yet joined the revoke leaf R. Dependent event D is then accepted with E as a critical causal dependency and materializes a projected write into data cell Y. R arrives later; once joined, E loses seal_ref authorization, so E and the complete direct/indirect dependency closure rooted at E MUST leave accepted projection inputs. The final state MUST equal that of a receiver that joined {S0,R} from the start, independent of arrival order.

vectors.name: actor_chain_realm_scope
vectors.description: Actor sequence and sibling detection are scoped to (realm_id, actor_id); equal actor_seq values in different Realms do not create a fork.

vectors.name: conflict_recovery_move
vectors.description: A bottom=reject control cell recovers only through a sealed ak.conflict.recovery Control Move with recovery_capability and a pre-conflict state_witness. The recovered value is the signed payload.resolved_value, projected by the registered cell_ref + reset form; no other kind may declare that form.

expected.note: reset is legal only on a cell already in bottom; on any other state the write is rejected, so recovery cannot be used as a general overwrite channel.
the state_witness must witness the cell named by payload.target_cell; witnessing a different cell proves nothing about the one being reset.

vectors.name: same_seal_bottom_reject_serialization

vectors.name: realm_alias_single_carrier

expected.create_time_alias_shape: registered conditional alias slot in the same ordered atomic Realm bootstrap unit
expected.rename_shape: successor set on the same cell carrying whole-value head_eq
expected.release_shape: explicit {tombstone:true} set; effective resolution treats it as absence and the Realm stays addressable only by realm_id
expected.resolution_source: resolve_realm / resolve_target / ak.edge.applet.realm.read.resolve.v1 read the effective cell; directory rows are a projection, not a second source of truth

fixtures/circle-scope-fixture.json.description: Machine-contract fixture for signed Event scope_ref, projected object effective_scope, and Circle lifecycle basis evaluation. Producer supplies scope_circle_id where the payload owns it and signs the matching scope_ref; the reducer verifies that scope and may materialize effective_scope only in object read projections. Covers rebind transitions, DataEvent seal_ref and Control Move seal_basis evaluation, linear and concurrent archive, tombstone, restore barriers, and negative cases. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md §6.1 / §6.2 / §7 / §9.2 / §10.2.

submit_payload_shape.description: Generic actor-supplied scope fragment for object payload schemas that own scope_circle_id (for example Strand, Morph, Relation, and scoped Space creation/update). It MUST NOT carry effective_scope. Message and structural-operation payloads that derive scope from accepted target references do not embed this fragment; they still sign Event.scope_ref.

canonical_reducer_output_shape.description: Reducer-stamped, immutable tagged scope written to Event envelope and materialized object cell. Two discriminated forms: kind=realm | kind=circle.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: none_to_none_noop
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=null -> scope_circle_id=null. No-op rebind; reducer MUST accept when the signed scope_ref remains {kind:realm}; the object projection effective_scope remains Realm-scoped.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: same_circle_to_same_circle_noop
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). No-op rebind; reducer MUST accept.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: none_to_circle_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=null -> scope_circle_id=Some(A). True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: circle_to_none_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=null. True rebind; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

scope_rebind_transition_cases.name: circle_a_to_circle_b_default_reject
scope_rebind_transition_cases.description: scope_circle_id=Some(A) -> scope_circle_id=Some(B). True rebind across circles; default reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile MAY enable audit-paired high-risk update.

negative_cases.name: submit_payload_carrying_effective_scope_rejected
negative_cases.description: Actor MUST NOT supply effective_scope in submit payload. Reducer MUST schema_violation with reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed.

negative_cases.name: relation_create_payload_carrying_effective_scope_rejected
negative_cases.description: ak.relation.create whose payload.relation carries effective_scope MUST be rejected with schema_violation reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed and MUST NOT produce any projection write. The decision is schema-level and needs no projection pre-state: event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/relation_create_object is relation.schema.json minus id, the banned `type` name and effective_scope, so Relation create is decided exactly like the Strand / Morph / Space create shapes while relation.schema.json keeps `fields` open for free edge metadata.

negative_cases.name: relation_update_patch_carrying_effective_scope_rejected
negative_cases.description: ak.relation.update whose payload.patch addresses effective_scope, or any effective_scope.* descendant, MUST be rejected with schema_violation reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed and MUST NOT produce any projection write. Patch atomicity applies: the whole map fails closed, so no sibling path in the same patch is applied. The forbidden set is registered per object kind in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json and, for Relation, is additionally enforced by the propertyNames guard on event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/relation_update_payload; implementations MUST read it from the registry rather than hard-coding a parallel list.

patch.fields.assignment_note: sibling path in the same patch, MUST NOT be applied

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_targets_inactive_circle
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle with state != active. Reducer MUST failed_precondition reason=circle_not_active.

negative_cases.name: scope_circle_id_realm_mismatch
negative_cases.description: scope_circle_id references a Circle whose realm_id != object.realm_id. Reducer MUST schema_violation reason=circle_realm_mismatch.

negative_cases.name: event_missing_scope_ref_rejected_at_schema
negative_cases.description: Every Event, including an ak.message.create derived from a Circle-scoped Strand, MUST carry signed scope_ref before reducer admission. Schema validation rejects a missing scope_ref; no receiver may accept first and later add or infer a wire field.

negative_cases.name: scope_ref_mismatches_scope_circle_id
negative_cases.description: The signed Event scope_ref MUST equal the scope derived from the target object's accepted projection: scope_circle_id=null -> {kind:realm}; scope_circle_id=C -> {kind:circle, circle_id:C}. Receiver MUST reject a mismatch and MUST NOT rewrite the signed field. A separately materialized object effective_scope is projection output and must copy the verified scope_ref.

negative_cases.name: signed_scope_ref_tamper
negative_cases.description: scope_ref is part of signed Event canonical bytes, so event_digest binds it directly. If a Seal later reports the DataEvent inside data_event_set_root, that root is an observational availability/projection proof, not control-plane finality. Mutating scope_ref after signing changes event_digest; receivers MUST reject with digest_mismatch. No separate scope field is added to seal.schema.json because the Event digest already carries this binding.

negative_cases.name: content_plaintext_under_e2ee_required
negative_cases.description: Realm.content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required requires the verified Event scope_ref for every Strand/Message/Morph/Blob content write to resolve to an MLS-backed scope (Realm-default MLS or Circle MLS). An ak.message.create carrying plaintext content, or whose verified scope_ref resolves to a Circle with encryption_profile=none, MUST be rejected with failed_precondition reason=content_encryption_floor_violation.

accepted_form.note: Realm ids are event-derived: the Realm token equals its ak.realm.create Event token byte for byte and retyping only swaps the typed prefix.

vectors.name: ak.vector.encoding.crypto.ed25519_detached_jws.v1
vectors.description: Ed25519 detached JWS over the canonical proof binding object for a Arkret Event Envelope.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only. Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.

vectors.name: ak.vector.encoding.crypto.es256_detached_jws.v1
vectors.description: ECDSA P-256 (ES256) detached JWS over the canonical proof binding object for an Arkret Event Envelope. Optional interop suite gated by ak.profile.signature.ecdsa_p256.v1.

test_private_key_jwk.note: Public conformance test key only (d = fixed seed bytes 0x00..0x1f). Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.

vectors.name: ak.vector.encoding.crypto.mldsa65_raw_detached_signature.v1
vectors.description: ML-DSA-65 (NIST FIPS 204) raw detached signature over the canonical proof binding object bytes (registry proof_kind = raw_detached_signature; no JOSE wrapping). PQC suite gated by ak.profile.signature.pqc.v1.
vectors.keygen_note: Public conformance test key only, generated as an ML-DSA-65 key and recorded with its 32-byte FIPS 204 seed. Production profiles MUST reject this test DID/key domain.
vectors.raw_signing_input: UTF-8 bytes of canonical_binding_payload (detached_payload_b64u is its base64url form, provided for cross-checking only; the signed bytes are the unencoded canonical JSON)
vectors.signature_note: Recorded valid deterministic ML-DSA-65 signature over canonical_binding_payload. Verifiers MUST verify the recorded bytes.

negative_cases.name: reject_flipped_signature_bit
negative_cases.description: One bit of the Ed25519 signature is flipped (first signature byte XOR 0x01); everything else is byte-identical to the valid vector.

expected.reason: signature bytes do not verify against the canonical proof binding object

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_none
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares alg=none. The signature segment carries well-formed base64url bytes so the rejection MUST come from the algorithm allowlist, not from shape validation.

expected.reason: alg=none is not an active row of signature-alg-registry.json; critical proofs MUST fail closed before any verification is attempted

negative_cases.name: reject_alg_key_type_mismatch
negative_cases.description: Protected header declares ES256 and the signature genuinely verifies under a P-256 key, but kid resolves to the Ed25519 OKP verification method. The verifier MUST bind alg to the resolved key type (jwk_kty/jwk_crv per signature-alg-registry.json) and fail closed.

expected.reason: declared alg ES256 does not match the resolved verification method key type (OKP/Ed25519); implementations MUST NOT verify with a substituted key

negative_cases.name: reject_truncated_public_key
negative_cases.description: The DID Document publicKeyJwk.x is truncated to 31 bytes; the JWS is the untampered valid vector value.

expected.reason: verification key fails to parse (31 bytes is not an Ed25519 public key length); key material errors MUST fail closed, not fall back to another key

negative_cases.name: reject_non_empty_payload_segment
negative_cases.description: The detached payload is re-attached as the JWS payload segment. The signature still verifies as an attached JWS over the identical signing input, so accepting it would silently downgrade the detached profile; receivers MUST reject on the non-empty payload segment alone.

expected.reason: detached_jws payload segment MUST be empty in compact serialization (encoding.md section 6) even when the attached form would verify

negative_cases.name: reject_es256_truncated_signature
negative_cases.description: The ES256 JOSE signature is 63 bytes instead of the required raw 64-byte r||s form.

expected.reason: ES256 detached JWS signatures MUST be exactly 64 raw bytes (r||s)

negative_cases.name: reject_es256_truncated_public_key
negative_cases.description: The P-256 x coordinate is truncated to 31 bytes while the detached JWS is otherwise valid.

expected.reason: ES256 verification keys MUST contain valid 32-byte P-256 x and y coordinates

negative_cases.name: reject_mldsa65_truncated_signature
negative_cases.description: The ML-DSA-65 raw signature is truncated by one byte.

expected.reason: ML-DSA-65 signatures MUST have the exact FIPS 204 byte length

negative_cases.name: reject_mldsa65_truncated_public_key
negative_cases.description: The ML-DSA-65 public key is truncated by one byte while the signature is otherwise valid.

expected.reason: ML-DSA-65 public keys MUST have the exact FIPS 204 byte length

fixtures/cursor-negative-fixture.json.description: Machine-readable negative cursor vectors mirrored from zh/conformance/conformance-vectors.md section 1.16. Complements the positive opaqueness vector ak.vector.encoding.cursor_opaque.core.v1: every case below is a schema-valid-looking ak:cursor: token that a conformant receiver MUST reject before advancing any server-side state. reason_code values are stable codes from error-code-registry.json (invalid_cursor is surfaced under top-level param_invalid).

cases.name: oversized_token
cases.violation: encoded token exceeds the 4KB body cap before any decode work

cases.name: invalid_base64url
cases.violation: token payload is not unpadded base64url

cases.name: malformed_json
cases.violation: decoded body is not valid JSON

cases.name: duplicate_json_key
cases.violation: duplicate JSON key violates canonical JSON ingress rules

cases.name: non_nfc_string
cases.violation: decoded issued_at string value is not Unicode NFC (it carries U+0065 U+0301 instead of the NFC composed form U+00E9); canonical JSON ingress MUST reject. The raw body is intentionally not inlined here so this fixture file itself stays NFC-clean; the base64url token is the authoritative input.

cases.name: inline_positions_rejected
cases.violation: v1 core cursor body carries only the opaque handle; inline position state (s) violates the closed {v,purpose,issued_at,expires_at,h} schema

cases.name: unsupported_version
cases.violation: cursor version is not in supported_versions (v1 core supports only "1")

cases.name: handle_too_short
cases.violation: stateful handle h is shorter than the 22-character minimum (>=128 bits of entropy)

cases.name: non_canonical_timestamp
cases.violation: issued_at must be a canonical UTC Z timestamp; the +00:00 offset form is rejected

cases.name: stream_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: expires_at - issued_at exceeds the stream-purpose hard TTL cap of 7 days (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: barrier_ttl_exceeds_cap
cases.violation: expires_at - issued_at exceeds the barrier-purpose hard TTL cap of 1 hour (encoding.md section 8.3 rule 12)

cases.name: missing_millisecond_fraction
cases.violation: issued_at omits the mandatory three millisecond digits; whole seconds MUST use .000Z

vectors.fixture_freshness_note: All timestamps are pinned so every case stays deterministically rejectable for the spec lifetime: expired cases use year-2020 values (always past), TTL-cap and negative-TTL cases use year-2099 x values (not expired before 2099) with a violation that is checked before any now-relative comparison could differ.
rules: receivers MUST reject every case before advancing subscription position, barrier wait, or any other server-side state

syntax / schema / TTL-bound failures surface as top-level param_invalid with reason_code invalid_cursor; expiry uses cursor_expired; handle lookup or cross-binding failures (not covered here, they need server state) use cursor_integrity_invalid
receivers MUST enforce the 4KB cap on the encoded token before spending base64 or JSON parsing work

TTL bound checks MUST validate issued_at and expires_at well-formedness first, then issued_at <= expires_at, then issued_at not in the future beyond clock skew, then expires_at - issued_at against the per-purpose cap, so a corrupt issued_at cannot bypass the cap

semantic_cases.name: first_canonical_acceptance_enters_pending_atomically

fixtures/did-binding-digest-fixture.json.description: Known-answer tests for the identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 5 binding digests: document_digest over the normalized DID Document projection, evidence_digest over the canonical evidence receipt (did-binding-contracts.schema.json#/$defs/evidence_receipt), and policy_digest over the canonical resolver policy snapshot (#/$defs/resolver_policy_snapshot). All digests are sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(object))). Every case is trust-domain-local: recomputability and change-sensitivity are asserted, cross-deployment equality is not.

cases.name: document_digest_normalized_projection
assertions: re-serializing the same document with any other raw JSON property order MUST produce the same digest
removing also_known_as MUST change the digest to sha256:41a9952f2759044d26d640dba9c54b4d7702de30bc4ca5621a56667495e1fb58
removing both also_known_as and metadata.primary_handle MUST change the digest to sha256:acbe292d7600ba1e26ca284e5f408795aae4ac3dc6247e4a4e312ae6ada5b251
duplicate or conflicting property, verification-method id, service id, metadata key, relationship or extension name MUST fail before digesting
a raw resolver response digest MUST NOT be carried in document_digest; raw bytes use raw_document_digest

cases.name: evidence_receipt_proofless_method
assertions: a proofless method degrades to an empty method_proofs array, never to an implementation-invented placeholder object
the receipt MUST be retained so the digest is recomputable by an auditor

cases.name: evidence_receipt_webvh_log
assertions: witnesses MUST be sorted by witness_did in UTF-8 byte order and duplicates rejected; resolver response order is not a canonical order
changing any witness row or the witness_proofs_digest MUST change evidence_digest

the extracted evidence_dependencies record for this receipt is {witness_dids:[did:web:witness-a.example, did:web:witness-b.example], witness_controlling_organization_dids:[did:web:witness-org-a.example, did:web:witness-org-b.example], history_heads:[1-QmZfixtureEntryHash11111111111111111111111]}

cases.name: policy_snapshot_base_profile
assertions: flipping fail_mode to allow_cached_on_error MUST change the digest to sha256:a0538d5c6aa75fabf0492476e68d3a97bf35ff050ee8df601f3f62cf98b8b595
enum values MUST use the registered wire tokens; a language-native debug rendering such as FailClosed MUST be rejected before digesting
an unknown policy_profile, an unknown profile_policy field, or a missing registered field MUST fail closed instead of digesting

cases.name: accept_scid_substituted_over_the_whole_entry
cases.note: identity-did.md 3.4.4: the literal {SCID} the holder placed inside state.alsoKnownAs is substituted exactly like the skeleton-owned members. Substituting only versionId and parameters.scid yields a different published entry and a different versionId from the same input.

cases.name: reject_residual_scid_placeholder_in_published_entry
cases.note: The same preliminary entry substituted only over versionId, parameters.scid and state.id. Its own entry hash is self-consistent and re-deriving the SCID from it still succeeds, so the residual {SCID} is the only detector: identity-did.md 3.4.4 makes it a fail-closed rejection.

fixtures/did-webvh-witness-fixture.json.description: Conformance vectors for the did:webvh witness rail (identity-did.md §3.4.1-§3.4.3). Two layers are exercised and MUST NOT be conflated. cryptographic_vectors[] contains a field-exact, externally sourced did:webvh v1.0 log and did-witness.json whose entry hash, controller proof and witness proof MUST all be recomputed and verified. method_policy_cases[] cover structural and policy semantics: witness policy is read only from parameters.witness = {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]} whose ids are did:key values that MUST decode to cryptosuite-compatible public keys during parameter validation, proofs come only from the separate did-witness.json keyed by versionId, and every malformed, aliased, unavailable or under-threshold condition fails closed with a registered code instead of degrading to threshold 0. schema_validation_cases[] cover the Arkret-layer carrier: ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1 is a distinct object family from ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1 and the two are returned as a tagged union discriminated on schema. The receipt is a cacheable, auditable observation record; it never substitutes for verifying the standard did-witness.json proofs, the entry hash chain or the controller proof. Placeholder values occur only in the explicitly structural cases; they MUST NOT be substituted for cryptographic_vectors[].

method_policy_cases.name: standard_witness_parameter_is_the_only_policy_source
method_policy_cases.notes: The did:webvh 1.0 shape. threshold is within 1..witnesses.length and every witness id is a unique did:key. This is the only structure an Arkret verifier reads as witness policy.

method_policy_cases.name: absent_witness_parameter_means_no_method_witness
method_policy_cases.notes: Absence is not malformation. A DID that never declared method witnesses is legitimately unwitnessed at the method layer; deployment policy may still refuse to use it on high-risk paths, but that is an overlay decision and not a parse failure.

method_policy_cases.name: aliased_witness_keys_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The single most dangerous case. A log carrying witnesses / witness_threshold instead of witness was produced against a non-standard dialect, so the true policy is unknown. Reading it as no policy would silently turn a DID that declares two witnesses into one that requires none, which is a fail-open, not a compatibility fallback.

method_policy_cases.name: arkret_overlay_fields_inside_method_parameter_fail_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: profileMinThreshold / structuredWitnesses / watcherEvidence / maxAgeSeconds are Arkret deployment policy. Inside method history they force external verifiers to cope with unregistered keys, make policy rotation require rewriting DID history, and let a holder self-declare both the threshold and the evidence that satisfies it.

method_policy_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: did:webvh 1.0 constrains witness identifiers to did:key. Any other form describes something that is not a method witness.

method_policy_cases.name: undecodable_did_key_witness_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: The witness id is shaped like a did:key and passes any pattern check, but its multibase payload does not decode to a well-formed public key compatible with the log's Data Integrity cryptosuite. did:webvh 1.0 requires this to be caught during parameter validation, not deferred to signature verification: an undecodable key that is allowed to occupy a threshold slot silently hollows out the threshold, because that slot can never be satisfied by any proof.

method_policy_cases.name: threshold_above_witness_count_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: An unsatisfiable threshold is a declaration error, not an instruction to ignore witnessing.

method_policy_cases.name: duplicate_witness_id_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: A repeated id would let one key be counted twice toward threshold.

method_policy_cases.name: missing_witness_proofs_file_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Policy is declared but did-witness.json is unreachable or has no entry for this versionId. Unavailable evidence is not absent policy.

method_policy_cases.name: proof_from_unlisted_signer_does_not_count
method_policy_cases.notes: A syntactically fine proof signed by a key outside parameters.witness proves nothing about the declared witness set.

method_policy_cases.name: fewer_valid_proofs_than_threshold_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: One valid proof against a declared threshold of two. Effective threshold is the strictest intersection of the method threshold and the deployment minimum, so a holder can raise this bar but never lower it.

method_policy_cases.name: holder_declared_threshold_cannot_lower_deployment_minimum
method_policy_cases.notes: The log declares threshold 1 while deployment policy requires 2. Effective threshold is 2; otherwise any holder could opt out of the deployment's witnessing requirement by editing its own log.

method_policy_cases.name: same_controlling_organization_does_not_satisfy_distinct_requirement
method_policy_cases.notes: Two distinct witness keys, one operator. Counting keys instead of controlling organizations would let a single operator satisfy a two-organization requirement alone, which empties the requirement of meaning.

method_policy_cases.name: evidence_older_than_max_age_fails_closed
method_policy_cases.notes: Age is measured from observed_at, not from when an Arkret receipt was signed. Re-signing an old observation does not refresh it.

schema_validation_cases.name: did_webvh_witness_receipt_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Binds subject DID, exact versionId, witness did:key, its controlling organization and the observation instant. The issuer service DID is the trust root for the receipt itself and is unrelated to the subject DID's controller.

schema_validation_cases.name: registry_consensus_receipt_stays_a_separate_family
schema_validation_cases.notes: The pre-existing family, unchanged. Its witness_role describes a replication role inside a DID registry consensus group and it binds seq + head_event_digest; it says nothing about did:webvh method witnesses. Both families ride ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list.v1 and are told apart only by the schema constant.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_expiry_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: An Arkret-layer cache record without an expiry is indistinguishable from a permanent assertion, which is exactly how stale witness evidence outlives the state it described.

schema_validation_cases.name: witness_receipt_without_controlling_organization_did_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Distinct-organization policy counts organizations, not keys. A receipt that cannot name the controlling organization cannot be counted toward that requirement, so the field is required rather than optional.

schema_validation_cases.name: non_did_key_witness_in_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: witness_did mirrors parameters.witness.witnesses[].id, which did:webvh 1.0 constrains to did:key. A receipt naming another form is describing something that is not a method witness.

schema_validation_cases.name: arkret_overlay_field_on_receipt_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: $: Additional properties are not allowed ('max_age_seconds' was unexpected)
schema_validation_cases.notes: The receipt records an observation; it does not carry policy. Letting an issuer attach its own max age would put the freshness bar back in the hands of the party whose evidence is being judged.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipts_tagged_union_accepts_both_families
schema_validation_cases.notes: One response carrying both families. A consumer MUST branch on the schema constant; threshold_met is an Arkret-layer convenience and its absence MUST NOT be read as true.

candidate_store_kat.material_instance_rule: Origin is excluded from material identity. Assign immutable material_received_sequence when bytes first become resident; same bytes from a new origin do not refresh it; refetch after byte eviction creates a new resident instance and sequence.
candidate_store_kat.origin_attribution_rule: origin_ref is retrieval-only and never selects quota identity. Exact duplicate is a no-op. Keep at most 4 rows per candidate, 64 per exact scope/group/epoch/origin_domain/origin_quota_domain and 256 total per epoch. Expiry is computed as immutable first_observed_at+2592000 seconds and is not stored; overflow fails closed. Prune expired first, then retain the minimum (first_observed_at,candidate_digest,origin_domain,JCS(origin_quota_domain),JCS(origin_ref)) tuples. Origin attribution never duplicates bytes or changes material_received_sequence.
candidate_store_kat.event_attribution_rule: A success or failure EventCandidateBinding contains no origin and origin cannot be inferred from it. It stores exact Event attribution, candidate_digest, outcome and bounded timestamps only; it never pins candidate secret bytes.

tier_order: received material with no success binding, including unbound and failure-only
deterministic_eviction.effect: Success/failure bindings choose only the tier and never pin bytes. Delete candidate secret bytes and the resident sequence only; retain bounded origin/Event-binding tombstones so refetch can restore material with a new sequence. local_authoritative is never a victim and does not count against received slots.

event_candidate_binding_ledger.expiry_rule: expiry is computed as immutable first_observed_at plus 2592000 seconds, is not stored, and timestamp overflow fails closed
event_candidate_binding_ledger.independence: Pruning attribution metadata never mutates the ciphertext replay ledger, local_authoritative material, or epoch authority.

fixtures/organization-registration-fixtu.description: Conformance vectors for registering an external, already-published Organization DID with a deployment (identity-did.md §8.4). The family separates five things that are routinely conflated: resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation. Being resolvable or referenceable never yields local administrative authority. Registration is two-phase by decision, not by preference: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge, and only then does the caller prove control at a pinned version. The control proof binds local_admin_subject_id so a captured proof cannot be redirected to another beneficiary, and registration_generation gives the binding an identity that changes across re-establishment so the terminal revoked state and the organization-keyed idempotency stop contradicting each other. Opening a new generation atomically supersedes the previous current generation; old receipts cannot authorize after the current pointer advances even when their immutable signed payload still says active. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs; creating a new Organization DID is a separate ceremony with no member here, so a receiver never has to guess whether a proof asserts existing control or creation. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true satisfy JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected, because cross-field invariants such as the challenge window, scope agreement and quorum sufficiency cannot be expressed in JSON Schema. Placeholder DIDs, digests and JWS strings are structural only and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors.

schema_validation_cases.name: challenge_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Every binding field closes one replay path: purpose separates this signature from any other the organization makes, audience and trust_domain pin it to this deployment, origin pins the HTTP surface, nonce makes it unrepeatable, and the 300-second window bounds how long a captured proof stays useful.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_with_resolved_verification_method_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Single-signature branch. The pinned version_id plus log_head_digest is what makes the later receipt auditable; without it a receipt would assert control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_with_governance_quorum_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Quorum branch with two distinct governance signatures meeting the declared threshold. Per identity-did.md §8.1 a witness attestation is not a quorum and MUST NOT be substituted here: witnessing proves history visibility, quorum proves governance authorisation.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipt_valid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The receipt proves this deployment accepted a local binding and nothing more: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a notary designation and not a service delegation. control_proof_kind travels alongside control_key_digest so a later auditor can tell which commitment the digest is over without refetching the request.

schema_validation_cases.name: quorum_threshold_on_single_signature_branch_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The discriminator is closed in both directions. A threshold on the single-signature branch would leave a receiver unable to say whether one signature was sufficient or two were promised and one delivered.

schema_validation_cases.name: governance_quorum_without_threshold_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Without a declared threshold, any number of signatures could be claimed sufficient after the fact.

schema_validation_cases.name: receipt_without_expiry_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: An unbounded receipt would let a single first-time control proof authorise the organization relationship indefinitely, which is exactly what the refresh operation exists to prevent.

schema_validation_cases.name: unregistered_scope_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The scope vocabulary is closed so a deployment cannot mint administrative authority the organization never consented to.

schema_validation_cases.name: handle_attestation_without_subject_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: Binding the subject inside the attestation is what stops an attestation issued for one organization from being presented for another.

schema_validation_cases.name: challenge_window_over_300_seconds_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the window is one hour. JSON Schema cannot compare two timestamps, so the receiver enforces the 300-second ceiling; a longer window buys nothing and widens the interval in which a captured proof remains usable.

schema_validation_cases.name: quorum_proofs_below_declared_threshold_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid: threshold 3, one proof. JSON Schema cannot compare an array length against a sibling integer, so the receiver enforces it and fails closed rather than accepting a partial quorum.

schema_validation_cases.name: ensure_scopes_disagreeing_with_challenge_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the challenge in challenge_valid requested only organization_profile_manage. The same challenge was already consumed by a successful request under a different canonical digest; consumption permits only a byte-identical retry. A scope mismatch means the control proof was produced for different authority than is now being claimed, so the binding MUST NOT be established.

schema_validation_cases.name: refresh_of_revoked_binding_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the stored binding is revoked, which is terminal. Reviving it by refresh would erase the distinction between a withdrawn relationship and a merely stale one, and would let a binding forced to revoked by DID deactivation come back despite the DID no longer being controllable.

schema_validation_cases.name: stale_binding_blocks_high_risk_path
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid stale receipt after a controller rotation. Low-risk reads may still consume it; a high-risk path MUST fail closed until refresh succeeds. stale rather than auto-invalidation was chosen because auto-invalidation lets an attacker force an unbind by triggering one rotation, while treating it as still valid lets a stolen-then-rotated organization keep its binding.

schema_validation_cases.name: control_proof_redirected_to_another_admin_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but local_admin_subject_id differs from the value bound into challenge_valid and signed over by the control proof. This is the redirection attack the binding exists to stop: a proof that named only the organization and the version would let anyone who obtained it submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. The receiver MUST compare against the stored challenge and reject.

schema_validation_cases.name: replay_of_current_generation_is_idempotent
schema_validation_cases.notes: Byte-identical retry of the request that successfully consumed this challenge: the challenge-consumption ledger digest matches, generation stays 1 and created is false. This is the only ensure replay that is idempotent; merely repeating organization/admin/scopes under a different challenge or request digest does not qualify.

schema_validation_cases.name: re_registration_after_revoke_opens_new_generation
schema_validation_cases.notes: revoke ended generation 1; a later ensure opens generation 2 with created=true. Without the generation, 'revoked is terminal' and 'ensure is idempotent on organization_id' would contradict each other and an implementation would have to pick between returning the old terminal receipt, raising duplicate_conflict, and illegally reviving the terminal state.

schema_validation_cases.name: scope_change_atomically_opens_new_generation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Changing local_admin_subject_id or the scope set also opens a new generation, because the delegation being granted is not the one the previous receipt attests. Returning created=false here would let a widened delegation hide behind an idempotent replay. Publishing generation 2, terminating generation 1 with organization_registration_superseded and advancing the current pointer are one atomic transition.

schema_validation_cases.name: superseded_active_receipt_cannot_authorize
schema_validation_cases.notes: The immutable generation-1 receipt still says status=active, but the registry current pointer is already 2. A verifier that trusts the signed status without checking the current-generation pointer would let the old admin or old scope set survive replacement. Opening generation 2 atomically terminated generation 1 with organization_registration_superseded, so this receipt no longer authorizes anything.

fixtures/proof-context-transcript-fixtur.description: Byte-level detached-JWS transcript KAT for every row of proof-context-registry.json. Each case pins the unsigned projection, its JCS bytes and digest, the canonical binding object built under encoding.md section 6.0.2, the JWS signing input and the Ed25519 signature over the shared conformance test key. Each negative case replays the same unsigned body under the adjacent object family's context and MUST be rejected.

transcript_rules.unsigned_projection: Delete the proof carrier member itself, never write null; keep every optional member that is actually present; never insert a default for an absent one.
transcript_rules.optional_binding_field_selection: Fixture convention only, not a wire rule: optional binding fields at an even index in binding_fields are omitted, odd index are present, so both branches occur across the corpus.
transcript_rules.audience_shape: A required audience uses the single-string form; an optional audience uses the array form, so both encodings carry canonical bytes.
transcript_rules.context_placement: The context constant is a member of the binding object under the key 'context'. It is never a JWS header parameter and never a wire field of the signed object.
transcript_rules.negative_context_selection: The adjacent object family is the next row of proof-context-registry.json, wrapping from the last row to the first.
transcript_rules.negative_case_reading: negative_cases[i] reuses the unsigned body and binding of cases[i] and differs only in the context member. Its signature is a real Ed25519 signature over signed_binding_jcs, so it verifies under the substituted context and MUST NOT verify against cases[i].binding_jcs, which is what the receiver rebuilds.

fixtures/push-notify-outcome-fixture.jso.description: Conformance vectors for the ak.edge.push.command.notify.v1 response contract (push-notifications.md §5.2). The response is conserved against notification.devices[]: every input device_id appears in outcomes[] exactly once, none is missing, none is duplicated, and none appears that was not requested. A target-level failure is expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device, so a second response shape never exists. gateway_status accepted/duplicate mean the gateway durably took the route over and the caller MUST NOT resend; only a rejected outcome carrying retry_after_ms transfers the next attempt back to the caller, and only for the two registered caller-retryable reasons. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true but whose semantic_outcome is reject satisfy JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected by a conforming verifier for the listed registered reason code, because conservation is a cross-field invariant JSON Schema cannot express. Placeholder pseudonyms and device ids are structural only and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors.

request_context.notes: Every response case below is evaluated against this one request. Its devices[] is the conserved input set.

schema_validation_cases.name: all_input_devices_accepted
schema_validation_cases.notes: Both input devices durably taken over. Neither outcome carries reason_code or retry_after_ms; the caller owns no further attempt.

schema_validation_cases.name: partial_rejection_drives_registration_cleanup
schema_validation_cases.notes: Second device has no live registration. Cleanup is addressed by (push_target_id, device_id); the response never returns push_key, so the caller can drop the registration without the raw provider token crossing the wire.

schema_validation_cases.name: target_level_failure_is_expanded_per_device
schema_validation_cases.notes: Unknown push target is a target-level failure. It MUST be expanded into one same-reason rejected outcome per input device rather than collapsing into a target-scoped shape, which is what keeps conservation unconditional.

schema_validation_cases.name: caller_retryable_rejection_carries_backoff
schema_validation_cases.notes: push_gateway_unreachable is one of exactly two caller-retryable reasons. retry_after_ms is the sole wire signal that the caller, not the gateway, owns the next attempt for that device.

schema_validation_cases.name: exact_replay_reports_duplicate
schema_validation_cases.notes: Replay under the same Idempotency-Key and body. duplicate means an earlier request already took the route over and this one produced no new delivery; like accepted it forbids caller resend. It never means the request repeated a device_id, which devices[] uniqueness already forbids.

schema_validation_cases.name: rejected_without_reason_code_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: reason_code is REQUIRED when gateway_status=rejected; without it the caller cannot tell a terminal rejection from a retryable one.

schema_validation_cases.name: reason_code_on_accepted_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: A durably accepted route has no rejection reason. Allowing one would reintroduce the ambiguity between acceptance and failure that the closed gateway_status enum exists to remove.

schema_validation_cases.name: retry_after_ms_on_accepted_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: The gateway retries what it accepted. A backoff on an accepted route would invite the caller to resend and produce duplicate provider delivery.

schema_validation_cases.name: retry_after_ms_with_terminal_reason_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: push_token_unknown is terminal: the caller must drop the registration, not retry it. Only push_gateway_unreachable and rate_limited may carry retry_after_ms.

schema_validation_cases.name: unregistered_reason_code_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: reason_code is a closed enum whose members are all registered in error-code-registry.json. A free-form string would let each gateway invent its own failure vocabulary.

schema_validation_cases.name: raw_push_key_in_outcome_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.first_expected_error: $: Additional properties are not allowed ('push_key' was unexpected)
schema_validation_cases.notes: The outcome object is closed. Returning the raw provider token would contradict the opaque-routing obligation in push-notifications.md §5.1 / §6.2, and the composite identity already addresses registration cleanup.

schema_validation_cases.name: rejected_bucket_response_is_invalid
schema_validation_cases.notes: A rejected-only bucket cannot prove what happened to the devices it omits. The response is a single conserved outcomes[] array; there is no bucketed alternative shape.

schema_validation_cases.name: missing_input_device_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the second input device has no outcome. The caller cannot tell whether it was taken over or silently dropped, which is exactly the ambiguity conservation removes. JSON Schema cannot express this cross-field invariant, so a conforming verifier MUST enforce it.

schema_validation_cases.name: duplicate_device_id_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the same device carries two contradictory conclusions. Exactly one outcome per input device_id is required.

schema_validation_cases.name: unrequested_device_violates_conservation
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the third outcome names a device the request never carried. An outcome set that can exceed its input is not a conservation proof and would let a gateway disclose device ids the caller did not address.

schema_validation_cases.name: echoed_push_target_id_must_match_request
schema_validation_cases.notes: Schema-valid but the echo names a different target than the request. The echo exists so an outcome set is self-describing under replay and audit; an echo free to drift provides neither.

schema_validation_cases.name: request_with_repeated_device_id_is_rejected
schema_validation_cases.notes: devices[] is a set keyed by device_id. uniqueItems only rejects byte-identical entries, so this pair differing only in app_id passes JSON Schema; the gateway MUST still reject it. Accepting it would make one input device demand two outcomes and break conservation at the source.

fixtures/reaction-fixture.json.notes: Reducer-level vectors for ak.reaction.add / ak.reaction.remove. The cell ak.component.message.reactions.v1 is the core or_set of reaction assertions: ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove each project exactly one or_set_add, so the remove is itself an assertion rather than an observed-remove. Convergence of the default view is the reaction-specific remove-wins rule keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key), which zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8.3 defines authoritatively as a projection over that set rather than as the or_set join; see §9.8 (Reaction model) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 (plaintext-vs-encrypted visibility).

cases.name: or_set_dedup_double_add_same_actor
cases.notes: Two add events from the same actor with the same key collapse to one OR-Set membership entry; the per-event audit log retains both.

cases.name: or_set_concurrent_add_remove_remove_wins_in_default_view
cases.notes: Two events from the same actor with no causal_refs between them; default view applies per-actor causal closure — concurrent (add, remove) collapses to the remove because the remove is itself a tombstone for the actor's adds in the concurrent past per OR-Set semantics chosen for ak.reaction.

cases.name: dangling_reaction_before_target_arrives
cases.notes: Reaction whose target_ref has not been observed yet MUST be held in pending; reducer materialises the OR-Set entry only after the target message becomes available.

cases.name: target_redacted_drops_default_view_keeps_audit
cases.notes: When the target message is redacted, the default view summary MUST NOT expose reaction members; the audit view retains the reaction events under the redaction stub.

cases.name: e2ee_routing_window_dedup
cases.notes: In an E2EE scope the plaintext key is the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag derived from the epoch routing root plus JCS({effective_scope,target_ref,routing_window}); routing_window=floor(unix_ms(outer Event.created_at)/3600000). The 32-byte tag is carried in `key` as a 256-bit digest and in encryption_context.routing_context.routing_tag as its unpadded base64url bytes. Two adds with the same target, emoji, actor, epoch root and routing window collapse to one OR-Set membership. The fixed one-hour window never requires an MLS Commit.

cases.name: e2ee_routing_window_change_breaks_dedup_without_commit
cases.notes: The same canonical emoji under the same epoch routing root yields a different tag after the signed outer Event crosses the one-hour routing window. The new add is a fresh OR-Set entry; no hourly MLS Commit or self-update is required.

cases.name: capability_revoked_blocks_subsequent_add
cases.notes: After ak.capability.revoke removes the actor's ak.reaction.add capability, the next add MUST be rejected before reducer state changes; in-flight events accepted before the revoke causal frontier remain in OR-Set state.

cases.name: rate_limit_high_rate_reaction_burst
cases.notes: Servers MAY rate-limit ak.reaction.add per actor; the reducer MUST treat rate-limited events as either rate_limited or quarantine, never as accepted-then-silently-dropped.

fixtures/realm-organization-fixture.json.description: Conformance vectors for the ak.realm.organization statement payload (organization-authorized Realm relationship endorsement / revocation). Validates schema_validation_cases[] against schemas/event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/realm_organization_payload via tools/artifact_lint. The verified organization relationship has two independent authorization layers (realm-and-space.md §2.3.0): Realm-side acceptance (writer holds ak.realm.admin or rides an allowed create-bootstrap batch) and Organization-side consent (payload.authorization proof verifies to the organization DID control state, a threshold governance quorum, or a delegated Account Authority / governance service whose delegation purpose covers ak.realm.organization, the relationship, and the control_scopes). Placeholder signature/proof strings are intentional and MUST NOT be treated as cryptographic vectors. Cases whose schema_only_valid is true but whose semantic_outcome is reject pass JSON Schema yet MUST be rejected by the reducer for the listed expected_reason_code; downstream SDK validators and cotest negative cases MUST assert that exact registered reason code rather than a bare string.

grade_definitions.V: Black-box verifiable by canonical conformance vectors and fixture runner results.
grade_definitions.A: Verifiable by the public SDK API shape and inventory; no implementation-private inspection is required.
grade_definitions.U: Verifiable only by implementation, configuration, or data-flow audit evidence.

sdk_conformance_contract.evidence_coverage_semantics_note: A clause's required_evidence enumerates the ACCEPTABLE evidence kinds for that clause (acceptable-set semantics), not a mandate that every listed kind be present. For a clause claim with result=pass or result=fail: at least one evidence entry MUST be present (already required by the schema when result != not_applicable), and every evidence[].kind MUST be a member of that clause's required_evidence set in this contract. Evidence whose kind falls outside the clause's required_evidence set MUST NOT be accepted as substantiation for that clause. result=not_applicable is exempt from evidence-kind coverage but MUST carry a machine-readable rationale.
rules: Each SDK release claiming Arkret v1 conformance MUST publish one claim object against this exact contract digest.
The claim MUST bind the exact SDK artifact digest and spec revision, and MUST carry an issuer signature over the domain-separated RFC 8785 JCS claim bytes with proof omitted.
Every evidence reference MUST carry a non-zero immutable content digest; consumers MUST verify all digests and the issuer verification method before accepting the claim.
Every applicable clause MUST appear exactly once; not_applicable MUST include a machine-readable rationale.
Evidence references MUST be content-addressed or carry an immutable CI run identifier.

A verifier MUST enforce evidence_coverage_semantics: for every clause claim whose result is pass or fail, it MUST reject the claim unless at least one evidence entry is present and every evidence[].kind is a member of that clause's required_evidence set. A pass/fail clause substantiated only by evidence kinds outside its required_evidence set MUST be rejected. This check is independent of, and applied in addition to, the digest and signature checks above.
Section numbers and table row numbers are not clause identifiers; only clause_id is stable.

clauses.summary: Validate Event Envelope and payload class before consumption
Do not expose a bypass for proof, HLC, actor sequence, prev refs, or authorization refs
Do not expose configuration that disables authorization constraints
Fail closed for causal, revoked, and invalid-proof states
Model cursor values as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Reject malformed or non-canonical JSON without repair
Reject malformed HLC without normalization or truncation
Preserve prev refs, authorization refs, and actor sequence constraints during retry
Verify governance binding and KeyPackage DID before decrypting or encrypting
Do not disclose plaintext or keys to unauthorized services
Light clients must not authorize a DataEvent from a single leaf proof
Apply late-key-recovery visibility checks before decrypting
Fail closed on unknown critical features or unmet requirements
Reject production use of test DIDs, keys, and trust domains
Reconcile trimmed build capabilities with every published profile claim
Preserve unknown values from open registries without failing whole-object deserialization
Preserve explicit extension-slot content through canonical round trips and forwarding
Model ack_token as opaque and expose no structured decode API
Do not automatically replay retry_safe=false operations and rotate the request key when content changes
Combine Retry-After and jittered local backoff with max; never accelerate for zero or short hints and never clamp a long hint
Continue pagination only when has_more is true
Expose the canonical confusable check as a callable SDK utility
Expose orthogonal closed Event outer-shape and payload-protection types and reject invalid combinations before network submission
Consume the protocol_version bootstrap discriminator before typed service claims, route caching, capability intersection, or business traffic

profile_sets.test_build_stance_rule: Test/conformance builds are marked solely by the canonical development_mode=true flag on the ServiceDescribe (see zh/sync/service-http-binding.md §2.1.2 and zh/sync/service-surface.md §3.0), which gates the test-only /_arkret/_conformance/* debug namespace and forces verified_profiles=[]. There is no separate ak.profile.* test-build profile: a test build is a deployment stance, not a negotiated interop capability.

profile_set_rules.v1_profile_catalog: Profiles that belong to the v1 stable catalog. This is not a bundle requirement; implementations MUST claim only the profiles, event kinds, schemas, and operations they actually support.
profile_set_rules.v1_minimal_interop_floor: Minimum profile for claiming v1 Event Store interop. Higher-level client, service, federation, blob, push, identity, and sovereign profiles remain independently claimable.
profile_set_rules.extension_profile_implementation: Optional. Tracks implementation profiles outside the v1 minimal interop floor, including evolving external standards (MIMI Internet-Drafts; A2A/ACP/MCP unstandardized agent protocols; Applet registry/audit SLA) and opt-in product features such as productivity, calendar events, pins, and search. Implementations claiming v1 core MAY omit these entirely; implementations MUST claim only entries they actually support. When an underlying external standard matures, a replacement profile with stable version pinning can supersede that entry.

profiles/conformance-profiles.json.candidate_profiles_tier_rule: Profiles pairing unregistered candidate workflow concept/action names / capabilities with an explicit fail-closed gate. Receivers MUST treat any capability action whose `profile` points to a candidate profile as unknown (risk_tier=high default) unless they implement the profile. Candidate profiles are NOT part of v1 active conformance and SHOULD be promoted (with paired wire Event.kind values registered under `ak.*`) once their underlying surface is formally registered.
profiles/conformance-profiles.json.profile_roles_rule: Every profile id MUST be annotated with exactly one role from the enum {client, server, gateway, directory, admin, interop}. Roles partition the profile namespace so that an implementation MUST NOT mistake e.g. a gateway profile (push_gateway, blob_node) for a client profile, or a deployment / hardening / vector profile (admin role) for a wire-conformance client / server profile. SDK manifests, client-side feature negotiation, and conformance harness loaders MUST consult `profile_roles` before claiming a profile as locally implemented. Roles in spec layer metadata; the per-profile object in `profile_requirements` MAY ALSO carry a `role` field for convenience, but `profile_roles` is the canonical source.

client_local_send_blockers.rationale: The Direct Conversation resolver may only report send blockers it can prove from accepted authoritative state. Two facts are structurally outside that boundary. ak.account.blocklist is holder-private account data that a synchronizing service is required to hold encrypted to holder devices only, so a service that evaluated personal_blocked would have to break that encryption invariant; and whether a given historical MLS secret was ever installed is device-private key state, so a client self-report of history_key_unavailable is a claim, not authority. Both values are therefore removed from the closed wire enum direct_conversation_send_blocker rather than merely annotated there: after removal a service that returns one produces a machine-detectable schema_violation, whereas an annotation would eventually be violated silently. They are carried instead by this closed client-local set, which is evaluated only on the holder's own device from state only that device holds. presence_offline and keypackage_empty stay on the wire because the service does hold provable facts for them, but they are visible only to an existing exact-pair participant of that pair, so they cannot serve as an enumeration oracle. The consequence is deliberate and MUST be documented by implementers: after a block, the fact that sending is refused is known only to the blocking client - not to its own service and not to the peer - and neither of them is entitled to know it. Implementations that habitually ask the server for send state will find the resolver returning found with an empty send_blockers[] and MUST still refuse the send locally. The normative conformance vector for this clause is ak.vector.direct_conversation.send_blocker_authority.v1.
rules: These values MUST NOT appear on any wire surface: not in direct_conversation_send_blocker, not in any operation request or response, not in any Event payload, and not on the peer carrier or federation surface.
A client MUST merge this local set with the server-returned found.send_blockers[] before releasing a send, and MUST fail closed locally when a local blocker applies.

A client-local blocker MUST NOT cause the resolver to return suspended and MUST NOT alter any wire state, so that server state is never polluted by device-local state and two devices of the same holder never disagree about the resolver outcome.
Implementations MUST NOT add any reporting, synchronization or probing channel whose purpose is to make the service or the peer aware that a client-local blocker applies.

binding_invariants: schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and fields.collaboration_role MUST equal direct_conversation; either marker without the other is schema_violation.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both equal e2ee_required.

The ak.realm.create Event requirements.schema MUST contain ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requirements.critical_extensions MUST contain fail_closed=true id ak.feature.direct_conversation_realm_role.v1 for payload scope.
Exactly the two ActorIds in the immutable binding may be Realm principal members; any third-party join or invite MUST be rejected.
Space events are forbidden in a Direct Conversation Realm with direct_conversation_space_forbidden; additional ordinary Strands remain allowed.
The canonical main Strand MUST be active, belong to the Realm, have no Circle scope, and expose an active primary discussion track.

First creation MUST be the founder's caller-authored four-Event unit submitted through the direct_conversation_founding branch of ak.self.events.command.submit.v1. realm_id and main_strand_id are retyped from the first and third Event IDs, so the service MUST NOT allocate an identifier, issue a reserved or materializing draft, or elect a coordinator; it only verifies the unit, CAS-closes its local (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot and accepts zero or four Events atomically.

The founding slot admits the first valid unit only. A second unit for the same pair MUST be refused with direct_conversation_slot_already_committed and zero writes; a byte-identical replay MUST return the stored receipt without advancing accepted_at; the same idempotency key with a different unit MUST be duplicate_conflict. The slot MUST NOT reopen into creation_required after a committed unit.

Cross-Station founding MUST NOT depend on the peer service: the founder creates the Realm and its one scope-derived MLS group and sends real ciphertext alone. Peer KeyPackage claim is participant-authorized, binds the accepted pair, Realm, main Strand and MLS group, and MUST NOT use a last-resort KeyPackage.

The unit's Genesis Seal MUST cover all four Events, every required founding write of an ordinary Realm create, and the create-locked baseline projection of join_rule=closed, content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1 and both e2ee_required floors together with the initial current history_access=since_join facet. Sealing any strict prefix and appending either membership Event or the Strand afterwards MUST be rejected, and a same-batch facet Event that repeats or overrides a baseline value MUST be rejected.

Between the accepted founding unit and the first legal binding endorsement, pre-binding writes MUST cite authorization_ref=ak.authority.direct_conversation_bootstrap_participant.v1 with exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit reference to the accepted ak.realm.create. The verifier recomputes the mutually exclusive phase from accepted facts; the producer MUST NOT declare it. Both phases retire permanently once the first legal endorsement is accepted.

The binding is immutable and fixes pair_key, participant pair, Realm and main Strand exactly once. It carries no authored lifecycle state or MLS group; an encrypted Direct Conversation has one scope-derived group and one monotonic epoch lineage projected from accepted history.

Leave, ban, block, either directional Contact terminal and participant terminal state suspend new writes without destroying the binding or creating a successor Realm. Consent changes never affect Personal DM authority. Recovery reuses the same Realm and MUST NOT automatically redeliver old epoch keys or history secrets.
Principal-private deletion and global content/key erasure retain stable pair, Realm and main Strand identity. The resolver never returns a competing candidate or performs winner selection.

Participant authority and root-owner masking are conjunctive profile admission rules and MUST be evaluated from the same accepted evidence basis as the target action; neither created_by nor membership alone is an authorization source.

The two client-local send blockers of client_local_send_blockers MUST NOT appear on any wire surface, and the resolver MUST NOT return suspended because one of them applies; the resolver reports only server-verifiable blockers, and personal_blocked or history_key_unavailable on the wire is a schema_violation.

ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1.description: Realm profile for a principal-scoped durable control stream. PCR genesis is one create-once atomic unit: identity-root-signed ak.realm.create plus founding-device-signed ak.device.authorize. After genesis, identity resolution, device state and recovery policy live in the PCR; the DID is only the identity-root key log and re-anchor fence.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Receivers that do not understand this v1 profile MUST NOT accept the Realm as principal control state.

rules: Agent PCR events MUST target the Agent DID bound to the Realm; controller execution uses actor_id=Agent DID, executed_by=controller DID, and a verified authorization_ref.

Initial provisioning MUST use one controller-owned ak.agent.provision Event in the controller PCR and atomically project provision, accountability and selector facts; later standalone accountability/selector changes remain controller-owned and MUST NOT move into the Agent PCR.
Pairing requests and account approval notifications MUST NOT be written to any PCR or Collaboration Realm.

binding_invariants: realm_id MUST equal the principal_control_realm_id resolved for the principal DID.
fields.purpose MUST be principal_control for human/organization PCRs or managed_agent_control for managed Agent PCRs; schema_refs MUST contain ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 in both cases.

Within a Principal Control Realm, ak.policy.set is admitted only for ak.root.identity.recovery_policy.command.publish.v1 with canonical payload {policy_id,value}, value.schema=ak.schema.recovery_policy.v1, equal policy ids, and no state/reason; admitting another policy family or bypassing ordinary Event, lease, reducer, allowlist, or Seal processing is non-conformant.
encryption_profile MUST be mls_rfc9420; PCRs MUST NOT use none or external.
content_encryption_floor and metadata_encryption_floor MUST both be e2ee_required; a PCR genesis declaring either floor below e2ee_required MUST be rejected (no plaintext-floor PCR exists in v1).

history_access MUST equal since_join. A standard-MLS PCR has no deliverable history secret; a new same-principal endpoint starts at its own initial Add/Welcome admission, while durable device-list and normalized principal views provide the control baseline without restoring foreign active MLS state.
Control events MUST bind principal_id / device_id / session grant audience to the same principal DID or an explicitly trusted recovery/session issuer.

A managed Agent principal_control_realm_id and immutable requested_scope commitment MUST be verified from the unique ArkretPrincipalControlRealm DID service entry at accepted-at; the public entry fixes only realm_id, controller_did, authorization_ref and the domain-separated requested_scope_digest. The complete scope MUST come from a controller-signed verifier/audience/challenge-bound private disclosure whose digest matches that commitment. Implementation-private deterministic derivation or a service-local Agent row is not protocol evidence.
Managed Agent PCR genesis created_by and notary MUST equal the Agent DID; a controller authoring under delegation MUST be recorded as executed_by and MUST NOT synthesize an Agent signature.

A managed Agent PCR genesis carries no anchor ref: delegated_pcr_genesis is selected by payload.object.purpose alone, and admission MUST instead reverse-look-up an already accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype(this genesis event_id). No match means zero writes. The genesis MUST arrive in a submission separate from that provision, because a same-unit or same-batch pair is the unconstructible shape encoding.md 6.0.1 forbids. The managed Agent PCR and its controller PCR MUST be hosted by the same Station, since the reverse look-up and the realm-id claim uniqueness are both local decisions.

A PCR MUST NOT carry a Realm alias. ak.realm.alias is absent from realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds, so a PCR is addressable only by realm_id; a human-readable alias on an identity-infrastructure control stream would publish the principal's control Realm under a guessable name.

realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds is closed in both directions: every kind whose normative prose requires a PCR write MUST appear in it, and every listed kind MUST have such prose. ak.identity.resolution.update is the only post-genesis successor of the create-locked ak.component.identity.resolution.v1 cell, and ak.contact.scope.update is the only directional Contact scope fact; both commit in the holder PCR and both are listed. The pcr-exposure-registry.json event-kind set MUST equal this allowlist, so an admitted kind can never lack a declared outward-exposure decision.
