conditional_requirements.exporter_all_history: A client that creates or joins a scope with content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1 and history_access=all_history_for_current_members MUST advertise ak.feature.history_key_recovery.v1 and implement the complete history-key request/manifest/chunk/response-stream plus receipt-bound direct accepted-Seal traversal contract through the standard Event, Seal and governance-dependency resolve surfaces. It MUST run the crash-safe automatic requester/source convergence loop: durable single-flight request create/resume, non-ack empty-page polling, exact source outbox retry, and a new manifest when later local-authoritative material remains uncovered. The stateless Seal-governance proof is near-current frontier only. Missing feature support is fail closed; standard MLS has no history-recovery fallback.

ak.profile.agent_signer_evidence.v1.description: Portable ordinary-Realm Native Agent signer authorization evidence. Producers publish one Agent authority snapshot with key and Agent-lifecycle witnesses, one privacy-minimal Account Authority controller gate, and a structural XOR between exact-request current observation and destination-signed historical Event admission receipt. Consumers independently verify all three orthogonal gates, reject cross-request replay, preserve accepted Event validity across later terminal transitions, and cross-bind encrypted Events to the historical MLS leaf.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Do not mark ordinary Native Agent Events Verified. Preserve ciphertext or quarantined plaintext with verification_pending and never fall back to keys/query or ordinary MLS leaf-only trust.

ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.description: Operation-local MLS binding interpreter for policy-derived relaxed E2EE. effective mls_send_pause=advisory selects this binding_profile; strict policy selects mls_governance_binding.full. This is not a Realm schema_refs or active-profile carrier.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Servers that do not advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 MUST reject ak.realm.policy_bundle writes that set mls_send_pause="advisory" with unsupported_profile. They MUST NOT silently accept advisory semantics.

downgrade_declaration_obligation.policy_declaration_required: The effective ak.realm.policy_bundle field mls_send_pause="advisory" is the sole Realm declaration. Realm genesis/schema refs and out-of-band deployment config MUST NOT activate relaxed mode.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.service_describe_required: The serving implementation MUST advertise ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 and the claimed profile in ServiceDescribe before accepting advisory writes or projecting the Realm as relaxed to a peer/facade.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.binding_profile_required: Every MLS governance_binding emitted for a relaxed Realm MUST carry binding_profile="ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1" and the negotiated reducer_profile. Missing binding_profile, binding_profile="ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1", or an unsupported profile id is a fail-closed mismatch.
downgrade_declaration_obligation.export_marker_required: Sync metadata, snapshots, backups, exports, and interop mapping receipts that summarize the Realm MUST preserve e2ee_relaxed=true and relaxed_window_max_ms. Consumers that observe advisory semantics without this marker MUST assume the downgrade is undeclared and reject new old-epoch decrypt admission.

client_ui_requirements.banner_warning: Realms declaring this profile MUST display a banner-level warning indicating that kick / ban is not cryptographically immediate; the warning MAY be temporarily collapsed but MUST NOT be permanently dismissable.
client_ui_requirements.invite_warning: When a user invites a new member, the UI SHOULD prompt with 'this Realm uses degraded E2EE' so the invitee can make an informed decision.
client_ui_requirements.export_marker: Sync metadata / backup / export MUST preserve a `e2ee_relaxed=true` marker so downstream consumers know the cryptographic guarantee is relaxed.

downgrade_window_constraint.rationale: Receiving client refuses to admit a message into verified timeline if the gap between receive_at and the most recent membership_change_at exceeds this window with old-epoch decryption.
downgrade_window_constraint.receiver_enforcement: Receiver MUST enforce the hard ceiling independently of any declared deployment value: if a Realm policy event sets relaxed_window_max_ms > absolute_hard_ceiling_ms (300000 ms / 5 min), the reducer MUST reject the policy update with reason_code `relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling` (mapped from `schema_violation`), and the receiver MUST treat the policy event as failed_precondition. Receivers MUST NOT silently clamp the value to the ceiling, because a silent clamp would let a deployment publish a longer window than receivers honor and split visible policy state across implementations. Negative vector: `ak.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1` covers (a) reducer reject on policy write > 300000 ms, (b) receiver reject on old-epoch decrypt admission when the gap exceeds the per-policy declared window, and (c) reject when any deployment tries to redefine the ceiling via an unrelated profile.
downgrade_window_constraint.compliance_profile_disabled: Profiles in the compliance / audited tier (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1, ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1, and any deployment with active Audit Applet Binding) MUST NOT enable ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Reducer MUST reject the combination with reason_code `e2ee_relaxed_disallowed_in_compliance_profile`. Rationale: compliance assurance presumes the kick-out semantic is cryptographically immediate; the relaxed window contradicts that presumption.

restricted_requires: each federation peer describes a fanout SLA not exceeding the relaxed window
each federation peer explicitly advertises ak.feature.e2ee_relaxed.v1 when it is expected to accept relaxed old-epoch decrypt admission
federation_guard.interop_floor: Full MLS governance binding (ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1) remains the federation E2EE interoperability floor. The relaxed profile (ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1) is a declared downgrade below that floor and is accepted across federation only for restricted/closed deployments that satisfy the bounded-SLA requirements above.

fail_closed_conditions: combination of ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1 with ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1, compliance-tier E2EE, active Audit Applet Binding, federation_policy=open, or federation_policy=quarantine
restricted federation without peer fanout SLA bounds within relaxed_window_max_ms
governance_binding.binding_profile missing, unsupported, or inconsistent with the Realm downgrade declaration
receiver old-epoch decrypt gap exceeds relaxed_window_max_ms or the absolute hard ceiling of 300000 ms
ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1.compliance_unfit: Compliance / regulatory contexts that require 'kick-out is immediately effective' MUST NOT use this profile. Use non-E2EE Realm (encryption_profile="none") + enclave channels instead. Spec deliberately does not allow further relaxation than this profile; deployments needing more leniency are out of v1 E2EE scope.

additional_requirements.invite_claim_reducer_authority_must: ak.invite.claim MUST be decided by the destination Realm reducer, not by an internal authentication component, verification service, Station transport ingress, or client projection caches.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_token_commitment_must: Reducer MUST match payload.token_commitment to the pending ak.invite.third_party invite and reject mismatch or already-claimed commitments with no membership proposal.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_allowlist_recheck_must: Reducer MUST re-check binding_proof.verification_id against the current effective Realm allowlist and any invite-pinned service DID before accepting subject_proof.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_nonce_dedup_must: Reducer MUST treat (invite_id, claim_nonce) and token_commitment as one-time constraints and reject replay with duplicate_conflict.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_membership_conversion_must: Successful claim MUST atomically transition invite pending -> claimed and materialize only a subject-bound standard invite or membership proposal; final join still requires ak.invite.accept or an explicitly profiled equivalent path.
additional_requirements.invite_claim_expiry_cleanup_must: Reducer MUST expire third-party invites before claim acceptance when expires_at <= now and trigger token material cleanup obligations from third-party-invites.md §6.1.
additional_requirements.history_key_recovery_conditional_must: A Station that accepts or serves an mls_exporter_aead_v1 scope with history_access=all_history_for_current_members MUST advertise ak.feature.history_key_recovery.v1 and expose the complete registered self/peer Seal-proof, request, response, relay and RRK archive operation set. Partial legacy realm_key feature claims are forbidden.
additional_requirements.account_authority_surface_must: The Station MUST publish exactly one auth_metadata.account_authority gate_account_base_url and expose all client-visible gate/account operations through that base. Any internal authentication process is deployment-private and MUST NOT publish a service kind, role-local Describe, service registration, federation identity, or peer-discoverable endpoint.
additional_requirements.session_grant_issuer_ledger_must: The Station Account Authority MUST be the sole durable authority for immutable SessionGrant issuance records and active, revoked, or superseded lifecycle. It MUST derive the suite-tagged grant ID and JWT jti from the complete closed issuance preimage, atomically persist issuance before response, provide durable exact replay for issue, refresh, and revoke, and use the same ledger for cascade and introspection.
additional_requirements.session_grant_dpop_binding_must: Issue, refresh, replay retrieval, and protected-resource presentation MUST verify current holder/DPoP proof, exact HTTP target and method, issuer/audience, and canonical request digest. An S2S HTTP Message Signature authenticates transport only and never substitutes for holder proof or principal, device, notary, or Event proof.
additional_requirements.account_status_publication_must: The Station Account Authority MUST atomically commit its account row, immutable AccountStatusRecord, audit, and outbox; genesis is status_seq=1 active and every successor is a current-head CAS. It exposes bounded ak.peer.account_status.read.resolve.v1 for authorized replica recovery and publishes exact record bytes through ak.peer.account_status.command.submit.v1 without maintaining a second status truth.

e2ee_mls_interop_floor.applies_when: Any federation transaction carries or depends on encryption_profile="mls_rfc9420", ak.mls.genesis, ak.mls.commit, ak.mls.welcome, MLS-backed E2EE DataEvents, or active MLS security-frontier state.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.downgrade_admission: Only closed or restricted federation may accept ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1, and restricted federation MUST satisfy the bounded-SLA federation_guard in that profile. Open and quarantine federation MUST reject the relaxed downgrade.
e2ee_mls_interop_floor.fail_closed_behavior: A receiver that cannot verify the minimum profile, sees a missing/inconsistent binding_profile or reducer_profile, or cannot prove the relaxed federation guard MUST reject or quarantine the affected MLS artifact/DataEvent before advancing Realm frontier.

ak.profile.service_resolution_mirror.v1.description: Optional Realm-scoped route-availability profile. It implements target-signed planned handover publication and authorized peer mirror resolution without becoming service identity or route authority.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: Omit the profile and both peer operations; normal current-record bootstrap and direct 1:1 handover remain usable when independently implemented, while an unannounced outage without another authorized carrier fails closed.

additional_requirements.target_signature_must: A mirror returns only byte-exact target-service-signed ServiceResolutionRecord and ServiceRouteHandoverNotice values; its own transport signature can never authorize a bare URL.
additional_requirements.visibility_must: Requester and target must both be currently visible in the named Realm through effective joined-member binding or explicit delegation; unknown, unauthorized, invisible and not-held responses are indistinguishable. No Realm-level transport endpoint grants visibility.
additional_requirements.durability_must: Remote record sequence/digest floors, notice revision/digest state and publish acknowledgements survive restart; replaceable TTL route cache is not this safety state.
additional_requirements.bounds_must: Resolve returns at most 32 continuous records and at most 256 KiB canonical response bytes.

ak.profile.signal_message_stream.v1.description: Optional client payload profile for authenticated transient Message generation previews carried inside the encrypted Signal Extension.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit live generation previews and continue receiving the final ak.message.create; never place ak.message.stream in durable Event history

additional_requirements.encrypted_only_must: Every ak.message.stream payload MUST be encrypted inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session; no plaintext branch exists.
additional_requirements.authorization_must: The recipient MUST verify ak.message.stream.send plus ak.message.create for the decrypted Strand at the envelope seal_ref basis before display.
additional_requirements.resource_must: Producer and recipient enforce 16 KiB preview, 5 frames/s, 8 concurrent streams, 15-second keyframes and 10-minute lifetime within the generic 46 KiB plaintext / 64 KiB Signal envelope limits.
additional_requirements.final_binding_must: Only a direct, verified ak.message.create with a message_id matching the complete retyped EventId token, actor, device, security scope, Realm, Strand and discussion track replaces the preview.

bounded batch/body/signature window and drop-unconfirmed retry behavior

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit ak.profile.signal_peer_relay.v1 and ak.peer.signal.command.relay.v1; local Signal and durable federation remain independently usable

additional_requirements.encrypted_only_must: Every relayed item MUST be ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1; plaintext or unencrypted ephemeral inputs fail closed with signal_plaintext_forbidden.
additional_requirements.single_hop_must: A destination MUST NOT relay a peer-received SignalEnvelope to a third service. The original sender-side service performs one direct request per eligible destination service.
additional_requirements.no_kind_advertisement_must: Describe MUST advertise only this profile and operation support; exact product signal kind and target remain encrypted and MUST NOT appear in supported-kinds or routing metadata.
additional_requirements.opaque_outcome_must: A valid authenticated request returns only {accepted:true}; no recipient, binding, capability, count or per-item outcome is exposed.
additional_requirements.retry_must: The operation forbids Idempotency-Key, is retry_safe=false and uses uncertain_outcome.strategy=drop_unconfirmed. A lost response MUST NOT cause automatic request replay.

ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1.description: High-assurance / sovereign / regulated / multi-writer federation profile. Adds mandatory proactive frontier exchange with fail-state semantics on top of the ak.profile.federation_minimal.v1 baseline. See zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.3 and zh/sync/sovereign-deployment.md §11.1.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: reject claim of ak.profile.federation.high_assurance.v1 if proactive frontier exchange or peer_stale fail-state is not implemented

additional_requirements.frontier_probe_capability_must: Peer MUST expose capability-gated frontier probe endpoint per federation.md §4.5.1.
additional_requirements.proactive_exchange_must: Per federation-visible Realm, per authorized peer, frontier probe interval MUST be <= 3600 seconds.
additional_requirements.fail_state_must: Three consecutive probe failures (peer unreachable or signature failure) MUST mark the peer as 'peer_stale' for that Realm. Separately, an aggregate-commitment difference MUST first be reduced via per-actor challenge/backfill on the intersection of replicated actors, comparing each (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) as a canonical sibling SET of (event_id,event_digest,prev_frontier_digest), not as a single hash. Different event_id/hash siblings at one actor_seq are legal within the event-and-patch.md §2.6 limits and MUST converge by validated set union. A same-event_id/different-digest conflict, an over-limit sibling set, a profile-declared non-joinable sibling conflict, or inconsistent witness payloads for the same complete attestation scope MUST quarantine the affected increments on the FIRST confirmed occurrence and MUST NOT be folded into the three-consecutive-failure window. Raw frontier_root/heads/range-root differences across different scopes, and incomplete subsets of a legal sibling set, MUST NOT alone count as probe failure or witness_disagreement.
additional_requirements.stale_peer_behavior_must: While a peer is in 'peer_stale' state: MUST quarantine its push payloads for the affected evidence scope (no local frontier advancement from that scope); MUST surface state via operator alarm channel; MAY refuse to fanout new Events to that peer. Stale status MUST clear after the original evidence is resolved: the disputed event id/digest or over-fork/non-joinable sibling bucket has an authorized canonical resolution and the peer matches that canonical sibling set, or witnesses for the same complete attestation scope again sign one consistent payload. Scope-different peers MUST NOT be required to have globally identical heads.

ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1.description: Default push gateway privacy baseline. Every implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile. Provider-facing payloads MUST NOT carry stable identifying fields (principal DID, sender DID, Realm id / name / avatar, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device verification-method DID URL, reaction value, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key). Payloads MUST be restricted to per-(recipient_id, principal, device, push_route) pairwise pseudonym push_target_id + closed-enum wakeup hint fields (wakeup_kind, badge_count, unread_increment, l10n_key). See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §2.2 / §4.5 / §5.1 and zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md §5.6.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: MUST fail closed; gateways unable to enforce blind wakeup MUST NOT claim ak.profile.push_gateway.v1

additional_requirements.stable_identifier_ban_must: Provider payload MUST NOT contain principal DID, sender DID / handle, Realm id / name, Strand id / name, Message id, event id, device verification-method DID URL, reaction emoji, attachment filename, IP, geolocation, or any cross-Realm stable correlation key.

additional_requirements.default_claim_must: Any implementation claiming ak.profile.push_gateway.v1 MUST also claim this profile and MUST NOT advertise downgrade switches that disable blind wakeup.

Even when claimed, payloads MUST stay minimised: no message body, no DID URL, no cross-Realm stable correlation key, no IP / geolocation, no free-form text outside the profile-declared field set. See zh/discovery/push-notifications.md §5.1.

Bridges MUST partition traffic so that any peer or device negotiated under ak.profile.push_gateway.blind_wakeup.v1 (i.e. the default v1 baseline) NEVER receives a matrix_passthrough payload. ak.profile.matrix_compat.v1.description: Optional Matrix interop compatibility profile. Declares wire-shape parity for the Matrix-derived surfaces: to-device queue, /keys/upload|query|claim, push gateway facade, and SAS verification message strand. Arkret device authorization remains PCR-native and is outside this compatibility profile. Account-aggregate sync is NOT covered: Arkret v1 chose a streaming push form (ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1 / GET /account/subscribe with NDJSON frames) over Matrix's long-poll /sync, so wire-shape parity is not claimed for this surface — Matrix clients MUST adapt the account-aggregate consumption loop. Implementations claiming this profile MUST treat the ak.* names of the listed surfaces as semantically equivalent to their Matrix counterparts so that Matrix client SDK code can be reused for those surfaces with only adapter changes. This profile does NOT add new wire fields; it is a conformance assertion about behavioural equivalence on the listed surfaces.

ak.profile.circle_seal_cadence.fixed_5m..description: Named cadence profile for confidential Circle sub-seal commitments. Implementations claiming this profile MUST emit ak.circle.seal_commit on a fixed time cadence (5 minutes, max jitter 30 seconds), MUST include empty-batch commitments, and MUST NOT use event-count or activity-triggered public commitments. Mobile energy saving may batch private sub-seal upload, but MUST NOT relax the public Realm seal cadence.

period_ms.rationale: Public Realm seal commitment cadence is fixed at 5 minutes for this profile.

max_jitter_ms.rationale: Bounded scheduling jitter; implementations MUST NOT encode activity by delaying beyond this window.

empty_batch_commitments.rationale: No-activity intervals still emit commitments to avoid leaking activity frequency.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: omit profile claim; confidential Circle deployments MUST NOT claim an event-count cadence as equivalent

ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1.description: Conformance profile pinning the machine-contract surface for Circle (intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary; see zh/models/circle.md). Splits actor content payload (`scope_circle_id` where that object schema defines it), the signed Event `scope_ref`, and the materialized object's `effective_scope`; it also pins the Circle event-kind family, member-state transition table, encryption-profile compatibility, and scope-rebind reducer-reject semantics. Required by implementations that emit or consume Circle events or that materialize Circle-scoped Strand / Message / Morph / Relation / Space objects.

feature_discovery.unsupported_optional: implementations that cannot verify the signed Event scope_ref and its equivalence to reducer-derived scope MUST NOT claim ak.profile.circle_conformance.v1; receivers MUST treat any unknown Circle event-kind as schema_violation

additional_requirements.submit_payload_must: Object payload schemas that own scope_circle_id (including Strand, Morph, Relation, and scoped Space create/update shapes) MAY carry only that field as their actor-authored scope selector and MUST reject effective_scope (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed). The rejection is decidable from the artifact schemas alone on both surfaces: every create shape reuses its object schema, and Relation - the one object schema that declares effective_scope on a patch surface - additionally forbids the effective_scope / effective_scope.* patch paths, registered per object kind in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json. Message and structural-operation payloads derive scope from accepted target references and MUST NOT invent a duplicate scope_circle_id; every Event still carries the producer-signed scope_ref.
additional_requirements.canonical_reducer_output_must: The producer MUST sign the tagged Event scope_ref. The receiver MUST derive the effective scope from the frozen pre-state and payload, require exact equality with scope_ref, and materialize the same value as the object's read-only effective_scope. A later scope_circle_id rebind MUST NOT re-interpret historical Events or objects.
additional_requirements.scope_rebind_default_reject_must: Default reducer MUST reject scope_circle_id rebind (None<->Some, Some(A)->Some(B)) with failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden. Profile-declared audit-paired rebind MAY be permitted, but MUST emit ak.audit.accessed pairing.
additional_requirements.circle_encryption_profile_floor_must: Circle.encryption_profile may be none or mls_rfc9420. Reducer MUST reject plaintext Circle creation or update when the parent Realm encryption_profile is mls_rfc9420 or the effective content_encryption_floor is e2ee_required (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor).
additional_requirements.circle_content_encryption_floor_must: Circle.content_encryption_floor (allow_plaintext | e2ee_required) is optional and symmetric with Circle.metadata_encryption_floor: when omitted it inherits the parent Realm content_encryption_floor, and the effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, Circle content_encryption_floor). Reducer MUST reject a Circle floor below the effective floor and MUST reject content_encryption_floor=e2ee_required on an encryption_profile=none Circle (reason=circle_encryption_below_realm_floor). See zh/models/circle.md §7.
additional_requirements.encryption_floor_ratchet_must: The effective content_encryption_floor and effective metadata encryption floor of any scope (Realm-default or Circle) are one-way ratchets: monotonically non-decreasing over time. A ak.realm.policy_bundle or ak.circle.update that lowers the effective content floor from e2ee_required to allow_plaintext MUST be rejected (reason=content_encryption_floor_downgrade); one that lowers the effective metadata floor MUST be rejected (reason=metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade). Tightening is always allowed. Vectors: ak.vector.e2ee.content_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.metadata_floor_downgrade_rejected.v1, ak.vector.circle.content_floor_below_realm_rejected.v1, ak.vector.e2ee.in_place_enable.v1.
additional_requirements.circle_membership_subset_must: Circle.members MUST be a strict subset of parent Realm.members; reducer MUST reject ak.circle.member.state -> join when the target actor is not a `join` member of the parent Realm (reason=circle_member_must_be_realm_member).
additional_requirements.scope_invariant_must: The Station sync surface MUST NOT deliver Events with scope_ref.kind=circle to actors not in that Circle's member frontier at the Event's causal frontier (see zh/models/circle.md §9.3 scope-delivery invariant).

registry/account-data-key-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of standard Account Data key patterns. Every row explicitly declares its closed writer authorities, holder self-surface operations, cross-device merge primitive, and delete semantics; see spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md section 5.
registry_rules: writer_authorities is a non-empty unique array over the closed v1 set holder_event | station_cas. holder_event requires non-empty write_event_kinds; station_cas requires plaintext_account_data plus plaintext_schema and does not mint an Event.

holder_self_operations is a unique array over put | delete. It explicitly controls ak.self.account_data.resource.replace.v1/delete for the row; an empty array forbids both. Implementations MUST NOT infer self mutability from storage or deletion_mode.

All v1 account-data keys use the cas_register merge primitive: the key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register, every write carries expected_revision and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1. Adding an uncoordinated merge primitive requires a registry revision with its comparison transcript, tombstone rule and an active conformance vector. Domain rules such as HLC last-writer-wins or delete-wins run inside the client's compare-and-set retry loop over decrypted plaintext; the server sees only opaque bytes and MUST NOT be asked to merge them.

deletion_mode declares how a key stops holding a live value. physical_delete uses ak.self.account_data.resource.delete.v1, which stores a versioned tombstone and MAY garbage-collect it later; the per-key revision high-water mark is retained forever so a stale write can never resurrect a deleted value. value_tombstone means the deleted state is itself a value written through ak.account_data.set and MUST NOT be physically deleted, because the domain requires an unrevivable terminal state that stays observable after tombstone GC.
encrypted_value_schema is optional and, when present, names the canonical schema file for decrypted encrypted_account_data plaintext. Producers and consumers MUST validate it after decryption.

account_data_key_patterns.description: Private per-Realm tags and ordering hints.
Principal-private notification and push rule configuration.

Principal-private dismissed/archived state for one derived Notification. The encrypted value binds notification_id, state, HLC and device tie-break material; read/unread remains derived from the read cursor.
Actor-private View definition. The encrypted value validates as ak.schema.view.v1 with visibility=private; it never enters a shared Realm View cell.
Principal-private do-not-disturb schedule used by notification routing. Decrypted plaintext validates as ak.schema.dnd_schedule.v1.
Principal-private custom emoji and sticker collection metadata.
Private client UI state such as sidebar, recent realms (canonical key recent_realms), language, and layout preferences.
Holder-private personal blocklist. It affects only the holder's local projection, notifications, contact handling, and trusted holder-side filtering.

Principal-private global petname, global display-name snapshot, note, tag, and pin metadata for one accepted human Contact peer.principal_id. principal_key is base64url(HMAC-SHA256(account_data_namespace_key, RFC8785_JCS(["ak.contacts.actor", peer.principal_id]))).
Private local remark, note, tag, and pin metadata for a Realm.

Principal-private sender-side presence visibility policy. Station sync surfaces MUST NOT project or read presence_visibility; encrypted Signal fanout is selected by the sender according to profiles-presence.md section 3.4.

Principal-private manual presence preference: pinned manual_state (online/idle/dnd), temporary status_message override, and clears_at expiry. Enforced client-side at send time across all of the principal's devices; services MUST NOT require plaintext or a projection of this key and MUST NOT treat it as a policy projection surface.
Private read-receipt send/display defaults and per-Realm or per-Strand overrides.
Principal-private reminders keyed by opaque id; target_ref and note remain inside encrypted value.

Principal-private scheduled-send plan keyed by an independent producer-allocated ScheduledSendId. The plan carries no future EventId or MessageId. Dispatch derives the final EventId only after the complete canonical Event preimage exists, then retypes that Event token into MessageId.
Principal-private snooze state keyed by HMAC-derived target_key.
Principal-private saved item in an HMAC-derived collection; each item is an independent account-data value.
Principal-private cross-device draft sync key. Raw target_ref MUST NOT appear in the account-data key.

Principal-private cross-device file transfer record keyed by an HMAC-derived transfer_key. Blob bytes are stored through ak.self.blob.*; raw blob_ref, filename, target device ids, and plaintext hashes MUST NOT appear in the account-data key.
Encrypted client search-index manifest keyed by an HMAC-derived realm_key.

Controller-owned encrypted draft created when Station materializes an agent's ak.agent.draft.propose / ak.agent.action_request after capability / policy / accountability / risk check. Draft MUST NOT enter shared Realm history; publishing produces a new shared event referencing only an opaque digest. See private-objects.md §4.1.

Controller-private per-context Sidecar hosted-view state. Synchronizes display_mode (context_merged or sidecar_only), pin/collapse state, and HLC without changing either Strand, Track, access, read, watch, notification, or search state.

Actor-private plaintext quarantine inbox for invites held by the consent gate default profile. The recipient Station is the sole CAS writer; holder self PUT/DELETE and synthetic ak.account_data.set are forbidden. Accepted writes fan out as service-sender ak.account_data.update hints and MUST NOT expose contactability signals to the inviter.

Actor-private holder-side carrier for delivered directed-invite credentials on the notify branch (invite-addressing.md section 7). Written by the recipient Station through the delivery path, so the value is plaintext JSON (ak.schema.invite_delivery.v1), not a client-encrypted envelope; invite_token is a server-issued private locator that MUST NOT enter the Invite object or Realm history. Bounded CAS register: at most 200 entries, expired entries purged first, then oldest evicted; accepted writes fan out as ak.account_data.update actor-private device updates.

registry/account-status-replica-decision.description: Canonical decision table for the account-status replica receiver classification defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3.1. A receiver of ak.peer.account_status.command.submit.v1 classifies an already transport- and proof-verified AccountStatusRecord by comparing it against exactly one baseline: the receiver's durable replica head for (account_authority_id, account_id). Rows are evaluated in the declared order and the first matching row decides the outcome.
registry_rules: The durable replica head is the only comparison baseline. A receiver MUST NOT classify a submission against a stored history row for the submitted status_seq, because how much history a receiver happens to retain is a local retention decision and MUST NOT change the typed outcome of a byte-identical request.

Rows are evaluated top to bottom and the first match wins. binding_version_rollback is evaluated before every sequence row so that a rolled-back binding can never be durably written by a submission that would otherwise advance the chain.

Within one head_state the sequence conditions are mutually exclusive and exhaustive over the four relations submitted.status_seq < head.status_seq, == head.status_seq, == head.status_seq + 1 and > head.status_seq + 1, so declaration order is documentation rather than a tie-break.

accepted and duplicate are the only terminal acks. duplicate means the durable head already is the submitted record, which is the only situation in which the replication objective for that record is genuinely met; it MUST NOT be returned for a lower status_seq, because that would let a bounded outbox mark a destination complete while the successor record is still unreplicated.

Every rejected row performs zero replica, receipt and outbox writes and is non-retryable for the exact submitted record. dependency_missing is the only outcome that keeps the exact record retryable, and it carries required_status_seq so the caller resolves the gap before resubmitting.

classifications.name: binding_version_rollback
classifications.description: The submission carries a binding version below the receiver's durable floor. Evaluated before the sequence rows so a rollback binding is never accepted by the advance branch.

classifications.name: genesis_admission
classifications.description: The receiver has no durable head yet and the submission is the genesis record. The replica is created at status_seq 1 in one atomic transaction.

classifications.name: genesis_gap
classifications.description: The receiver has no durable head and the submission is not the genesis record. The response carries required_status_seq = 1 and triggers a bounded resolve.

classifications.name: advance
classifications.description: The submission is the exact successor of the durable head and its predecessor reference matches. The replica advances by one in one atomic transaction.

classifications.name: fork_predecessor_mismatch
classifications.description: The submission claims the next sequence but does not name the durable head as its predecessor. Automatic retry and gap recovery stop; the record is quarantined for operator investigation.

classifications.name: duplicate
classifications.description: The submission is byte-identical to the durable head. This is the idempotent terminal ack: the replication objective for this record is met and the caller dequeues the destination.

classifications.name: fork_same_sequence
classifications.description: The durable head sequence already names a different record. Automatic retry and gap recovery stop; the record is quarantined for operator investigation.

classifications.name: stale
classifications.description: The submission is below the durable head. This holds even when the submitted record is byte-identical to a history row the receiver still stores for that status_seq: the baseline is the head, never a retained history row, so the outcome is stale and never duplicate.

classifications.name: sequence_gap
classifications.description: The submission is beyond the next sequence. The response carries required_status_seq = head.status_seq + 1 and triggers a bounded resolve; the exact record stays retryable once the gap is filled.

registry/authority-set-policy-registry.j.description: Canonical registry of authority-set policy symbols and deterministic projections from accepted CBA control state. Registry rows are templates, not authority: each lease carries the concrete AuthoritySetPolicy and its digest, and verifiers rederive it from basis_ref plus CBA closure.
registry_rules: authority_set_id values MUST be unique and MUST match the concrete AuthoritySetPolicy.authority_set_id
A concrete policy MUST use the registered policy_kind and source_kind, then project authorization_rules exactly from fixed_rules or rules_source
authorization_rules MUST be ordered lexicographically by rule_id; each rule's issuers MUST be ordered lexicographically by verification_method and allowed_actions MUST be ordered lexicographically

A lease is authorized only by the unique registered rule whose rule_id equals authorization_rule_id and whose allowed_actions covers action; different rules MAY cover the same action, rules are alternatives, and proofs MUST NOT be combined across rules
authority_set_digest is SHA-256(JCS(the complete concrete AuthoritySetPolicy object))
A verifier MUST rederive source_ref, source_digest, generation_ref and issuer verification methods from the accepted basis; inline policy bytes are portable evidence, not an authority source
A candidate or post-basis control object MUST NOT create authority for a lease evaluated at an earlier basis

policies.rules_source: accepted recovery policy and current Account Authority recovery admission state

projection.authorization_rules: only recovery factors admitted by the Account Authority for the named account subject

policies.rules_source: accepted_recovery_policy.publication_authorization_rules rederived from allowed_proof_kinds and linked accepted state

projection.authorization_rules: one rule per allowed proof kind; did_root/recovery_unlock/trusted service use threshold 1, device_quorum uses device_quorum.k, threshold_recovery uses its recovered signing key with threshold 1 (Shamir reconstruction k is not a signature quorum)

registry_rules: A non-grant authorization source is active only when one exact active row is selected by authority_source_id; syntax or an arbitrary Event/cell reference never creates authority.

The evaluator MUST rederive all activation, actor, resource and lifecycle predicates from accepted signed evidence at the Event CBA basis or the current non-event request basis and MUST fail closed on missing, conflicting, non-canonical or freshness-unknown dependencies.
Profile-scoped sources do not enter issuer_authority_refs, cannot authorize ak.capability.grant, and cannot be widened by Realm owner/admin aggregation.

When an Event is directly participant-authored, authorization_ref uses the source wire_ref and refs contains the registered binding_ref_role. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref continues to bind the delegated executor grant/delegation; the profile source is an independent conjunctive evaluator gate and is never replaced by that delegation.

entries.description: Mandatory Arkret v1 core HTTPS JSON/NDJSON binding.
Optional HTTPS tus companion binding; operation coverage comes only from advertised operation bundles.
Optional authenticated multiplexed WebSocket binding; operation coverage comes only from advertised operation bundles.

registry_rules: A calendar schedule MUST carry a signed tzdb_version naming one release row below. Receivers resolve timezone and every derived instant with that release, never with their locally installed release.

Release rows are append-only and each row is frozen once published, including its own required_normalizations table, because historical schedules signed that row. Withdrawing a release is expressed by setting status=deprecated, never by deleting or rewriting the row.

required_normalizations is per release, not global. A later IANA release that changes a Link target expresses that by carrying a different mapping in its own row; the earlier row keeps the mapping that was in force when those schedules were signed. A global table could not represent both at once and would silently break the append-only promise.

Determinism comes from the release tag: IANA tzdata release tags are immutable once published. This registry deliberately does not mirror the full Zone/Link table and does not pin a distribution digest, because a hand-copied mirror would drift from IANA and become a second truth source, and this repository cannot verify third-party distribution bytes. Deployments that additionally need supply-chain pinning verify the distribution in their own build; that pinning is out of scope for v1 interop.

Canonicalization is defined by the Link declarations of the pinned IANA release as published by IANA, in particular its backward and etcetera files: the canonical Zone is the Link target. It is NOT defined by whatever a given platform time zone library happens to expose, since distributions may build the same release with different link handling.

Producers MUST rewrite timezone to the canonical Zone before signing. Receivers MUST NOT re-canonicalize a signed value: an alias that reaches the wire is a producer defect and MUST be rejected, not repaired. The RSVP occurrence key reuses the exact signed timezone value.

Each row required_normalizations is the conformance-required subset that vectors pin for that release. It is not the full alias set; an input outside the table is still canonicalized by that release Link declarations.

Updating a schedule tzdb_version MAY change derived instants but MUST NOT change the signed timezone value or any local occurrence key. When any occurrence instant or end changes, the significant-change table requires RSVP needs_reconfirmation plus a schedule notification.

A service that cannot execute a schedule tzdb_version MUST fail closed with calendar_tzdb_mismatch or unsupported_feature, or mark instant projection unresolved. Falling back to a nearby or newer release is forbidden. Services declare their executable set in ServiceDescribe.calendar_tzdb_versions.

releases.notes: v1 conformance baseline release. Frozen: this row required_normalizations is the mapping schedules pinned to 2025a were signed against.
Appended release; schedules pinned to it expand with its rules only. Its required_normalizations is identical to 2025a because no listed Link target changed between the two releases.

registry/canonical-lexeme-registry.json.description: Closed adjudication table for Arkret-owned domain words that have historically acquired shortened aliases. Ordinary words stay complete on every contract surface; abbreviations are admitted only by one of the registered authority classes. The lint rejects every forbidden alias on schema property, type, symbolic-value, registry-symbol, fixture and normative JSON-example surfaces.

abbreviation_authorities.rule: The initialism is the canonical name of an externally anchored standard or algorithm and the owning schema or registry records that authority; examples include DID, MLS, JWS, JWK, JWT, HTTP, TLS, URI, URL, UUID and OIDC.
The initialism is a canonical Arkret term explicitly defined by spec/v1/zh/overview/glossary.md; examples include CBA, PCR and E2EE.
The compact word is part of a closed structural naming table; v1 registers id and ref through common-fields.md identifier rules and the NC-TYPE-001 wrapper table.
A field or value is preserved byte-for-byte from an external specification at an exact schema path carrying the required external anchor.

namespace_qualification_policy.internal_name_rule: An Arkret-owned field, type, claim kind or symbolic value is already interpreted in the Arkret namespace and MUST NOT repeat the product name as an arkret_ or Arkret prefix.
namespace_qualification_policy.qualification_rule: A product or protocol qualifier is admitted only at an externally owned extension point, in a shared global namespace, as a cryptographic domain-separation label, or as a provider/backend discriminator where an unqualified word would collide. The exact qualified name and boundary MUST be registered before use.
namespace_qualification_policy.external_import_rule: Imported semantics use the external authority's stable registered name (for example oidc, scim, mimi or matrix) only when the contract intentionally distinguishes parallel authorities; generic future-proof prefixes are forbidden.
namespace_qualification_policy.reserved_protocol_namespaces: The globally serialized ak. symbolic namespace and ak: typed-ID namespace are mandatory protocol namespaces, not redundant product-word prefixes.

exact_non_contract_exceptions.name: controllingOrg
exact_non_contract_exceptions.reason: Raw did:webvh witness method evidence preserves the external controllingOrg member byte-for-byte.

canonical_terms.reason: Organization is an Arkret core domain noun, not a standard initialism. Shortening it creates competing wire, type and profile vocabularies.
canonical_terms.identifier_rule: When the value is an Organization DID, the field MUST use organization_id or a more specific <role>_organization_id form; bare organization is reserved for an embedded Organization value rather than its identifier.
allowed_non_contract_contexts: internet DNS names including the .org top-level domain
opaque or externally owned identifier payloads
historical changelog text and negative conformance cases that name the rejected alias

canonical_terms.reason: Arkret is the default namespace for Arkret-owned claim kinds and credential concepts. Repeating the product name does not disambiguate an external authority and would force internal renames whenever another protocol is imported.
canonical_terms.identifier_rule: Use organization_membership_credential on Arkret-owned claim/type axes. An externally owned extension point that truly needs qualification must register its exact mapped term and external boundary instead of leaking that qualifier back into the Arkret claim kind.

qualified_external_forms.name: https://arkret.org/v1/credentials/organization-membership
qualified_external_forms.boundary: W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model type extension point
qualified_external_forms.reason: The W3C type value occupies an externally owned shared namespace and therefore uses an absolute Arkret-owned type IRI; this external name does not rename the internal claim_kind.

allowed_non_contract_contexts: historical changelog text and negative conformance cases that name the rejected spelling

canonical_terms.reason: Presentation request is an Arkret-owned object in an Arkret specification, so the product qualifier is redundant.
canonical_terms.identifier_rule: Use presentation_request for the local symbolic value and ak.identity.presentation_request for its globally serialized protocol kind.
allowed_non_contract_contexts: historical changelog text and negative conformance cases that name the rejected spelling

risk_tier_definitions.low: Read, projection, discovery, ack, and account-private affordances. Freshness fail-closed treats unknown / stale as local-pending allowed (capabilities.md §18).
risk_tier_definitions.medium: Object create / update / delete, message authoring, invite issuance, MLS proposal, audit query. Freshness requires recent frontier within freshness_required_ms.
risk_tier_definitions.high: Capability mutation, policy mutation, lifecycle freeze / tombstone / destroy, schema redefinition, MLS commit / welcome / genesis, audit export, moderation decision, admin / hierarchy / upgrade. Freshness MUST be within freshness_required_ms; partition forces local pending with no peer visibility.

registry_rules: Wire capability grant.actions[] entries MUST be drawn from this registry; wildcards / segment globs are statically rejected by capability-grant.schema.json.

Receivers MUST default to risk_tier=high when an action submitted in a grant or evaluated in policy is not present in this registry; this is the freshness fail-closed default required by capabilities.md §18.

required_constraints lists typed-constraint shorthand names that the capability evaluator MUST enforce for the action regardless of the grant author's declarations; absence in this list does NOT disable other declared constraints.

required_evaluator_checks lists non-grant-field invariants (for example actor_eq_target_author or audit_pair_required) that admission control MUST enforce from Event context, reducer state, or paired audit evidence. These are not grant-constraint schema fields.

target_event_kinds links the action to one or more ak.* event_kinds in event_kind_registry. Empty array means the action authorizes a read / projection / signaling path that does not produce a durable reducer-input event. Reducer admission for a listed event_kind MUST verify the actor holds at least one matching action grant.

profile is null for v1 core actions, or a ak.profile.*.v<n> id when the action is only meaningful inside that profile. Receivers without the named profile MUST treat the action as unknown (risk_tier=high default).

Every action MUST declare event_mapping_kind. action == single target_event_kind uses same_name; empty target_event_kinds uses non_event_surface; any other mapping MUST use one of the allowed deviation categories.

grant_authority_actions lists the action ids an issuer holding this action MAY sign a grant for (capabilities.md section 3.2 issuer upper bound). It is a separate namespace from target_event_kinds, which only expresses direct Event admission: several actions can map to one event kind, so an event-kind subset MUST NOT be used to satisfy an action-level grant authority question.

coverage_rule and grant_authority_rule declare how target_event_kinds and grant_authority_actions are derived from the other rows. When a rule is present the materialized list is a cached projection: tools/artifact_pipeline.py generate rewrites it and check rejects any hand edit on either this registry or the generated view.

root_control_only=true marks an action that only the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell may author. It is never grantable and never enters a derived owner authority set. subject_only=true marks a self-service action whose only authority is the target subject's own signature. reducer_only=true marks a record the reducer materializes and no principal may author. The three flags are orthogonal and combinable.

actions.notes: Authorizes only actor_role=ghost ak.applet.managed_actor.provision inside the closed four-Event Ghost unit: provision, applet_managed_control PCR genesis, accountability grant and profile create. The conditional Event admission and operation validator require the exact active registration/grant/scope and atomic set.

Reducer-materialized record of a Realm-link inheritance derivation (zh/models/realm-links.md section 6). No principal authors it and no principal can be granted it, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Subject-only self-service release of the actor own grant. Authority comes from the target grant subject signature and the reducer target guard, never from a capability, so it is excluded from every derived authority set.

Read-only audit access for a Realm admin NOT in the target Circle. MUST be paired with ak.audit.accessed event. Does NOT yield historical decryption keys unless the admin is formally added to the Circle.

Creates an intra-Realm Circle (scoped event/message boundary; optionally MLS-backed depending on parent Realm floor). NOT in default member bundle by default — Circles should be few and stable. See zh/models/circle.md §8.
Manage an existing Circle. MUST be constrained to specific circle_id selectors; unconstrained Realm-wide grant is not a normal management permission.
Self-service: actor accepts an invite, joins a join_rule=open Circle, or leaves. Reducer enforces payload.actor_id == envelope.actor_id and transition legality. Self-unbanning MUST fail closed.
Cross-actor write (rare). MUST carry ak.audit.accessed pair (same model as ak.strand.watch.set.others).
Invite / remove others. Held by Circle admin. payload.actor_id != envelope.actor_id.

Authorizes only the transaction-bound old-series targets in a fixed SecurityRotationTransaction plan after both replacement active-series pointers are accepted. It never authorizes deleting an active or unplanned backup series.
Direct Conversation participant self-leave only. It never authorizes leave/ban/remove of the other participant or any join transition.

Accepted-at compensation for a self-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard leave transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it cannot be transferred or used as ordinary membership authority.

Accepted-at compensation for a delegated/admin-authored join only. It authorizes one fresh standard remove transition for the exact admission and old membership incarnation; it grants no Realm admin capability.

Direct Conversation exact-pair self-rejoin only. It never authorizes a first join, a third participant, or a join authored on behalf of the other participant, and it never authorizes any grant, policy, admin, Strand or binding change.

Authorizes adding an audience_mention node such as @all or @here to a Message create/revise. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered. This is an additional gate: the actor MUST also be authorized for the underlying message create/revise action. Effective Realm/Circle policy MUST allow the audience and declare finite max_recipients/quota before notification fanout.

Authorizes a decrypted ak.message.stream Signal payload for one discussion Strand. It is an additional recipient-verified gate: the sender MUST also hold ak.message.create. The service cannot inspect or advertise the encrypted payload kind or Strand target.

Narrow Direct Conversation participant authority for welcoming another currently authorized device of the same stable participant. It cannot add a third principal or a device of the other participant.
Authorizes reading an object's discussion / history events (message timeline, redacted-message metainfo, prior revisions). Read / projection surface only; emits no durable reducer event.

Claims, renames or tombstones the Realm's human-readable alias (ak.realm.alias event; projects ak.component.realm.alias.v1). high risk because an alias is the address users type and share: capturing or re-pointing one is a phishing / impersonation primitive. Holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. See zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3.
Advances the authority generation, invalidating every grant anchored to the previous one at read time. Destructive root control; never grantable.

Terminal Realm lifecycle. Authored only by the current controller of the Realm authority-root cell with an independent destructive confirmation; it MUST NOT be granted to anyone, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Highest explicit authority inside one Realm. Held either by the current controller of the ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell (root authority, not a grant) or by an ordinary revocable co-owner grant. Both derived sets are rule-generated; hand edits are rejected by tools/artifact_pipeline.py check.

Rotates the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. Authored only by the current controller with successor acceptance; it MUST NOT be granted, so it is excluded from every derived owner authority set.

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer (ak.realm.set_default_strand event; projects Realm default_strand_id). Same-name discipline. The Realm authz gate is realm-admin: holding ak.realm.admin (aggregate admin coverage) satisfies admission, or grant this specific action directly. Reducer MUST verify the referenced Strand already exists (failed_precondition otherwise). See zh/models/strand-and-message.md default-Strand discovery section.
Terminal Realm lifecycle with a successor pointer. Same root-control family as ak.realm.destroy: authored only by the current authority-root controller and never grantable.
Holder-private consent is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm; it is never grantable to a Realm co-owner or another principal.
Holder-private consent revocation is authored only by the current controller of the holder Principal Control Realm and must remove caller-observed dots; it is never grantable.

New writes MUST use an active row. Unknown, deprecated, duplicate, or owner-unresolvable names fail closed with schema_violation.
owner.kind=schema requires schema_ref to resolve to an effective reference registered by schema_registry; owner.kind=profile requires profile_id to resolve in conformance-profiles.json.

registry_rules: A non-grant authorization source is active only when one exact active row is selected by authority_source_id; syntax or an arbitrary Event/cell reference never creates authority.

The evaluator MUST rederive all activation, actor, resource and lifecycle predicates from accepted signed evidence at the Event CBA basis or the current non-event request basis and MUST fail closed on missing, conflicting, non-canonical or freshness-unknown dependencies.
Profile-scoped sources do not enter issuer_authority_refs, cannot authorize ak.capability.grant, and cannot be widened by Realm owner/admin aggregation.

When an Event is directly participant-authored, authorization_ref uses the source wire_ref and refs contains the registered binding_ref_role. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref continues to bind the delegated executor grant/delegation; the profile source is an independent conjunctive evaluator gate and is never replaced by that delegation.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=managed_agent_control Native Agent branch MUST carry exactly one critical refs[] role=agent_provision pointing to the accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event; the verifier cross-binds actor_id, realm_id, controller, PCR delegation and provision payload before the reducer materializes the Agent active status cell. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch MUST carry zero agent_provision refs and MUST prove its separate accepted organization authority. The two branches are disjoint; a self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact hosted-principal ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Native Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the managed-Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the sorted_pair_member_ids entry that is not the request_event_ref issuer_id, i.e. the responder; glare branch: the requests[0] issuer_id), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry. Signal payload types and DeviceMessageEnvelope message kinds are intentionally outside this Event registry.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

lifecycle_modality applies to physical object lifecycle writes, identified mechanically by an fsm_contract whose axis is object_lifecycle, plus explicitly registered reversible Realm lifecycle facets. Every active event kind that writes such a family MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition. Workflow, membership, status, audit, key-material and OR-Set revocation axes are excluded. Reducers and SDKs MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell_writes[] contract; no parallel single-target fields or aliases exist. Each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional. Payload conditions use the closed grammar field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present; a signed semantic-ref condition uses only critical_ref_role_exact_count{role,count}. All are pure functions of the schema-validated signed Event. When the condition holds the target is required and the reducer MUST derive exactly one matching write from kind+payload; when it does not hold the reducer MUST NOT derive that write. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a canonical_json descriptor for a closed structured identifier (key bytes are its RFC 8785 JCS bytes), a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor whose structured components use the same canonical_json descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any reducer write has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Every lattice=fsm cell write MUST resolve by cell_family to exactly one fsm_contract. Event-kind parameters MUST NOT duplicate states or allowed_transitions. Template-backed contracts resolve their instance_parameters before transition validation; unresolved templates, parameters or conditional edges fail closed.

Every active wire_scope=actor_private_event kind MUST resolve to exactly one entry in actor_private_contracts.event_writes. Actor-private writes use only the registered actor_private_contracts.cell_families merge contract, never shared Realm plane/sealed routing, CBA fields, reducer_input, or shared cell_contracts.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 and ak.component.realm.reducer_profile.v1 are canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md; their genesis values come from ak.realm.create, and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary and ak.realm.upgrade respectively.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

Every ordered_log append MUST project issuer_seq from envelope.actor_seq exactly. The coordinate is sparse within a cell; join retains every accepted Event sibling and digest order is serialization-only. A registry row MUST NOT declare a cell-local constant or payload counter, slot winner, prefix gap, or authorization effect for ordered_log.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent writes are projected and locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move writes are projected and finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST be listed in at least one action's target_event_kinds - admission has a single direction of truth and no per-event capability list. Enforced by tools/artifact_lint; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

ak.conflict.recovery is the single registered exception to literal cell addressing. Its one cell_writes[] entry declares cell_ref (a cell_id sourced from the payload) instead of cell_family/cell_subject, and effect_projection kind=reset instead of a lattice op, and it omits lattice and bottom. That combination is closed: no other kind may declare cell_ref or reset, and this kind MUST declare both together. A recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family, so the target cannot be a literal ak.component.*.v<n> URI; and a reset is not a join, so it has no lattice. The safety envelope is not static reachability but zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5: the reducer MUST apply a reset only to a cell already in Bottom, and only when the Event carries refs[] role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness satisfying every condition in that section. On a cell in any other state the write MUST be rejected.

Every active standard Event kind MUST declare exactly one payload_schema_ref. The reference MUST resolve to an existing schema location and MUST equal the single Event Envelope payload dispatch for that kind. Consumers MUST NOT infer payload schemas from Event.kind spelling, schema-name conventions, or fallback definitions.

For every v1 built-in reducer-input Event kind, plane, sealed, lattice and bottom are frozen registry authority. Realm policy_bundle.cell_lattices is restricted to Realm-specific extension families and MUST NOT shadow, override or reinterpret a built-in cell family.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

ak.mls.commit.effective_epoch_cell_rule: ak.component.mls.epoch.v1 value is the closed reducer-effective winner tuple {transition_ref,transition_event_digest,mls_transition_digest,effective_scope,mls_group_id,previous_epoch,next_epoch,content_scheme}. transition_event_digest is the outer signed Event digest. mls_transition_digest is payload.commit_digest. A CAS conflict is Bottom, creates no state_root leaf and cannot serve as activation evidence.

ak.mls.genesis.effective_epoch_cell_rule: ak.component.mls.epoch.v1 value is the closed reducer-effective winner tuple {transition_ref,transition_event_digest,mls_transition_digest,effective_scope,mls_group_id,previous_epoch,next_epoch,content_scheme}. transition_event_digest is the outer signed Event digest. mls_transition_digest is the closed Genesis core digest excluding organization_recovery_archive, outer EventId and proofs. A CAS conflict is Bottom, creates no state_root leaf and cannot serve as activation evidence.

new_key_tuple.hpke_suite equals ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 and frozen_public_key_b64u is canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 X25519 bytes

Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

concurrency_class_definitions.merge_safe: Operation commutes under its declared lattice and may execute concurrently with other merge_safe operations after ordinary causal validation.
concurrency_class_definitions.exclusive: Operation requires exclusive compare-and-apply for its target cell set but does not globally serialize unrelated security authority.
concurrency_class_definitions.security_barrier: Authority, membership, key, scope, policy, recovery, or identity transition that serializes against every concurrent security_barrier touching the same signed scope.

merge_definitions.server_revision_cas: Whole-value compare-and-set on expected_revision; accepted revision increments by one and the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC.
