A deployment profile requires witnesses from distinct controlling organizations, but the controlling organization of at least one witness cannot be verified, or two witnesses resolve to the same organization. Counting unverifiable or colliding organizations would let one operator running several witness keys satisfy a distinct-organization requirement alone; the verifier MUST fail closed on high-risk paths. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.2.

Witness evidence is older than the effective max age set by deployment / Realm policy, measured from when the proof was observed rather than from when any Arkret receipt was signed. Re-signing an old observation does not refresh it. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.2.

parameters.witness is present but is not the did:webvh 1.0 shape {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]}: threshold outside 1..witnesses.length, a duplicated witness id, a witness id that is not a did:key, a did:key whose multibase/multicodec payload does not decode to a well-formed public key compatible with the log's Data Integrity cryptosuite, or an unregistered extension key. Key decoding happens during parameter validation, not at signature time; accepting a witness id on string shape alone would let an unverifiable key occupy a threshold slot and hollow out the threshold. Also raised when parameters carries a look-alike key such as witnesses, witness_threshold or witnessThreshold, because that shape is evidence the log was produced against a non-standard dialect and the true policy is therefore unknown. A verifier MUST fail closed and MUST NOT fall back to treating the DID as unwitnessed: silently reading a malformed or aliased declaration as threshold 0 turns a DID that declares witnesses into one that requires none. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

A witness proof in did-witness.json fails signature verification, is signed by a key outside the witness listed in parameters.witness, or does not bind the versionId it is offered for. The proof does not count toward threshold and the entry MUST be treated as under-witnessed. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

parameters.witness declares a witness policy but the did-witness.json proofs file is unreachable, unparseable, or contains no entry for the versionId under evaluation. Unavailable evidence is not absent policy; the verifier MUST fail closed on high-risk paths rather than proceed as if no witnessing were required. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1.

Valid distinct witness proofs for the versionId are fewer than the effective threshold, which is the strictest intersection of the method-native parameters.witness.threshold and the deployment / Realm policy minimum. A holder-declared policy can raise this bar but MUST NOT lower it. See zh/identity/identity-did.md §3.4.1 and §3.4.2.

`ak.mls.welcome.payload.claim_ref.capabilities_digest` does not match the claimed KeyPackage capabilities, or the Welcome requires capabilities outside the claimed subset. Receivers MUST reject before decrypting the Welcome. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.6.

Confirmed fork/witness evidence: two distinct canonical Event preimages independently recompute to the same complete suite-tagged event_id (full-hash collision evidence); a validated per-actor sibling set exceeds the registered single-bucket or per-position limit; a profile declares the observed sibling combination non-joinable; or witnesses required to sign the same complete (realm_id, from_frontier, to_frontier, actor_seq_ranges, root, count) attestation payload return inconsistent values. A carried event_id whose recomputed digest differs is only event_id_digest_mismatch and MUST be rejected before quarantine. Different valid event_id values at the same (realm_id, actor_id, actor_seq) are not by themselves disagreement: event-and-patch.md §2.6 permits a bounded legal sibling set, which peers MUST reconcile by validated set union. Raw frontier_root / heads / range-root differences across different replication, disclosure, or attestation scopes also are not disagreement. The verifier MUST quarantine only the affected evidence scope and fail closed; recovery requires raw replay, an aligned same-scope quorum, or operator-approved fork resolution. See zh/sync/operations-sync.md §12 and zh/sync/federation.md §4.5.1.

vocabulary.description: Closed naming vocabulary for protocol error codes. Word order and predicate choice are registry-governed so two codes cannot describe the same failure under different spellings.

word_order.rationale: Suffix order clusters codes by the thing that failed, which is what a consumer branches on and what prefix search needs.

registered_prefix_form.rationale: The subject of an unsupported_* code is a capability CLASS this deployment does not implement, not a specific instance that failed, so the predicate leads.

predicates.denied: A policy, capability or admission gate evaluated and refused. Supersedes rejected and not_permitted.
predicates.unauthorized: The caller lacks the required authorization credential or grant. Supersedes not_authorized.
predicates.invalid: The subject was present but failed syntax, schema, binding or verification.
predicates.unknown: The subject is not recognised by the active registry or resolver.
predicates.stale: The subject is older than the freshness window the operation requires.
predicates.exhausted: A consumable resource was fully used up; retry after replenishment (HTTP 429).
predicates.exceeded: A declared threshold or ceiling was crossed (HTTP 403 / 413).
predicates.unsupported: This deployment does not implement the named capability class.

wire_scope_definitions.durable_event: Valid Event Envelope kind for persisted canonical history and reducer input.
wire_scope_definitions.actor_private_event: Persisted actor-private/account-data event; not shared Realm history and not Realm reducer input.

admission_class_definitions.capability_gated: Gated by capability actions. The authorizing actions are exactly the ones whose target_event_kinds list this kind in capability-action-registry; there is no second per-event list. Reducer MUST verify the actor holds a matching action grant. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.conditional: Admission is selected from the event row's closed admission_variants. Receivers evaluate every non-otherwise predicate using admission_predicate_contract: exactly one match selects that variant, more than one match is fail-closed, and zero matches selects the single final otherwise variant. The otherwise branch is a fallback and is not counted as a simultaneously matching predicate. Each selected variant applies its own admission class and capabilities.
admission_class_definitions.crypto_verifiable: Admitted by cryptographic verification of the payload against group/key state (MLS epoch, key material, franking) and its policy preconditions. Reducer MUST verify the cryptographic binding; not a user capability. Fail-closed.
admission_class_definitions.delegated_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for a PCR ak.realm.create with no did_inception ref and with both executed_by and authorization_ref. A purpose=managed_agent_control Native Agent branch MUST carry exactly one critical refs[] role=agent_provision pointing to the accepted controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event; the verifier cross-binds actor_id, realm_id, controller, PCR delegation and provision payload before the reducer materializes the Agent active status cell. An explicitly organization-governed purpose=principal_control branch MUST carry zero agent_provision refs and MUST prove its separate accepted organization authority. The two branches are disjoint; a self-principal or generic realm.create capability substitution is rejected. This class never authorizes a following device-authorize slot by itself.
admission_class_definitions.applet_managed_pcr_genesis: Admitted only for purpose=applet_managed_control ak.realm.create carrying exactly one critical refs[] role=applet_managed_actor_provision. The referenced accepted ak.applet.managed_actor.provision is immutable and cross-binds the exact hosted-principal ActorId, applet/service/registration/authority, role, event-derived realm_id and object.initial_resolution. executed_by MUST equal the provision service_id and authorization_ref MUST equal its applet_authority_ref. It never substitutes Native Agent or human PCR admission.
admission_class_definitions.deny: Explicit fail-closed admission branch. Selection always rejects the Event as failed_precondition/schema_violation and MUST NOT consult capabilities or alternate proof paths.
admission_class_definitions.registration_anchor: Admitted only for self-principal PCR genesis using durable registration-time DID control evidence and one critical did_inception ref. The verifier validates the accepted-at adapter/method evidence and project(did)=actor_id; current DID state after registration is irrelevant.
admission_class_definitions.pcr_recovery: Admitted only for ak.device.reanchor under the account-local lineage's accepted PCR recovery policy/session and monotonic generation CAS. did_root is merely one optional policy-enabled factor. A current DID proof without the matching account-local lineage and policy cannot enter this class.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_agent_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_agent_provision pointing to an accepted ak.agent.provision Event. Used solely for the controller-to-own-Agent Direct Conversation branch, which has no Contact round. The verifier cross-binds participants to exactly that controller and Agent, requires the Direct Conversation profile rather than a PCR profile, checks the controller binding is current, and fixes founder = controller so the Agent runtime key never needs Direct Conversation founding scope. This role is structurally exclusive with direct_conversation_contact_round and with the managed-Agent PCR agent_provision role.
admission_class_definitions.direct_conversation_genesis: Admitted only for an ak.realm.create that carries exactly one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_contact_round pointing to the portable Contact round evidence bundle and its continuity chain to the pair's root Contact round. The verifier derives founder from the root Contact round (normal branch: the sorted_pair_member_ids entry that is not the request_event_ref issuer_id, i.e. the responder; glare branch: the requests[0] issuer_id), then requires created_by == actor_id == founder, recomputes pair_key from sorted_pair_member_ids and the trust domain, and pins the Direct Conversation profile, exact-two participants and the create-locked encryption and history baseline. Accepted-at Contact round validity and current directional Contact gates are evaluated separately so Event validity never depends on delivery order.
admission_class_definitions.self_authored_proof: Admitted by a proof bound to the subject principal's identity: either the subject's DID-bound signature / proof of possession, or a currently valid delegated-control proof whose authorization_ref is bound by the subject DID Document. Reducer MUST verify actor == subject, executed_by/authorization_ref when delegated, a fresh replay-protected proof, and that the accepted-at delegation purpose/scope explicitly covers the target event kind, resource and operation; mere presence of a DID-bound delegation is never sufficient. No Realm capability grant is consulted. Fail-closed: missing, stale, unbound, purpose-inapplicable or scope-inapplicable proof MUST be rejected.
admission_class_definitions.service_attested: Written by a protocol service component (Auth/Gate server, Events node, applet host, agent runtime) under its service-ID attestation as part of operating the protocol. Reducer MUST verify the issuing service's authority and its binding to the subject/scope; not a user capability. Fail-closed.

admission_predicate_contract.selector_semantics: All selector fields in one non-otherwise when object are ANDed. payload_path is relative to Event.payload; const uses exact JSON value equality, while not_const matches inequality or an absent path. top_level_fields_present requires every listed Event Envelope field. ref_* selectors evaluate Event.refs after schema validation. Unknown selectors, missing companion selectors, multiple matching non-otherwise variants, or evaluation errors are fail-closed.

registry_rules: Every standard ak.* Event.kind admitted through Event Envelope MUST appear in this registry. Signal payload types and DeviceMessageEnvelope message kinds are intentionally outside this Event registry.

Events API, Sync durable history, Federation, and canonical reducers MUST accept only active entries with wire_scope=durable_event unless an implementation profile explicitly defines a private channel for actor_private_event.

Entries with wire_scope=actor_private_event MAY be persisted in encrypted account data or an actor-private stream, but MUST NOT be inserted into shared Realm data-plane history or control-plane Seal history.

lifecycle_modality applies to physical object lifecycle writes, identified mechanically by an fsm_contract whose axis is object_lifecycle, plus explicitly registered reversible Realm lifecycle facets. Every active event kind that writes such a family MUST declare lifecycle_modality. Use reversible for a reversible facet or either member of an archive/restore pair, and terminal for an irreversible transition. Workflow, membership, status, audit, key-material and OR-Set revocation axes are excluded. Reducers and SDKs MUST read this field and MUST NOT infer modality from event-kind spelling.

Every active reducer-input durable kind MUST declare plane, sealed, and a complete machine-readable cell_writes[] contract; no parallel single-target fields or aliases exist. Each entry declares cell_family, cell_subject, lattice, bottom, optional initial_value, and optional condition. A condition marks the target as conditional. Payload conditions use the closed grammar field_present|field_absent|field_equals|any_field_present; a signed semantic-ref condition uses only critical_ref_role_exact_count{role,count}. All are pure functions of the schema-validated signed Event. When the condition holds the target is required and the reducer MUST derive exactly one matching write from kind+payload; when it does not hold the reducer MUST NOT derive that write. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2. cell_family is a stable ak.component.*.v<n> URI; cell_subject is null, an explicitly sourced payload.* or envelope.actor_id field path, a canonical_json descriptor for a closed structured identifier (key bytes are its RFC 8785 JCS bytes), a coalesce descriptor, or a composite descriptor whose structured components use the same canonical_json descriptor. Bare field paths and other envelope.* fields are invalid. plane MUST be data or control; sealed is a boolean and MUST be true iff plane=control. plane/sealed are the machine-readable authority for DataEvent versus Control Move routing and plane_cross_write validation; payload prose is explanatory. bottom is reject, expose, or inert; inert MUST be used when the lattice cannot produce Bottom. initial_value declares the value the cas_register reports before any reducer write has been applied; declaring `initial_value="__unset__"` combined with `head_eq:"__unset__"` implements singleton-once-set cells.

Every lattice=fsm cell write MUST resolve by cell_family to exactly one fsm_contract. Event-kind parameters MUST NOT duplicate states or allowed_transitions. Template-backed contracts resolve their instance_parameters before transition validation; unresolved templates, parameters or conditional edges fail closed.

Every active wire_scope=actor_private_event kind MUST resolve to exactly one entry in actor_private_contracts.event_writes. Actor-private writes use only the registered actor_private_contracts.cell_families merge contract, never shared Realm plane/sealed routing, CBA fields, reducer_input, or shared cell_contracts.

Protocol-singleton cells MAY take their genesis value from a create payload, but every subsequent write MUST use a registered event_kind. ak.component.notary.v1 and ak.component.realm.reducer_profile.v1 are canonically defined in zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md; their genesis values come from ak.realm.create, and subsequent writes use ak.realm.notary and ak.realm.upgrade respectively.

Lattice MUST be one of the fully specified core types: or_set, mv_register, cas_register, fsm, counter, ordered_log. A new lattice type cannot become active until its join, bottom, op schema, profile gate, and conformance vectors are all registered.

Every ordered_log append MUST project issuer_seq from envelope.actor_seq exactly. The coordinate is sparse within a cell; join retains every accepted Event sibling and digest order is serialization-only. A registry row MUST NOT declare a cell-local constant or payload counter, slot winner, prefix gap, or authorization effect for ordered_log.

State convergence is defined by CBA: DataEvent writes are projected and locally accepted against seal_ref, Control Move writes are projected and finalized by Seals, and per-cell Lattice join remains deterministic. Event Envelope routing fields MUST NOT be used as ordering authority.

Every active durable reducer-input event_kind MUST have a machine-readable admission source: either at least one capability action targets it (capability_action_registry.target_event_kinds), or it declares an admission class from admission_class_definitions. capability_gated events MUST be listed in at least one action's target_event_kinds - admission has a single direction of truth and no per-event capability list. Enforced by tools/artifact_lint; no active durable reducer-input event may lack an admission source (fail-closed).

A conditional admission MUST use only selectors defined by admission_predicate_contract. All non-otherwise predicates are evaluated independently; exactly one match selects its branch, zero matches selects the final otherwise branch, and multiple matches fail closed. otherwise is never evaluated as an ordinary predicate.

ak.conflict.recovery is the single registered exception to literal cell addressing. Its one cell_writes[] entry declares cell_ref (a cell_id sourced from the payload) instead of cell_family/cell_subject, and effect_projection kind=reset instead of a lattice op, and it omits lattice and bottom. That combination is closed: no other kind may declare cell_ref or reset, and this kind MUST declare both together. A recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family, so the target cannot be a literal ak.component.*.v<n> URI; and a reset is not a join, so it has no lattice. The safety envelope is not static reachability but zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5: the reducer MUST apply a reset only to a cell already in Bottom, and only when the Event carries refs[] role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness satisfying every condition in that section. On a cell in any other state the write MUST be rejected.

Every active standard Event kind MUST declare exactly one payload_schema_ref. The reference MUST resolve to an existing schema location and MUST equal the single Event Envelope payload dispatch for that kind. Consumers MUST NOT infer payload schemas from Event.kind spelling, schema-name conventions, or fallback definitions.

For every v1 built-in reducer-input Event kind, plane, sealed, lattice and bottom are frozen registry authority. Realm policy_bundle.cell_lattices is restricted to Realm-specific extension families and MUST NOT shadow, override or reinterpret a built-in cell family.

payload_schema_contract.validation_rule: Every active standard ak.* event kind MUST be validated by the Event Envelope schema and one payload class selected by kind. Unknown standard kind, unmatched active kind, or payload class failure is schema_violation before reducer execution.
payload_schema_contract.non_critical_extension_rule: Unknown non-critical payload fields are preserved in canonical bytes and MAY be ignored by reducers. Unknown critical payload semantics MUST be declared in Event.requirements.critical_extensions and fail closed when unsupported.
payload_schema_contract.explicit_binding_rule: Each active standard event kind declares exactly one payload_schema_ref, and the Event Envelope dispatch selects that exact location. Missing, dangling, duplicate, or divergent bindings fail closed. Consumers MUST NOT infer a payload schema from kind spelling or naming conventions.

Realm privacy-preserving search policy

Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. payload = {realm_id, strand_id}; reducer projects payload.strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify the referenced strand_id already exists in this Realm (a projected, non-tombstoned Strand); a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. Strand-side is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage; clients discover the default Strand deterministically from the Realm projection default_strand_id or the Strand projection is_default, NOT from any shared-token implementation detail. Notary equivocation evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id plus the two conflicting Seal wire objects: same (realm_id, notary_seq) slot with different canonical bytes, or a notary_seq=k+1 Seal that does not descend from the same signer's notary_seq=k Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1). Admission is verification-only: any Realm member MAY submit and the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted and reducer MUST NOT require one. Reducer MUST re-verify both signatures and the slot rule, then add a per-signer fault record to the notary_fault cell. Once a fault record is accepted: receivers MUST reject later Seals signed by the fault signer, the two conflicting Seals and their descendants enter fork_quarantine, and Realm-wide pause applies only when no eligible signer remains.

Notary censorship evidence (Control Move). Payload carries signer_id, the signed control-plane receipt, the seal_ref of the Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the pending Control Move, a control_event_set_root non-membership proof for the censored event digest, and the missing rejection-or-defer proof (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2). Admission is verification-only: the receipt holder MAY submit; the receipt signature plus the non-membership proof are the complete authorization. This evidence does NOT automatically disqualify the notary: reducer adds an audit fault record that MUST raise governance alarms, feeds inclusion-list / recovery obligations, and is evaluated by governance or the genesis recovery path.

Agent signing key authorization. Payload MUST validate as event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/agent_key_authorize_payload and bind agent_id, key_id, verification_method, accountable_principal_id, agent_key_scope, audience, issued_at, and approval_evidence; expires_at is optional (absent means non-expiring, revocation-governed). The agent-key cell is an observed-remove OR-Set. First authorization adds one authorization dot. Same-key re-authorization MUST atomically remove every active authorization dot visible at the Move seal_basis and add the replacement dot; it MUST NOT select a winner by arrival time. Concurrent replacement dots that survive the join are evaluated by the deterministic strictest fold: intersect agent_key_scope and audience, take the earliest finite expires_at (absence is +infinity), and fail closed if accountable_principal_id or verification_method disagree. Key replacement has no dedicated rotate kind: runtime replacement re-pairing authorizes the new key and revokes every prior active key (reason=superseded_by_repairing) in the same accepted transaction.

concurrency_class_definitions.merge_safe: Operation commutes under its declared lattice and may execute concurrently with other merge_safe operations after ordinary causal validation.
concurrency_class_definitions.exclusive: Operation requires exclusive compare-and-apply for its target cell set but does not globally serialize unrelated security authority.
concurrency_class_definitions.security_barrier: Authority, membership, key, scope, policy, recovery, or identity transition that serializes against every concurrent security_barrier touching the same signed scope.

merge_definitions.server_revision_cas: Whole-value compare-and-set on expected_revision; accepted revision increments by one and the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC.
merge_definitions.fsm_cas: Closed FSM transition checked against the family table and current revision; concurrent siblings fail closed.
merge_definitions.cas_register: Single actor-private register; concurrent distinct values fail closed rather than using arrival order.
merge_definitions.causal_then_hlc_then_device: Causal dominance wins; only causally incomparable positions compare HLC, and only equal HLC values compare device_id lexicographically.

request_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyRequest including requester_proof

request_receipt_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyRequestReceipt including service_proof

request_replica_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyRequestReplica with relay_proof removed

history_traversal_access_binding.preimage: no new digest is computed; each closed branch carries the already registered full-object digest named by its semantic field
history_traversal_access_binding.rule: self request_receipt.request_receipt_digest uses request_receipt_digest; self archive_replica.archive_replica_digest and peer pending_archive_replica.pending_archive_replica_digest both use archive_replica_digest. Member request replicas never grant traversal access. A branch kind/field mismatch or an unknown digest fails closed.

response_capability_commitment.rule: response_capability_b64u is the canonical unpadded base64url encoding of exactly 32 service-generated CSPRNG bytes

manifest_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyResponseSigningInput whose content.kind is ak.history_key.response_manifest

history_source_agent_observation_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyResponseSigningInput with source_signer_evidence_ref and source_signer_evidence_digest removed
history_source_agent_observation_digest.rule: Native Agent CurrentAdmission current_observation.request_digest equals this digest. The exclusion breaks the signer-evidence content-address cycle while source_proof still signs the complete HistoryKeyResponseSigningInput including both evidence coordinates.

manifest_admission_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryManifestAdmission with manifest_admission_digest removed
manifest_admission_digest.rule: traversal_intent_digest binds the request receipt's exact direct Seal traversal and authorized_ranges equal the complete manifest descriptor range union that passed replay-derived T0

source_authority_digest.rule: member and organization_recovery_holder are mutually exclusive closed branches; the RRK branch includes the complete RrkHolderAuthorityObservation rather than a bare digest locator

rrk_holder_authority_observation_digest.rule: holder principal/service and archive_authorization_tuple_digest match the immutable archive tuple; current_holder_signing_ref, accepted_key_evidence_ref and holder_trusted_basis prove current holder authority and need not equal historical tuple coordinates; current_holder_signing_ref and expiry match the outer source proof and relay byte-for-byte

agent_signer_evidence_digest.rule: AgentEvidenceViewLocator also binds the exact Agent verification method, key-authorize Event, active lifecycle Event and complete accepted PCR Seal basis; no singular control Seal or ambiguous evidence Event locator exists

source_relay_attestation_digest.preimage: the complete closed SourceRelayAttestation including service_proof
source_relay_attestation_digest.rule: the release service hashes the exact source-local signed bytes; retries reuse the first durable attestation bytes

release_attestation_digest.rule: the attestation has no nested service proof; the enclosing response-record service_proof authenticates it

response_record_digest.rule: manifest_admission is present only for a manifest; release_attestation is present only for a chunk

send_receipt_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt with receipt_digest and service_proof removed
send_receipt_digest.rule: release_attestation_digest is JSON null for a manifest and a sha256 digest for a chunk

lost_record_digest.preimage: the complete closed HistoryKeyResponseLostRecord, including its release-service signer-evidence ref and digest, with service_proof removed

organization_recovery_archive_digest.rule: the digest is the exact immutable archive identity used by archive-set coverage and candidate origin attribution; container_event_ref and replica transport metadata are not part of this object digest

archive_authorization_tuple_digest.preimage: the complete closed ArchiveAuthorizationTuple including accepted_key_evidence_ref and holder_trusted_basis
archive_authorization_tuple_digest.rule: accepted_key_evidence_ref is Event provenance and holder_trusted_basis is the independently pinned complete prior accepted Seal antichain; direct Seal traversal to the archive target proves the effective tuple and no singular activation Seal is carried

archive_set_digest.rule: rows are sorted by (epoch numeric ascending, container_event_ref UTF-8 bytes, archive_digest UTF-8 bytes), duplicate-free, exactly cover covered_range and all share one archive_authorization_tuple_digest

archive_replica_digest.preimage: the complete closed OrganizationRecoveryArchiveReplica with service_proof removed
archive_replica_digest.rule: the archive, container Event, independent exact-one-epoch direct traversal retention, source/holder services and replicated_at are bound; semantic uniqueness is (effective_scope,mls_group_id,epoch,container_event_ref,archive_authorization_tuple_digest), while this full body digest is only the exact-retry identity and cannot allocate a second sequence when replicated_at changes

archive_list_query_digest.preimage: the complete closed OrganizationRecoveryArchiveListQuery with cursor removed
archive_list_query_digest.rule: continuation cursor does not change semantic query identity; accepted_key_evidence_ref and holder_trusted_basis are both included

accepted_authority_view_vector_digest.rule: object property names are fixed by schema; absent optional profile slots are absent rather than null

availability_event_bytes_digest.formula: <Realm-suite>:<digest of UTF8('ak.availability_event_bytes.v1') || 0x00 || JCS(complete accepted EventEnvelope with unsigned removed)>
availability_event_bytes_digest.preimage: the complete accepted canonical EventEnvelope with only unsigned removed; event_id, actor_kind and every accepted producer/station proof remain included
availability_event_bytes_digest.rule: the receiver also recomputes the ordinary event_digest/event_id from their separately registered preimage and verifies every included proof before accepting bytes_digest; bytes_digest is not an alias for event_id

history_governance_traversal_intent_dige.rule: member_history_delivery trusted_history_base_basis equals the signed request bootstrap basis byte-for-byte; organization_recovery_archive base equals holder_trusted_basis and requested_ranges is exactly one singleton epoch; target must dominate the complete trusted current and base antichains

proof_query_digest.preimage: the complete closed read_request including local_mls_leaves and byte_limit
proof_query_digest.rule: The query is stateless, near-current and explicitly binds exact proof_base_basis and proof_target_basis antichains, the caller's canonical every-and-only public RFC 9420 leaf coordinates and the group_security_frontier selector. Bulk or old epoch activation is forbidden on this surface.

proof_page_digest.preimage: query_digest is the registered domain-separated digest of the caller-retained complete closed read_request; page_body is the complete matching read_outcome with query_digest and page_digest removed
proof_page_digest.rule: The response completely covers the exact near-current frontier selector or is rejected with mls_governance_proof_bounds_exceeded. Deterministic regeneration for identical retained closure and query produces the same page_digest.

mls_genesis_transition_digest.formula: sha256:<lowercase hex SHA-256(UTF8('ak.mls-genesis-transition-v1') || 0x00 || JCS(closed mls_genesis_payload with organization_recovery_archive removed))>
mls_genesis_transition_digest.preimage: the closed mls_genesis_payload core after removing organization_recovery_archive
mls_genesis_transition_digest.rule: This is mls_transition_digest for Genesis. Commit mls_transition_digest is the existing payload.commit_digest over raw RFC 9420 Commit bytes. transition_event_digest is always the separate outer Event digest.

ack_token.rule: ordered_ack_entries is the exact strictly sequence-ascending array of {sequence,kind,response_id,entry_digest}, where entry_digest is record_digest for kind=record or the complete signed lost-record digest for kind=lost. service_record_lost is admitted only for a matching lost entry.

archive_cursor.rule: Rows are ordered by holder-assigned archive_sequence then container_event_ref. No cursor expiry or temporary proof-retention coordinate exists; authorization and proof closure live with the archive.

history_response.rule: Request, response, manifest and inner source-record limits are distinct. Manifest source record <=256 KiB; chunk source record <=2 MiB; every complete non-streaming send/relay/record/list-item/small-receipt JSON body <=8 MiB. All size admission uses final canonical bytes. Before durable high-water ack, complete response records/attestations are charged to max_unacked_response_bytes. Ack is valid only after durable disposition/install, atomically GC's the large record/attestation and releases active quota, while the compact exact HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt ledger remains through request expiry for source retry. The compact ledger has independent request/requester/service hard limits and cannot admit a receipt if it would exceed them. Expiry converts it to a 30-day minimal tombstone. A limit failure occurs before enqueue. Staged blobs become sendable only with an atomic ready marker.
history_response.attempt_rule: Attempt identity is exactly (request_id,source_sender_domain,manifest response_id,manifest_digest). It is completed only after every descriptor-named chunk has a durable HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt. v1 has no abandon operation: an unfinished attempt becomes expired only at request expiry; a permanent chunk rejection requires a new manifest but does not silently complete the old attempt. completed/expired atomically GC staged blobs and outbox bytes while compact accepted receipts remain through their normal ledger horizon. Only unfinished attempts count against the 4-per-source and 8-per-request concurrent limits. A request may create any number of sequential bounded manifests before expiry; there is no lifetime split/attempt cap.

governance_proof.rule: The stateless governance operation is only the near-current group_security_frontier selector. Its response is complete, independently verifiable, cursor-free and at most max_exact_response_bytes. Bulk or old history is reconstructed through receipt-bound direct accepted-Seal traversal and standard object/dependency resolve.

history_governance_traversal.rule: Member request ranges total at most 65,536 epochs; each RRK ArchiveListItem traversal has one singleton archive epoch. Before accepting a member request receipt or an organization-recovery archive replica, the service atomically pins the complete target-to-base accepted Seal cut, base Seal bodies, delta Control Moves, AvailabilityReceipts, signer-resolution evidence, external semantic dependencies and exact governance registry plus transitive replay-schema closure for the retention horizon. A member request replica does not promise or authorize governance traversal retention. Event/Seal resolve and governance-dependency resolve are caller-split point reads; dependency resolve is cursor-free and returns zero partial items on bounds failure. Disk-backed work queues and CAS dedupe bound memory without introducing a page/package/result-set wire.

archive_projection.rule: The fixed HPKE suite seals one closed single-secret plaintext. enc<=2048 base64url characters, ciphertext<=16384 characters and the complete public archive object<=32768 canonical bytes. Recipient-bound archive rows are canonical-byte paged and independently verifiable. A byte_limit below min_page_byte_limit is limit_exceeded; every admitted page limit can hold at least one maximum legal item plus framing, so limited pages cannot make zero progress.

quota_keys.origin_attribution_key: (material_key,origin_domain,origin_ref); origin_quota_domain is a separately persisted stable quota projection

history_store.material_dedupe_rule: Received secret bytes are globally deduplicated by material_key; origin never participates in material identity. A material instance receives one immutable monotonic material_received_sequence when bytes first become resident. The same bytes from a new origin add only CandidateOriginAttribution and never refresh that sequence. After bytes are evicted, a later refetch creates a new resident material instance and receives a new sequence.
history_store.origin_domain: Closed enum response_sender|rrk_archive|portable_backup. Stable origin_quota_domain is respectively {source_sender_domain}, {holder_principal_id,holder_id,recovery_key_id,accepted_key_evidence_ref}, or {backup_series_id,producer_actor_id}. For RRK the accepted evidence EventId is the rotation identity; no independent key-version field exists. origin_ref is retrieval-only: {response_id,source_record_digest}, {container_event_ref,archive_digest}, or {backup_origin_id}; backup_origin_id is backup:<BackupId> or backup:sha256:<hex exact envelope bytes> and never a sender identity.
history_store.origin_attribution_rule: CandidateOriginAttribution key is exactly (material_key,origin_domain,origin_ref), while quotas use the separately persisted stable origin_quota_domain. The ledger admits at most 4 rows per material_key, 64 rows per exact (scope,group,epoch,origin_domain,origin_quota_domain), and 256 rows total per (scope,group,epoch). first_observed_at is immutable; expiry is computed as first_observed_at+2592000 seconds, is not stored, cannot be extended by duplicate/refetch, and timestamp overflow fails closed. Exact duplicate is a no-op. Before admission prune expired rows, then when any cap remains exceeded retain the minimum canonical tuple (first_observed_at,material_key.candidate_digest,origin_domain,JCS(origin_quota_domain),JCS(origin_ref)) and reject/prune larger rows. Origin attribution never duplicates bytes or changes material_received_sequence.
history_store.material_quota_rule: The 8-slot limit counts only resident received candidate material instances under material_key. local_authoritative material is stored in a separate accounting class, consumes no received slot, and is never evicted. CandidateOriginAttribution and EventCandidateBinding metadata consume no material slot and never pin bytes.
history_store.material_eviction_rule: Before inserting resident received material over quota, deterministically evict secret bytes in two tiers: first material with no success EventCandidateBinding, including unbound and failure-only; then success-bound material. Within a tier choose (material_received_sequence ascending,candidate_digest UTF-8 ascending). Success/failure bindings only select the tier and never pin bytes. Eviction deletes bytes plus the resident sequence only, preserves bounded origin attribution/Event binding tombstones for refetch, and never selects local_authoritative.
history_store.event_candidate_binding_rule: EventCandidateBinding key is exactly (event_binding_key,candidate_digest,outcome), where event_binding_key=(effective_scope,mls_group_id,epoch,event_id,verified_sender_domain) and outcome is success|failure. The suite-bearing event_id losslessly supplies the Event digest. The binding contains no origin and origin cannot be inferred from it. The independent ledger is capped at 256 rows per (scope,group,epoch); expiry is computed as immutable first_observed_at plus 2592000 seconds, is not stored, and timestamp overflow fails closed. Prune expired rows first, then (first_observed_at,event_id,verified_sender_domain,candidate_digest,outcome) canonical ascending. Pruning never changes the ciphertext replay ledger, material authority, or local_authoritative.
history_store.rule: Every received history secret remains a candidate; neither AEAD success nor failure promotes an epoch-wide winner. Candidate bytes and bounded Event attribution metadata are separate stores. A malicious sender's fake secret/ciphertext can affect only its signed Event attribution and cannot pin received material or exhaust all slots permanently. Portable backup writes only local_authoritative secrets.

backup.rule: Each object belongs to one exporter effective scope and is split by final encrypted bytes, never by guessed epoch count.

registry/history-recovery-scalability-re.requested_epoch_budget_rule: For canonical sorted, disjoint and non-adjacent requested_ranges, compute sum(to_epoch-from_epoch+1) with checked unsigned 64-bit arithmetic. Reject overflow or a sum above max_total_requested_epochs. Gaps between ranges are excluded.
registry/history-recovery-scalability-re.global_identity_rule: HistoryRequestId and HistoryResponseId are globally unique object identities. Reuse of a response_id under another request response stream, requester, service or scope is duplicate_conflict; request_id plus sequence is only an internal pagination index and never a second identity namespace.
registry/history-recovery-scalability-re.deployment_rule: A deployment may reject a new request earlier only if the smaller advertised limit is checked before acceptance. It cannot lower retention/size guarantees for already accepted objects or silently discard them.

registry/history-release-attestation-reg.wire_registry_binding: HistoryReleaseAttestation.verifier_profile_id is ak.history_release_predicates.v1. The enclosing HistoryKeyResponseRecord.service_proof covers the complete attestation. An unsupported verifier profile is rejected only for the affected object and is never translated to an authorization failure.
registry/history-release-attestation-reg.trust_model: The first durable enqueue is linearized by an honest release service. Its service proof authenticates a closed T1 decision receipt and exact locator/digest vector; the vector is not a portable multi-authority proof. A malicious or stale release service is outside v1's cryptographic guarantee. A future adversarial-service profile requires a separately registered notary/quorum design.

required_inputs: byte-identical signed manifest and request/receipt ledgers
receipt-bound HistoryGovernanceTraversalIntent with exact bootstrap base/current/target SealBasis antichains
the complete retained target-to-base accepted Seal cut, base Seal bodies, delta Control Moves, AvailabilityReceipts, signer-resolution evidence and semantic dependencies
requester current authorization incarnation and replay-derived winning join/reactivation transition
the scope's current monotone history_access value at target
manifest descriptor exact continuous ranges and their canonical union
closed_predicates: require traversal intent trusted_history_base_basis equal the request-signed predecessor-free bootstrap basis and target_basis dominate trusted_current_basis

reverse-walk every target predecessor until exact base leaves, include each interval predecessor or exact base leaf, consume every base leaf, include base Seal bodies and deltas but stop before base predecessors

topologically verify every Seal against predecessor-state frozen notary descriptors, every AvailabilityReceipt and signer/semantic dependency, then apply every delta Control Move with the Realm's frozen compiled profile
derive the current requester membership incarnation, winning join/reactivation transition, every winning MLS epoch transition, ciphersuite and content_scheme exclusively from replayed state
require every descriptor range be a subset of canonical request ranges

read the current monotone history_access cell only: since_join requires every epoch >= the replay-derived current incarnation join_epoch; all_history_for_current_members ignores that floor but still requires the current incarnation
require every transition to be the reducer-effective winning cell value; conflict recovery, Bottom and continuity are reconstructed by normal replay rather than a separate activation witness
require exporter content_scheme in the winning value; standard MLS is ineligible for history delivery
manifest_t0_registry.failure_rule: Any missing, extra, stale, Bottom, mismatched, unauthorized or unavailable input rejects the whole manifest before sequence allocation, response record, admission row or attestation write. Partial range admission is forbidden.

closed_predicates: exact current Realm history_access is evaluated
recipient exact current membership incarnation is active
member source exact current membership incarnation is active
Realm is readable and not tombstoned
exact current Circle-owned history_access is evaluated without parent history_access inheritance or cap
recipient and member source have active exact Circle membership incarnations
recipient and member source have active exact parent-Realm membership incarnations
Circle and parent Realm are readable and not tombstoned
membership_reconcile_required is false for the exact Circle group state

seal_view_locator_rule.basis: Each scope slot carries the complete canonical accepted non-quarantined seal_basis antichain. Selecting one accepted Seal leaf is forbidden, including open_set.
seal_view_locator_rule.projection: RealmCurrentGateProjection and CircleCurrentGateProjection are the only closed projection shapes. They contain current monotone history_access, exact recipient/source authorization incarnation when the registered branch requires it, tombstone facts, and for Circle the parent-Realm intersection plus membership_reconcile_required=false.
seal_view_locator_rule.cas: The first durable chunk-enqueue transaction re-resolves the exact basis, rejects any known successor, recomputes every projection field and digest, and CAS-compares the complete basis+projection before writing anything.

closed_predicates: latest issuer-ledger AccountStatusRecord for the exact account/principal binding has status=active
exact canonical DeviceId has a current PCR device authorize Event not superseded by revoke or reanchor generation
exact Agent lifecycle is active
exact current Agent signing key is authorized
closed control/evidence chain for the exact Agent endpoint incarnation is current
release service verifies the exact requester pairwise ActorId is the current active Realm/Circle membership subject and projects its destination service from that ActorId
minimal_metadata.note: The release service does not maintain or apply the MLS public tree. The receiver verifies its own exact active pairwise leaf in its current local group state; source identity is verified against the exact historical group-state material. Neither leaf fact is claimed as a service CBA proof or directory lookup.

required_source_relay_facts: exact source DeviceId has a current PCR authorize Event not superseded by revoke or reanchor generation
closed_predicates: release service verifies the complete short-lived SourceRelayAttestation from the source's current delivery-bound Station
relay destination, source record digest, request receipt, source identity/profile/incarnation and expiry match exactly

required_source_relay_facts: exact Agent lifecycle, signing key and registered control/evidence chain are current
closed_predicates: release service verifies the complete short-lived SourceRelayAttestation from the Agent's current authority service

required_source_relay_facts: exact Realm-global pairwise ActorId is the current delivery-authorized source incarnation
closed_predicates: release service verifies the relay service equals the deterministic route projection of the current source ActorId and verifies current scope membership locally
minimal_metadata.note: The receiver separately verifies the source's exact historical active leaf; the service does not claim an MLS-tree proof.

closed_predicates: one chunk covers one byte-identical archive authorization tuple
every epoch in released_range has an exact archive Event whose historical tuple and transition provenance match

each archive tuple binds accepted_key_evidence_ref and distinct holder_trusted_basis; retained direct Seal traversal proves the effective registered/rotated key tuple from that complete holder basis to the archive target without a singular activation Seal
source local authority service verifies current holder lifecycle/signing authority and signs those coordinates into the complete SourceRelayAttestation
archive_tuple.holder_signing_ref is historical provenance only and never authorizes the current response

source_local_only: holder-private blocklists or local UI policy; these are never asserted by the service attestation

registry/history-release-attestation-reg.linearization: Before the local enqueue transaction the service obtains intent-bound short-lived observations from each required local authority, verifies the source relay and scope facts, then atomically verifies every observation is unexpired. For every Realm/Circle/PCR Seal authority it re-resolves the complete canonical accepted non-quarantined Seal antichain, requires no known successor, recomputes the closed current-gate projection, and CAS-binds the exact basis+projection vector. It then stores the immutable response record and ReleaseAttestation, assigns the request response-stream sequence/cursor, freezes the compact HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt and charges quota. It does not claim a cross-service atomic snapshot. Failure writes nothing. Exact source retry returns the original byte-identical compact send receipt through request expiry. Recipient high-water ack atomically removes the large response record and attestation; they are not readable after ack.
registry/history-release-attestation-reg.release_service_route_rule: The request receipt's frozen release_id is the only release authority for that request. Before first enqueue it must project the requester destination from the exact ActorId: account and hosted_principal use station_id, while service uses service_id, and require that destination to equal this service DID. A ServiceResolution successor for that same service DID is permitted and becomes the current endpoint; a different projected service DID rejects first enqueue and requires a new request. v1 does not migrate a mailbox or idempotency ledger. Already accepted records remain byte-identically retryable from the old ledger until expiry.
registry/history-release-attestation-reg.audit_record: The immutable service-signed ReleaseAttestation created in the first durable chunk-enqueue transaction is the sole history-release audit record. v1 has no history_release_audit policy facet, pre-release audit token, audit evidence carrier or audit authority slot. Compliance projections index attestations; separate approval workflows are orthogonal capabilities.
registry/history-release-attestation-reg.predicate_failure: Any required locator, authority response, subject, incarnation, tuple, digest or exact binding that is missing, Bottom, stale, mismatched or unavailable rejects the chunk before enqueue. No caller-supplied boolean can replace a predicate.

registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.description: Canonical HPKE (RFC 9180) suite vocabulary for v1 application-layer public-key sealing surfaces that are NOT carried inside MLS: key-backup `recovery_public_key` envelopes, to-device sealed material (`ak.secret.send`), member-application reviewer envelopes and file-transfer key envelopes. An HPKE suite names the (KEM, KDF, AEAD) triple; its canonical_id is the wire scheme / `hpke_suite` selector value. The KEM (DHKEM-X25519-HKDF-SHA256), the KDF (HKDF-SHA256) and the application-layer seal/open transcript are standard RFC 9180 base mode (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR): the RFC 9180 key_schedule with LabeledExtract / LabeledExpand derives key, base_nonce and exporter_secret from the DHKEM shared secret and the caller `info`, and the AEAD nonce is the internally derived base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0), NOT carried on the wire. This is the fourth algorithm-agility registry, symmetric to signature-alg-registry.json, digest-suite-registry.json and mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. MLS group messages keep their own HPKE internals via mls-ciphersuite-registry.json and are out of scope here.
registry/hpke-suite-registry.json.suite_id_grammar: suite_id = 'ak.hpke_' kem_id '_aead_' aead_id '.v' major ; each id segment matches [a-z0-9]+ . The canonical_id is the full wire string; it is NOT freely composed from parts — only suites present as rows below exist, and only status=active rows are valid on wire.
registry_rules: Only suites present as rows in this registry exist. Implementations MUST NOT compose KEM/KDF/AEAD ids freely; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

A suite id not present as an active row MUST fail closed with unsupported_hpke_suite when it appears in an HPKE-sealed surface (key-backup recipient_method=recovery_public_key, ak.secret.send, member-application encryption_envelope, file-transfer key_envelope). Receivers MUST NOT infer suite parameters from the AEAD name alone.

Schema enum values for HPKE suite selector fields (e.g. ak.schema.key_backup.v1 encryption.hpke_suite, the ak.secret.send / member-application / file-transfer envelope `scheme` const) MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema version, then frozen for that schema version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

When a surface carries both an explicit `hpke_suite` selector and an AEAD `name`/profile field, the AEAD MUST equal the selected suite's aead; a mismatch MUST be rejected (schema_violation). A surface MAY omit the selector only where a single default-MUST suite is pinned by its defining document, in which case the absent selector denotes that row.

status=reserved rows pin the wire id and profile gate but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_hpke_suite) on a reserved suite id seen on wire before activation.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/artifact_lint enforces this binding.

For every surface_profiles row, info_and_aad names one exact canonical byte string. The sender MUST pass those identical bytes as both RFC 9180 SetupBaseS info and the single-shot AEAD Seal aad; the receiver MUST pass the same bytes as both SetupBaseR info and AEAD Open aad. Empty, domain-only, differently wrapped, or independently serialized info/AAD values are forbidden.

The registry is intentionally minimal: new KEM families (post-quantum / hybrid), new KDFs and new AEADs enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the ak.hpke_*_aead_*.v* wire form needs no rewrite. Nonce handling is RFC 9180 key-schedule-derived, uniformly across every HPKE-sealed surface (`recovery_public_key` envelopes, the to-device `ak.secret.send` seal, member-application and file-transfer key envelopes): the AEAD nonce is base_nonce XOR seq (single-shot seq=0) and MUST NOT be carried on the wire; each seal mints a fresh ephemeral key, so base_nonce is unique per envelope. See zh/identity/key-management.md §7.5 for the symmetric (non-HPKE) key-backup nonce-uniqueness rules.

kem_strength_order.note: Classical KEMs are treated as equal classical strength; the hybrid xwing row is strictly stronger (adds ML-KEM-768 post-quantum confidentiality). Consumed by any future no-downgrade rule on suite transition.

surface_profiles.encapsulation: fresh single-shot seq=0; never reused with a history chunk

surface_profiles.info_and_aad: RFC 8785 JCS bytes of closed {purpose:'history_secret_chunk',manifest_admission_digest,chunk_response_id,chunk_index,source_actor_id,source_sender_domain}. manifest_admission_digest commits the exact all-or-nothing T0 admission and its accepted request, receipt, intent, manifest and authorized ranges; the receiver reconstructs those verified values before opening the chunk. No proof/package/page/selection digest or range-index key exists.
surface_profiles.encapsulation: fresh independently verifiable single-shot seq=0 per chunk; no cross-chunk state or authorization-basis input

surface_profiles.info_and_aad: RFC 8785 JCS bytes of every public organization_recovery_archive field except enc and ciphertext, in the closed shape {effective_scope,mls_group_id,epoch,transition_digest,recovery_key_id,holder_principal_id,holder_id,key_agreement_ref,holder_signing_ref,hpke_suite,frozen_public_key_b64u,accepted_key_evidence_ref,holder_trusted_basis}. transition_digest is the exact mls_transition_digest, never the outer Event digest. holder_trusted_basis is the canonical complete SealBasis object; accepted_key_evidence_ref becomes reducer-effective only by direct Seal traversal replay and no singular activation Seal is carried. hpke_suite is fixed to this profile and frozen_public_key_b64u is canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 X25519 bytes. No field may be omitted or caller-selected outside the closed schema.
surface_profiles.encapsulation: fresh single-shot seq=0 inside the same signed Genesis/Commit Event; EventId and container digest are forbidden pre-encryption inputs

suites.security_note: All-RFC-9180 suite for key-backup recovery_public_key envelopes on platforms with AES hardware acceleration. Classical.

v1 default-MUST application-layer HPKE suite: all-RFC-9180 base mode DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) + HKDF-SHA256 + 96-bit-nonce ChaCha20-Poly1305 (SetupBaseS / SetupBaseR, key_schedule-derived base_nonce, no wire nonce). Software-friendly (constant-time, no AES hardware needed), the default for the recovery_public_key / to-device / member-application / file-transfer envelopes. Classical (not post-quantum).
P-256 KEM for WebAuthn/FIDO2/PKI key-agreement interop, mirroring the ECDSA-P256 signature row. Profile-gated; receivers not advertising ak.profile.hpke.p256.v1 fail closed. Classical.

suites.kat_absence_reason: The X-Wing HPKE construction remains reserved until the profile and per-suite KAT activation requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: ak.profile.kem.hybrid_xwing.v1 fully specifies draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10 and HPKE KEM id 0x647A; any incompatible draft change requires an explicit registry release and refreshed KAT digest before activation
Per-suite HPKE conformance vectors published (KEM encap/decap, key schedule, sealed bytes)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: key-backup envelope before MLS KeyPackage (static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target; reuses the reserved ak.aead.hybrid_kem.* namespace)
suites.security_note: Reserved post-quantum hybrid KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768) per the encryption-and-audit.md §2 PQ roadmap. The KEM identifier is the IANA-assigned HPKE value 0x647A and the exact construction is pinned to draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10. Hybrid confidentiality: secure if either X25519 or ML-KEM-768 holds. Not on wire until the profile and KAT activation requirements are complete.

storage_rules: Protocol wire objects, canonical JSON, signatures, hashes, fixtures, logs, API DTOs, and cross-service references MUST use the full typed form declared by each id_kind row.

Storage implementations MAY store producer-allocated raw 16-byte UUID values (e.g. PostgreSQL `uuid` column) without the ak:<kind>: prefix when the table, column, or explicit kind field already supplies the type context.
Implementations that store raw IDs MUST restore the full typed form before computing canonical JSON, event IDs, payload hashes, detached proofs, federation payloads, sync cursors, or audit logs.
The <kind> segment is part of the signed/canonical wire value. It MUST NOT be changed, inferred differently, or stripped during verification, forwarding, backfill, or replay.

The payload construction MUST be fixed by that kind's id_form and identity_authority columns, never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses UUIDv7; event_derived uses the creating Event's 33-byte token; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest-suite code followed by the complete 32-byte digest under its registered kind-specific preimage contract. v1 Event and suite-tagged identities accept only registered active suite codes with high nibble 0x0; this constraint does not give that nibble any meaning beyond the suite code. A UUID version nibble or digest-suite byte alone never proves identity authority.

A producer_allocated UUIDv7 is never a globally sufficient protocol identity. Its canonical identity key is (mint_authority, typed_id), where mint_authority is the DID whose accepted proof authorized the first durable appearance of that ID. Bare typed-ID lookup, cross-authority deduplication, and last-writer-wins collision repair are forbidden.

Storage implementations MAY store producer_allocated UUID values as raw 16-byte UUIDs. Event-derived and suite-tagged full-digest IDs MUST instead store their raw 33-byte token; they MUST NOT use a native UUID column.

The id_form is fixed by registry kind and never chosen per call site: producer_allocated uses RFC 9562 UUIDv7; event_derived uses the same canonical 33-byte token as its creating Event ID; suite_tagged_full_digest uses a full uint8 digest suite code followed by all 32 digest octets. Both token forms serialize as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters.

A database MAY intern any full Realm wire identity in a canonical Realm table and use a database-local surrogate pk for joins, indexes, and foreign keys. That pk is never serialized or signed. The canonical table MUST retain a unique lossless 33-byte Realm identity (or its full typed wire form), and every realm_pk foreign key MUST resolve to the same wire Realm identity carried by the protocol record.

Every special_forms row declares payload_pattern, the machine-readable value space of everything after its ak:<kind>: prefix; wire_form remains the human-readable template and payload_pattern is its only normative expansion. A schema, OpenAPI or profile carrier MAY be narrower than payload_pattern for a specific field, but MUST NOT accept an octet payload_pattern rejects, and MUST end-anchor so no trailing byte escapes the declared value space.

producer_allocated_identity_contract.security_rationale: UUIDv7 randomness and timestamp layout do not authenticate the allocator. Binding every producer-selected ID to the accepted genesis signer prevents an attacker from claiming another producer's ID by copying or predicting the UUID.

issuer_record_identity_contract.v1_suite_code_constraint: The complete uint8 suite wire code is encoded unchanged, but v1 accepts only registered active codes whose high nibble is 0x0; this is not a Realm derivation-class nibble.

closed_encoding.audience_id: canonical_bare_resource_service_did; never an HTTP origin or endpoint URL
closed_encoding.credential_binding: credential_class is standard or recovery_session; holder_binding is required; device_binding is required only for standard human_device and forbidden for recovery_candidate_device and agent_runtime

issuer_record_identity_contract.signed_claim_binding: Every preimage field except fixed schema is a signed JWT claim, including credential_class and holder_binding; kind is the fixed credential kind and jti is the derived typed ID. Verifiers MUST reconstruct the complete preimage from signed claims and recompute jti, so different credential classes or holder bindings cannot share one valid ID.
issuer_record_identity_contract.session_chain_rule: session_id is independently allocated before first issuance, refresh inherits it, and it MUST NOT equal or derive from grant_id
issuer_record_identity_contract.device_id_rule: No independent top-level device_id claim enters the preimage; standard human holder_binding and its complete device_binding carry accepted-device authority. Recovery candidate-device and Agent runtime holder bindings carry their own device_id and forbid device_binding.

lifecycle.refresh: one issuer transaction creates active successor and supersedes predecessor with successor_session_grant_id

account_status_record_identity_contract.digest_input: SHA-256(JCS(record fields excluding account_status_record_id and proof))
account_status_record_identity_contract.sequence_rule: status_seq starts at 1; seq=1 is active and has no previous_account_status_record_id; every successor is current+1 and names the exact current account_status_record_id

realm_token_layout.event_derived_retype_compatibility: Realm and Event token headers are identical, so an ak.realm.create Event token is byte-identical to its Realm token and retyping only swaps the ak:event: / ak:realm: prefix. v1 Realm identity is fixed to SHA-256, so only a creating Event with header 0x01 is Realm-eligible.
realm_token_layout.high_nibble_carries_no_category: The high nibble is reserved zero and carries no category information. Realm purpose lives in the signed create payload; implementations MUST NOT infer purpose from realm_id.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque token or store server-private cursor state keyed by a raw token.
special_forms.description: Opaque sync/query cursor; not a typed-UUIDv7 object ID.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store digest bytes/hex separately from any logical blob row ID.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed blob reference using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3); distinct from ak:blob:<uuid> blob metadata IDs.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store profile and raw profile_id separately.
special_forms.description: MLS-profile scoped reference such as KeyPackage IDs; validated by the E2EE profile, not by the generic typed-UUIDv7. payload_pattern is the core-registered outer value space the profile MUST stay inside; the profile MAY narrow it further but MUST NOT accept an octet outside it.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store scope and random identifier separately when used in credential tables.
special_forms.description: Profile-scoped pseudonymous reference. Each consuming profile defines its own scope boundary and narrows the core-registered outer payload_pattern; it MUST NOT accept an octet outside that space. E2EE credential pseudonyms are Realm-scoped, while push pseudonyms are scoped to the registered recipient service, principal, device, route and salt epoch. Matrix-style Room terminology is only allowed in MIMI/Matrix interop modules.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as an opaque install-plan token; do not parse it as UUIDv7.
special_forms.description: Applet install-plan identifier. The suffix is an opaque non-empty base64url token.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed ServiceRegistrationReceipt identifier derived from canonical receipt claims. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims)).

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32 raw challenge octets together with the challenge consumption ledger row; it is registry-local single-use state, never a federated object ID and never a native UUID column.
special_forms.description: Single-use Organization registration control challenge identifier issued by ak.root.identity.organization_registration.command.prepare.v1. It is registry-allocated, neither content-addressed nor Event-derived, and it never denotes a durable protocol object.

allocation.payload_encoding: 32 octets rendered as exactly 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters
allocation.uniqueness_rule: The registry MUST atomically reserve the value before returning it and MUST reallocate on any collision with a live or consumed ledger row; a challenge value is never reissued.
allocation.consumption_rule: The registry MUST consume the challenge inside the same transaction that persists (challenge_id, canonical_request_digest, outcome).
allocation.replay_rule: Only a byte-identical retry may return the recorded outcome; the same challenge_id carrying any different canonical_request_digest, or a consumed challenge_id with no matching successful ledger row, MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.
allocation.security_rationale: A caller-chosen or request-derived challenge would let the caller pick freshness and defeat single-use consumption, so the registry mints the full 256-bit value itself and binds the outcome to the exact canonical request bytes.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte receipt-claims digest or the complete typed content-addressed identifier.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed OrganizationRegistrationReceipt identifier. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims)), where receipt_claims is exactly the receipt object with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted; it is the same content-addressed family as service_registration_receipt and MUST NOT be reused as a Realm capability, membership, notary designation or service delegation.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the 32-byte delegation digest or the complete typed content-addressed reference.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed membership-compensation delegation reference. The lowercase hexadecimal suffix MUST equal the SHA-256 delegation_digest derived from the profile-defined digest-free canonical core.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store as a content-addressed canonical Seal hash.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed Seal identifier using an active digest-suite id (v1: sha256 or profile-gated blake3), the same suite-tagged shape as ak:blob:<digest-suite>:<digest>. The suite segment is not fixed to sha256: a Seal id is a critical field, so its suite prefix MUST equal the Realm digest_algorithm and MUST be an active row of registry/digest-suite-registry.json; any other prefix fails closed with unsupported_digest_algorithm. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 6.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store canonical tuple fields separately when indexing cell state.
special_forms.description: Canonical protocol cell identifier. The complete ak.component.<facet-path>.v<n> family identifier is embedded unchanged after ak:cell:. When the registry declares cell_subject: null for a family, the canonical subject segment is the literal ASCII string 'null' (ak:cell:<component>:null); the cell is located by the Event envelope realm_id and implementations MUST NOT encode realm_id, Realm role classification, or any payload-derived value into that segment. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical value for equality and indexing; generic consumers MUST NOT split or normalize the adapter-defined core segment.
special_forms.description: Stable DID-derived principal, actor or service identity core. It is not a DID, is not directly resolvable, and MUST be projected only by a registered DID method adapter from a canonical bare did. Registered as a special form rather than an id_form because its identity authority is the external DID method, not an Arkret producer or Event digest.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete canonical ak:trust_domain:<scope> value by default. A compressed schema may store the raw scope only in an explicitly named trust_domain_scope column and MUST restore the typed prefix at the persistence boundary.
special_forms.description: Deployment-scope trust domain identifier. Scope is a lowercase opaque label (alphanumerics, dot, dash, underscore, colon; max 128 chars). Used to prevent cross-deployment / cross-sovereign replay of high-risk root, recovery and authorization proofs. NOT a typed-UUIDv7 object id. See identity-did.md §3.6.

special_forms.storage_recommendation: Store the complete typed content-addressed identifier together with the exact canonical signer-evidence bytes.
special_forms.description: Content-addressed authenticated signer-resolution evidence reference. The suffix is the SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical evidence object under its registered digest rule.

id_kinds.description: Actor profile object ID
Moderation appeal ID derived from ak.moderation.appeal.submit and referenced by review / decision / close events. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.
Directory-local announce ingest record ID. It is typed and UUIDv7-shaped for validator consistency, but it is scoped to the issuing Directory and is not a global federated object authority.
Applet registration/service ID
Audit Applet Binding ID derived from ak.audit.applet_binding.create and referenced by binding state and audit session events.
Audit release session ID derived from ak.audit.session.request. Threads request, authorize, notice, release, and close events for one bounded historical audit window.
Audit release manifest ID derived from ak.audit.release for a sealed historical release under an active audit binding/session.
Encrypted backup object ID

Stable identifier for one chain of encrypted backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during rotation or migration; the active series is selected by the signed active-series record, not by server return order. Used by ak.schema.key_backup.v1.series_id and recovery strands to detect rollback. See identity/key-management.md §7.6.
Discovery/private-contact batch ID
Blob metadata row ID; content-addressed blobs use the special digest form
Actor-private blocklist entry ID
Call/session ID derived from the accepted ak.call.create genesis Event.

SFU-local participant handle. Scope limited to `(call_id, focus_id, sfu_did)`; derived from `(realm_id, call_id, focus_id, device_id, issuer_id, ice_bucket(issued_at))` by the media service token issuer, where v1 ice_bucket is the fixed 300-second UTC bucket. Identifier for a durable or reserved multi-phase protocol operation instance. id_kinds.id_form_note: All Realm IDs are 33-byte Event tokens (encoding.md section 4.1): reserved-zero high nibble, uint4 digest suite, then all 32 digest octets, encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters. The token is byte-identical to its ak.realm.create Event token; retyping only swaps the typed prefix.

id_kinds.description: Durable RecoveryTransaction, SecurityRotationTransaction, federation, or applet transaction identifier.
View object ID
Producer-allocated identity of a principal-private scheduled-send plan. It is not an Event or Message identity and MUST NOT be retyped into either one.
Producer-allocated immutable scope-private history-key request identity.
Producer-allocated immutable history-key response record identity.

registry/id-kind-registry.json.uuid_form_rules: The construction is declared per kind by id_form. producer_allocated = RFC 9562 UUIDv7. event_derived = the creating Event's 33-byte token (zero reserved high nibble plus uint4 suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of its digest), canonically encoded as 44 unpadded Base64URL characters and retyped only by replacing the ak:<kind>: prefix. The token requires strict decode plus canonical re-encode validation; regex alone is insufficient.

registry/keypackage-capability-registry..description: Canonical open registry for application content and policy capability identifiers advertised by Arkret MLS KeyPackages and selected as an MLS group capability floor.

registry_rules.unknown_values: preserve but treat as unsupported; an unknown value never satisfies claim admission, a group floor, or sender authorization
registry_rules.claim_rule: required_capabilities MUST contain active registered values and be a subset of both the signed LeafNode keypackage_capabilities extension and the outer claim record capabilities
registry_rules.group_rule: required_keypackage_capabilities GroupContext values MUST be active registered rows and every current or added LeafNode keypackage_capabilities value set MUST be a superset
registry_rules.sender_rule: an application capability may be used in an MLS application message only when it is present in the current required_keypackage_capabilities GroupContext extension

capabilities.description: Arkret v1 Content Block and encrypted application-content semantics.
MIMI Content interoperability profile selected by an Arkret group that carries MIMI application content.

registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.description: Canonical MLS (RFC 9420) ciphersuite vocabulary for v1 KeyPackage cipher_suites[] negotiation and server describe surfaces. Completes the algorithm-agility registry symmetry with digest-suite-registry.json, signature-alg-registry.json and hpke-suite-registry.json.
registry_rules: Schema / describe enum values for MLS ciphersuite fields MUST be generated from active rows' canonical_id only when publishing a new schema/describe contract version, then frozen for that version. Activating a reserved/new suite requires a new contract version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).

A ciphersuite not present as an active row MUST fail closed in KeyPackage claim / group negotiation (unsupported_ciphersuite); receivers MUST NOT accept unregistered suites even if the underlying MLS library supports them.

New suites (e.g. ChaCha20-Poly1305 for AES-accelerator-less devices) enter additively as new rows with their own profile gates and conformance vectors; the registry stays minimal for classical suites, but pre-registers post-quantum hybrid rows as status=reserved to match the HPKE / TLS PQ pre-registration discipline (hpke-suite-registry.json, transport-bindings.md §5).

status=reserved rows pin the canonical_id, profile gate and activation_requirements but MUST NOT appear on wire until every activation_requirements entry is met and the row is flipped to active in a registry release. Receivers MUST fail closed (unsupported_ciphersuite) on a reserved suite seen in KeyPackage cipher_suites[] or group negotiation before activation — same discipline as encryption-and-audit.md 'MLS 内容 KEM 边界'.
