Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/artifact_lint enforces this binding.

ciphersuites.security_note: RFC 9420 mandatory-to-implement suite; classical X25519 KEM (not post-quantum). Conformance pins the MLS WG byte-level vector corpus at commit cfd450286d1bfd9cd2519b95c80f9771f94a5b1a; implementations MUST run all cases for ciphersuite 0x0001 in the listed files.

ciphersuites.kat_absence_reason: The upstream corpus is identified, but byte-level digests and an active 0x0003 conformance vector are not yet published.
activation_requirements: Publish and pin byte-level KAT digests for every ciphersuite 0x0003 case in the listed MLS WG corpus
Publish an active conformance vector covering KeyPackage negotiation, Welcome/Commit processing and mixed-member unsupported-suite fail-closed behavior
Publish a new negotiated schema/describe contract release whose ciphersuite vocabulary includes this canonical_id; do not widen a frozen enum in place
ciphersuites.security_note: Reserved RFC 9420 suite for software-only devices without constant-time AES acceleration. It is not on wire until activation; receivers MUST fail closed on 0x0003 before the profile gate and contract release are active.

ciphersuites.kat_absence_reason: No stable MLS code point or byte-level KAT exists until the pinned PQ drafts and activation requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: The exact suite mapping MUST match draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-06 Table 2: MLKEM768-X25519 KEM 0x647A, HKDF-SHA256 KDF 0x0001, AES-128-GCM AEAD 0x0001, SHA256 transcript hash and ed25519 signature. MLS derives keys with the two-stage Extract/Expand pair, which draft-ietf-hpke-pq does not define for single-stage SHAKE KDFs, so the HPKE PQ SHAKE256 KDF 0x0011 MUST NOT be used as the MLS KDF. Any incompatible MLS/HPKE/CFRG draft change requires an explicit registry release and refreshed KAT digest

IETF/IANA MLS ciphersuite code point assigned for MLS_128_MLKEM768X25519_AES128GCM_SHA256_Ed25519 and recorded here as rfc9420_id (registry release required; receivers MUST NOT improvise a private code point)
Per-suite MLS conformance vectors published (KeyPackage encoding, welcome/commit KEM encap/decap, group key schedule)

Coverage-priority alignment recorded: activates only after the non-MLS HPKE row for the same MLKEM768-X25519/X-Wing construction (hpke-suite-registry.json ak.hpke_xwing_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1) — static ciphertext backups are the primary Harvest-Now-Decrypt-Later target, MLS group KEM is the second wave
ciphersuites.security_note: Reserved MLS WG post-quantum hybrid suite using MLKEM768-X25519, AES-128-GCM, SHA256 and classical Ed25519 signatures. The CFRG concrete construction is identical to X-Wing, retained only as a supplemental KEM reference; MLS naming and activation track draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites. This suite targets post-quantum confidentiality, not post-quantum authentication. Not on wire until activated; receivers MUST fail closed on this suite before activation.

ciphersuites.kat_absence_reason: No stable MLS code point or byte-level KAT exists for the pinned PQ KEM plus ML-DSA authentication suite until all activation requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: The exact suite mapping MUST match draft-ietf-mls-pq-ciphersuites-06 Table 2: MLKEM768-X25519 KEM 0x647A, HKDF-SHA384 KDF 0x0002, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD 0x0003, SHA384 transcript hash and ML-DSA-44 signature. MLS derives keys with the two-stage Extract/Expand pair, which draft-ietf-hpke-pq does not define for single-stage SHAKE KDFs, so the HPKE PQ SHAKE256 KDF 0x0011 MUST NOT be used as the MLS KDF. Any incompatible draft change requires an explicit registry release and refreshed KAT digest
IETF/IANA MLS ciphersuite code point assigned for MLS_128_MLKEM768X25519_CHACHA20POLY1305_SHA384_MLDSA44 and recorded here as rfc9420_id; receivers MUST NOT improvise a private code point

Per-suite byte-level MLS conformance vectors published for KeyPackage encoding, credential and LeafNode signatures, Welcome/Commit KEM operations, group key schedule, invalid ML-DSA-44 signatures and mixed-member unsupported-suite fail-closed behavior
Publish a new negotiated schema/describe contract release whose ciphersuite vocabulary includes this canonical_id; do not widen a frozen enum in place

Document the full-PQ claim boundary: this suite covers MLS KEM confidentiality and MLS credential/LeafNode/KeyPackage authentication, but does not automatically replace Arkret Event, receipt or capability proof profiles
ciphersuites.security_note: Reserved MLS WG suite following the standard PQ/T hybrid KEM plus ML-DSA-44 authentication route. It is distinct from ak.profile.signature.pqc.v1 and is not on wire until every activation requirement is met; receivers MUST fail closed on this suite before activation.

registry/mls-extension-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of MLS (RFC 9420) extensions required by Arkret profiles, including the standard required_capabilities extension and Arkret private-use extensions. Maintained so SDKs and conformance tooling have a single machine-readable entry for every required codepoint and context.

private_use_range.reference: RFC 9420 §17.6; IANA MLS Extension Types registry (private-use range)

extensions.name: required_capabilities
extensions.carries: RFC 9420 extension, proposal, and credential codepoints that every group member must support; Arkret lists 0xF1C0, 0xF1C1, and 0xF1C2

extensions.name: mls_governance_binding
extensions.carries: Arkret Realm/Circle governance binding inside the MLS GroupContext

extensions.name: keypackage_capabilities
extensions.carries: Canonical supported KeyPackage capability identifiers in the signed LeafNode
extensions.wire_encoding: deterministic CBOR definite-length array of UTF-8 text strings, byte-lexicographically sorted and unique

extensions.name: required_keypackage_capabilities
extensions.carries: Canonical active KeyPackage capability identifiers required of every member and authorized for use in the current group epoch
extensions.wire_encoding: deterministic CBOR definite-length array of UTF-8 text strings, byte-lexicographically sorted and unique

registry/mls-security-frontier-registry..description: Closed machine contract for the accepted state that changes current or historical MLS key access. Producers never choose frontier members. Verifiers project these inputs from one accepted Seal view and the RFC 9420 group state, then compare the resulting digest with the governance binding.
registry/mls-security-frontier-registry..artifact_digest_rule: frontier_registry_digest = sha256(RFC 8785 JCS bytes of this exact complete registry artifact). The digest is carried by each proof projection and compared against the verifier's locally pinned artifact bytes.

cell_entry_shape.ordering: Sort by UTF-8 bytes of cell_family, then canonical JCS bytes of cell_subject, then projected_value_digest; reject duplicates.

digest_input.digest_rule: security_frontier_digest = sha256(JCS({profile_id,effective_scope,group_genesis_binding,cell_entries,mls_leaf_set_digest})). group_genesis_binding is exactly {content_scheme,durability_policy?} from the verified accepted Genesis/group state. accepted Seal ids, ordinary Event seal_ref values and producer-supplied Event lists are not digest members.

cell_rules.include_when: The subject is in the effective Realm scope. invite and knock do not create an MLS leaf and are excluded.

cell_rules.scope: Parent Realm membership gate for a Circle MLS scope
cell_rules.include_when: Include exactly the parent-Realm member.state cell for every authorization subject that owns a current or pending leaf in the Circle group; exclude all unrelated Realm members. A missing/Bottom cell or any change of one of these exact cells makes the Circle frontier stale and requires membership reconciliation. This rule is independent of the Circle's own circle.member cells.
The cell subject names the effective Circle. invite and knock are excluded.
The Agent owns a current or pending MLS leaf and status=deactivated changes leaf eligibility. pause alone is an admission gate and is excluded.

cell_rules.projection: Effective authorization set for the exact principal/device keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves.
cell_rules.include_when: At least one current or pending leaf references the exact device key. Unreferenced devices are excluded.

cell_rules.projection: Effective device generation for principals that own a current or pending MLS leaf.
cell_rules.include_when: The generation fence changes validity of a key referenced by a current or pending leaf.

cell_rules.projection: Effective authorization set for exact Agent runtime keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves.
cell_rules.include_when: At least one current or pending leaf references the exact Agent key. Unreferenced Agent keys are excluded.

cell_rules.scope: Realm-default scope; for Circle scope only the content/metadata encryption floors that are explicitly parent gates
cell_rules.include_when: Only the mutable encryption floors and media-service plaintext recipient toggle are projected. content_scheme and durability_policy are create-locked and come from the exact accepted group Genesis/group state, never this cell.

cell_rules.scope: Realm authority for every Realm/Circle group whose immutable durability_policy is organization_recovery_key
cell_rules.include_when: Required exactly for durability_policy=organization_recovery_key. The reducer-effective unique active cell contains only the key tuple, accepted evidence Event provenance and prior holder-trusted basis. Before Genesis, verifier directly replays accepted Seals from that complete basis and proves accepted_key_evidence_ref is the effective active tuple; no singular activation Seal is carried or written into the state value it would activate. Missing/Bottom or tuple mismatch rejects Genesis/Commit. Circle uses the parent Realm cell and never registers its own key.

cell_rules.scope: Realm-default and parent floor for Circle MLS scopes
cell_rules.projection: Service principals and data classes permitted to receive current or historical plaintext/key material.
cell_rules.include_when: A value change expands or contracts actual plaintext/key recipients; endpoint-only metadata is excluded.

mls_tree_rule.input: The canonical current/pending RFC 9420 leaf set for the effective group, including leaf credential and referenced device/Agent key identity but excluding tree-shape-only metadata.
mls_tree_rule.digest: mls_leaf_set_digest = sha256(JCS(canonical_leaf_entries)). Leaf entries are sorted by their canonical JCS bytes and duplicates are rejected.
mls_tree_rule.commit_rule: For a Commit, compute the next frontier against the post-Commit winning leaf set and the accepted control state selected by the Commit authoring frontiers. The governance binding is inside the same RFC 9420 transcript; the key-schedule cell containing that binding is never recursively included.

always_excluded: message, Strand, display and directory metadata
media or routing endpoint metadata that does not change plaintext/key recipients
contact, consent, block or pause facts whose accepted effect does not remove an MLS leaf
ordinary Event seal_ref and accepted Seal identifiers
producer-supplied Event, Seal, root or frontier member lists

group_genesis_rules.source: Resolve the exact accepted MLS Genesis and the winning group_state_ref named by the Event or candidate transition; verify the immutable scope-derived mls_group_id and Genesis activation Seal before projection.
group_genesis_rules.immutability: content_scheme and durability_policy are frozen at Genesis. A later Event, policy bundle, Commit extension or group-state material that changes either value is failed_precondition and does not produce a new frontier.
group_genesis_rules.frontier_projection: The verified immutable pair is a required security-frontier input in addition to cell_entries and mls_leaf_set_digest; it is never read from ak.component.realm.policy_bundle.v1.

registry/morph-kind-decision-table.json.describes: Canonical merge precedence for the four declaration sources that can contribute to 'what a Morph is and what it allows'. Mirrors morph.md §4. Reducers, capability checks, query/projection paths, and conformance tests MUST follow this table.

precedence.notes: Declares the field set, types and requiredness. It is create-locked. Generic transition rules are not inferred from JSON Schema.

Tightens the order-1 declaration inside a single Realm (allowed facets subset, writable fields subset, required schema_refs, required capability actions). MUST NOT widen order-1; widening attempts produce `schema_violation` at Realm accept time.
Wire-stable string key. Create-locked so capability grant selectors do not silently break.
Pure hint. Reading facets to make a security / state-machine / interop decision is a conformance bug.

conflict_resolution.rationale: Facet is a hint, not a contract.
Field + capability are truth; facet is presentation hint only.

conformance_must_test: Reading order-4 facets to decide authorization → MUST fail.
Reducer field validation that ignores order-2 tightening → MUST fail.
Mutating morph_kind after create → MUST fail with `morph_kind_immutable`.
Order-2 morph_kind_profile that widens order-1 schema → MUST be rejected at Realm accept time with `schema_violation` / `morph_profile_widens_schema_ref`.

registry/normative-clause-registry.json.description: Canonical reverse-coverage registry for testable normative clauses. Each row pins one protocol obligation to a stable clause_id, an exact prose anchor, a digest of that section's current text, and the evidence that proves it. It closes the direction vector-registry.json cannot: from prose obligation to executable proof. See spec/v1/zh/conformance/conformance-suite.md section 2.

coverage_scope.rule: This registry covers the high-risk observable obligation set named in included_categories. It is deliberately not a numbering of every normative sentence under spec/v1/zh; mechanically numbering prose would manufacture meaningless MUSTs. A green release gate proves that every registered clause has live evidence and that no registered section changed without review. It does NOT prove that every MUST in the specification is registered.
coverage_scope.extension_rule: Adding or changing a high-risk observable obligation that this registry is intended to evidence requires adding or updating a clause in the same change. Obligations without executable evidence stay explicitly outside this registry rather than pointing at unrelated evidence. Because section_digest pins registered anchors, editing a registered section fails the release gate until its existing clause and evidence are re-reviewed; this rule does not imply exhaustive coverage of every normative sentence in an included category.

registry_rules: clause_id values are stable and MUST NOT be reused after a clause is retired; retire a clause by setting status=deprecated instead of deleting the row.
source_anchor MUST be a repository-relative markdown path plus an existing heading slug. section_digest MUST equal the sha256 of that heading's section text as computed by tools/artifact_lint.

testability_grade=vector rows MUST list evidence_refs containing active vector ids from vector-registry.json. testability_grade=api_shape or audit rows MUST instead declare test_plan describing the non-vector proof.
A clause MUST NOT claim evidence it does not have: an obligation with no executable proof stays out of this registry rather than pointing at an unrelated vector.

clauses.requirement: Canonical JSON serialization (key order, number form, NFC strings, duplicate-key rejection) is the single encoding used for every digest, signature and canonical comparison.
Digest suite identifiers, canonical event digest computation and the bytewise tie-break order are fixed; implementations MUST NOT substitute another hash encoding or comparison direction.

The signature carrier MUST cryptographically protect its algorithm selection, and the binding payload MUST bind domain and audience; a signature valid for one algorithm, domain or audience MUST NOT verify for another. Section 6.0.2 fixes one construction for every registered proof context: the unsigned projection deletes the proof carrier member rather than nulling it and never defaults an absent optional, an absent optional binding field is omitted rather than written as null, audience is a single string or a duplicate-free array with the single-value form mandatory for one audience, and the context constant is a binding object member rather than a JWS header parameter, so a signature valid under one object family's context MUST NOT verify for another.

HLC well-formedness, logical-counter overflow handling and the causal-first usage boundary: HLC breaks ties between causally incomparable items only and MUST NOT select a winner in shared protocol state.
Cursors are opaque server-issued tokens bound to their query scope; clients MUST NOT parse or forge them and cross-scope replay MUST be rejected.
Encrypted envelopes carry a pre-encryption immutable header; AAD digest and ciphertext digest are computed over fixed transcripts and any mismatch MUST fail closed.
Transport encoding bounds: Content-Encoding is forbidden on non-streaming JSON operations and every size limit MUST be enforced before the body is fully buffered or parsed.
Every operation_id ends with <kind>.<action> drawn from the closed kind set, and the action MUST describe a protocol effect rather than an HTTP method name.
clauses.test_plan: Enforced mechanically by tools/artifact_lint: every operation_id in operation-registry.json is checked against the closed kind set and against forbidden HTTP-method action names. There is no runtime vector because the obligation is on the published contract, not on request handling.

clauses.requirement: Every write operation declares a machine-readable idempotency mechanism and retry safety; clients MUST NOT be left to guess the recovery path of an uncertain outcome.
Protected current-v1 endpoints require sender-constrained proof of possession; a bare bearer session grant MUST NOT authenticate a protected request.

MLS integration boundary: only registered active ciphersuites reach the wire; Welcome and KeyPackage binding is verified byte-exactly; every peer claim binds the accepted authorization Event id plus its in-envelope Station admission proof and a destination-signed claim receipt without separate PCR/device/Agent signer-evidence sidecars; encryption floors MUST NOT be downgraded; every encrypted envelope uses only the minimal encryption_context wire and reconstructs the exact closed pre-encryption header from the outer signed Event, verified producer domain, scope-derived group id and exact winning group state; MLS leaf ownership and Proposal targets preserve complete ActorId including Station and never collapse to the signing principal; every MLS epoch binds the independently re-derived security frontier for its accepted key-access state; and epoch-0 leaf indices are recovered only from digest-verified RFC 9420 GroupInfo/ratchet-tree bytes committed by the accepted genesis.
Directory resolution failures are indistinguishable: unauthorized, non-existent and policy-denied targets MUST NOT be separable by error code, field set or timing.

A Control Move MUST carry a CBA basis covered by an accepted Seal except in the two closed anchor-unit contexts; same-batch events MUST NOT advance their own authorization basis, and basis-free anchor Events remain Control Moves with Control Proposal Acks and pending-index obligations. Ordinary Collaboration bootstrap uses the ordered machine-registry facet closure with an explicit final creator membership and no implicit creator membership. The mutually exclusive Direct Conversation branch is exactly create, explicit peer membership, one basis-free main ak.strand.create, then explicit founder membership with head_eq null. Batch admission MUST reject both no-basis shapes anywhere else.

Seal canonical bytes exclude self-reference and DataEvent digests, compaction preserves control roots, Realm reducer selection comes from the authenticated singleton control cell, equivocating notaries are quarantined instead of silently merged, and a full-digest collision under a sealed Control Move is normalized by canonical bytes rather than by an ambiguous digest. Availability admission is authorized only by the joined predecessor state: genesis has no such authority, commits no AvailabilityReceipt, and materializes policy only for successor Seals.

A grant stays within the union of the authorities its issuer_authority_refs name and within their per-action validity window. A grant without ordinary authority_control cannot be a grant ref; a ref with authority_regrant_allowed=false can issue only an explicitly terminal max_authority_depth=0 child. A grant ref supplies issuer authority only when its concrete subject ActorId equals the child issuer ActorId in full; cycles, inactive refs and same-DID cross-Station replay MUST fail closed rather than widen the effective permission set.
Revocation rolls back downstream grants and forces a re-check of dependent decisions; a revoked grant MUST NOT keep authorizing pending or cached writes.
Lattice joins are idempotent, commutative and associative per family; data-plane conflicts return structured bottom instead of electing a winner by arrival order or HLC.

Field patches apply atomically against the declared pre-state; a partially applied patch or an unbound pre-state MUST be rejected. $op="unset" MUST NOT remove a registered redactable content-carrier slot, while $op="set" on the same slot and $op="unset" on metadata paths MUST be accepted. A patch path MUST NOT address a reducer-managed field of the target object kind; the per-object forbidden set, its universal minimum set and its one named View state exemption are read from registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json, never re-derived from prose.
Every reducer-input event kind declares a closed cell contract (cell family, subject, lattice, bottom, effect projection); an unregistered projection MUST NOT be improvised.
Call state transitions follow the registered matrix, terminal states are absorbing, replaying the same state is a no-op, and concurrent siblings resolve to bottom.
Invite claim is a state machine: a consumed token MUST NOT be re-subjected, expiry uses canonical time, and the membership transition is atomic with the claim.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers with explicitly registered writer authority and holder self operations: a stale write MUST fail with cas_conflict, the revision high-water mark never goes backwards, and domain merge runs client-side on plaintext.
Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins regardless of HLC, HLC decides only concurrent positions, and device_id only breaks equal HLCs.
To-device delivery executes each durable handler effect exactly once: redelivery is deduplicated by the closed sender endpoint plus device_message_id and queue removal happens only on explicit ack.

A revoked authorization whose old basis-to-revocation Seal distance is inside the configured grace remains deterministically accepted in reducer input even if first delivered or replayed much later; receiver arrival time is not an input, while high-risk capability uses effective grace zero.
Every accountable principal on an Actor Event must have an active matching accountability grant; any missing grant rejects the whole Event without a stripped projection.

Realm proposal configuration must leave a realizable decision schedule: decision window does not exceed the absolute deadline, equality is valid only when deferral is disabled, and invalid create/update writes reject without state change.
Optional nullable fields normalize absent and null unless a conditional branch requires the field or x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct explicitly assigns three business states.
clauses.test_plan: tools/gen_property_presence_manifest.py must classify every tristate audit target with zero unresolved dispositions; the Rust SDK draft202012_runtime and Circle payload tests pin the sole distinct target and its Missing/Null/Value round-trip.

clauses.requirement: An accepted ordinary-Realm or managed-Agent closed-anchor Control Move, its Control Proposal Ack and pending index are committed atomically; the covering Seal atomically applies lineage and cell effects and marks every covered pending digest sealed, rolling back if any digest is absent. The separately specified human self-principal PCR authority-authored path omits the Ack but not the pending index or covering-Seal obligation.

Fields inside the event_digest preimage MUST NOT commit to the enclosing Event's own event_id, event_digest or any retype of them, nor to the identity of a not-yet-formed sibling Event in the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch; those two classes have no fixed point, MUST be rejected as event_id_digest_mismatch, and MUST NOT be exempted by any registry. Commitments of that kind MUST instead use the counterpart's payload digest or a structure outside the preimage (proofs, receipts). A one-way forward declaration naming a later Event from a separate submission whose canonical bytes the author already froze is constructible and MUST be allowed only when preimage-identity-exemption-registry.json carries an active row for exactly that field and the field's own description declares the forward commitment.

A client MUST NOT admit a Seal into its local MLS governance trust store because a service reported it as a head, because a proof bundle self-reported it, or because an error suggested it. A candidate is admissible only when the client verifies it locally: for an event-derived Realm, the genesis Seal must cover the ak.realm.create Event derived from realm_id and be signed by the notary named in that create payload; for a Principal Control Realm, the genesis Seal must cover the principal's critical did_inception root anchor; otherwise only a Seal verified as a descendant of an already-trusted anchor may replace the pin.

A cross-object ak.redaction whose target_ref uses the ak:event: form only trims that Event's fields per preserve[] and MUST NOT change any object's state, including the event-derived object minted from a targeted create Event; an object enters state=redacted only through the object typed-id form of target_ref (Message still goes exclusively through ak.message.redact). The two spellings of one 33-octet token land in two distinct ak.component.object.redaction.v1 cells that are independent and never merge; a reducer MUST NOT canonicalize the ak:event: spelling into the derived object typed id.

registry/operation-bundle-closure-lock.j.algorithm: sha256 over canonical sorted-key JSON closure

registry/operation-clause-registry.json.description: Canonical selector-based normative-clause coverage registry for service operations. A profile conformance claim computes its inherited operation_requirements closure and MUST satisfy every active clause whose selector matches each operation. This registry complements operation-registry shape; it does not create a second operation namespace.

clauses.requirement: The canonical operation id and every advertised HTTP binding shape MUST match contract-registry, generated operation-registry, OpenAPI and operation schema index.
Protected operations MUST enforce the OpenAPI security declaration and sender-constrained proof rules before any durable side effect or sensitive response.
Every write operation MUST expose machine-readable idempotency, retry safety, and an uncertain-outcome recovery strategy when blind retry is unsafe.
HTTP headers, aggregate headers, path/query and canonical request envelopes MUST obey the v1 transport bounds and reject generated over-limit inputs before unbounded allocation.
Operation-specific and universal failures MUST use registered error codes and preserve the minimal-disclosure Problem Details.
Stream operations MUST implement the registered frame ordering, dropped/resync recovery, cursor binding and reconnect cooldown behavior.
Batch and fanout operations that admit partial outcomes MUST account for every input item and define safe partial retry identity.
Privacy-sensitive operations MUST preserve indistinguishable failures and the minimum response/metadata disclosure defined by their profile.

registry/operation-contract-closure-lock.algorithm: sha256 over canonical sorted-key JSON closure

registry/operation-registry.json.description: Canonical operation catalog for generated service operation views and transport bindings.

generated_views.role: HTTP/OpenAPI binding shape aligned to the catalog; not a second operation namespace.
Descriptive operation map and governance notes; excerpt-only unless explicitly marked generated.

high_security_session_authentication_pol.public_projection_rule: Without valid sender-constrained proof, an allowlisted operation may return only its contract-defined public metadata projection and MUST NOT grant session or capability semantics. All other ak.self.* operations fail closed.
high_security_session_authentication_pol.new_operation_rule: A new or unknown ak.self.* operation is protected by default; adding an unauthenticated public projection requires explicit registration in this list and a normative operation contract defining that projection.

registry_rules: New operation_id values MUST be added here before any OpenAPI, HTTP binding table, SDK generator, or alternative transport binding references them.
Generated views MAY change shape, grouping, or field order, but MUST NOT introduce, rename, or remove operation_id values that are absent from this catalog.
Supporting Arkret core does not imply support for every registered operation. Implementations MUST advertise registered supported_operation_bundles and supported_profiles explicitly.

Each surface_groups entry carries a tier (see surface_classes); only the core tier is implied by claiming v1 protocol support. Extension, interop_bridge, and deployment_local surfaces require explicit advertisement.
surface_classes defines the closed tier vocabulary and surface_groups is the sole canonical operation grouping view; generators MUST NOT emit a third top-level surfaces collection.

Profile matrices in artifacts/profiles/conformance-profiles.json define role-level MUST/SHOULD requirements; the surface groups below define machine-readable capability families for discovery, docs, and lint.
Each operation MUST declare success_shape_kind so SDKs can determine success handling without endpoint-name hard-coding.

Operations with typed OpenAPI bodies SHOULD declare request_schema_ref and/or response_schema_ref. The referenced schema fragment is the source for generated DTO docs and MUST match the OpenAPI component referenced by the HTTP binding.

Operations that still bind OpenAPI request/response bodies to OperationRequest or OperationResult MUST declare generic_binding with request/response booleans, reason, profile_gate, and migration_plan; core-tier operations MUST NOT use generic bindings.

operation_id values MUST end with <kind>.<action>.v1. The kind segment MUST be one of read, stream, resource, command, upload, or exchange; the action segment MUST describe protocol semantics and MUST NOT be an HTTP method name. read is the only safe/idempotent computation kind; its exact GET, QUERY, or POST binding is declared by the operation row according to request shape.
An operation row MUST declare exactly one HTTP binding and MUST NOT declare http_compatibility_bindings or unregistered method/path aliases.

resource.replace operations MUST bind to HTTP PUT; resource.delete operations MUST bind to HTTP DELETE; command, upload, exchange, and complex read-body operations SHOULD bind to HTTP POST unless their operation notes define a stricter resource URI replacement contract.

Every write operation (kind command/upload/exchange, and resource.replace / resource.delete) MUST declare idempotency_mechanism (one of idempotency_key, object_id, request_id, canonical_hash, protocol_sequence, none) and retry_safe (boolean). Read-only operations (read/stream/resource.get/resource.head) MUST NOT declare these fields.

An operation that invokes current DID authority MUST carry exactly one did_authority object that byte-matches its did-freshness-profile-registry call_sites row. Operations without a real DID-authority call MUST omit it; risk tier never implies DID freshness.

idempotency_mechanism is the machine-readable source of truth for which idempotency mechanism from api-conventions.md section 6 an operation uses. canonical_hash operations MUST also declare canonical_hash_input as either full_body or an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. retry_safe=true means a byte-identical full retry of the same request cannot produce duplicate side effects: it returns the original outcome, an equivalent idempotent no-op, or a deterministic conflict. retry_safe=false means blind retries MAY duplicate side effects or consume one-time material; clients MUST NOT retry such operations without out-of-band reconciliation.

Every write operation MUST declare durable_effect. kind=event_log identifies an Arkret Event committed by successful completion and declares either event_kinds[] or an event_kind_source JSON path; kind=actor_private_event declares the actor-private Event kind committed; kind=none declares no Arkret Event and requires a stable rationale. kind=branched declares a semantic request discriminator plus a closed effect_branches[] list with unique equals values and one final otherwise branch; each branch contains a complete event_log, actor_private_event, or none leaf effect. An event_log branch that is not unconditional MUST additionally name event_submission_path pointing to the caller-signed EventInitialSubmission used by that branch. Field presence is evidence carried by a branch, never the branch discriminator itself. Service-local durable state, identity-method logs, queues, session/material stores, external effects and returned-but-uncommitted Event material all use kind=none with an accurate rationale. Missing, unknown or inactive declared Event kinds fail closed.

Every operation MUST declare body_class, a closed value of non_streaming_json, streaming_ndjson, or binary_stream. body_class=non_streaming_json binds the operation to the general size contract in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md section 2.1: canonical request/response body <= 8 MiB, HTTP message content wire bytes <= 16 MiB, Content-Encoding MUST be absent, and every byte overflow maps to payload_too_large. streaming_ndjson and binary_stream operations are excluded from the whole-body limits and MUST define their own per-frame / per-chunk / pending bounds (scalability-constraints section 2.1.7).

max_canonical_body_bytes is OPTIONAL and only for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose normative limit is LOWER than the general 8 MiB. It MUST NOT declare a value above 8 MiB, and deployments MUST NOT lower the general interoperability constants through Describe (scalability-constraints section 2.1.6).

max_items is REQUIRED for a body_class=non_streaming_json operation whose request or response carries a top-level array with a normative count bound. max_items and the byte budget are a conjunctive two-dimensional constraint: a count bound never promises that max_items objects of near-maximum size fit in one body, and implementations MUST NOT lower a registered count because a fixture-median product exceeds the byte budget (scalability-constraints section 2.1.5).

Every operation_id is an explicit versioned operation identity ending in .v1. Its stable HTTP endpoint identity is derived by removing the terminal .vN and is used as the OpenAPI operationId; the unversioned identity is not an alias for a versioned operation_id.

Every canonical Arkret HTTP request MUST carry exactly one Arkret-Operation header naming the exact versioned operation_id before body parsing. The receiver MUST verify that the selector is locally advertised and belongs to the selected method/path family and binding. A missing selector fails with operation_selector_required; an empty candidate set, unknown id, duplicate selector, or value outside the route family fails with unsupported_operation_version. Endpoint uniqueness, payload-shape inference, client SDK version, implicit defaults, and version fallback MUST NOT replace the selector. This invariant keeps existing clients stable when another operation version is added to the same HTTP endpoint family.

operation_bundles is the only canonical bundle member source. Each registered bundle freezes one service_kind and a canonical unique set of (operation_id,binding_kind) members; changing a member requires a new bundle id.
Within one service_kind, active current-v1 bundles MUST NOT overlap on an identical (operation_id,binding_kind) pair. Pairs using a different binding kind are distinct.

Only registered ak.operation_bundle.*.v1 ids may appear in current-v1 ServiceDescribe. Current-v1 defines no vendor bundle wire namespace; vendor-private collections may only appear as ignorable x_* metadata and never affect capability decisions. Unknown bundle ids fail closed and are never expanded by name.

surface_classes.core: Base interoperable surfaces implied by claiming Arkret v1 protocol support (service discovery, identity registry, events/account aggregate).
surface_classes.extension: Optional interoperable surfaces that are part of the Arkret specification but require explicit discovery/profile advertisement.
surface_classes.interop_bridge: Adapter surfaces that bridge Arkret to external protocols (MIMI Internet-Drafts, third-party Applet hosts). Implementations advertise these only when the external protocol is supported; bridge operations are not part of any core or extension profile and frequently mirror an in-spec operation via bridges_to.
surface_classes.deployment_local: Deployment-specific, operator, or product-local surfaces that MUST NOT be assumed from core protocol support alone.

delivery_authentication_record.node_to_applet: Source-Service-ID current service DID verification method and key digest; Destination-Service-ID MUST equal the Applet registration service_id; registration_epoch is the effective destination Applet registration.
delivery_authentication_record.applet_to_arkret_inbound: Applet registration webhook_auth.key_ref; its canonical bare did MUST be validated by the registered method adapter and project to both Source-Service-ID and the active effective install service_id. The effective registration_epoch and actual verification key digest are bound. Direct DID/core-id comparison and did_core_id fragment concatenation are forbidden.
delivery_authentication_record.equality: Receivers recompute sha256(UTF8(digest_domain + newline) || RFC8785_JCS(record)); equal recomputed digests define replay equality. Caller-supplied records or digests are forbidden.

did_authority.purpose: Verify the announce governance proof of the announcing service or organization, and resolve the Station endpoint inside the same first-ingest admission.
Verify the withdraw governance signature of the service or organization that owns the directory entry.

operations.notes: Server-to-server session-grant introspection (RFC 7662-style). The Station validating a presented grant calls this with the grant id or grant_jwt (+ optional audience and optional S2S holder confirmation) and learns whether the issuer ledger considers it active, plus non-secret grant metadata. The Account Authority MUST read the same issuer ledger used by issue, refresh, revoke and cascade; lifecycle status distinguishes active, revoked, superseded and dynamically expired records rather than consulting a Principal Event/cell. Introspection does not call back to the origin Station and carries no reusable revocation-gate receipt: before accepting each protected self request, that origin Station checks its own exact device/generation pending/Seal state locally in the request transaction. The introspection response MUST include the grant's cnf_jkt (RFC 7638 thumbprint of the bound DPoP holder key) so the Station can verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3); clients do not send a separate introspection-proof header on self-path requests. session_public_key is also returned for RFC 9421 PoP verification. READ-ONLY: introspection MUST NOT consume/revoke the grant. Authenticated by the configured session_grant_introspection_bearer (server-local); not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Account Authority S2S producer operation for Native Agent signer evidence. The request carries agent_authority_resolution: the current signed ServiceResolutionRecord, adapter-discriminated method evidence and authenticated normalized DID Document. The receiver independently validates method evidence, document digest, record proof/currentness, project(did), and active assertion key before verifying an RFC 9421 signature that covers method, target URI/path, Content-Digest, Source/Destination-Service-ID, operation id and request id. A did_core_id, URL, bearer or caller-supplied public key is never the verification key source; bearer may only be an additional deployment gate. The authenticated source service MUST equal request.agent_authority_id and MUST byte-match service_id in request.principal_id's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding; that Station is the Agent PCR authority under the managed-Agent same-server invariant. Ordinary clients and a caller-supplied account identity are forbidden. The Account Authority reads its own authoritative account binding/status projection, selects account_binding_default or account_status_event basis, and signs the closed controller_account_gate_attestation under domain ak.controller_account_gate.v1. issued_at <= expires_at and expires_at-issued_at MUST be <=300s. Unknown principal, missing current service binding, wrong source service and unauthorized caller are indistinguishable not_found outcomes and disclose no account status. Exact request_id plus canonical intent replay returns the byte-identical outcome while retained; same request_id with different principal or service is duplicate_conflict with zero issuance. The attestation is intentionally a reusable short-TTL controller-lifecycle snapshot and omits operation, request_digest, audience and challenge: per-request current_observation and outer_attestation bind its digest to those exact values, so a bare gate replay cannot validate another request. account_id and raw account cells never enter the request, outcome, logs visible to the caller or portable evidence.

Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, validates the complete unpublished DID operation, derives principal_id, its canonical operation digest, did_version_id, log_head_digest, and control_key_digest, persists the holder-authenticated operation checkpoint, rate-limits same-holder renewal, and issues a <=300s single-use challenge bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, lease/fence, all derived DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose, and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

Issue a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to the authenticated service account under stable principal_id. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header. Unlike issue_identity_binding_challenge the caller supplies principal_id plus did rather than an unpublished DID operation: the Account Authority MUST resolve did itself at the high freshness tier (synchronous refresh or fail closed), MUST require the registered adapter to project(did)=principal_id, MUST NOT attempt to resolve did_core_id, MUST NOT accept caller-supplied history, and derives did_version_id, log_head_digest and control_key_digest from the resolved current entry. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST additionally require method-native witness / freshness evidence, because accepting registry and Station co-location does not extend trust to third-party DIDs. The <=300s single-use challenge and returned control proof bind account_subject, principal_id, did, holder cnf.jkt, the resolved DID pins, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation performs no PCR genesis and reserves no principal: it only proves current control of an existing DID.

Issue a single-use challenge that authorizes explicitly abandoning a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted (zh/identity/key-management.md §5.0.2). Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header, and by nothing else: the PCR was never accepted, so the holder has no principal and therefore no principal-bound ak.session.grant. The Account Authority verifies the current lease holder and fence, requires principal_id and did_version_id to equal the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint, and MUST refuse to issue a challenge once that PCR is accepted. The <=300s single-use challenge is bound to account_subject, holder cnf.jkt, the abandoned principal_id, did_version_id, lease id and fence, the closed consequence disclosure, audience, origin, trust domain, purpose and expiry. Repeating the same request_id returns the same unconsumed challenge. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states. This operation abandons nothing by itself and MUST NOT be reachable from ordinary login, session resume, lease fence advance or any automated flow.

Consume an identity-abandonment challenge and explicitly abandon the provisional identity. Authenticated by Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus a matching DPoP header; the presented handoff MUST be a fresh one and MUST NOT be the grant that was presented when the challenge was issued. Whether that fresh handoff required re-authentication, which risk checks ran and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified. One transaction consumes the challenge, records the orphan anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppresses the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and releases the identity-creation lease; any step failing means zero writes. If the PCR was accepted between issuance and confirmation the request MUST fail with identity_creation_already_accepted and MUST NOT abandon anything, because removing an established identity is the account deletion path. Replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second tombstone. The abandoned entry 0 stays a permanently unusable orphan anchor; its later handling is deployment governance.

Account Authority single-call issuer-ledger SessionGrant issuance with a closed HumanSessionGrantRequest | RecoverySessionGrantRequest | AgentSessionGrantRequest union. OIDC authorization code is never accepted here; authentication-handoffs is the unique code consumer. Returning-human and recovery requests use Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP. Returning-human issuance requires AcceptedDevicePossessionProof and origin revocation-gate allow, consumes the handoff, and emits Standard + complete device_binding. Recovery issuance requires credential_class=recovery_session, binds the account principal/audience, candidate device and handoff DPoP JWK, emits a <=15 minute non-refreshable recovery_candidate_device grant without device_binding, consumes only the request DPoP JTI, and preserves the handoff for recovery completion. Agent issuance keeps its independent agent_key_proof validator. The issuer uses branch-specific request identity and canonical intent to persist one immutable issuance record and signed JWT before responding. Exact replay is byte-identical; conflict and terminal replay fail closed. The client presents every grant only as Authorization: DPoP plus matching DPoP proof. No Principal Event is authored.

Account Authority ordinary hard logout (account-lifecycle §4.1): single client-visible logout entry. The presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The handler validates the ak.session.grant + DPoP when metadata remains, idempotently terminates the Auth-side auth session / complete grant rotation chain through ak.gate.account.command.logout_auth_session.v1 when Auth-side is split out, and completes or durably schedules the Principal-side local account session + device session cleanup and to-device/push removal. Exact retries on an already terminal or pruned chain return an equivalent successful no-op; audience mismatch still fails closed. Distinct from revoke_session (targeted session-grant revoke). HTTP-only Account Authority op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

The only client entry point for self-initiated account erasure (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface: it authenticates the holder as a high-risk action, durably records the erasure intent and continues its existing erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord issuance flow within the same service — there is no cross-service handoff, because the record issuer, the status-transition legality oracle and the section-8 fanout orchestrator are all the Account Authority, so no 'accepted but issuance pending on another service' intermediate state exists. Authentication freshness is judged locally by the Account Authority, the only party holding recent login / WebAuthn / recovery key facts; a Station MUST NOT determine or approximate it from session-grant introspection or local session state (introspection deliberately projects neither auth_time nor proof kind). The success response is an acceptance confirmation only: the current status is observed through the existing account-status read surface and physical completion only through the erasure receipt rail. The Account Authority MAY insert a deployment-governed withdrawal window (possibly zero) between acceptance and record signing, echoing withdrawal_window_ends_at when one exists; once the erasure_pending record is signed the request is irreversible and any withdrawal MUST fail closed. Replaying the same request_id returns the recorded acceptance outcome; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes; a different request_id while a live unsigned-record intent exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending. A session that does not satisfy the deployment's fresh high-risk action authentication policy is rejected with reauthentication_required.

Account Authority to Auth Server S2S Auth-side logout sub-operation (account-lifecycle §4.1): the presented grant chain is the stable protocol-sequence identity. The Account Authority has already validated the client-visible ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1 request, then calls this operation with service-to-service authentication to log out the Auth-side browser/auth session owning the presented ak.session.grant and terminate that session's complete grant rotation chain. Exact retries, including an already logged-out, revoked, unknown or pruned chain, return an equivalent successful terminal outcome without a second side effect. Ordinary clients MUST NOT call this operation; they only call ak.gate.account.command.logout.v1. HTTP-only S2S op; not exposed over gRPC/MQ.

Final native Agent runtime-key authorization. The closed Ed25519 possession proof MUST be byte-identical to the current persisted runtime request and still fresh; the authority rebuilds its server-record-bound transcript, stable runtime binding and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1 (including current proof digest) before accepting the controller-signed authorize Event. A stale prompt or any body/record/evidence mismatch fails closed without consuming the pairing handle.

Authorizes a sibling device only after verified current-device confirmation. This operation always produces authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, so device_signature MUST verify under ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1 and registration_anchor/pcr_recovery domains MUST be rejected. The authority recomputes the pairing transcript, verifies exact request/Event equality and submits the current-device-signed Event through ordinary PCR admission; it never resolves current human DID authority.

Issues the replacement device's first Standard grant after a PCR-policy RecoveryTransaction completes. The body carries the terminal device-attested receipt, coordinator attestation, PCR generation and InitialSessionGrantIntent; DID-root evidence is relevant only when that optional factor was enabled. If deployment policy permits reactivation and the original account is deactivated, this operation alone atomically authors the deactivated-to-active successor, restores the same account row, creates the publication outbox entry and issues the first new-generation grant. It never creates a replacement account or second PCR, and it never revives an old session, device or KeyPackage; policy denial or incomplete recovery returns account_deactivated with zero authoritative writes.

DPoP-bound issuer-ledger SessionGrant rotation with a closed HumanSessionGrantRefreshRequest | AgentSessionGrantRefreshRequest union. Both branches present the predecessor as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof and carry no client-generated challenge or generic proof_kind. Human refresh additionally carries AcceptedDevicePossessionProof purpose=session_grant_refresh; the origin verifies it under the locked current accepted-device key and applies the predecessor signed device_binding as expected binding in the same current-authorization linearization. Agent refresh carries only AgentSessionRefreshProof and revalidates current runtime-key authorization/lifecycle through its independent validator. The stable request identity is (predecessor_grant_id, refresh_request_digest). One issuer transaction creates the active successor with a fresh issuance nonce, preserves subject/scope/audience/cnf.jkt/session_id, and atomically supersedes the predecessor. Exact replay returns the recorded successor; conflicting or terminal replay never issues another. Account/passkey restoration uses a fresh AccountHandoff then issue, and PCR recovery uses its dedicated completion operation; neither is a refresh proof kind. No Principal Event is authored.

Canonical account creation/binding operation. The body selects exactly one branch: an already-published DID control proof, or account-first identity_creation. Both branches submit outer did and principal_id; every repeated did/principal_id in the selected proof, identity-creation object and PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte. The Account Authority independently validates the registered method adapter and requires project(did)=principal_id. The published-DID proof branch uses the durable challenge pins and creates no identity-creation lease or PCR genesis. In the account-first identity_creation branch the caller MUST additionally present Authorization: DPoP <account_handoff_grant> plus matching DPoP, the current lease/fence, the exact reserved DID inception operation, and a fresh identity-root control proof over the persisted challenge transcript. For did:webvh the verifier takes parameters.updateKeys[0] of the entry pinned by did_version_id (the root is not a DID Document verificationMethod), requires verification_key_multibase to match it exactly, and requires its canonical multikey SHA-256 to equal control_key_digest. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0. The Account Authority CAS-validates account/holder/lease/fence/reservation, consumes the challenge, submits the DID operation internally, accepts only accepted or byte-identical duplicate with a verified head digest, derives pcr_realm_id only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id, and writes the service-account binding. Account-first PCR genesis persists the same verified did, method_history_head and version_id in initial_resolution. Every success returns a signed binding_receipt that binds binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id and control_key_digest; identity_creation_lease_id and lease_fence appear only for binding_kind=identity_creation. The (account, principal_id, operation_digest) result is idempotent; published-but-not-yet-bound state is durably completed for that same account and can never be rebound to another account. The operation never accepts recovery words, seed material, or identity-root private keys.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: Beyond authoring the genesis Events this operation publishes a public did:webvh log entry and commits a one-account-one-principal binding that can never be rebound. Retry and audit logic MUST treat it as cross-service irreversible even though the closed durable_effect kind vocabulary can only name the Event-log half.

operations.notes: Durable issuer-ledger session revocation. The stable request identity binds issuer, operation kind, authenticated principal/session, canonical target selector and canonical request digest. One issuer transaction records the exact outcome and idempotently transitions matching active records to revoked. Same identity and canonical intent replays the byte-identical recorded outcome after current caller authorization is revalidated; the same identity with different intent is duplicate_conflict with zero additional state changes. Introspection is not a substitute for resolving an uncertain mutation outcome.

Unique current-v1 OIDC authorization-code consumer. Account Authority exchanges and validates the code and issues an opaque, short-lived account_handoff_grant bound to the request DPoP key plus the deployment-local stable account_subject. The external callback receiver that owns the redirect transaction validates state; Account Authority validates state only when it owns that transaction, and always validates issuer, token exchange/PKCE, redirect_uri and ID Token nonce. The handoff is not ak.session.grant, has no refresh-token semantics, and its closed operation allowlist is issue_identity_binding_challenge, issue_did_binding_challenge, issue_identity_abandonment_challenge, abandon_identity_creation, register, issue_session_grant, and issue_recovery_completion_grant. It returns bound, identity_creation_active, or identity_creation_busy. Bound clients normalize local evidence before choosing returning issue, pairing-first Device Setup or diagnostics; identity onboarding accepts only the other two states. Repeating the same request_id returns the same live outcome. When deployment policy allows reactivation, fresh account authentication may return a bound recovery-candidate handoff for the original deactivated account, but the handoff does not change status and ordinary register, issue and refresh remain blocked; only recovery completion may reactivate it. Policy denial returns account_deactivated with zero recovery writes.

Read-only DPoP-bound projection of the current Account Authority identity-creation lease or established binding. The response is rebuilt from durable server state on every call and accepts no client-authored phase, goal, checkpoint, or recovery material. Clients use it to reconcile local onboarding artifacts after reload, callback, process restart, or an uncertain command result.

Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The closed Ed25519 proof binds the local key to the authoritative pairing handle, at-least-128-bit pairing secret, authority service DID, stable runtime binding and no-more-than-five-minute window; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize bound to the current proof digest. Pairing secret and proof MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 digest: same-binding retries retain approval/notification ids and atomically replace the current freshness proof, while a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

Resolves a short-lived agent pairing token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the six-field agent_pairing_bootstrap.

Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id + pairing_code + agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). Once approved, the outcome carries authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key and treat a mismatch as paired-by-another-runtime. HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and use 1s/2s/5s/10s then at most 30s backoff, stopping after pairing expiry.

Unauthenticated stage of a device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). The new device submits a canonical new_device_pubkey and a client_nonce (plus optional display_name / device_metadata) and MUST NOT submit a challenge proof, because the proof must commit to values this call mints; the service mints a fresh device_pairing_request_id, an 8-character Crockford-style 40-bit CSPRNG pairing_code, a gate_audience and a server_nonce, and stores a bounded-TTL account-less record in state pending_authorization. The staged record deliberately carries no hpke_key, no algorithms, no challenge proof and no target attestation: those reach the approving device only over the out-of-band channel, so this anonymous surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint, and a mirrored copy could never be authoritative anyway. The staged record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it. Stage, resolve and status are rate limited. Each call mints a fresh request, so blind retries duplicate staged records: not retry-safe.

Resolves a device-pairing short-link token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The pairing token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is the DevicePairingBootstrap. The bootstrap carries only server-minted challenge material: it does not carry the challenge proof, the target attestation, or the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs, and those MUST NOT be mirrored here. resolve MUST return a uniform not_found for unknown id, pairing_code mismatch, expiry, or a non-pending record so the failing condition is not enumerable. Authorization is unchanged: the returned bootstrap is only consumed by an authenticated device that has independently verified the out-of-band challenge proof and target attestation before driving ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

Unauthenticated poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). While the record is open the outcome carries only state pending_authorization; once an authenticated device has authorized the pairing the outcome carries state authorized plus required device_id and authorized_event_ref; an expired record reports only state expired during a bounded cleanup retention period and becomes not_found after deletion. authorized_event_ref is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in device-lifecycle.md §5.4.1: the target device MUST fetch that accepted ak.device.authorize and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did / hpke_key / algorithms and an expected principal_id before it assembles the identity locally, and MUST fail closed and warn the user otherwise.

Reads the current public principal resolution projection from the known Station. The response carries only the account pair, the projection, bounded adapter method evidence and the Station projection attestation; it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted Seal. Account-internal audit material moved to ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1, so this surface has no history selector. This is a second-hop projection fetch, not a global resolver or authorization oracle. Sensitive consumers fetch fresh, verify the attestation proof under the current station_id method history, independently run the registered DID method adapter, and require project(did)=principal_id; durable storage of arbitrary remote-principal bindings is not required.

Returns the current AuthenticatedServiceResolution at the stable current_record_url carried by bootstrap material. TLS is transport only. For did:webvh, method_history_evidence includes the complete gap-free native log from inception through the signed record position and every required witness record; a resolver summary or partial segment is invalid. Consumers independently verify the complete method-native history, terminal DID document, record proof, project(did)=service_id, time ordering, record_sequence/previous_record_digest and describe binding. Same-core successors refresh route caches without Realm rebind; a changed did_core_id requires a new authorized service binding.

Resolves an online invite locator token carried out-of-band, usually as a URL fragment in a QR/link. The locator token MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string; the response is a signed principal_locator.

The caller MUST author and sign the exact ak.consent.grant (decision=accept) or ak.consent.revoke (decision=deny or revoke) EventInitialSubmission. The facade verifies the detached operation signature and the Event authority/correlation, then submits the Event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign consent state. A revoke with no matching active observed dots is rejected without disclosing holder state. Exact Event replay returns the same accepted Event reference.

discriminator.description: The caller-declared semantic MIMI update kind. The decoded opaque payload MUST carry the same kind before a branch is admitted.

operations.notes: Replicates one exact Account Authority-signed AccountStatusRecord. The receiver verifies transport authentication, record identity/proof, exact account/principal/binding tuple, sequence continuity and previous_account_status_record_id, then atomically advances its monotonic replica and emits a signed receipt. A gap returns dependency_missing with zero writes; stale, duplicate and fork are distinguished without rebuilding or re-signing the record. For status=erasure_pending, accepted or duplicate is returned only after a durable physical-erasure intent keyed by receiver service, account, triggering record and storage boundary exists. Same Idempotency-Key plus different canonical body is duplicate_conflict.

durable_effect.irreversibility_note: The signed record is the only erasure command. Acceptance is forbidden until the receiver has a durable execution intent; physical completion is established only by a verified ErasureReceiptPackage.

operations.notes: Service-authenticated bounded read of a contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range for freshness and replica gap recovery. The Account Authority returns original signed records in status_seq order and never exposes an account to a service without an existing exact account/principal relationship. Empty, unknown and unauthorized are non-enumerating at the operation boundary.

Unique closed XOR delivery carrier for original holder-signed Contact request, normal response, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, or bilateral continuity-checkpoint control. The continuity branch carries a one-sided proposal; the receiver recomputes the exact core, verifies the proposer signature, appends only its own participant service-authority signature, durably commits the complete checkpoint and returns it with a signed control receipt. Exact replay returns the same bytes; same-sequence different-digest forks fail closed. It never carries Direct Conversation binding or Realm Events.

Service-authenticated terminal erasure-result fanout only; it never requests or triggers deletion. Source-Service-ID MUST equal receipt.issuer. The receiver verifies the closed trigger union, receipt, issuer authority, every proof, receipt_digest and exact retained-stub binding before durable acceptance. Same key and canonical body returns the byte-identical signed acceptance; different body returns duplicate_conflict with zero writes. Account erasure requires the account_status_record trigger branch to equal the accepted erasure_pending record; other erasure uses the event branch.

Service-authenticated exact receipt-package lookup for the issuer, receiver or an explicitly authorized auditor. It is non-enumerating: unauthorized, unknown and hidden receipt identifiers produce the same not_found response. The returned retained stub is the exact object accepted with the receipt and MUST NOT be reconstructed from later state.

Authenticated Account-Authority-to-origin-Station current-device and revocation gate. returning_session_grant_issue and human session_grant_refresh bind AcceptedDevicePossessionProof; registration/recovery session_grant_issue uses its separately verified durable evidence and forbids this proof. Under one device lock/serializable transaction the origin reads the durable current accepted-device projection, verifies any required proof with its key, derives authorization Event/generation, evaluates pending/revoked state and persists a signed decision receipt binding proof digest and intent. A lock-external key/status read followed by a second gate transaction is forbidden. expected selectors are required for refresh and may be omitted for both issue action classes. Only allow carries derived selectors and can produce complete human device_binding; authority_mismatch maps to device_unauthorized and every non-allow yields zero grant. Exact replay returns the byte-identical <=30 second receipt.

Federation peer Event publication. Each EventFederationSubmission carries the original signed Event. Ordinary online publication omits AuthorizationLease and uses an empty ingress_receipts array; explicit delayed/offline publication carries the lease and at least one original lease-bound IngressReceipt. An ak.member.state compensation publication additionally carries the unchanged transport-only membership_compensation_evidence and the receiver applies the same exact admission/join/action/executor/single-use evaluator as initial submission. Request-level CbaProofBundle values provide receiver-relative dependency closure. The receiver independently validates every Event, optional lease, receipt threshold, compensation evidence, bundle object and reducer result. Ordinary missing dependencies use HTTP 200 partial items with reason_code=dependency_missing and non-empty typed missing sets; registered atomic units use top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with EventsDependencyMissingProblem and zero writes. A received response terminates that Idempotency-Key; a post-backfill submit uses a fresh key. The caller MUST use service-to-service authentication with Source/Destination service DID and trust-domain headers. Federated ak.invite.claim remains decided by the destination Realm reducer. The request union additionally registers the discriminated direct_conversation_founding branch for the Direct Conversation founding exception of zh/sync/federation.md section 4.0.4: it carries exactly four ordered EventFederationSubmission items (Realm create, peer membership join, main Strand create, founder membership join), the source DirectConversationFoundingAcceptanceReceipt and bounded dependencies, and it omits service_binding_ref because the Realm does not yet exist at the receiver. The receiver freshly verifies transport source authority over founder_id, cutover/fence continuity when the receipt came from a pre-migration service, destination binding to the local participant, body closure, recomputed founding_unit_digest and coordinates, and the full direct_conversation_genesis admission before admitting the unit at one atomic boundary. The agent_membership_cascade branch preserves the origin-signed controller terminal Event and Agent transitions and applies the same exact controller pair/generation, pre-state exact-set, signer and atomicity rules as self submission. A missing dependency for either registered unit is a retryable top-level HTTP 409 dependency_missing with zero writes, never a per-item partial and never a permanent rejection.
Federation peer actor/data Event causal frontier probe. It never returns a Realm Seal frontier; use ak.peer.seals.read.frontier.v1.

Read-only federation dependency resolution for canonical-bytewise sorted exact Event IDs/digests in one Realm. It never attaches covering or first-activation Seals; Control-Move effectiveness uses the separate Seal frontier/resolve closure. Ordinary DataEvents are authorized by their signed existing seal_ref and never enter Seal.delta. Optional peer history_traversal_access accepts only a pending_archive_replica_digest and authorizes delta Control Moves in that exact target-to-base cut; request replicas never grant it.
Authenticated peer Realm Seal frontier discovery using the same RealmSealFrontierView as self.

Authenticated exact Seal-only resolve by canonical seal_refs; no Event envelope is returned. Optional peer history_traversal_access accepts only a pending_archive_replica_digest and authorizes Seal refs in its exact retained cut; request replicas never grant traversal.

Federation peer pull/backfill query. Uses the same selector, cursor, order, and response semantics as ak.self.events.read.scan.v1, but the HTTP trust surface is peer and the caller MUST be an authorized federation peer service.

Private Station to Station invite delivery. Requires service-to-service authentication, Destination-Service-ID equal to invite_address.recipient_id, a ak.invite.create event whose invitee equals invite_address.subject_id, and introduction_evidence accepted by the recipient invite_receive_policy.

Authenticated client dispatch of private invite evidence through the inviter Station. invite_event_id must resolve to an Event already accepted by this service and authored by the current session actor. The service reads its own stored canonical Event bytes; local delivery reuses the peer receive policy path and remote delivery builds the peer request from those bytes.

Atomic cross-Station KeyPackage claim. The destination Station is the sole CAS authority. The authenticated source Station first admits the participant request against its exact local account/device/generation durable state; revocation_pending fails before any remote call or inventory disclosure and is exposed only as the existing opaque claim_failed result. Request and response carry no PCR/control-history or signer-evidence sidecar. Every claim binds the matching accepted authorization Event id, whose in-envelope Station admission proof, the signed destination claim receipt, exact selectors and KeyPackage signature MUST all validate. Idempotency is scoped by (Source-Service-ID, claim_request_id) and the canonical request digest.

Read-only recovery of the destination authority's durable peer-claim ledger after an uncertain command outcome. It requires the same authenticated source service and exact request_digest and returns only opaque claim state plus the original signed success outcome when one exists.

Read-only service-authenticated retrieval of the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo and ratchet_tree extension bytes committed by one accepted ak.mls.genesis Event. The provider resolves the Event, verifies every echoed scope/group/epoch/ref/digest selector, hashes raw bytes against both explicit digests and content-addressed refs, and validates GroupInfo/tree consistency before returning an all-or-nothing response. It never returns private tree material, secrets, inferred leaf DTOs or proof-bundle leaves; consumers derive leaf_index only from occupied leaves in the verified RFC tree.

Account Authority transparently relays the exact client-signed PCR genesis unit after authenticating the service account and freezing the account/principal reservation. The outer service signature is transport authentication only. Principal admission independently validates the DID inception root, identity_creation_control_proof, the event-derived PCR id retype(create.event_id) which is never derived from the principal DID or subject and is never server-chosen, empty frontier, ordered root-signed create plus founding-device-signed authorize, single-direction payload digest binding, lease fence and expiry. Acceptance is atomic and create-once at the account dimension: two genesis attempts produce two different realm_id values, so implementations MUST NOT detect concurrency by id equality. Exact replay returns the original pcr_genesis_unit receipt and a conflicting unit performs zero writes.

Realm-scoped service-authenticated publication of exactly one target-signed ServiceResolutionRecord or ServiceRouteHandoverNotice. Idempotency-Key is required, is covered by the HTTP Message Signature, and MUST equal body.request_id. Transport replay is keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, request_id) and binds the complete canonical request digest: exact replay returns the original ack and a different digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (Source-Service-ID, realm_id, target service_id, artifact family/key/revision): the same artifact key with another digest conflicts with zero overwrite. The receiver validates source peer authority, target visibility, exact artifact_digest, target proof, did-to-core projection, sequential record/notice basis, time rules and hard bounds before writing its service-local mirror ledger. The receiver-signed ack cross-binds both keys, request_digest and accepted time; it proves durable receipt of exact bytes only and never makes a URL authoritative or declares a migration safe unless the deployment-required peer set has all acked.

Read-only Realm-scoped recovery of at most 32 continuous target-signed successor records and one active target-signed handover notice within a caller-selected response budget capped at 256 KiB.
