registry/outward-disclosure-policy-regis.description: Reusable outward-disclosure policies. Operations and carrier exposures reference a policy id instead of reproducing operation/profile matrices. Authorization decides whether a caller may reach a value; this registry decides which internal failures may cross the boundary and which observable response properties must remain equivalent.
registry_rules: Every referenced policy_id MUST exist exactly once. Missing policy references fail closed.
gate_order is normative and left-to-right. A target read, inventory lookup, relationship probe, or target-scoped limiter MUST NOT run before the policy's target_read gate.

An outward bucket fixes code, HTTP status, body shape class, target-sensitive headers and timing class together. Implementations MUST NOT merge only the code while leaking the internal reason through another observable property.
internal reasons remain available only to restricted audit. Ordinary logs and metric labels MUST use the outward bucket id.

An operation references the narrowest reusable policy. Per-profile rows are forbidden unless the profile genuinely changes the trust boundary; duplicating an identical policy by operation or profile is a lint failure.

body_shape_classes.standard_error_constant: The standard RFC 9457 Problem Details with no target-derived fields and one fixed size class.
body_shape_classes.standard_not_found_constant: The standard not_found RFC 9457 Problem Details with no selector-derived detail.
body_shape_classes.none: No failure envelope is defined by this policy.

header_classes.no_target_sensitive_headers: Retry-After and every other target-sensitive response header are absent; authentication challenge headers may depend only on the failed outer authentication gate.
header_classes.authentication_only: Only headers required by the failed transport or holder authentication mechanism may vary.
header_classes.not_applicable: No failure envelope is defined by this policy.

timing_classes.target_private_quantized: All merged target-private failures use the same deployment-declared quantized delay distribution, measured after outer authentication succeeds.
timing_classes.ordinary: No target-private timing equivalence beyond the ordinary operation budget.
timing_classes.not_applicable: No failure envelope is defined by this policy.

policies.diagnostic_rule: Detailed registered operation errors are allowed only after the authenticated holder/device is proven to own the exact material selector.

The two codes expose only whether exact portable material must be retrieved or whether supplied material is unsafe. They never reveal peer existence, Contact status, prefix length, failing edge or signature identity.

success_constraints: Return the exact verified mirror Event bytes only.
Do not return or satisfy seal_refs and return an empty derived seals list.
Authorization closes atomically when the Contact leaves pending_incoming.

registry/payload-validator-profile-regis.description: Executable validator profiles for Event payload contracts that cannot be expressed by a closed finite JSON Schema document family. Unlisted active Event kinds have no external payload validator and MUST be fully validated by their kind-bound payload schema.

registry/pcr-exposure-registry.json.description: Closed outward-exposure decision for every event kind admitted into a Principal Control Realm. ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds closes the write direction; this registry closes the read direction. A kind with an empty exposures[] is PCR-private and MUST NOT be reachable through any ak.open.* / ak.peer.* / cross-principal ak.self.* surface or public DID Document entry. A kind with exposures[] declares every path by which it legitimately leaves the Realm, each with its carrier form, exact schema location and gating authorization policy. Adding an outward path without registering it here is a release-gate failure, not an implementation detail.
registry_rules: The event_kind set MUST equal ak.profile.principal_control_realm.v1 realm_event_kind_policy.allowed_event_kinds exactly. A kind admitted for write with no exposure decision, and an exposure decision for a kind that cannot be written, both fail the gate.
exposures[] is a list, not a single value: one kind MAY leave the Realm through several independent paths, and each path carries its own authorization policy.
An empty exposures[] means PCR-private. The gate rejects a private kind whose literal kind string is reachable inside any outward carrier schema fragment registered here.

carrier declares what actually crosses the boundary: exact_event is the verbatim signed Event, derived_field is a projected value, receipt and seal are acceptance evidence over the Event, did_service_entry is a public DID Document service entry.
authorization_policy_id and anti_enumeration_policy_id MUST reference a policy registered below. public is an explicit policy value; a missing authorization_policy_id is never read as public.

Every exposure resolves exactly one reusable outward disclosure policy through outward_disclosure_policy_mapping, unless it carries an explicit outward_disclosure_policy_id override. The referenced policy is defined in outward-disclosure-policy-registry.json.

surface=operation requires an operation_id registered in operation-registry.json and a direction of request or response. surface=did_document carries no operation_id because a DID Document is published outside the operation registry.

carrier_kinds.exact_event: The verbatim signed Event Envelope, byte-preserved by the carrier.
carrier_kinds.derived_field: A value projected from the Event or from the cell it writes; not the Event itself.
carrier_kinds.receipt: Signed acceptance evidence naming the Event.
carrier_kinds.seal: An accepted Seal disclosed as coverage evidence for the named Event digest.
carrier_kinds.did_service_entry: A service entry in a publicly resolvable DID Document.

surface_kinds.operation: A registered service operation in operation-registry.json.
surface_kinds.did_document: A publicly resolvable DID Document, outside the operation registry.

authorization_policies.description: Current holder session bound to the exact target account authority pair. A recovery actor first completes the existing recovery transaction and becomes current holder; caller-declared intent is never authorization.
Caller and subject are both effective joined members of the request Collaboration Realm at evaluation time. That Realm MUST NOT be a Principal Control Realm.
A current authorization relationship between caller and subject: a shared Realm the caller is joined to, or a current call, session or Contact context.
Authenticated federation peer service with Source/Destination service DID and Content-Digest binding over the exact carrier bytes.
Authenticated Account Authority or Station service call carrying that operation's own authority evidence.
Authenticated exact target holder with a pending_incoming Contact row and a CAS-persisted verified mirror whose Event bytes and source receipt bind the requested ak.contact.requested Event.
Deliberately unauthenticated. Only a value the subject itself chose to publish may use this policy.

anti_enumeration_policies.description: Unknown subject, wrong authority pair and unauthorized caller share one not_found outcome.
Per-subject failure uses a single value, so absent, withheld and unauthorized are indistinguishable.
Uniform failure shape plus a registered per-caller rate limit on the subject selector.

registry/preimage-identity-exemption-reg.description: Closed named-exemption registry for zh/conformance/encoding.md 6.0.1. That section forbids any field inside the event_digest preimage from committing to an Event identity. Class A (the enclosing Event's own event_id/event_digest and their retype results) and class B (a not-yet-formed sibling of the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch) are unconditional: they have no fixed point and this registry MUST NOT carry a row for them. Only class C, a one-way forward declaration naming a later Event from another submission whose canonical bytes the author already froze locally, is registerable, and only with the compensating admission checks recorded here. Every active row MUST also appear in the 6.0.1 closed list table; the prose table and this registry are bound in both directions.

registry_rules.forbidden_direction_rationale: Class A and class B commitments make the digest preimage contain a function of the digest itself. No ordering of the unit can produce a value that survives the encoding.md 4.0 recompute-and-compare, so the shape is unconstructible rather than merely risky. Accepting such a row here would present an impossible construction as a ruling; the machine gate MUST fail instead.
registry_rules.candidate_field_scope: Schema properties named event_id, *_event_id, *_event_ref or *_event_digest, plus any property whose description declares that its value is derived from an Event identity (retype(...), event-derived and equivalent derivation wording).

omitted_fields: the realm_id member of the Event envelope scope_ref

exemptions.one_way_rationale: realm_id = retype(event_id) is a function of the digest whose preimage would otherwise contain it. The exemption is an omission, not a commitment: the three fields never enter the preimage, and every receiver derives realm_id forward from the accepted event_id exactly once.
admission_compensating_checks: the Event envelope realm_id MUST be absent and its scope_ref MUST be the realm_genesis form that carries no realm_id
the create payload object id MUST be absent
receiver MUST recompute event_id from the canonical bytes and derive realm_id = retype(event_id, "realm"); a carried or mismatching value is rejected with realm_id_not_event_derived

exemptions.one_way_rationale: The controller freezes the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope locally, computes its event_id, and only then authors the provision Event that declares realm_id = retype(event_id). The genesis preimage contains no provision identity, no provision reference and no provision digest, so the dependency runs in exactly one direction and both Events remain constructible.
admission_compensating_checks: the genesis ak.realm.create MUST be submitted separately from the provision Event; the same atomic unit or ordered submit batch is the forbidden class B shape and MUST be rejected

genesis admission MUST reverse-look-up an already accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype(this genesis event_id); no match means zero writes
the controller PCR carries a cas_register, bottom=reject cell keyed by payload.principal_control_realm_id, so two provision Events MUST NOT declare the same realm id
the managed Agent PCR and its controller PCR MUST be hosted by the same Station, because the reverse look-up is a local projection query
exemptions.absent_target_semantics: The declared Realm simply never comes into existence. The provision fact stays accepted and the operation stays at awaiting_pcr_genesis: no DID service entry, pairing handle or list/get visibility is published, and the Agent never reaches lifecycle active. The controller releases the slug and this realm id claim through the explicit agent provisioning abandonment operation pair; nothing expires the claim implicitly.

registry/profiles-dependency-graph.json.description: Generated DAG view of profile inheritance / dependency / mutual-exclusion edges. Derived from profile_requirements[<profile_id>].{inherits, depends_on, mutually_exclusive_with} in conformance-profiles.json. Consumed by zh/conformance/conformance-profiles.md §2.1 visualization tooling. Profiles whose only relationship is to be claimable on their own (no inherits / depends_on / mutually_exclusive_with) MAY be omitted from the edges[] list; they still appear in nodes[].

edge_kinds.inherits: A profile that inherits another transitively re-declares its operation_requirements / required_event_kinds / required_schemas / required_capability_actions. Inheritance edges are transitive and form a DAG (no cycles).
edge_kinds.depends_on: A profile that depends_on another MUST be claimed alongside that target profile; absence of the target MUST cause the claimant to be treated as unsupported.
edge_kinds.mutually_exclusive_with: Profiles linked by this edge MUST NOT be claimed together; reducer / discovery MUST reject the combination (typically with reason_code conflicting_*_profiles).

cycle_check.tooling_hint: Consumers of this artifact MUST topologically sort `edges[]` filtered by kind=='inherits' to verify cycle-freeness before using it as a profile inheritance resolver.

registry/proof-context-registry.json.description: Canonical security-domain labels for Arkret detached proofs and non-Event cryptographic transcripts. contexts remain schema-bound; domain_separations cover hash, signature, Merkle, HPKE-info and replay-cache-namespace separators and are not a general string registry. A replay_cache_namespace row separates replay-ledger partitions, never a signing transcript, and MUST NOT be carried by a wire or fixture field named proof_context.
registry_rules: context values and object_family values MUST be unique
Every Arkret non-Event schema that uses event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof MUST register an object-family context here

contexts[] closure is triggered by a terminal use point of the shared event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof leaf. A non-Event schema that declares its own local detached-proof or signature leaf instead of referencing the shared leaf is outside contexts[] by construction and MUST NOT be registered there

Such a locally anchored signing domain MUST instead appear in domain_separations[] with primitive detached_signature and binding_fields naming the transcript fields its proof covers, so that membership of this file is decidable from the schema alone rather than by convention
A verifier MUST reject a valid signature made under a context registered to a different object family
schema_ref MUST resolve to a real node: the file part MUST exist and the JSON Pointer fragment, when present, MUST resolve to a schema object

Every terminal use point of the shared detached-proof leaf (a schema node whose $ref chain terminates at event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof and that no other node references) MUST be covered by exactly one most-specific row here; a fragmentless schema_ref is exact only when the file root itself is the object family
A row whose schema_ref subtree contains shared-proof use points that all belong to deeper rows is over-broad and MUST be tightened to the inner $defs node it actually describes

One shared wire leaf MAY carry several consumer contexts. Every row anchored on a shared anchor MUST declare a distinct consumer_operation from operation-registry.json, and the anchored schema node MUST list exactly those contexts in x-arkret-proof-contexts
A schema node MAY project its single context as x-arkret-proof-context; when both the annotation and a registry row exist they MUST agree byte-for-byte

A shared-proof use point whose enclosing top-level $defs entry is reached by $ref from more than one other top-level $defs entry of the same file is a packed leaf. Unless every covering row declares its own consumer_operation, each object family MUST hold its own proof node and its own row; one row MUST NOT stand for several request/outcome families

domain_separations rows MUST have unique domain and object_family values, MUST NOT reuse a label or object_family already registered in contexts[], and MUST declare a primitive from the closed set canonical_json_sha256, merkle_leaf_sha256, merkle_node_sha256, merkle_root_sha256, detached_signature, http_message_signature, hpke_info, replay_cache_namespace

Every contexts[].context and domain_separations[].domain MUST match ak.<dot-separated snake_case symbol path>.v1. A dot separates naming levels, an underscore joins words inside one level, and a label MUST occur in exactly one array; the array and primitive, not delimiter spelling, determine its semantics. Legacy ak.<kebab-case>-proof-v1 spelling is invalid and is not an alias

A replay_cache_namespace row MUST declare defined_in, and the normative document it names MUST contain the domain literal. Every fixture field named replay_cache_namespace MUST carry a registered replay_cache_namespace domain, and every fixture field named proof_context MUST carry a registered proof context

contexts.defined_in: zh/crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md#14-全设备丢失恢复与设备重锚定

contexts.regime_rule: Exactly one event-level branch applies. With one valid station_admission proof, producer signer evidence fields are absent and admission.producer_signing_key verifies the bound producer proof. Without admission, both signer evidence fields are present, enter this transcript and resolve to the exact producer verification_method.

contexts.conditional_binding_rule: content.kind=manifest requires manifest_admission and forbids release_attestation; content.kind=chunk requires release_attestation and forbids manifest_admission. A ? field is included iff its closed branch requires it.

source_kind=member requires source_author_profile and source_authorization_incarnation; organization_recovery_holder forbids both and requires source_authority_locator.authority_observation to match source_actor_id, source_id, service_proof.verification_method, the exact archive authorization tuple and expires_at. A ? field is included iff its closed branch admits it.

domain_separations.conditional_binding_rule: kind=did_root MUST omit proof_body; kind in recovery_unlock|device_quorum|trusted_recovery_service|threshold_recovery MUST include the matching closed signature-independent proof_body projection

registry/protocol-layer-registry.json.description: Exhaustive ownership of every active Arkret v1 Event.kind by Kernel, Collaboration Base, or Extension. Each kind appears exactly once. Layer ownership constrains conformance packaging and dependency direction; it does not change the Event Envelope wire shape.

layer_rules.kernel: Security and convergence primitives only: identity proof, native realm/circle/sidecar security scope shapes plus the create-only realm_genesis exception, Realm/Circle lifecycle, CBA/authz/membership/policy, MLS/key delivery, audit commitments, invitations, and device/account security. Sidecar domain Event kinds remain Extension-owned.
layer_rules.collaboration_base: Official collaboration object package: Strand, Message/content interactions, Relation, View, and their direct reducer projections.
layer_rules.extension: Optional product, deployment, privacy-hardening, discovery, organization, automation, media, moderation, and specialized object families.

invariants: Every active Event.kind in event-kind-registry.json MUST appear in exactly one layer array.
Kernel MUST NOT depend on a Collaboration Base or Extension schema, reducer profile, operation, or fixture.
Collaboration Base MAY depend on Kernel and MUST NOT depend on an Extension.
An Extension MAY depend on Kernel and Collaboration Base and MUST declare its closure through an Extension Manifest.
A layer reassignment is a conformance-packaging change and requires updating dependent profiles, manifests, and vectors in the same change.

registry/redactable-field-registry.json.description: Canonical machine-readable projection of the redactable content-carrier slots listed in zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 4.2.4. One row registers one slot path on one object kind. An ak.schema.patch.v1 $op="unset" that addresses a registered path MUST be rejected with schema_violation reason=patch_unset_redactable_field; $op="set" on the same path is ordinary authoring and MUST be accepted, including when the new value carries an empty body. Realm-defined fields marked redactable: true are governed by the same rule and are declared by their own Realm schema, never by this registry.
registry_rules: A redactable content-carrier slot is a field that carries an object's authored body. Its absence on the materialized object is reserved for exactly two causes: the body was never authored, or it was cleared by redaction. message.schema.json already encodes that reservation (state=active requires exactly one of content / encrypted_content, state=redacted forbids both), so an ordinary ak.<kind>.update MUST NOT create a third cause and $op="unset" on a registered path is rejected.

The plaintext and encrypted forms of one slot are registered as two rows bound by paired_path, and the binding MUST be symmetric. Both rows carry the same decision, so whether a body can be removed never depends on whether the Realm is end-to-end encrypted.

This registry is not a capability boundary and MUST NOT be read as one. Redaction is whole-object, terminal, audit-sealed, and additionally invalidates history, search indexes, local caches and Blob access; no patch op can produce that effect, so no patch op can escape it. A $op="set" that overwrites a registered slot with an empty body is ordinary authoring, not an unaudited redaction.

Every row MUST declare a non_terminal_clear_op other than unset plus the terminal_clear_event_kinds that remove the slot entirely. Registering a slot therefore can never turn a field into a write-once field: there is always a documented way to empty it while the object stays active.

Fields that are not content-carrier slots MUST NOT be registered here. metadata, encrypted_metadata, metadata.title, metadata.summary and every path under metadata.fields are ordinary optional members whose non-terminal clear path is $op="unset", subject only to post-state object schema validation.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Set the slot to a ContentBlock whose body is empty, for example {"kind":"ak.content.text","body":""}. The slot stays present and the Message stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Message body, plaintext form. Exclusive with encrypted_content; required while state=active and forbidden once state=redacted.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Re-seal a ContentBlock whose body is empty and set the resulting EncryptedPayload on the slot. The slot stays present and the Message stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Message body, encrypted form. Exclusive with content; required while state=active and forbidden once state=redacted.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Set the slot to a ContentBlock whose body is empty, for example {"kind":"ak.content.text","body":""}. The slot stays present and the Strand stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Strand Description body, plaintext form. Exclusive with encrypted_content and independent of every track.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Re-seal a ContentBlock whose body is empty and set the resulting EncryptedPayload on the slot. The slot stays present and the Strand stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Strand Description body, encrypted form. Exclusive with content and independent of every track.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Set the slot to a ContentBlock whose body is empty, for example {"kind":"ak.content.text","body":""}. The slot stays present, the Strand stays state=active, and tracks.synthesis must remain active.
redactable_fields.description: Synthesis track body, plaintext form. Exclusive with tracks.synthesis.encrypted_content and writable only while the track is active.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Re-seal a ContentBlock whose body is empty and set the resulting EncryptedPayload on the slot. The slot stays present, the Strand stays state=active, and tracks.synthesis must remain active.
redactable_fields.description: Synthesis track body, encrypted form. Exclusive with tracks.synthesis.content and writable only while the track is active.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Set the slot to a ContentBlock whose body is empty, for example {"kind":"ak.content.text","body":""}. The slot stays present and the Morph stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Morph body, plaintext form. Exclusive with encrypted_content.

redactable_fields.non_terminal_clear_contract: Re-seal a ContentBlock whose body is empty and set the resulting EncryptedPayload on the slot. The slot stays present and the Morph stays state=active.
redactable_fields.description: Morph body, encrypted form. Exclusive with content.

registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.j.description: Canonical machine-readable projection of the reducer-managed-field protection defined in zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 4.2.5. It answers one question per object kind: which ak.schema.patch.v1 paths a generic update surface MUST reject because the value is owned by the reducer, by the create Event, by a dedicated event kind, or by a cell, rather than by the actor writing the patch. patch.schema.json is a generic document format and cannot express a per-object forbidden set, so before this registry existed every reducer, SDK and conformance runner had to hard-code its own copy of the list. Reducers, SDKs and conformance runners MUST read the set from here and MUST NOT re-derive it from prose.
registry_rules: The effective forbidden set of an object kind is universal_forbidden_patch_paths, restricted to the paths its object schema actually declares, minus that object's universal_exemptions, plus its own forbidden_patch_paths. A path and every dotted descendant of it are forbidden together: banning `effective_scope` also bans `effective_scope.circle_id`.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths is the general minimum set of zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 4.2.5 and MUST stay identical to the list that section spells out. Object-specific bans belong in the object's forbidden_patch_paths, never in the universal list.

A universal_exemptions entry is a documented normative carve-out, not a relaxation of the general rule, and MUST name the clause that assigns the path to the generic update surface. v1 has exactly one: a shared View reaches its durable terminal state through an ak.view.update patch setting state=tombstoned (zh/models/views.md section 3.1), so `state` is authored on View while `state_changed_at` stays reducer-derived.

Only object kinds whose update payload embeds event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/patch appear here. Message carries reducer-managed members too (`effective_scope`, `state_changed_at`), but it has no patch surface at all: ak.message.revise and ak.message.redact are dedicated payloads that are additionalProperties:false, so the ban is already decided by their schemas.

schema_enforced=true means the named update payload already rejects the path through its own propertyNames guard, so a conforming implementation gets schema_violation from artifact validation alone. schema_enforced=false means only the reducer can decide it. The flag is an assertion about the shipped schema, not a preference: it is verified in both directions, so a guard can neither register a path it does not forbid nor forbid a path it did not register.

This registry does not classify create payloads. A create payload names its object shape directly, so it expresses its own bans in schema (see event-payload.schema.json#/$defs/relation_create_object); only the generic patch surface needs an external table.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.owner: The create Event's own event_id, retyped (zh/models/common-fields.md section 6.0). A payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.
universal_forbidden_patch_paths.description: Object identity is derived, never authored.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.owner: Fixed by the create Event; a patch MUST NOT retype an object in place.
universal_forbidden_patch_paths.description: Validation schema id of the materialized object.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.owner: Fixed by the create Event. No canonical object rebinds to another Realm.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.description: Most recent update authorship. Allowing a patch to write it would let an actor attribute an update to somebody else.
Most recent update timestamp. Allowing a patch to write it would let an actor forge update ordering, contradicting the anti-forgery intent behind state_changed_at.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.owner: The ak.<kind>.archive / ak.<kind>.restore / ak.<kind>.tombstone lifecycle events of zh/models/common-fields.md section 5.1.
universal_forbidden_patch_paths.description: Physical lifecycle axis. View is the one registered exemption; see its universal_exemptions row.

universal_forbidden_patch_paths.owner: max(Event.created_at, min(covering accepted Seal.sealed_at)) as defined in zh/models/common-fields.md section 3.
universal_forbidden_patch_paths.description: Timestamp of the most recent state transition. Reducer-derived on every object that carries it, including View.

forbidden_patch_paths.description: Read-only current principal did projection derived from the PCR identity resolution cell. The cell is the sole write authority, and the projection is not an authorization root.
Circle content encryption profile is create-locked: a Circle never migrates between plaintext isolation and its own MLS group in place.
Reference to the independent MLS group bound to (realm_id, circle_id). Populated by the ak.circle.create reducer and never actor-supplied on wire.
Morph kind is fixed at creation; retyping a Morph in place would invalidate its facet and schema_refs contract.
The Morph field-validation contract is fixed at creation.
Business progress axis, single-sourced by the stage event so that same-value self-transitions and stage_changed_at stay derivable.
Reducer overwrites it with the triggering stage event's created_at and ignores any wire value.

forbidden_patch_paths.owner: Materialization of the verified Event.scope_ref after the receiver checks it against scope_circle_id and endpoint pre-state (zh/models/circle.md sections 6.1-6.2).
forbidden_patch_paths.description: Relation is the only patch-surface object whose schema declares effective_scope, so the generic patch surface is the only place an actor could still supply it. The materialized value is immutable across any later scope rebind.
Business progress axis, single-sourced by the stage event so that same-value self-transitions and stage_changed_at stay derivable.
Reducer overwrites it with the triggering stage event's created_at and ignores any wire value.

universal_exemptions.justification: zh/models/views.md section 3.1: a shared View has no separate tombstone event kind. Its protocol-level removal is an ak.view.update patch setting state=tombstoned, so state is authored on this one object kind. state_changed_at remains reducer-derived and stays forbidden, and tombstoned is terminal: any later update or reconcile MUST fail with view_already_terminal.

registry/reducer-profile-registry.json.description: Canonical Realm reducer profiles. A Realm selects exactly one profile through its reducer-profile singleton control cell.
registry_rules: profile_id MUST use the ak.reducer.*.vN namespace and is immutable once stable.
A receiver selects the profile from the Event's authenticated CBA governance basis. Ordinary Events and federation service bindings do not declare a reducer profile.
ak.realm.create supplies the genesis profile. ak.realm.upgrade is interpreted by the source profile and writes the target profile to the same singleton control cell.
An upgrade is valid only when the source profile declares the target in upgrade_edges and the declared deterministic state transition succeeds.
The current v1 registry has no active upgrade edge. ak.realm.upgrade therefore fails with failed_precondition unless and until a successor profile and a source-to-target edge are published.
A successor profile MUST NOT be published before an inbound upgrade edge and the edge's complete positive and negative conformance-vector bindings are published in the same release.

Every active profile requires conformance vectors for admission, cell projection, lattice join, state root, security frontier, and genesis. Every published upgrade edge additionally requires the complete upgrade-behavior vector bindings defined by upgrade_release_gate.

profiles.description: Arkret v1 Realm consensus semantics for every active durable reducer-input Event.

registry/registry-manifest.json.value_set_evolution_note: Per zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1: entries carrying value_set_evolution='open' are open registry sets (adding a value is a backward-compatible minor; codegen SHOULD use non-exhaustive Unknown(String) fallback). value_set_evolution='schema_selector' registries are algorithm-agility token sources whose canonical-object selectors are frozen per schema version (codegen MUST generate per-schema-version closed types; adding an active value requires a schema version bump). Registries WITHOUT this field are simply not classified here (they may be structural sources such as the contract registry or manifest, or value sets not yet classified); consumers MUST consult §6.1 and the registry's own registry_rules rather than assuming a registry is or is not a codegen value-set source from the mere absence of this field.

registry_rules: relation.schema.json relation_kind stays a free string so extension profiles can introduce new kinds; kinds listed here are the v1 standard vocabulary and MUST follow their registered row.

A relation_kind not present here and not declared by an extension profile is an unregistered kind: implementations SHOULD preserve it as an opaque edge marked unknown_relation_kind in projections and MUST NOT infer container, dependency, or visibility semantics from it (relation.md section 3.1).

Rows (or shapes) with truth_source_class=derived_projection MUST NOT be written via ak.relation.create / update / delete; the listed write_path Move or durable event is the only truth source and direct Relation writes MUST be rejected with schema_violation.

Every shape_dependent row MUST declare per-shape writability=derived_only or direct. SDK constructors MUST resolve the most-specific matching (canonical_id,from,to) shape before selecting an event path; wildcard fallback applies only when no specific shape matches.
weak_semantic=true rows are non-structural, non-cascading reference edges; they never imply containment, lifecycle coupling, or visibility changes.

Relations not declared multi-edge dedupe on the full tuple (realm_id, relation_kind, from_ref, to_ref); concurrent duplicate creation defaults to require_review, retains the complete bounded head set, and projects no active winner until an explicit resolution covers every current head.

shapes.cardinality: one_to_many; single active board parent per list

registry/request-material-supply-exempti.description: Closed named-exemption registry for zh/sync/service-http-binding.md 2.2.2. That section requires every gate-scoped required request input (evidence-shaped or CAS/echo-shaped leaves, and untyped required objects) to have a registered supply source, and every declared FSM state and allowed transition to have a registered write. Rows carry individually adjudicated exceptions in two kinds: request_input rows per operation and json-path prefix, fsm_transition rows per cell family with the waived states and transitions. Structural rules live in the machine gate, not here: this registry only carries individually adjudicated exceptions so that a blanket category can never be smuggled in as a row.

disposition_semantics.external_form: The field intentionally carries an external standard's own wire form (for example a did:webvh operation object). rationale MUST name the external standard and where its shape is defined. The row is permanent until the carrier design changes.
disposition_semantics.open_finding: A confirmed supply or reachability gap that is not fixed yet. review_anchor MUST point at a review/spec-open entry in arkret-work that still exists; when the finding closes the row MUST be deleted in the same change, otherwise the reverse check fails.
disposition_semantics.deferred_supply: The supply surface is adjudicated but its implementation is scheduled for a later wave. review_anchor MUST point at the adjudication record.

registry_rules.review_anchor_shape: Relative path from the arkret workspace root plus a heading substring that MUST appear verbatim in that file. Only consulted for open_finding and deferred_supply rows; the gate skips the file check when the workspace root is absent (spec repo checked out alone).

registry_rules: A schema row with omitted status defaults to active. New or edited rows MUST spell status explicitly.
The only allowed schema status is active. Unknown or any non-active status fails closed; the registry defines no historical compatibility rows.

consumer_binding, when present, is the machine-readable disposition for a logical schema that is not directly named by an operation, Event kind, or another schema. Runtime and dynamic wire bindings MUST declare kind, selector, and normative_ref. A prose_only binding MUST instead declare a non-empty rationale and MUST NOT be counted as wire coverage.

The effective schema reference of a row is the literal concatenation (file + optional fragment): fragment already includes its leading '#', so consumers MUST NOT insert another separator. For example file='schemas/agent-operations.schema.json' plus fragment='#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap' resolves to exactly 'schemas/agent-operations.schema.json#/$defs/agent_pairing_bootstrap'. Consumers MUST resolve that URI-fragment JSON Pointer and MUST NOT bind schema_id to the top-level document of file. When fragment is absent, the effective reference is the top-level document of file. Two schema_id rows mapping to the same file MUST be distinguished by fragment (or one MUST omit fragment to denote the whole document); a consumer that ignores fragment and loads the top-level document for a fragment-bearing row is non-conforming.

fragment, when present, MUST be a non-empty RFC 6901 JSON Pointer in URI-fragment representation starting with '#/'. If the pointer does not resolve within file, or a row that shares a file with another row omits fragment while that other row also omits fragment (ambiguous whole-document mapping), consumers MUST fail closed rather than silently pick a schema.

registry/service-kind-registry.json.description: Canonical service_kind vocabulary. A service_kind names an independent protocol identity or trust role that a remote party must distinguish. It never classifies Station-internal processes, operation bundles, features, limits, or transport bindings. This registry is the single source of valid values and per-context eligibility for Service Describe, Realm join candidates, ServiceRegistrationKey, and the MIMI provider directory. Consumers MUST derive their closed value space from active rows whose valid_in includes the applicable context.
registry_rules: A service_kind id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is lowercase snake_case. Only ids present as rows in this registry exist; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

Value spaces are NOT interchangeable. Each row declares valid_in, the set of contexts the id may legally appear in. A service_kind valid for Service Describe is not thereby valid as a Realm join-candidate class or as a ServiceRegistrationKey component. Consumers MUST derive their enum from the rows whose valid_in contains that consumer's context, never from the full row list.
Schema enum values for every service_kind selector field MUST be generated from active rows filtered by valid_in; tools/artifact_lint check_service_kind_registry asserts each declared JSON pointer.

service_registration_key is the most restrictive context: it admits only service types that are a standalone deployment owning a service DID under a canonical public base. Adding a row to this context means that service type can hold a service identity and appear in ak.root.identity.service_registration.* operations.

New service types enter only when a remote party must distinguish an independent service DID or signature, explicit delegation or allowlist, plaintext/key/recovery/compliance boundary, direct discovered base URL, or different normative authority/state result. Process separation, scaling, private RPC, internal hostnames, compute cost, or future deployment flexibility are insufficient.

service_kind is a role name, not a product, process, module, operation bundle, feature, or transport name. Deployment or implementation identifiers (for example a binary called soland or starid) MUST NOT be registered. A single physical deployment MAY fill more than one independent role, but each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role. Co-located roles sharing a public binding are selected with GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>; each response advertises only that role's exact supported_operation_bundles, profiles, authentication metadata, limits and plaintext visibility. Compound service_kind values are forbidden.
This registry governs service_kind selector fields, including the policy source_service_kind attribution field.

registry/signature-alg-registry.json.description: Canonical signature algorithm vocabulary and explicit per-standard mappings for v1 JOSE, Arkret raw signatures, and RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures.
registry_rules: A JWS protected header MUST use the standard JOSE member alg and its value MUST equal the active row's jose_algorithm. Arkret MUST NOT rename members inside a JOSE object.
An Arkret-owned raw-signature carrier MUST use signature_algorithm and its value MUST equal an active row's raw_signature_algorithm. It MUST NOT use the JOSE abbreviation alg as an Arkret field name.
An RFC 9421 Signature-Input alg parameter MUST use http_message_signature_algorithm. JOSE names such as ES256 are not HTTP Signature Algorithms registry names and MUST NOT be substituted.

Activating a reserved/new algorithm requires a new schema version and profile negotiation; registry activation MUST NOT expand an existing schema enum in place (zh/conformance/schema-registry.md §6.1 b.1).
Algorithms not present as active rows MUST fail closed with unsupported_signature_alg on critical proofs.

Every status=active row MUST declare kat_vector_id naming an active vector-registry entry; every status=reserved row MUST instead declare kat_absence_reason and MUST NOT declare kat_vector_id. tools/artifact_lint enforces this binding.

A reserved hybrid row is a single negotiated verification policy over two independent proof entries, not a new unregistered compact signature encoding. Both components MUST bind the same canonical payload and proof purpose; accepting a stripped single component as hybrid-verified is forbidden.

algorithms.security_note: Classical Ed25519 default signature suite; not post-quantum.
Classical ECDSA P-256 suite for WebAuthn/FIDO2 and PKI interop.

NIST FIPS 204 ML-DSA category 3 suite for post-quantum hardening profiles. JOSE/JWK serialization follows RFC 9964: alg=ML-DSA-65, kty=AKP, required pub, optional private seed in priv, and empty ML-DSA context.

algorithms.kat_absence_reason: Reserved hybrid policy has no canonical proof-set ordering or anti-stripping KAT until all activation_requirements are complete.
activation_requirements: Publish canonical proof-set ordering and duplicate-component rejection rules
Publish anti-stripping vectors proving that both components bind identical canonical payload bytes and proof purpose and that either missing/invalid component fails hybrid verification
Define verifier capability tiers and downgrade display semantics without ever reporting a single-component result as hybrid verified
Publish a new negotiated proof contract release; reserved policy MUST NOT widen frozen JOSE or raw-signature enums in place
algorithms.security_note: Reserved hybrid verification policy. Before activation, the canonical_id itself is not a wire alg and MUST fail closed if presented as one; active Ed25519 and ML-DSA-65 proofs retain their independent existing semantics.

registry/vector-registry.json.description: Canonical registry of conformance vector identifiers. Every ak.vector.* identifier referenced by prose or fixtures MUST appear here, and every row MUST point at the prose or fixture source that defines it.

vectors.description: Personal blocklist whole-value CAS updates, target closure, shared-history receive-before-filter behavior, unblock projection rebuild and non-enumerable holder-side filtering.

Account Data keys are server-versioned compare-and-set registers: a stale byte-identical retry after a newer write is rejected with cas_conflict, concurrent delete/update elects exactly one winner, opposite arrival orders reach the same final state, the revision high-water mark survives tombstone GC so deleted values cannot be resurrected, and value_tombstone key patterns refuse physical delete.

A human Contact petname is globally keyed by peer.principal_id through an opaque holder-private HMAC/JCS suffix; raw principal IDs, Realm IDs, pairwise actor IDs, and peer service IDs are forbidden key material, and decrypted slot swapping fails closed.

The two registered typed-id account-data namespaces are closed: ak.views.private.<view_id> and ak.notifications.inbox.<notification_id> accept only a full typed id tail, reject the bare namespace instead of falling through to the permissive unregistered-key branch, refuse plaintext content, bind the decrypted private View to visibility=private and its own view_id while the shared ak.view.* surfaces reject visibility=private, close the inbox value to dismissed/archived with an HLC-then-device_id merge, and delete physically without allowing revival.
Account Authority issuer-ledger genesis/CAS, signed record identity, exact replay/conflict, monotonic replica gap/fork handling and bounded Station fanout.

Actor Profile accountability admission is deterministic: every declared principal needs an active matching grant, any missing grant rejects the whole Event, and field-stripped acceptance is non-conformant.
Actor-chain sequence and sibling buckets are Realm-scoped; cross-Realm equal sequence values are independent, while same-Realm conflicting siblings fork and cross-Realm predecessor references fail.
Realm-scoped actor frontiers bind realm_id and actor_id, start at actor_seq 0, retain the complete sorted sibling head set, and hash the closed realm_actor transcript deterministically.

Byte-exact I2OSP(counter, AEAD.Nn) KAT for exporter content and Signal nonces. Non-zero high-order padding, counter rollback/reuse and increment after u64 exhaustion fail closed; no sender nonce prefix or random fallback exists.

Historical Agent signer evidence is materialized under the registered selector tuple: same tuple with the same receipt digest and canonical root is an exact replay checked before signing a new outer, a different receipt or root is duplicate_conflict with zero overwrite, a different receiver_id is a separate legal branch, an incomplete dependency closure or a permanently lost receipt stays unresolved, the historical outer attestation verifies long after attested_at with no verifier-now TTL, and the receiver method is resolved at receipt.accepted_at rather than from current state.

Controller-owned recovery_public_key backup of exporter history-secret ranges for a managed Agent PCR, exact public/plaintext identity-tuple binding, no pairing readiness gate, and prohibition on portable active MLS state, Agent runtime private-key backup or per-Agent human mnemonic.
Managed-agent DID-to-PCR binding, controller delegated authoring attribution, control-fact placement, and rejection of non-PCR Realms at either principal control id.

Native Agent effective membership is bound to the exact controller authority pair and join Event generation; self leave is one complete atomic cascade, while third-party terminal removal freezes a durable exact-set cleanup intent without delaying immediate authority loss or synthesizing Agent Events.

Native Agent MLS KeyPackages bind exclusively to the current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event and its runtime signing key, never to a controller delegated-device authorization; stale, mixed, cross-principal, revoked, superseded, expired, or key-mismatched bindings fail closed.

Managed Agent bootstrap is constructed in one acyclic order: controller-signed PCR-independent DID entry 0 -> exact initial_resolution -> frozen genesis create -> realm_id=retype(event_id) -> accepted provision -> accepted PCR -> controller-signed create-locked DID entry 1. Covers awaiting_pcr_genesis and awaiting_did_binding invisibility, exact durable commitment comparison, activation only after entry 1, and rejection of same-batch submission, undeclared genesis, duplicate claim, service-chosen realm id, cross-server split or wrong DID update key/tuple.

Provision requested_scope is a required immutable global ceiling rather than a grant; narrower key scopes and Realm grants are accepted, while action/resource/mandatory-constraint widening fails closed and provisioning emits no Realm grant.

The public managed-Agent DID history contains only the requested_scope commitment digest; complete scope disclosure is controller-signed, verifier/audience/challenge-bound, short-window private evidence, and public-copy, mismatch, stale, wrong-audience, and replay variants fail closed.
Stable runtime key binding digest, same-binding idempotent retry, different-binding HTTP 409 conflict, and stale approval fail-closed behavior.

Executes the portable Agent signer evidence transcript across exact-request current admission, destination-receipted historical verification, three orthogonal lifecycle gates, canonical witnesses, MLS cross-binding and tamper cases.

High-risk agent session scope returns claim_required with closed details {reason_code=human_approval_required, approval_request_id}; controller approval is out of band and CAPTCHA, OTP, password, and browser challenges are forbidden on the runtime path.
Request-key canonical body conflict, scope binding, canonical_hash_input and 24-hour retention semantics.

Applet-managed Bot/Ghost creation uses an exact hosted-principal ActorId, independently verified method evidence, immutable provision/PCR anchors, fixed atomic units, DID namespace matching, ordinary PCR rotation and a generic registration/grant/revoke write fence.

Deterministic Applet registration_epoch recomputation from the closed normalized transcript, UTF-8 domain separator, JCS bytes, and SHA-256; covers set sorting and duplicate rejection, optional omission, DID method version evidence, and security-field rotation.

Caller-signed Applet revoke plan binding, durable pre-effect ledger bound to principal service and admin actor, exact replay, conflict rejection, non-skip partial outcomes, restart recovery, and first-accepted-event write fencing.

Applet transaction push delivery authentication record: per-delivery RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature covering method/target/authority/content-digest/source-service-id/destination-service-id/idempotency-key, receiver-derived delivery_authentication_record and its domain-separated digest are persisted into the idempotency/replay record, duplicate body/record conflicts fail closed, and source service authentication does not replace Event actor/applet/capability checks.
Release requires an active binding, unexpired authorization, and accepted session head notice; suspended, revoked, expired, or wrong-stage inputs fail closed.
Audit binding is a closed control-plane FSM: active and suspended may transition as registered, revoked is terminal, and same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.
Same-basis close dominates release, earlier accepted releases must be frozen in close release_refs, post-close releases fail, and ordered_log ordering is deterministic.
Release recipient actor and public key must exactly match authorization and resolve to the same authorized audit actor; substitution fails closed.
Release is bounded by binding activation, first_auditable_epoch, encryption-time eligibility, sealed epoch state, and sealed_by_commit_ref.
Release material output is gated on accepted release plus a profile-valid RYW receipt, matching policy digest, and independent witnesses where attested hardware is claimed.
Audit session stages follow the registered request-authorize-notice-close FSM, permit explicit early close, reject skipped stages, and make close terminal.
field_access.sensitive_fields read projection handling: redact/hash/omit remove original values, hash uses keyed/salted digest discipline, and unenforceable handling falls back to omit.
Closed SessionGrant issuance preimage, typed ID/JWT jti derivation, holder/recovery binding, canonical public-JWK normalization, durable exact replay, conflict and terminal outcomes.
Authority lease issuance, ordered batch delivery, exact idempotent refresh, founding anchor basis, stale/quorum failure and cache-clearing boundaries.

Executable closed WebSocket discovery and frame bytes, application-context DPoP KAT and replay binding, account/events/signal multiplex isolation, duplicate/unknown/oversize negatives, reauth, drain, close-code traces and mandatory HTTP fallback.

Streaming AEAD declared-bounds negatives (declared fields only, no multi-MiB payload materialised): segment_count above 2^20, segment_bytes below 1 KiB or above 8 MiB, and segment_count inconsistent with ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) MUST all be rejected fail-closed (schema_violation, reason_code segment_bounds_invalid) before key derivation or any segment download.
Streaming AEAD ordering: out-of-order / skipped / gapped segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_sequence_invalid; a repeated segment_index MUST be rejected with segment_replay.

Streaming chunked AEAD (ak.blob.stream_aead.v1) happy path: Event and proof-hash group-state refs derive the exact winning epoch without a wire epoch; multi-segment plaintext with a short final segment is split, per-segment AEAD encrypted, incrementally verified, and the top-level ciphertext_digest is recomputed. Unresolved/non-winning refs and a different derived epoch fail closed.

Streaming AEAD scheme closure: an unknown attachment scheme MUST fail closed with unsupported_attachment_scheme (no fallback decrypt); an envelope carrying both whole-file nonce and chunked nonce_prefix/segment_* fields MUST fail blob.schema.json encrypted_attachment oneOf validation.

Streaming AEAD truncation: a dropped final segment, a last segment whose flag stays 0x00, or segment_count exhausted without last_segment_flag=0x01 MUST be rejected with segment_stream_truncated and buffered plaintext discarded.

calendar.attendees is the single canonical roster: actor ids are unique, the omitted role defaults to required, at most one organizer exists, and roster membership creates no Realm or Circle membership and widens no history access.

One schedule patch derives exactly one notification per receiver over the pre/post roster union filtered by post-state access, mute, DND and push rules; encrypted schedules only produce the profile-defined blind wakeup; RSVP changes derive no schedule notification.

Calendar Strands activate exactly one way: Strand.schema_refs carries ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 and metadata.fields.calendar co-occurs in both directions on the post-patch object, the container self-schema is refused in schema_refs, flat schedule fields and metadata.fields.profile/profile_refs impostors are refused, and writes bind the schema in requirements.schema[].

Nonexistent and ambiguous local times both resolve with the offset in effect before the transition, so a fixed local meeting time does not drift across a DST boundary and the overlap emits exactly one occurrence.

RFC 8984 subset defaults, base start as the first occurrence counted against count, implicit inheritance of base time and weekday components, count/until typing and exclusivity, by_* companion preconditions, and the paginated expansion with its candidate-period scan budget and revision-bound continuation.
Excluded recurrence rules, recurrence overrides, RDATE/EXDATE, per-instance reschedule or cancellation, and the JSCalendar @type discriminator all fail closed instead of being silently ignored.

RSVP admission is capability-based rather than attendee-based, refuses cancelled events, and layers basis checks so that e2ee and plaintext Realms accept the identical canonical set: shape admission rejects without resolving anything, target admission reads only the referenced Events plaintext envelope and pends on dependency_missing, and basis validity is projection-only. It also fails closed above the 128-entry frontier bound and keeps missing, invisible, cross-Realm and non-calendar targets externally indistinguishable.

RSVP derives a typed composite subject from payload event_ref, nullable occurrence, and the explicitly sourced envelope actor_id; causal successors dominate while concurrent mv_register heads remain exposed independently of HLC.

Instance heads override series fallback without unioning them into a false conflict, causal successors dominate independently of arrival order and HLC, missing keys project encrypted_unresolved instead of a fabricated status, and equal decrypted plaintext is not a conflict merely because ciphertexts differ.
RSVP occurrence key canonicalizes recurrence instance local wall-clock start in the event timezone.

The RSVP response branch follows the effective scope encryption floor: plaintext is refused under an e2ee floor, permitted only with the declared rsvp_response data class otherwise, never silently downgraded, and the routing-visible metadata set is disclosed explicitly.

ak.rsvp.set declares one deterministic reducer projection, set(payload.entry): an implementation that omits the registered write, projects an extra target, or derives a value different from the canonical payload entry fails conformance. Those writes are reducer-local output and never producer-selected Event fields.

Identity-affecting schedule edits orphan instance RSVPs and mark series RSVPs needs_reconfirmation, non-calendar updates are not schedule revisions, divergent concurrent heads block RSVP until a resolution Event, and byte-identical concurrent heads settle without picking a winner.

all_day selects the date branch and its negation the whole-second LocalDateTime branch for start, end and recurrence.until; intervals are half-open so end is strictly later than start; UTC timestamps, offsets, bracketed zones and fractional seconds are refused.

Producers canonicalize Link aliases to the canonical Zone before signing, receivers refuse non-canonical signed zones, a schedule-signed tzdb_version outside the executable set fails closed, and a release bump may move derived instants without changing the signed timezone or any local occurrence key.
Same-basis sibling transitions to different states return fsm bottom instead of selecting a winner.
Accepts the three legal first call states and rejects active or terminal first states.
Moderator kick/ban requires ak.call.moderate (call_moderation_unauthorised otherwise); the call moderation effective OR-Set gates token re-issue with call_participant_removed.

P2P calls converge to SFU when participants exceed two, reusing the oldest_membership no-vote session_focus election; mode does not auto-downgrade, and ak.call.summary is gated on a terminal call state (call_summary_invalid otherwise).

Recording ready results MUST carry ak.schema.call_recording_artifact.v1 metadata bound to the recording start event, Arkret blob pipeline, recording exporter label/context, retention policy, deletion audit trigger, and erasure receipt.

Recording retention: audit_lock blocks deletion (legal_hold_active) regardless of retention_expires_at, and ak.call.recording.start cannot enter a capturing state without an atomically persisted consent_confirmed result.
Same-basis replay of the same from/to transition is idempotent and does not create a divergent head.
Terminal call states reject every attempted outgoing transition with call_state_terminal.

Transcription requires ak.call.transcribe (transcription_denied otherwise), and transcript artifacts MUST use the ak.rtc-transcript-key/v1 exporter label with a dedicated Context (transcription_artifact_pipeline_bypassed otherwise).
Covers every legal call lifecycle transition and representative non-terminal illegal transitions.
Profile-declared non-event grant authority permits only exact Realm-admin-to-active-bridge-registration ak.applet.ghost.provision grants and rejects owner shortcuts or binding drift.

Capability materialization preserves exact issuer and concrete-subject ActorIds, derives maximum depth plus canonical sorted and deduplicated root identities, and requires each parent subject ActorId to equal the child issuer ActorId in full. Producer-supplied derived members and same-DID cross-Station replay are rejected; missing parents remain dependency-pending and independent reducers produce the same state-root input.

A multi-level authority chain built from one grant shape: each grant records the grant it was issued under in issuer_authority_refs, and revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.
Delegation cycle rejection across direct, multi-hop, revoke/redelegate and atomic batch variants.
A fixed authority expiry seal prevents rolling renewal and stops a re-granted authority from widening the window of the refs that cover it.

Grant-ref liveness follows upstream revocation without cascade writes; root refs survive controller transfer but fail after generation reset. Transfer authoring supplies only controller_id, reset supplies no patch, registered increment_members computes the respective successor counter from the CAS-frozen pre-state, and safe-integer overflow fails closed with zero write. Root-control terminal events reject ordinary grant-based authorization.

A grant without ordinary authority_control, including one carrying only applet_authority, cannot authorize a child. A false or default-false parent can issue only a wire-explicit ordinary max_authority_depth=0 terminal child; missing carrier, positive depth, regrant reopening, terminal-child reuse, and non-narrowing true-parent depth fail closed.
Reducer-only ak.capability.derived follows the unified issuer-authority rules while retaining Realm-link inheritance behavior and remaining unauthorable by principals.
Direct Conversation participant authority is a profile-scoped non-grant source, survives root generation changes, requires the pair's unique immutable binding, and cannot issue child grants.

Authority-surface coverage for ak.authority.direct_conversation_repair.v1, whose action_allowlist is exactly ak.member.rejoin.own. A self leave -> join ak.member.state under the repair source matches that action and reports it as the matched authority source; joining on behalf of the other participant, carrying a first join, admitting a third participant, presenting ak.member.leave.own under the repair source (daily self-leave belongs to the participant authority) and running rejoin.own backwards as join -> leave all fail closed. Behavioural rejoin vectors that never name the action or the authority source would stay green with an empty allowlist and therefore do not cover this.
Risk-tier freshness matrix fails closed and keeps unknown low-risk pending outcomes local.
Global cross-grant decision merge prevents any allow from bypassing deny, quarantine or review.
Issuer effective-authority and freshness-unknown fail-closed checks for first-issued grants.
Static depends_on_moderation_state requirement rejects missing or false declarations.

Subject-only relinquish needs no revoke grant, rejects non-subjects and root-cell targets, and both revoke and relinquish stay dependency-pending without prewriting tombstones when the target grant is unresolved.

The unified grant form preserves depth, expiry-seal, cycle and constraint inheritance, permits unbounded low/medium-risk multi-hop agent grants, and requires finite expiry for high-risk agent or service grants.
Effective grant validity-window intersection rejects empty windows.
External authority authority Ack issuance, canonical receipt-set assembly, common-window calculation, threshold deduplication, exact replay and decision-chain binding.
Control Proposal Ack deadlines, at most two immutable-horizon signed defers, decision-overdue evidence, and acceptance of a later cryptographically valid Seal.
Realm proposal decision windows are ordered and realizable: decision <= absolute, equality is accepted only with zero defers, and invalid configurations fail before any Realm state write.
cas_register writes on non-initial state require an explicit CBA basis: Control Move preconditions or equivalent DataEvent causal/lattice proof; null-basis blind overwrites fail closed.
bottom=reject control cell recovery accepts only a sealed conflict-recovery Move with valid recovery_capability and pre-conflict state_witness; negative cases pin recovery_witness_* reasons.
open_set concurrent revocation is evaluated against the joined control view; revoked or bottom authorization cells fail closed without a freshness window.
Seal canonical bytes exclude id and notary_signature; verifier recomputes the typed id and signature payload digest from signed top-level fields only.
directory_visibility=realm_members exposes only the Realm-member preview field set and gives non-Realm callers the same locked stub/timing bucket as members-only circles.

Circle lifecycle is evaluated at the Event CBA basis; linear archive uses the revocation freshness window, tombstone and concurrent archive fail closed immediately, and restore never rehabilitates a pre-archive basis.

Hard quota counters use one logical linearizable authority across every service node: a race for the last slot cannot overshoot, idempotent retries count once, unavailable authority fails closed, and calendar-month periods are rejected.

Temporal action gates are neutral for unrelated actions according to effect, while edit/redact windows use the verified target created_at and the fixed verification time/skew to accept inside the deadline and fail closed outside or on missing target time.

A mutually signed, root-anchored bilateral checkpoint compacts an arbitrary Contact prefix while retaining a maximum 64-round explicit tail; fork, rollback, missing predecessor, wrong root/pair/accumulator and single-signature inputs fail closed, while missing material remains distinguishable from invalid material without disclosing Contact state.

The ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 projection carries the closed next_prepare_input successor cursor: an accepted row MUST carry it and the five non-authorable contact_state values MUST NOT, its basis_id, version and predecessor_event_ref are copied verbatim into the scope_update and tombstone prepare phases, version is the next Event's version and predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head rather than that head's predecessor, and a stale cursor is refused with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale and MUST be re-read rather than guessed or retried unchanged.

The ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 projection carries the complete signed request_receipt on a pending_incoming row, so respond and reject become authorable: the field name is byte-identical to the prepare field that consumes it, it is copied verbatim and never narrowed to a reference, and because it is signed by the peer's source service rather than by the holder's own server the client verifies it independently instead of trusting its server's retelling. pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired and tombstoned rows MUST NOT carry it, a glare pair is structurally never pending_incoming so respond and reject stay forbidden without a new code, and a consumed receipt is refused by prepare with zero writes and MUST be re-read rather than cached or replayed. The client obtains the exact request Event itself only through the closed Contact mirror branch of ak.self.events.read.resolve.v1: it reads exclusively from a Contact verified mirror whose receipt was cryptographically verified at ingest and CAS-stored, it opens only while the row is pending_incoming, it returns the complete payload including the original message because the stub rule constrains delivery surfaces rather than the exact target holder, and it discloses no covering Seal at all, so seal_refs is never satisfied through it. When the row leaves pending_incoming the receipt is cleared and the visibility closes in the same transaction, and the selector is accounted into missing rather than unauthorized.

KeyPackage upload, entry upload, minimal consume command, consume service receipt, and revoke signatures use byte-exact domain-separated typed JCS transcripts. Consume authority and all owner/KeyPackage/Welcome/service coordinates have one carrier in recipient_durable_receipt; wrapper mirrors and legacy selectors fail closed.

Universal durable accepted-to-Seal revocation state: mandatory Ack and exact reducer-derived authority/device/generation binding, closed five-action pending gate, origin-PS session issuance fence, exact signed-reject release, multiple proposal isolation, overdue alerts, terminal reject/Seal races, restart reconstruction and non-retroactive historical admission.

accepted_device pairing signs a closed target-owned possession attestation under ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1 whose only replay boundary is the pairing challenge transcript digest: the approving device and the Account Authority each rebuild it independently, it is the sole authority for hpke_key and algorithms, short-link and to-device share one schema and one domain, transcripts never cross between root_anchored and accepted_device, and the target device fails closed before local assembly when the accepted Event does not match its attestation or the expected principal_id.

document_digest is sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(normalized DID Document projection))): any raw JSON property reordering keeps the digest identical, changing any controller / verification relationship / service / security-relevant extension property necessarily changes it, and raw response bytes are never carried in document_digest (they use raw_document_digest).

evidence_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical evidence receipt (ak.did.binding_evidence.v1): a proofless method degrades to an empty method_proofs array rather than a placeholder, webvh witness rows are sorted by witness_did with duplicates rejected, any method evidence change changes the digest, and unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

policy_digest is recomputable from the retained canonical resolver policy snapshot (ak.did.resolver_policy.v1): required core dimensions (accepted_did_methods, fail_mode, trust_roots) plus the profile-closed profile_policy, registered wire tokens only (language-native debug renderings rejected), and flipping any security-relevant field necessarily changes the digest while unknown profiles or fields fail closed.

Byte-exact KAT for the receiver-derived off-wire Direct Conversation binding digest: fixed v1 domain separator, closed normalized binding object, unordered participant and authorization-ref normalization, created_at and Event-context exclusion, and semantic-field mutation separation.

A lost Direct Conversation founder never transfers the existing pair slot: ordinary recovery of the exact same (principal_id, station_id) resumes as the original founder, while timeout, root Contact recovery policy, third-party attestation and after-the-fact bilateral designation all write nothing. The non-founder remains awaiting_founder, the closed wire union has no founder_unrecoverable state, and only a genuinely different stable participant pair derives a new pair_key with no inherited history, MLS state, keys, audit identity or authority.

One accepted founding unit per (founder_id, trust_domain_id, pair_key) slot across same-Station, dual-Station and founder multi-device concurrency: first valid unit wins, the loser gets direct_conversation_slot_already_committed with zero writes, exact replay returns the byte-identical receipt without advancing accepted_at, the same idempotency key with a different unit is duplicate_conflict, every crash point converges to the same coordinates, and the federation branch reports a missing bounded dependency as a top-level retryable dependency_missing rather than a partial.

The creation_required resolver outcome carries next_founding_input with member names identical to the founding unit submission, exactly one founding_authority_evidence branch, no Event bytes or coordinates, temporarily_unavailable when the material cannot be assembled, and submission-side re-verification that never trusts the echoed copy.

Caller-authored first-valid founding unit: byte-exact founding_unit_digest KAT over the four ordered Event IDs, realm_id and main_strand_id retyped from the first and third Event IDs, explicit founder membership with head_eq null, closed self and peer carrier branch shapes, and rejection of server-allocated identifiers, reserved or materializing drafts, coordinator election, reordering, a fifth Event and a carried coordinate field.

Canonical direct-conversation pair_key KAT over exact ActorIds sorted by RFC 8785 JCS bytes and the Realm trust domain, including order-independence and bare-principal/unresolved-pairwise-DID rejection rules.
Direct Conversation Realm profile/discriminator bidirectional schema guard, MLS and closed-join shape, exact-two membership, no-Space policy and main-Strand invariants.

The Direct Conversation resolver reports only server-verifiable send blockers. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are absent from the closed wire enum because holder blocklist state is encrypted to holder devices and history key installation is device-private, so a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation; they are carried instead by the closed client-local blocker set, which never appears on any wire surface and never turns the resolver state into suspended. presence_offline and keypackage_empty remain server-verifiable but are returned only to an existing exact-pair participant, and a non-participant probe gets the same opaque failure as a nonexistent pair.

Leave, block, either directional Contact terminal and participant terminal gates suspend the immutable conversation; Consent is not consulted. Recovery reuses the same Realm, main Strand and unique MLS group with an ordinary Commit and never automatically redelivers old epoch secrets. Total private-state loss makes the old Realm terminal.

Minimal encrypted-envelope wire digest over RFC 8785 JCS {version,content_type,encryption_context} followed by decoded ciphertext bytes. Scope, Event kind, group id, scheme and sender domain are reconstructed inputs and never duplicated in the envelope.
Canonical JSON object key ordering follows UTF-16 code units for supplementary-plane keys.

Closed uri cell-subject encoding: every octet outside ALPHA / DIGIT / - . _ ~ becomes upper-case %HH, including : / and % itself, so an escaped separator and a real path separator address different cells; non-canonical mimi_room_uri spellings are rejected before any subject is derived.
Canonical confusable-check test set and callable SDK utility behavior.
ECDSA P-256 (ES256, RFC 6979 deterministic) detached JWS golden vector over the canonical proof binding object, mirroring the ed25519 vector structure for the optional interop signature suite.

BLAKE3 KAT over fixed UTF-8 bytes plus wrong-prefix, wrong-length, Realm-suite mismatch, and unknown-suite downgrade rejection cases.

Canonical OR-Set dot (ak:event:<event_id>:<write_index>, write_index taken from the registry cell_writes[]) and the or_set_batch_add tag digest encoding, with negative cases for a bare event_id tag and for deriving the third segment from a wire array index.

Hand-written deterministic CBOR bounds: a definite-length array declaring/carrying 65537 items (generator-described, built by the runner) exceeds the v1 cap of 65536 items per array/map and MUST be rejected (reason_code cbor_bounds_invalid) without preallocating from the declared count.

Canonical structure depth cap: a JSON object nested 65 levels deep (generator-described, built by the runner; top-level container = depth 1) exceeds the v1 maximum nesting depth of 64 (objects and arrays combined) and MUST be rejected (reason_code structure_depth_exceeded) with bounded recursion; a depth-64 control input MUST be accepted.

Requires every active reducer-input kind to have a complete machine-readable cell contract and pins exact multi-target atomicity, missing/extra reducer-projection rejection, and data/control plane-cross-write rejection.

ak.realm.alias is the only wire carrier of a Realm alias: declaration / tombstone shapes, the create-time bootstrap follow-up and post-bootstrap seal_basis shapes, head_eq rename, issuer-authority binding, namespace occupancy, disjointness from the handle namespace, cas_register bottom on concurrent distinct declarations, and rejection of alias on the closed Realm object or in a PCR.

Realm Event canonical acceptance atomically freezes the complete distinct member-service target set and durable intents; route miss is pending_route rather than submission failure, authority is rechecked before every send, lost authority terminally cancels the exact old intent, restart never loses an obligation, and authorized reads preserve topology visibility.

Every accepted or byte-identical duplicate Native Agent Event in a peer submission returns exactly one receiver-signed admission receipt written in the same acceptance transaction, rejected, quarantined and dependency-missing items return none, exact duplicates replay the first stored bytes, and the source durable outbox only completes the handoff after the receipt set matches the producer-evidence-pair Events one to one and the materialization obligation is committed atomically.

The standard peer dependency resolve operation is a bounded read-only Event/CBA fetch surface with canonical sorted exact typed selectors, complete selector accounting, indistinguishable missing and undisclosable results, atomic limit_exceeded on response-budget overflow, bounded verifiable supersets, strict progress, an eight-round automatic-fetch ceiling, and a fresh-key submit after closure completion.

Each Event selects its Realm reducer from the authenticated CBA governance basis; ordinary Events and federation service bindings carry no reducer identity, unsupported settled profiles fail with unsupported_profile, and an unregistered upgrade target fails closed.

Ordinary dependency gaps are per-item HTTP 200 partial outcomes with non-empty typed missing sets while registered founding units remain zero-write atomic HTTP 409 dependency_missing outcomes; every received response terminates the prior Idempotency-Key and only a no-response byte-identical transport retry reuses it.

Federation push carries one Realm's bounded, receiver-verifiable CbaProofBundle superset rooted at DataEvent seal_ref and Control Event seal_basis leaves on the sole peer Event write rail; receivers reject unreachable bundle objects, resolve Control Events and basis Seals topologically before DataEvents, and never grant same-batch unsealed authority or advance actor frontiers from proof transport.
