Crash-safe automatic requester/source convergence for exporter all-history: durable single-flight create, empty-page non-ack polling, exact outbox retry, later-material follow-up manifests, closed terminal diagnostics, since-join/current-authorization negative cases, and the closed send/relay rejection disposition that splits exact retry from permanently_rejected manifest replacement and request-terminal stop.
Closed private request, manifest-first continuous-range chunk, relay, honest release-service attestation, exact duplicate, list/ack/expiry and quota matrix.

Closed split between the bounded near-current stateless group-security frontier and receipt-bound bulk direct Seal traversal. Covers caller-pinned bootstrap/current bases, target dominance, complete predecessor cut replay, registered dependency resolution, current monotone history access, join floor and RRK singleton traversal; no stateless epoch-range or package/page profile remains.

Executable service-behavior vector for organization-recovery durability: deterministic HPKE archive bytes, typed transition/container provenance, first durable replica receipt, exact duplicate replay, barrier/list reread, atomic coverage-ledger states and GC-before/after decisions are all frozen without defining private storage rows.

Realm create precedes holder-accepted recovery-key register; direct replay must derive the key-evidence Control Move as reducer-effective before any opted-in exporter Genesis. The reducer cell and archive tuple contain the key tuple, provenance EventId and holder-pinned basis; no service-selected effectiveness locator exists. Rotation is exact CAS and historical tuples remain verifiable from the retained archive-lifetime Seal/Event/dependency cut.

Ordinary, Native Agent and minimal sender domains bind history-secret KDF, derived nonce, reconstructed AAD, HPKE chunk context and replay rejection. Received bytes globally deduplicate by (scope,group,epoch,candidate_digest). CandidateOriginAttribution separates stable response-sender/RRK-holder-key/backup-series-producer origin_quota_domain from retrieval-only origin_ref, with immutable 30-day TTL and 4-per-candidate/64-per-quota-domain/256-total caps. Two-tier eviction uses immutable material_received_sequence then candidate_digest, including success-bound material as the second tier.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_p256_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(P-256, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM, profile-gated interop suite): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_aes256gcm.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / AES-256-GCM): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

RFC 9180 base-mode byte-level KAT for ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1 (DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256) / HKDF-SHA256 / ChaCha20-Poly1305): DeriveKeyPair, encap, key-schedule intermediates, seq-0/1 ciphertexts and export values MUST reproduce byte-for-byte.

Accountability scope string/singleton-array and array permutations converge through a domain-separated canonical string-set digest before outer composite subject derivation; exact-set revocation remains isolated per cell.
UTS #39 skeleton collision state is scoped to one registration authority and one namespace and never defines canonical equality or wire bytes.

did:webvh witness policy is read only from parameters.witness = {threshold, witnesses:[{id}]} with unique did:key ids, and proofs only from the separate did-witness.json keyed by versionId. Malformed, aliased (witnesses / witness_threshold / witnessThreshold), Arkret-overlay-polluted, unavailable, under-threshold, stale or same-controlling-organization evidence all fail closed with a registered code; none of them may degrade to threshold 0. Deployment policy raises but never lowers the method threshold. The fixture includes a field-exact official signed vector that requires entry-hash recomputation plus controller and witness proof verification. Arkret carries observations in ak.schema.did_webvh_witness_receipt.v1, a family distinct from the registry-consensus ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1, returned as a schema-discriminated tagged union that never substitutes for verifying the standard proofs.

Before the first DID registry / method-native publication request the Account Authority MUST, in one atomic step, validate the live identity-creation lease, matching fence, holder, reservation and challenge, and freeze principal_id, did and the complete canonical DID operation bytes with their digest; holder-originated commands without a matching live lease/fence fail closed with zero writes before any registry I/O, and after the freeze any first submission, retry, crash recovery, response-loss reconciliation or fence takeover only queries or exact-replays the frozen operation, so a registry spy observes at most one canonical DID operation per reservation and a single stable accepted_at.
RFC 8265 human-identifier preparation, canonical-receiver rejection, Unicode localparts and Agent slugs, UTS #46 A-label conversion, and dual code-point/octet limits.

Registering an external Organization DID separates resolution, control verification, local registration, Realm relationship and service delegation; being resolvable or referenceable yields no local administrative authority. prepare/ensure is two-phase by decision: the registry issues and remembers a single-use challenge bound to purpose, audience, origin, trust domain, nonce, local_admin_subject and a window of at most 300 seconds, and the control proof binds that beneficiary to block redirection. Challenge consumption atomically records the canonical request digest and outcome, so only a byte-identical retry is idempotent; the same challenge under a different digest fails closed. proof_kind is a closed two-member discriminator over mature DIDs, witness attestation is never a governance quorum, requested scopes MUST match the challenge, and quorum proofs MUST meet the declared threshold. registration_generation reconciles idempotency with terminal revocation: replacement atomically terminates the old current generation and advances a monotonic current pointer, so an old receipt cannot authorize after supersession. Status is the closed triple active/stale/revoked with rotation mapping to stale and DID deactivation forcing revoked, and revoked is terminal against refresh.

Root-committed FoundingDeviceDescriptor, device possession, one-way authorize payload digest binding, ordered atomic create-once PCR genesis unit, extended identity creation transcript, exact replay and mutation rejection.

Every PCR outward carrier has an exact registered operation/direction/schema/pointer/policy reverse edge; private kinds have none, and shared-Realm Actor Profile resolution merges unknown, unauthorized and wrong-selector failures.

Registry-parameterized producer UUIDv7 identity suite. Every producer_signature ID kind executes authorized first reservation, exact replay, same-authority conflicting binding quarantine, cross-authority same-UUID separation, and bare lookup or unauthorized allocation rejection.

Explicit abandonment of a provisional identity whose PCR was never accepted is a two-step account handoff challenge plus confirmation: a confirmation without a challenge or reusing the challenge-issuing handoff is rejected with zero writes, a PCR accepted between issuance and confirmation fails with the stable identity_creation_already_accepted terminal and abandons nothing, the successful path commits challenge consumption, orphan-anchor tombstone, checkpoint suppression and lease release in one transaction, the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint is afterwards unreadable on every holder-readable surface, and replaying the same request_id returns the same terminal outcome with exactly one tombstone.
The unauthenticated principal-resolution response contains only a service-attested current projection and method-history evidence; every PCR id, Event, receipt, Seal and history field is forbidden.

Threshold-recovery publication-signing-key closure, canonical recovery-policy EventInitialSubmission shape, PCR allowlist/reducer admission, acceptance-basis materialization and fail-closed retry semantics.
Byte-exact did_root plus four generic recovery factor transcripts, closed proof_body projections, public session tuple binding and mandatory cross-factor replay rejection.

Identity-creation saga crash/resume, lease fencing, single-use challenge terminal-state separation, exact replay, client echo validation, signed account binding and post-registration did:webvh history verification.

Lifetime AccountId uniqueness including deactivation tombstones and cross-Station replacement, signed exact Event ActorId, route-derived origin-only admission, exact producer-proof binding and replica preservation.

Minimal-metadata author verification binds Event.actor_id and proof.verification_method to exactly one active MLS basic credential / LeafNode signature_key at the envelope epoch, rejects rollback/removal/duplicate/key-mismatch cases, and forbids principal-scoped keys/query fallback. The same vector pins the IdentityLink proof preimage that binds the independent Ed25519 history response-signing method, key, and key digest so signer evidence cannot self-select a proof key.

Realm reducer authority for ak.invite.claim: binding_proof and subject_proof signature transcripts, token_commitment match, verification_id allowlist re-check, claim_nonce replay rejection, pending -> claimed membership-proposal conversion, and expiry cleanup are enforced before acceptance.

Failure-indistinguishability vector covering both the third-party claim endpoint and the invite-locator resolve endpoint; each endpoint's failure classes MUST share one external response shape and bounded timing distribution.

Active-series tail deletion accepts exactly the three high-risk authority proof branches (principal_signing / device_quorum / trusted_recovery_service) over the canonical delete-intent transcript bound to a server-issued single-use challenge: ordinary current-device proof on an active tail, non-tail single deletion, deduplicated quorum below policy k, expired or consumed recovery session, replayed or expired challenge, and any tampered transcript field (backup_id / reason / audience / nonce) MUST all be rejected; a byte-identical retry returns the stored terminal outcome without re-admitting the consumed challenge.

New passphrase_kdf backup envelopes below the unconditional base KDF floor (Argon2id memory_kib>=65536 / iterations>=3 / parallelism>=1; PBKDF2 iterations>=600000 with allowed digest_algorithm) MUST be rejected.
Key backup retrieval requires a session-bound unlock proof (ak.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1); any binding mismatch or bearer-token-only access fails closed before ciphertext is returned.

The signed LeafNode keypackage_capabilities list exactly matches the outer KeyPackage record; the required_keypackage_capabilities GroupContext extension is enforced on Add, Update, floor changes, Join and application-profile selection, while RFC 9420 required_capabilities requires every member to support the Arkret extension codepoints.

Last-resort KeyPackage Realm affinity, optionality, and profile gating: cross-intended_realm_id reuse MUST be rejected with last_resort_realm_affinity_violation; a server not declaring the feature MUST fail closed on an empty pool and MUST NOT return a last_resort package, with explicit last-resort fallback returning last_resort_not_supported; high_security_organization and sovereign_deployment Realms MUST treat last-resort as forbidden even when the service supports the feature.

Last-resort KeyPackage (ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1): when the normal pool is empty, claim MAY return last_resort=true; the package is reused across multiple Welcomes within the same intended_realm_id, consume is idempotent (stays published, never keypackage_already_consumed), and each consumption emits an append-only audit record per encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

Last-resort KeyPackage forced rotation: on next online the holder MUST publish fresh init key material, transition the old package to revoked with revocation_reason=keypackage_rotated, and trigger an MLS self-update Commit on every group joined via it to advance the epoch and close the forward-secrecy weakening window.

Realm-local minimal-metadata pairwise endpoint completes publish, exact claim, Welcome, recipient durable receipt and singular consume without an Account, Device, Native Agent or transport-session identity carrier; every stage binds the exact did:key method, current joined Realm delivery authority and intended Realm, and all mixed branches fail closed.

Cross-Station KeyPackage claim linearization and uncertain-outcome recovery: claim CAS, request ledger and serialized result commit atomically; same source/id/digest replays byte-identically; another digest conflicts without a second claim; query recovers the original outcome.

Peer KeyPackage claim requires both a participant signature bound to the exact request/service destination and the source-service HTTP Message Signature. Destination authority, both directional Contact heads/scopes, capability, freshness and Direct Conversation no-last-resort gates fail closed behind one claim_failed surface without inventory leakage; Consent is not queried.

Self and peer KeyPackage claim share one closed device|native_agent|minimal_metadata_pairwise requester authorization bound to exact claim fields and stable source/destination service DIDs. The source service admits current durable requester authority before local CAS or durable remote relay; uncertain remote outcomes are queried by the original claim id and request digest before any exact resend. The destination-authority ledger atomically binds request digest, KeyPackage CAS and signed receipt; exact retry never claims twice and conflicting reuse fails before inventory lookup.

cas_register join is the pure maximal-chain function over set ops carrying from: a sequential governance lifecycle (declaration -> whole-value head_eq tombstone -> re-declaration) joins to the single terminal value instead of bottom; two ops with the same from and different values form two maximal chains and join to bottom; a non-initial op whose from matches no covered value is a dangling supersession and fails closed to bottom; duplicate (value, from) sets are idempotent; supersession binds by value, so ABA reuse is the documented value-CAS semantic and families needing generational distinction embed a monotonic component in the value.
counter join/validate_op convergence for the same CBA Event set.
fsm join: identical (from,to) sibling transitions converge idempotently; same-from different-to siblings return bottom (reject path).

Provider delivery state, provider message ids and raw push tokens never appear in the response.
Byte-level reaction routing HMAC KAT covering RFC 9420 exporter derivation, NFC normalization, combining code points, emoji modifiers, and cross-label/Realm/epoch negatives.

Multi-device read cursor merge is causal-first: a causally dominating position wins even when its HLC is lower, HLC max decides only causally concurrent positions, device_id breaks equal HLCs, and an undecidable causal closure stays provisional.

Realm create atomically materializes five registered cell writes including the singleton ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell whose controller is created_by at epoch 0 and generation 0; missing roots, author-supplied root values, unrecomputable registry digests, non-root founding-grant shapes, and staged/accepted root proofs used outside their basis all fail closed without leaving a partial Realm or membership.

Realm Link FSM: all declared initial states and transitions are accepted, tombstoned is terminal except byte-equivalent replay, undeclared transitions reject with realm_link_invalid_transition, same-basis divergent siblings return bottom, general graph cycles remain valid, and self-reference rejects with realm_link_self_reference.

An event-targeted ak.redaction (target_ref in ak:event: form) only trims that Event's fields per preserve[] and MUST NOT change any object's state, including the event-derived object minted from a targeted create Event; object state=redacted is driven only by the object typed-id spelling of target_ref. The two spellings of one 33-octet token are both schema-valid and land in two distinct ak.component.object.redaction.v1 cells (verbatim scalar subject, encoding.md 9.5.1); the cells are independent OR-Sets and neither spelling canonicalizes into the other.

Message reaches state=redacted only through the object-scoped ak.message.redact. The cross-object ak.redaction payload class excludes Message mechanically: message_id is not a member and target_ref removes the ak:message: branch, so both spellings fail schema validation before any cell write, while a non-Message object target and the ak.message.redact positive both validate.

Strand state=redacted forbids both its Description pair (content / encrypted_content) and tracks.synthesis content pair; Morph forbids its content pair. An object carrying any applicable slot alongside state=redacted MUST fail its schema, the redact post-state with all slots absent MUST validate, and state=archived MUST keep the slots legal.

Relation is the only patch-surface object whose schema declares effective_scope, so it is the only place an actor could still supply the reducer-materialized value. Both surfaces MUST be decided by schema and MUST produce zero projection writes: an ak.relation.create carrying payload.relation.effective_scope, and an ak.relation.update whose patch addresses effective_scope or any effective_scope.* descendant, both fail with schema_violation reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed.

Typed Seal submit admission covers genesis completeness, current device generation, recomputed roots, predecessor notary authority and non-terminal future-clock deferral.
Blind-index stale postings after revocation, visibility tightening, redaction, expiry, or epoch rotation MUST not produce unauthorized recall.
Search hit is not an authorization proof; unauthorized or unverifiable hits return non-enumerating stubs.
Directory search, privacy-preserving search, and bridge interop surfaces stay separated and do not leak private plaintext.

FLOW-GAP-015 closure for target-signed planned endpoint handover and Realm-scoped mirror recovery within one unchanged service DID: exact current basis and time ordering, cancellation continuity, no notice-authorized business traffic, same-core formal successor validation, durable publish acknowledgement and replay conflict, bounded visibility-blinded resolve, fork quarantine, durable anti-rollback floor with replaceable TTL cache, and bilateral cross-ack cutover. A change of the ActorId-projected service DID is an identity change and is outside this route-handover flow.

Production current-v1 SessionGrant presentation has one wire scheme: Authorization: DPoP plus the matching DPoP proof. Authorization: Bearer carrying ak.session.grant is rejected even when another proof header is present; a DPoP proof outside its replay window is rejected.
A DPoP/RFC 9421 grant-binding session key must not reuse bytes, fingerprints, thumbprints, or key identifiers from the long-term device identity key; reuse fails closed.

DPoP htu binds scheme, authority, and path: cross-authority/scheme reuse, untrusted forwarding headers, and missing authority are rejected; only a configured trusted proxy with scrubbed headers may reconstruct the external URI.

Sender-constrained session PoP: a write request with a valid RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signature (kid = current grant session_public_key, covering @method/@target-uri/@authority/content-digest) is accepted; a signature whose transcript mismatches the method/path/body digest fails verification and is rejected per api-conventions.md section 3.2 and service-http-binding.md section 2.5.

Human returning-device issue and human refresh require a current accepted-device possession proof bound to the exact intent and verified in the same current-authorization linearization; non-current device states produce zero grants.
Runtime producer and controller consumer bind exchange identity only to the accepted request Event id and reject message, local-intent and unaccepted identities.
Same-sequence request and control siblings choose the bytewise maximum canonical accepted Event envelope digest, never Event id, HLC, arrival or database order.
Controller-only complete pagination and structural Event pairing recover private Sidecar context locators without adding a disclosure endpoint.

Explicit response closed loop with runtime addressed/self eligibility and restart dedupe gates, coordinator completion policy, causal request refs, controller validation, fail-closed non-echo handling, and controller-authored durable close control.

Containment: plaintext or shared-scope occurrences of exchange binding/control schema ids or exchange_id are hard rejects/invalid; publish output, Account Data, and public/shared surfaces carry no exchange material.

Event-fold and local-cache recovery: rebuild from accepted private history, causal folded-frontier validation, no Account Data merge, controller control ordering/sibling resolution, terminal absorption, reassignment, action-by-response-set mapping, and projection schema state invariants.
Only explicit controller confirmation creates one allowlisted ordinary shared Event, with zero private identifiers, history or locators.
Chrome and Edge execute the hosted multi-track, multi-mode, multi-device, multi-Agent and responsive UI matrix with preserved state and incremental switching evidence.
Every shared list, expansion, activity, export, URL, log and telemetry surface discloses no Sidecar locator, identity, content or fold input.
Accepted Agent revoke, pause or deactivate immediately stops new delivery, execution and writes without implicitly terminating exchanges.
Incomparable device histories require complete backfill and union refold with maximal causal heads and a digest over all contributing Event ids.

Signal verification uses two independent state domains: seal_ref selects only the Realm/scope authorization basis, while device authorization resolves against each verifier's current accepted device directory. A device authorized after seal_ref but currently active passes the device check; a device active at seal_ref but currently revoked/fenced/conflicted is rejected; a verification_method whose full value is not byte-identical to sender_actor_id#sender_device_id is rejected; a missing current directory key or missing Tier-2/service-attested trust anchor is rejected; a currently active device whose sender lacks scope send eligibility or the signal_class action under the Realm seal_ref is rejected.

Byte-level ak.history-v1 -> ak.signal-v1 ExpandWithLabel KAT for per-sender-device SignalEnvelope AEAD keys, including JCS({sender_device_id}), distinct valid-device keys under a forced equal nonce, and label/context/device/epoch negative mutations.
Encrypted Message preview keyframe/delta/abort state machine, identity derivation, attempt fork handling, resource limits, and direct final binding.

Signal payload_sequence is a durable per-device/per-canonical-scope u64 high-water: forward gaps from reservation/crash/failure are accepted, repeat or rollback is stale, exact envelope replay is diagnosed separately, and scopes remain independent.

High-assurance snapshot inclusion-challenge sampling verifies sufficient event_id and actor_seq_range coverage, recomputes the RFC 6962 domain-separated event-set Merkle root (0x00 leaf / 0x01 node), rejects the unprefixed root, rejects commitment-root mismatch, and rejects silent actor sequence gaps.

Snapshot witness attestations are a typed object family signed under ak.snapshot_witness_attestation_proof.v1 over the signature-free canonical projection: missing attestations under authority_kind=witness_quorum, a duplicate signer, an unauthorized or revoked witness, a deduplicated count below the policy threshold, the manifest context reused as the witness context, a mutated projection, and a rewritten or reordered witness list MUST all be rejected, while a valid quorum is accepted and the top-level issuer signature binds the final sorted witness set.
Canonical filter/query-scope cursor binding and cross-scope replay rejection.
Opaque delivery ack token, monotonic cumulative acknowledgement, binding rejection and lost escalation.

Client events.query backfill with include_completeness=true detects withheld actor branches via ak.attestation.range_completeness verification; feature-less servers ignore the parameter; single_source attestation does not satisfy high-assurance realms.
Deterministic limited-timeline window-start state basis with safe omission on unresolved bases.

Account and events NDJSON stream trace conformance: catchup completion ordering, cursor-bearing frame closure, dropped-versus-resync branching, and reconnect position advancement are evaluated over complete traces rather than isolated frame schemas.

DeviceMessageEnvelope requires a sender-assigned device_message_id; unacknowledged byte-identical redelivery executes durable handler effects once, conflicting reuse fails with duplicate_conflict/device_message_id_conflict, and distinct ids remain distinct logical messages.

Shared View removal is an ak.view.update patch setting state=tombstoned, so that patch MUST be accepted; state_changed_at is reducer-derived and an actor-supplied value MUST be rejected by view.schema.json.

reports/event-reference-field-inventory..description: Complete schema-property inventory for Event ID/ref/digest fields. EventId is itself the complete suite-tagged cryptographic identity; no companion-digest wrapper or truncated identity class exists. External protocol event identifiers are classified separately and never enter the Arkret EventId value space.

reports/operation-schema-index.json.description: Generated DTO index for registered operations with request_schema_ref/response_schema_ref. JSON Schema files remain the canonical source; this report is a machine-readable summary for SDK/conformance tooling and prose drift review.

reports/operation-string-field-classific.description: Exhaustive classification of operation DTO schema/status/reason_code/reason properties into closed literals/enums, validated open protocol tokens, or bounded human-readable text. Any unconstrained audited string fails generation.

reports/property-presence-manifest.json.description: Per-property wire presence contract derived from the schema documents. required, nullable and default are independent axes; presence_class is their normative combination. An SDK MUST reproduce the class exactly: a tristate property needs an explicit SDK disposition: the protocol-wide default normalizes absent/null, conditional requiredness is enforced by the Draft runtime, and only x-arkret-presence-semantics=distinct requires Missing / Null / Value. Repeated conditional schema occurrences are also grouped into semantic audit targets by shape and instance path so SDK audits do not count the same DTO field multiple times.

presence_class_definitions.required: must be present and never null.
presence_class_definitions.required_nullable: must be present and may be null; absent and null are different wire facts.
presence_class_definitions.tristate: optional, nullable, no default; absent, explicit null and a value are three accepted wire spellings whose semantics require a disposition.
presence_class_definitions.optional_defaulted: optional with a schema default; omission means the default.

sdk_disposition_definitions.distinct: business semantics distinguish Missing / Null / Value; SDK must preserve all three.
sdk_disposition_definitions.condition_guarded: missing is invalid in an applicable conditional branch and is enforced before typed decoding.
sdk_disposition_definitions.absent_null_equivalent: v1 default normalization; SDK uses an optional value and canonical output omits None.

reports/schema-consumer-coverage.json.description: Per-logical-schema consumer coverage. A schema that only compiles has no proven wire consumer; this report separates operation request/response binding, admitted Event contracts, structural $ref use and conformance vector coverage so an unused schema cannot hide behind a startup compile.

consumer_definitions.inbound: bound as an operation request body, or an admitted Event envelope/payload contract.
consumer_definitions.outbound: bound as an operation response body.
consumer_definitions.schema_reference: referenced by another schema document, so it is a structural component; local self-reference is not a consumer.
consumer_definitions.event_kind: bound by the Event kind registry, so a durable Event selects it by kind.
consumer_definitions.declared_wire: explicit machine-readable runtime, dynamic, nested-value or alias binding declared by the canonical schema registry.
consumer_definitions.prose_only: explicitly declared as having no whole-object v1 wire admission surface.
consumer_definitions.vectors: required by a conformance profile or vector group, or referenced by a fixture.
consumer_definitions.prose: named by the normative text, which is where a runtime-dispatched contract is defined.
consumer_definitions.startup_compile: a schema registry row, compiled by the startup catalog gate.

binding_kind_definitions.exact: the reference targets this logical schema itself.
binding_kind_definitions.fragment: the reference targets a $defs fragment of the same document.
binding_kind_definitions.registered: the schema ID appears in the Event kind registry.
binding_kind_definitions.required_schema: listed in a conformance profile or vector group required_schemas.
binding_kind_definitions.fixture: the schema ID appears in a conformance fixture.
binding_kind_definitions.normative_text: the schema ID appears in the normative prose.
binding_kind_definitions.declared: the canonical schema registry carries an explicit disposition.

vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.direct: named by a conformance profile/vector group or fixture.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.operation_e2e_owned: the logical schema is an operation catalog/DTO whose instance cases belong to the listed request/response E2E owners.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.composed_schema_owned: the schema is only admitted inside the listed higher-level logical schemas.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.event_envelope_owned: the payload is selected by Event kind and is covered only inside signed Event admission.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.runtime_dispatch_owned: the schema is selected by an explicit dynamic/runtime binding in the canonical schema registry.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.no_v1_wire_instance: the canonical registry explicitly declares that v1 has no whole-object wire instance.
vector_coverage_disposition_definitions.unresolved: no direct vector or reviewed higher-level coverage owner has been identified; this is a release blocker.

schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.title: Arkret Account Data Encrypted Value
schemas/account-data-encrypted-value.sch.description: Principal-private Account Data value sealed client-side. Services validate and store this envelope but never receive the account secret or plaintext.

schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Data Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/account-data-operations.schema.j.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface actor-private account_data operations (ak.self.account_data.*). PUT builds a ak.account_data.set actor-private write; the server stores content verbatim (clients own canonical encoding and, for sensitive keys, client-side encryption). Every key is a server-versioned compare-and-set whole-value register: writes carry expected_revision and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1, so concurrent multi-device writes converge instead of silently overwriting each other. See spec/v1/zh/models/account-data.md §5. account_data_key keys are dot-delimited namespaces validated against account-data-key-registry.json.

account_data_key.description: Dot-delimited account_data namespace key (e.g. ak.contacts.realm.<realm_id>, ak.account.blocklist). Control chars / whitespace / path separators are forbidden so the key is URL- and log-safe.

revision.description: Monotonic per-key revision counter. 0 means the key has never been written. Each accepted write or delete stores expected_revision + 1. The counter is a high-water mark: it MUST NOT go backwards, not even after a tombstone is garbage-collected, so a stale offline write can never resurrect a superseded value.
Revision of this stored value. Pass it back as expected_revision to replace or delete the entry.

content.description: Caller-supplied opaque payload, stored verbatim. Any JSON value.

account_data_replace_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. The actor-private cell subject is composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key], so the subject *is* the owner: the Event MUST be signed by the holder and the service MUST NOT author it under its own DID. key, expected_revision, and body / encrypted_payload live exclusively in set_event.event.payload and MUST NOT appear at the request top level. A tombstone payload is rejected here: erasure goes through ak.self.account_data.resource.delete.v1, which enforces the registered deletion_mode.

account_data_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed tombstone ak.account_data.set Event and nothing else. Same subject rule as the replace body: composite[envelope.actor_id, payload.key] makes the holder the only legal signer. expected_revision is the payload's, not a query parameter -- one CAS precondition, one place. deletion_mode=value_tombstone keys MUST still be refused on this endpoint.

revision.description: Revision of the stored tombstone (expected_revision + 1). Recreating the key requires this value as the next expected_revision.

account_data_cas_conflict_details.description: Closed error.details payload for cas_conflict and not_found on ak.self.account_data.resource.*. It always carries the current revision so the caller can decrypt, re-apply its domain merge rule and issue exactly one new compare-and-set write without a second round trip.

current_entry.description: Present only when the key currently holds a live value. Omitted when the key is unset or holds a tombstone; current_revision is still authoritative in that case.

schemas/account-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Operation DTOs
schemas/account-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account self-service operations and Account Authority issuer-ledger account-status publication and resolution.

account_subject.description: Deployment-local, non-reversible authentication subject: SHA-256 over utf8('ak.account-subject.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of the issuer identity and issuer-local authentication row key. It is confined to the private Account Authority boundary, is always issuer-scoped, and is never an AccountId or resource-owner selector.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 SHA-256 JWK thumbprint of the holder key, encoded base64url without padding.

status.description: Lifecycle projection only, matching device-lifecycle.md section 14.1. revocation_pending is reducer-derived from durable accepted ak.device.revoke proposal state; trust/evidence quality is reported separately in verification_state.

verification_state.description: Trust verification of the device authorization evidence, separate from lifecycle status. A consumer MUST NOT interpret lifecycle status=active as usable authority unless verification_state=verified.

revocation_states.description: All gate-relevant durable revoke records for the exact device/generation, sorted by (acceptance_seq, proposal_digest). At most 128 distinct unresolved proposals may be admitted; exact replay consumes no slot, signed_reject removes one pending slot, and an already revoked generation accepts no new proposal. Sealing one record makes lifecycle status revoked but MUST NOT hide other surviving pending records.

handle_claim_ref.description: Opaque reference to a signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 claim, such as an event ref, issuer-local receipt ref, or content-addressed artifact ref.

audience_id.description: Stable target-service authorization identity. A service DID used for signature verification is supplied separately and MUST project to this did_core_id.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

account_registration_control_proof.description: Closed control proof for binding an already-published did to principal_id through account register. OIDC, passkey, or agent authentication alone is insufficient to establish DID control. The Account Authority resolves did at high freshness, requires project(did)=principal_id, and selects the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id from verified method history rather than from request-supplied key material. The signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.account_registration_control_proof.v1 and MUST replay the durable challenge issued by ak.gate.account.command.issue_did_binding_challenge.v1.

request_canonical_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete account_register_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

account_subject.description: Service account subject this identity is being bound to. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed to bind the same identity to a different account.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id echoed by the challenge and equal to project(did).

did.description: Complete DID resolved by the Account Authority and signed by the holder; it MUST equal the register request did byte-for-byte.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined versionId of the entry whose current active update key signed this proof.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the verified current active update key.

dpop_jkt.description: DPoP holder thumbprint echoed by the durable challenge.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

verification_method.description: Current active update-key DID URL under did. The verifier parses its bare DID component with the registered adapter and requires the projected did_core_id to equal principal_id; it never appends a fragment to principal_id.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest for the external DID, required by deployments that do not host the DID themselves.

account_handoff_authentication_proof.description: OIDC authorization-code exchange proof used only to create a DPoP-bound account handoff. The signature is made by the same Ed25519 holder key as the request DPoP proof over utf8('ak.account_handoff_authentication_proof.v1\n') || RFC8785_JCS(this object with signature omitted).

challenge.description: Account Authority-generated challenge persisted with the OIDC authorization transaction and consumed by this exchange.

request_canonical_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete account_handoff_request_body with proof.request_canonical_digest and proof.signature omitted.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 signature encoded base64url without padding.

reserved_identity_creation.description: Server-persisted identity-creation checkpoint, readable only by the authenticated current holder of the owning service account's identity-creation lease. It is NOT public: an unfinished reservation would otherwise leak that a specific account is mid-registration, and abandoning it would leave a permanent public trace. Once registration completes the public artifact is the published DID log entry itself, so this checkpoint never needs to become public. It contains the exact unpublished or already-published DID operation, never recovery words, seed material, private keys, or an encrypted root export.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete did_operation object.

state.description: Account-Authority-authored durable identity-creation saga state. Clients MUST derive their onboarding phase from this value and MUST NOT infer a phase from local checkpoint presence. reserved_identity MUST be absent only in active and present in every later state.

expires_at.description: Lease expiry. Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 15 minutes; 15 minutes is also the v1 default.

reserved_identity.description: Holder-authenticated identity-creation checkpoint carried while a reservation exists. It MUST be omitted once the provisional identity has been explicitly abandoned through ak.gate.account.command.abandon_identity_creation.v1: after abandonment the checkpoint MUST NOT remain readable on this or any other holder-readable surface, because leaving it would keep publishing that some account once tried to create an identity. That is a security property, not a cleanup policy.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the conflicting live identity-creation lease. The client uses this authenticated upper bound for waiting UI; it conveys no holder identity or authority.

account_handle.description: Canonical handle of the authenticated service account. This unsigned UX hint is only for display and local artifact naming; it MUST NOT be treated as principal identity evidence, authorization, or a service-account-to-principal binding.

account_subject.description: Stable subject for the authenticated service account. The client freezes this value from the DPoP-bound handoff and MUST require the identity-binding challenge to echo it byte-for-byte before signing.

preferred_locale.description: Optional private UI-language preference of the authenticated service account. It is returned only in this DPoP-bound handoff response so the client can continue the just-completed authentication flow in the selected language; it MUST NOT be copied into a public actor profile.

account_handoff_grant.description: Opaque, short-lived credential bound to the request DPoP key. It is not ak.session.grant and has no refresh-token semantics.

allowed_operations.description: Closed set of operations this handoff may be presented at. The two abandonment operations are members because a never-accepted PCR leaves the holder without a principal, so no principal-bound ak.session.grant can carry them; membership here does not widen the handoff into a session credential.

fresh_authentication_required.description: Authoritative Account Authority decision. true means the current handoff is the challenge-issuing handoff and confirmation requires a new authentication; clients MUST NOT infer this by comparing locally persisted credentials.

did.description: Complete standard DID whose registered method adapter MUST project to the principal_id derived from did_operation.

identity_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into identity_creation_control_proof, adds proof_kind and verification_key_multibase, and signs that complete proof object with signature omitted. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the root-control transcript.

operation_digest.description: sha256:<lowercase-hex> of SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the complete request did_operation object.

did_version_id.description: Validated did:webvh inception versionId copied into the root-control transcript.

log_head_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the exact method-native inception log entry.

control_key_digest.description: SHA-256 over the canonical multikey bytes of the current active update key (parameters.updateKeys[0]) of the DID entry pinned by did_version_id; never private key material or a next-key commitment. For account-first inception that entry is entry 0; for an already-published DID it is the entry current at binding time, so a spent inception key is never required.

pcr_genesis_unit_kinds.description: Closed ordered declaration copied into the identity-root creation transcript.

identity_creation_control_proof.description: Fresh proof signed by the did:webvh inception operation's parameters.updateKeys[0] identity root. The verifier selects that key from did_operation and MUST NOT treat a request-supplied key or a DID Document verificationMethod as authority. Signature covers every field except signature as canonical JSON with domain separator ak.identity_creation_control_proof.v1.

pcr_realm_id.description: Principal Control Realm id obtained only by retyping the exact root-signed ak.realm.create event_id; it is not derived from principal_id and MUST equal the pcr_genesis_unit create Event's retyped id.

realm_create_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the ak.realm.create payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

founding_authorize_payload_digest.description: Canonical digest of the founding ak.device.authorize payload only. Event ids and envelope digests are forbidden from this transcript.

initial_session_request_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS InitialSessionGrantRequest. The embedded session_public_key MUST thumbprint to dpop_jkt; this binds the first Standard grant intent without turning it into a separate root-signed object.

signature.description: 64-byte Ed25519 identity-root signature encoded base64url without padding.

registration_did_evidence_draft.description: Dedicated registration-time control proof and frozen method evidence. It is distinct from identity_creation_control_proof and MUST bind the exact did_operation pins.

binding_kind.description: Discriminates the already-published DID proof branch from account-first identity creation.

did.description: Verified DID whose registered adapter projects to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: Adapter-defined version identifier pinned when the account binding was accepted.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the verified current control key that authorized this binding.

identity_creation_lease_id.description: Present only when binding_kind=identity_creation. The published_did branch creates no identity-creation lease.

head_event_digest.description: DID registry log head digest for the exact did:webvh inception entry accepted during this binding saga; it is not a PCR Event head.

proof.description: Account Authority detached proof. payload_digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete receipt with proof omitted, including binding_kind, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, operation/head digests, and the identity-creation lease/fence only when that branch applies. JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.account_binding_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, account_authority_id, account_subject, principal_id, did, did_version_id, control_key_digest, verification_method, created_at}); proof.created_at MUST equal issued_at and verification_method MUST be an assertion method of account_authority_id valid at issued_at.

propertyNames.description: ak.self.account.command.update_profile.v1 only accepts display_name, avatar_blob_ref, and profile_fields.<key>. The bio is carried as profile_fields.bio.

account_materialized_profile.description: Materialized Actor Profile returned on the account surface. id is the actor_profile ID derived by retyping the accepted ak.profile.create Event ID; realm_id is the exact Principal Control Realm that carries the profile Event lineage.

profile.description: Present only when the authenticated principal has exactly one unambiguous accepted Actor Profile across its account-local-lineage PCR lineages. Because this request has no authority selector, multiple accepted lineages MUST fail closed by omitting profile; the service MUST NOT choose an implicit current PCR.

is_server_admin.description: True when the authenticated principal is a deployment server administrator (the server's configured admin principal set). Operator-only product surfaces (e.g. organization creation) gate their UI on this. Reducer/config-derived, not a stored account field; absent or false means non-admin.

account_register_request_body.description: Canonical account binding request. Exactly one branch is required: proof binds an already-published did, while identity_creation carries the account-first DID operation and PCR genesis unit. In either branch every repeated principal_id and did in the selected proof/creation objects and genesis initial_resolution MUST equal the outer values byte-for-byte, and the Account Authority MUST independently require project(did)=principal_id before any write.

did.description: Required for both externally created and account-first identities. The server verifies the method evidence and project(did)=principal_id before persisting the PCR resolution state.

preconditions.description: This account self-service surface forbids Event preconditions. ak.profile.update concurrency is expressed only by the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest.

account_profile_event_submission.description: Holder-signed Actor Profile Control Move. (event.actor_id, event.station_id) MUST equal the authenticated session's exact account authority pair, and event.realm_id MUST select that pair's local unique PCR lineage. Accepted-profile presence is evaluated only within that lineage. With no accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.create and its materialized actor_profile ID is derived by retyping event.event_id; the create payload MUST NOT carry id. With an accepted profile there the exact Event MUST be ak.profile.update and payload.target_ref MUST equal that accepted create-derived ID. On create payload.object.principal_id MUST equal event.actor_id; on update the accepted target profile's materialized principal_id MUST equal it. Holder direct proof is required without executed_by, authorization_ref or Applet provenance. Event preconditions MUST be empty; update concurrency uses only the optional signed payload.expected_state_digest. The service submits the exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign, choose an ID or add a concurrency guard. A valid Control Move not yet covered by an accepted Seal returns frontier_unavailable; after coverage, exact retry returns the stored outcome.

account_update_profile_request_body.description: Carries exactly one holder-signed profile create-or-update Event and no unsigned profile patch.

account_update_profile_outcome.description: Stored outcome after the profile Control Move is accepted and its effect is materialized. profile.id is the create-derived ActorProfile ID, profile.realm_id is event.realm_id, and an update projects updated_by/updated_at from event.actor_id/event.created_at. Exact Event replay returns the byte-identical stored outcome and emits no second account-aggregate delta.

account_status_record.description: Immutable Account Authority issuer-ledger record. account_status_record_id is the suite-tagged full digest of RFC 8785 JCS over every field except account_status_record_id and proof. The proof uses context ak.account_status_record_proof.v1 over that same closed unsigned core. principal_control_realm_id is a verified account-binding coordinate only and is never a finality scope.

binding_version.description: Monotonic Account Authority-local account-to-principal binding generation.

account_status_publication.description: Constrained carrier for one exact AccountStatusRecord. Initial publication carries record only; downstream fanout carries the byte-identical record plus prior receiver receipts. No receiver rebuilds or re-signs the record.

account_status_receipt.description: Receiver-signed receipt proving durable monotonic replication of one exact AccountStatusRecord. It grants no authority. proof uses context ak.account_status_replication_receipt_proof.v1 and payload_digest over RFC 8785 JCS of every field except proof.

account_status_resolve_request_body.description: Service-authenticated bounded issuer-ledger range request used for freshness checks and predecessor-gap recovery. Unauthorized or unrelated callers receive the operation's non-enumerating authority outcome.

account_status_resolve_outcome.description: Contiguous Account Authority issuer-ledger range. Records are ordered by status_seq, begin exactly at from_status_seq when present, and retain the Account Authority's original bytes and proofs.

account_status_publication_outcome.description: Durable replica operation state. accepted/duplicate are terminal for this receiver and dependency_missing performs zero writes while identifying the exact next sequence required for gap recovery.

did_binding_challenge_request_body.description: Request a single-use challenge for binding an ALREADY-PUBLISHED did to principal_id. Unlike identity_binding_challenge_request_body this carries no unpublished did_operation and no PCR genesis digests: the DID already exists, and the Account Authority resolves did at high freshness, requires project(did)=principal_id, and never attempts to resolve did_core_id directly.

principal_id.description: Stable did_core_id to bind. It is not directly resolvable.

did.description: Already-published DID. The Account Authority MUST resolve it at the high freshness tier, require project(did)=principal_id, and MUST NOT accept caller-supplied DID history.

did_binding_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for binding an already-published did to principal_id. The client copies every field from challenge_id through expires_at into account_registration_control_proof, adds proof_kind, request_canonical_digest and verification_method, and signs the closed proof with the current active update key of the entry pinned by did_version_id. The client MUST byte-compare principal_id, did and every other echoed field against what it expects before signing and MUST fail closed on any mismatch. request_id is idempotency metadata and is not part of the signed transcript.

account_subject.description: Service account subject that will own the binding. Signed so the proof cannot be replayed against another account.

did.description: Server-resolved did echoed into the signed proof transcript; it MUST project to principal_id.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the entry the Account Authority resolved as current; the proof MUST be signed by that entry's active update key.

witness_evidence.description: Method-native witness / freshness evidence digest resolved for this DID. Deployments that do not host the DID MUST require it: same-origin trust between registry and Station does not extend to third-party DIDs.

expires_at.description: Issued lifetime MUST be no greater than 300 seconds.

identity_abandonment_challenge_request_b.description: Request the single-use challenge that makes abandoning a provisional identity explicit. It applies only while the Principal Control Realm was never accepted and the identity root is lost, so the caller can sign nothing and the account handoff grant is the only available credential. principal_id and did_version_id pin exactly which reservation is being given up.

principal_id.description: Provisional principal recorded in the holder-authenticated reserved_identity_creation checkpoint. The Account Authority MUST reject any other value and MUST NOT issue a challenge for a principal whose PCR is already accepted.

did_version_id.description: versionId of the published entry 0 that becomes the orphan anchor. Pinning it lets the confirmation detect a PCR acceptance that landed after the challenge was issued instead of abandoning a live identity.

identity_abandonment_consequence_disclos.description: Closed ordered set of consequences the client MUST present before it may submit the confirmation. The protocol fixes which consequences must be disclosed; the localized wording is deployment-owned. This list is not a self-asserted acknowledgement receipt, which would be forgeable; the anti-automation property comes from the challenge itself, which no login, session resume, lease fence advance or other automated flow ever fetches.

identity_abandonment_challenge_outcome.description: Persisted, single-use server challenge for provisional identity abandonment. It is the evidence that the abandonment was an explicit user action: the identity root is lost, so the holder cannot sign a confirmation. Challenge state MUST be shared durable state, not process-local memory; expiry and prior consumption are distinct terminal states.

lease_fence.description: Identity-creation lease fence at issuance. The confirmation MUST be rejected when the current fence differs, so a concurrent holder cannot have its reservation abandoned underneath it.

expires_at.description: MUST be at most 300 seconds after issued_at.

identity_abandonment_request_body.description: Confirm the explicit abandonment of a provisional identity. It MUST present a fresh account handoff grant and MUST NOT reuse the grant presented when the challenge was issued; how strong the authentication behind that fresh handoff is, which risk checks run and how long any cooldown lasts are deployment governance and are deliberately not specified here.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the abandonment. Replaying it returns the recorded terminal outcome and MUST NOT produce a second orphan-anchor tombstone.

identity_abandonment_outcome.description: Recorded terminal outcome of an explicit abandonment. One transaction consumed the challenge, recorded the orphan-anchor tombstone / audit reservation, suppressed the reserved_identity_creation checkpoint on every holder-readable surface and released the identity-creation lease. There is exactly one success terminal; every other terminal is an error reply. Whether the orphan anchor is annotated on a discovery surface, when its handle and namespace are released and how long the reservation is retained are deployment governance and are not carried here.

principal_id.description: The abandoned provisional principal. Its published entry 0 is now a permanently unusable orphan anchor: it MUST NOT be reused and continuity MUST NOT be claimed over it.

account_request_erasure_request_body.description: Record the authenticated account holder's explicit request to erase the account (ak.gate.account.command.request_erasure.v1; zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8.1). The Account Authority accepts it directly on the gate surface; acceptance only records the intent and continues the Account Authority's existing erasure_pending issuance flow within the same service — it is neither the signed AccountStatusRecord nor a completion receipt. The Account Authority MUST treat this as a high-risk action and require fresh high-risk action authentication (recent login, WebAuthn, recovery key or a deployment equivalent), judged locally by the Account Authority; re-authentication strength, risk checks and cooldown are deployment governance.

request_id.description: Idempotency identity of the erasure request. Replaying it returns the recorded acceptance outcome and MUST NOT record a second intent; the same request_id with different canonical bytes is duplicate_conflict with zero writes. A different request_id while a live intent whose erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is not yet signed exists is failed_precondition with reason_code erasure_request_already_pending.

account_request_erasure_outcome.description: Acceptance confirmation of a self-initiated account erasure request. At most one live intent record exists per account while the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord is unsigned. This outcome proves only that the intent is durably recorded; it MUST NOT be read as record issuance or physical erasure completion. Completion is observed through the existing account-status read surface, and physical completion through the erasure receipt rail (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 8).

principal_id.description: The authenticated principal whose account erasure intent was recorded.

recorded_at.description: Time the intent was durably recorded; an exact replay returns the first recording's value.

withdrawal_window_ends_at.description: Present only when the deployment grants a withdrawal window. The Account Authority MUST NOT sign the erasure_pending AccountStatusRecord before this time; once the record is signed the request is irreversible (zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md section 3 rule 3) and no withdrawal is possible.

schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.title: Arkret Account Subscribe Frame
schemas/account-subscribe-frame.schema.j.description: Single NDJSON frame on the ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1 streaming channel (GET /_arkret/self/account/subscribe, Content-Type: application/x-ndjson). Each newline-delimited line is one frame object. Discriminated by the `kind` field: `delta` carries account-aggregate data (cross-Realm frontier, to_device, account_data, device_lists, notifications, unread counts); the other kinds are control frames that mirror ak.self.events.stream.subscribe.v1 (`catchup_complete`, `frontier`, `heartbeat`, `dropped`, `resync_required`, `unauthorized`). Encrypted broadcast signals use the optional Signal Extension rail and never appear in this durable/account aggregate stream. `dropped` and `resync_required` MAY carry `reconnect_after_ms` as a server-directed minimum delay before opening another account subscribe stream for the same principal/device/filter scope.

cursor.description: Stream cursor (purpose='stream'). On `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` frames it points to the position covered by this frame; pass back as `after=` on the next subscribe call to resume. REQUIRED on `dropped` frames as the account-aggregate catch-up start for `GET /account/subscribe?after=<cursor>&catchup=true`. MUST be present on `delta` / `catchup_complete` / `frontier` / `dropped`; absent on `heartbeat` / `resync_required` / `unauthorized`.

realms.description: Per-Realm map on `delta` frames. Keys are `ak:realm:*`; values are that Realm's aggregate timeline/state/account-data entry. Membership lifecycle (`join` / `invite` / `knock` / `leave`) is carried by the events inside the Realm entry.

device_lists.description: Principal DID sets whose authoritative device list changed or left the caller's visibility scope on `delta` frames.

account_data.description: Account-scoped private data updates on `delta` frames.

notifications.description: Account-private notification projection deltas on `delta` frames. These are not Realm Events and are authorized by the authenticated account context rather than realm_id visibility.

agent_signer_evidence_bundle.description: Bounded signer-evidence sidecar for Agent-authored Events in this delta. Clients MUST verify each evidence item before caching or using it.

partial.description: When true on a `delta` frame, the per-Realm timelines are limited (truncated); client SHOULD backfill via ak.self.events.read.scan.v1 for any Realm whose timeline carries `limited=true`.

priority.description: Optional server-side priority hint for the frame (UX scheduling).

reconnect_after_ms.description: Optional server-directed minimum delay, in milliseconds, before opening another `ak.self.account.stream.subscribe.v1` stream for the same principal/device/filter scope. MAY appear only on `dropped` and `resync_required` frames. This is a stream reconnect hint, not a generic error retry field; it does not apply to unrelated API calls. Clients MUST wait at least this delay before reconnecting, and servers MUST reject earlier reconnect attempts with `429 rate_limited` plus `Retry-After`.

ack_token.description: Server-issued opaque acknowledgement token, REQUIRED whenever messages[] is non-empty. Bound server-side to (principal_id, device_id, queue high-water position of this batch) and covering this batch plus all previously delivered messages. NOT a cursor: no ak:cursor: wire form, no cursor schema/TTL/purpose. The client passes it verbatim to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1 AFTER durably persisting the batch payloads; queue deletion happens only through that explicit ack, never through stream cursor advancement (client-sync.md §10.1).

lost.description: SHOULD be set true when the server has dropped unacknowledged messages for this device (expiry or capacity) since the device's last acknowledged position. Clients SHOULD trigger key recovery paths (key backup / key re-request) and MUST NOT silently assume the queue was complete.

limited.description: True when this account subscribe to_device batch is truncated because the device queue exceeds the stream frame budget. When true, `next_cursor` is REQUIRED and the client MUST continue with ak.self.device_messages.read.list.v1?after=<next_cursor>; the top-level account stream cursor MUST NOT be used as the to-device queue pagination cursor.

next_cursor.description: Read-only to-device queue continuation cursor for ak.self.device_messages.read.list.v1?after=... . It is not an acknowledgement and MUST NOT delete queued messages; queue deletion happens only through `ack_token` passed to ak.self.device_messages.command.ack.v1.

ordered_log_sibling_diagnostic.description: User-visible diagnostic for multiple accepted ordered-log siblings at one actor_seq. Every listed sibling remains in timeline.events and the joined state leaf; none is a winner or loser.

prev_cursor.description: Stream cursor pointing backward in the timeline for backfilling history before this batch.

preview_only.description: Fallback path of client-sync.md §5.2: when timeline.limited=true and the server does not return realm_sync_entry.state_at_window_start, it MUST set preview_only=true. Clients then render window-start events as preview only.

ordered_log_siblings.description: Accepted ordered-log sibling groups affecting this timeline window. Clients render every event normally and MAY group them in conflict/audit UI; no event may be hidden as a loser.

event_states.description: Per-event protocol-state views (event_id + event_state) for reducer-input events carried by this entry. The 'bottom' detail object lives separately in 'bottoms' below — keyed by cell, not duplicated per event — so wire body is not doubled. Receivers correlate event_state=failed_bottom with the cell-level bottom diagnostic via the cells listed in bottom.cells[]. See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

event_state_reason_code.description: Optional short reason code (e.g., 'recovery_witness_missing'). For failure detail beyond the enum.

bottoms.description: Structured Bottom diagnostics for cells whose effective Lattice join resolved to ⊥ under the current CBA query basis. Each entry pins (cell, status, bottom). See zh/sync/service-surface.md §5.3.

state_at_window_start.description: Derived projection-only state at the timeline window start. NOT part of state hash, frontier, or causal graph.

actor_profiles.description: Window-start profile rows keyed semantically by the complete ActorId. A principal DID alone is not a key: accounts on distinct Stations remain distinct rows.

collaboration_role.description: Projection-only strong Realm role, emitted only after the server validates the registered Realm profile and discriminator.

member_roster.description: Lightweight roster page derived from effective ak.member.state, effective ak.member.identity.update references, and currently visible handle-claim evidence. Entries MUST NOT carry display fields or naked handle strings directly; handle strings may appear only inside signed ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects.

limited.description: True when entries[] is truncated and MUST NOT be treated as the complete Realm roster.

next_cursor.description: Optional pagination cursor for continuing member roster retrieval.

subject_account_id.description: Optional exact account identity disclosed for this member. Omit when subject disclosure is only available inside encrypted MemberIdentity or not authorized for the caller. Required whenever handle claim evidence or digest hints are included.

identity_event_ids.description: Effective ak.member.identity.update event ids for this actor after replacement refs are applied.

member_display_state_digest.description: Digest over the effective identity event references plus the current visible handle claim digest set for this roster entry.

identity_events.description: Optional inline effective ak.member.identity.update Event envelopes. When present these are the original events, not query-time re-encryption or projection rewrites. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because plaintext or decryptable identity events can disclose the same member subject.

handle_claim_digests.description: Digests of currently visible effective ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 objects for this member in the current Realm context. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, because stable claim digests are linkable across contexts. Absence is not proof that the member has no handle.

handle_claims.description: Optional inline signed handle claim evidence. MUST be omitted unless subject_id is disclosed, and every included claim MUST have claim.subject equal to subject_id. Services may omit this for privacy, size, or freshness; clients can backfill by subject via ak.find.directory.read.list_handles_for_subject.v1.

handle_claims_limited.description: True when handle_claims[] is truncated or replaced by digest-only hints. Clients MUST NOT interpret missing claims as no handle.

oneOf.description: Catch-up replay or initial baseline completed; no data fields are allowed.
Cursor-only frontier advancement; no data fields are allowed.
Account stream gap signal; cursor is the account catch-up start. No data fields are allowed. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Keepalive frame; cursor and data fields are forbidden.
Hard reset signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden. `reconnect_after_ms` MAY be present to enforce a server-directed reconnect holdoff.
Authorization-loss signal; cursor and data fields are forbidden.

schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.title: Arkret Accountability Grant
schemas/accountability-grant.schema.json.description: Issuer-signed endorsement used to verify Actor Profile accountable_principal_ids entries. This is the payload contract for ak.identity.accountability_grant.

issuer_id.description: Stable principal did_core_id accepting accountability for subject. Verifiers MUST take the proof verification-method DID URL's bare controller did, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(did) to equal issuer; direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden.

accountability_scope.description: Non-empty duplicate-free closed set used only for display and accountability governance; never grants authorization. A string is the singleton-set wire form. Array order has no semantic meaning. Canonical authors emit singleton sets as strings and multi-value sets in ascending raw UTF-8 byte order; receivers accept every schema-valid ordering and normalize only for cell-subject derivation, domain equality, and projection union.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the accountability grant is non-expiring and governed by grant_status revocation and controller lifecycle cascade.

proof.description: Detached proof by issuer over utf8('ak.accountability-grant-v1\n') || canonical_json(the object with proof omitted).

schemas/actor-profile-operations.schema..title: Arkret Actor Profile Operations
schemas/actor-profile-operations.schema..description: Authorized, anti-enumeration projection of another principal's global Actor Profile. A global profile Event lives in its owner's Principal Control Realm, so a co-member cannot reach it through an ordinary Realm-scoped read and MUST NOT reach it through a cross-principal actor selector. This operation is the only outward carrier for that PCR-resident fact: it is gated on a current shared Realm, returns the exact signed profile Event with its covering Seal, and never discloses any other PCR Event.

resolve_request.description: Resolves current global Actor Profiles for actors the caller currently shares realm_id with. The caller MUST be an effective joined member of realm_id and every returned actor MUST also be one at evaluation time; realm_id is the authorization basis, not a display hint.

realm_id.description: Shared Collaboration Realm establishing the relationship. A Principal Control Realm MUST NOT be used here: PCR co-membership is the owner's own devices and would make this operation a self-read with an outward shape.

profile_event.description: The exact accepted profile Event that produced the returned projection. Its envelope realm_id is the owner's Principal Control Realm; disclosing this Event is the declared exposure for ak.profile.create and ak.profile.update and does not extend to any other kind in that Realm.

resolved_actor_profile.description: One actor's current global profile with the evidence needed to verify it independently. The consumer recomputes the projection from profile_event and checks that accepted_seal covers profile_event.event_digest; a bare actor_profile is a server assertion, not evidence.

accepted_seal.description: Accepted Seal in the owner's Principal Control Realm covering profile_event.event_digest. It is disclosed only as coverage evidence for that exact Event and MUST NOT be used to enumerate the Realm's other sealed Events.

resolve_failure.description: Per-actor failure. The reason vocabulary is deliberately single-valued: unknown actor, actor without an accepted profile, actor that is not an effective joined member of realm_id, and a caller not authorized for that actor MUST all report profile_unavailable so the operation cannot be used to probe membership or account existence.

resolve_outcome.description: Closed outcome. Every requested actor_id appears exactly once across profiles and failures, so a caller cannot distinguish an omitted actor from a withheld one.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

actor_kind.description: Directory / UX classification only. MUST NOT participate in authorization, reducer acceptance, capability resolution, or any wire-protocol decision: those MUST consult DID + Grant + Constraint exclusively. Implementations are free to use actor_kind for icon selection, directory filtering and presentation, but a wrong value MUST NOT widen or narrow what a principal can do. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and has no DID of its own; its identity is device_id (ak:device:<uuid>) plus a verification method under the owning principal DID. See zh/models/actor.md.

handle.description: Arkret canonical handle string: <localpart>:<domain>. The @ mention sigil is not part of the handle.

agent_slug.description: Projection hint for a controller-scoped selector slug backed by ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1. Only valid when actor_kind=agent under ak.profile.personal_agent_provisioning.v1; it is not a global handle and MUST NOT be used for authorization, attribution, or Directory discovery. The mention input token @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> resolves to this actor's principal_id before persistence only after selector claim validation.

status.description: Public projection of the AccountStatusRecord lifecycle values defined in zh/identity/account-lifecycle.md §3. Implementations MAY hide or coarsen this field in projection views.

resolution.description: Read-only current principal did projection derived from the PCR identity resolution cell. It is not writable through Actor Profile create/update patches and is not an authorization root.

schemas/agent-membership-cascade.schema..title: Arkret Native Agent Membership Cascade
schemas/agent-membership-cascade.schema..description: Closed binding and durable cleanup state for Native Personal Agent Realm membership. Effective membership is the AND of the Agent member cell, the exact controller membership generation, Agent lifecycle and provision/accountability validity. Canonical Agent leave transitions are always caller-signed; a service never synthesizes them.

membership_lifecycle_cause.description: Closed audit-only lifecycle cause. It never supplies authorization or proves reducer provenance.

controller_membership_generation_ref.description: Exact accepted controller ak.member.state join Event that establishes the bound membership generation. A later rejoin has another Event ID and never revives this binding.

controller_terminal_event_ref.description: Required only on an explicit controller-membership-ended cleanup Event. It identifies the accepted terminal controller transition whose pre-state determines the exact Agent set and one-shot cascade authority.

expected_agent_ids.description: Lexicographically sorted exact set of active controlled Agents frozen from terminal pre-state.

cleanup_intent_digest.description: sha256 of the RFC 8785 canonical record fields through expected_agent_ids. It is the durable idempotency key for emergency cleanup.

cleanup_due_at.description: Governance alert deadline only. Crossing it changes pending to overdue but never restores controller or Agent authority.

schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Account Pairing and Agent Operation DTOs
schemas/agent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for account pairing and native personal agent management operations.

agent_slug.description: Required controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug. Used only as the right-hand component of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>; not a global handle or authorization subject. Provisioning services MUST issue or update a ak.schema.agent_selector_claim.v1.

opaque_local_id.description: Deployment-local short-lived account/auth artifact id. It is an opaque_correlation value, so its lexical space is disjoint from the ak: typed-ID namespace: a value MUST NOT begin with ak:.

pairing_secret.description: One-time CSPRNG pairing secret carrying at least 128 bits of entropy. It is transmitted only in JSON bodies, never in URLs or logs.

device_pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style code carrying 40 CSPRNG bits, bound to a short-lived SAS/QR transcript and protected by a ten-failure lockout.

agent_runtime_key_possession_proof.description: Closed Ed25519 proof that the submitter controls the proposed native Agent runtime key and possesses the authoritative pairing secret. Canonical transcript, equality, freshness, and final-commit re-verification rules are defined in key-management.md section 3.6.2.

audience_id.description: Stable target-service authorization identity; any verification_method remains a DID URL whose bare DID MUST project to this did_core_id.
