signature.description: Unpadded base64url encoding of the 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature over the canonical transcript.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey DTO. Defined once in public-key.schema.json so device, agent and account surfaces share one definition.

agent_runtime_public_key.description: Closed v1 Native Agent runtime signing-key profile. Ed25519 is the fully-specified JOSE algorithm identifier from RFC 9864; polymorphic algorithm identifiers are rejected.

agent_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent axis. Closed enum; only the controller's pause / resume / deactivate lifecycle events change it. Pairing and key facts are reflected through the generic readiness axis and open-handle fields, never through a fourth generic state axis (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_runtime_state.description: Operation-local diagnostic enum used only by agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome on the unauthenticated pairing poll. It is mechanically derived from the polled handle and key facts, is never writable, and MUST NOT appear in generic Agent list/get/key_state projections: no active accepted key authorization with an unexpired bootstrap handle is pending_runtime_key; no active key with the bootstrap handle expired is pairing_expired; an active key with no unconsumed replacement handle is ready; an active key with an unexpired replacement handle is replacing.

agent_presence.description: Short-lived reachability signal only. It never substitutes for lifecycle or readiness and does not use a protocol-wide fixed five-minute refresh interval.

realm_id.description: Realm that owns the capability grant cell and therefore the required ak.capability.revoke write surface.

key_state.description: Controller-private key, pairing-handle and authorization material for a generic Agent view. This object deliberately carries no lifecycle, readiness, presence, runtime_state or backup-readiness field: the only three generic status axes are siblings on agent_projection, while pairing poll alone exposes its operation-local runtime_state diagnostic.

requested_scope.description: Controller-private projection of the required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling captured at provision time, not a grant. Content actions are the maximum actions that later key scopes, Realm-scoped grants and sessions may allow; an omitted action cannot be added later. Participation is a separate action-time deny gate and cannot add authority. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants. Receiver authority comes from a valid agent-requested-scope-disclosure whose digest matches the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, not this service projection.

pairing_request_id.description: Current unconsumed, unexpired pairing handle. Its presence means pairing is open. Services MUST omit this field and its pairing_mode / pairing_code / pairing_expires_at siblings immediately after the handle is consumed or expires.

pairing_mode.description: Durable branch discriminator for the current open handle. bootstrap is valid when the Agent has no active accepted runtime-key authorization; replacement is valid when it already holds an active authorized key and lifecycle is active or paused. This field is pairing material, not a fourth generic status axis.

pairing_expires_at.description: Authoritative pairing expiry instant in the shared byte-canonical UTC millisecond profile. The projection and ak.agent.key_pairing_request_binding.v1.expires_at use the same exact string; offset or sub-millisecond wire spellings are schema violations and MUST NOT be normalized by a verifier.

challenge_proof.description: Structured proof of possession of new_device_pubkey. The Account Authority MUST recompute the signing transcript itself and MUST NOT settle for byte equality against a stored copy. Which transcript applies is fixed by the request shape: with device_pairing_request_id it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 rebuilt from the staged record; with challenge_transcript it is ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 rebuilt from those inputs plus the Account Authority own gate_audience origin. The digest of that recomputed transcript is also the value the target device_signature commits to, so one recomputation gates both proofs. A mismatched transcript_digest, a transcript name that does not match the request shape, a kid other than new_device_pubkey.kid, or a failing signature MUST NOT authorize a device.

authorize_event.description: Fully signed ak.device.authorize initial submission authored by a current accepted device. The service MUST admit this exact Event through the ordinary Event validation/reducer path; it MUST NOT mint an Event id, rewrite the Event, or directly insert a device projection. Its typed payload is the sole source of hpke_key and the target-device possession device_signature, MUST match new_device_pubkey by device id and Ed25519 key bytes, MUST set authorization_binding_kind=accepted_device, and MUST name the approving current device id in authorized_by. The proof.verification_method bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to principal_id and its fragment MUST equal authorized_by; appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden. That Event proof, not the target device_signature, binds principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at and scopes, because only the approving device knows those values.

device_pairing_request_id.description: Server-mediated short-link request id. Present exactly for the short-link path. The Account Authority MUST atomically authorize only the still-pending staged record whose pairing_code and new_device_pubkey exactly match this request, and MUST verify challenge_proof against the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript rebuilt from that record (device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce, new_device_pubkey digest). A record whose proof does not verify MUST NOT authorize a device.

challenge_transcript.description: Transcript inputs for the to-device path, where there is no staged record for the Account Authority to rebuild from. Present exactly when device_pairing_request_id is absent.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Controller-signed private disclosure addressed to the authoritative pairing verifier. The endpoint MUST consume its presentation challenge once, match agent/controller/audience, recompute the public DID commitment digest, and use the disclosed scope for the subset check. It MUST NOT copy the disclosure into authorize_event or any durable/public history.

signing_key_binding.description: Controller-signed minimal public binding created in the same approval action. Its agent/method/raw-key/authorization id and both digests MUST match the runtime request and authorize_event exactly.

authorize_event.description: Fully-signed ak.agent.key.authorize initial submission approved by the controller or policy engine. Its Event MUST target the Agent Principal Control Realm, carry actor_id equal to agent_id, executed_by equal to the controller DID, authorization_ref equal to the controller delegation DID URL bound by the Agent DID Document, and a proof verification method belonging to the controller or one of its currently authorized devices. The submission MUST carry ordinary publication authority evidence without rewriting the Event. Its payload.agent_key_scope MAY be narrower than, but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of, the immutable provision requested_scope; every provision constraint remains mandatory. Required so key activation never depends on an unaudited pairing side effect. authorize_event.event.event_id is the pair operation idempotency identity.

activation_state.description: Two-phase pairing result. awaiting_accepted_frontier means the exact authorization Event is durable but is not yet authorization state; the controller MUST close it into a managed Agent-PCR Seal and retry the identical idempotent request. active means portable signer evidence can be built from an accepted Seal and only then may the runtime be treated as authorized.

agent_runtime_approval_request_body.description: Runtime-to-controller pending approval request for native personal-agent key pairing. The runtime proves possession of the local key and the short pairing code; the controller still must approve by signing ak.agent.key.authorize and submitting agent_key_pair_request_body. The service computes ak.agent.runtime_key_binding.v1 from agent_id, pairing_request_id, verification_method, public-key digest and attestation digest. One open pairing_request_id has at most one pending stable binding: same-binding retry is idempotent and refreshes the full request while retaining approval/notification ids; a different binding fails with HTTP 409 agent_runtime_request_conflict without replacement.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_controller_projec.description: Authenticated controller-safe projection of the pending runtime key request. It is deliberately not agent_runtime_approval_request_body and not agent_key_pair_request_body: pairing_code is exposed only by the sibling controller key_state field, while requested_scope_disclosure and authorize_event do not exist until the controller approves. Services MUST also omit any other runtime secret or unregistered field.

agent_human_approval_error_details.description: Closed RFC 9457 extension set returned by ak.gate.account.command.issue_session_grant.v1 when an agent_key_proof request needs out-of-band controller approval. The enclosing Problem type MUST be https://arkret.org/problems/claim_required. The agent runtime MUST NOT be given CAPTCHA, OTP, browser-login, or other interactive human challenge material.

agent_runtime_approval_status_request_bo.description: Runtime-side poll for the controller decision on a previously submitted runtime key request. The pairing_request_id, pairing_code, and agent_id triple is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body, never in URL path or query string. A record miss and a pairing_code or agent_id mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found). HTTP responses MUST carry Retry-After; clients wait at least that interval and stop polling after pairing expiry.

pairing_request_id.description: Single-use pairing artifact id returned by agent_provision_outcome. Profile-local, short-lived and not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_runtime_approval_status_outcome.description: Controller-decision status for one runtime key pairing request. runtime_state is an operation-specific pairing diagnostic, not a fourth general Agent status axis. While the polled pairing is open it is pending_runtime_key (bootstrap) or replacing (replacement). Once the controller has approved this exact pairing, authorized_event_ref plus the authorized key binding fields are present; the runtime MUST compare authorized_public_key_digest against its own key. Presence and digest match of those fields — never lifecycle, readiness, presence or runtime_state alone — is the approval signal. An expired bootstrap reports pairing_expired; an expired replacement reports ready with no authorization fields for this request.

authorized_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. This is not the canonical runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

agent_provision_request_body.description: Controller-authored managed-Agent bootstrap. Before prepare, the controller publishes a signed, PCR-independent did:webvh inception whose document contains the managed-controller delegation but no ArkretPrincipalControlRealm service. prepare receives that did, verifies the accepted inception and returns its exact initial_resolution plus an opaque allocation. The controller freezes the managed-Agent PCR genesis with that commitment, derives principal_control_realm_id, and commits one ak.agent.provision Event. After PCR acceptance, the controller publishes the pre-rotation-authorized DID update containing the create-locked Realm binding. The service exposes the Agent and pairing handle only after that update is accepted.

did.description: Controller-authored Agent did:webvh whose accepted inception is independent of the future PCR Realm id.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope it froze locally, and signed into provision_event. A service MUST NOT choose it; commit MUST reject any value that differs from the provision payload byte for byte. It is distinct from the controller PCR that carries provision_event. This transport field is not inside any digest preimage; the ordering the controller MUST follow is key-management.md 3.6.3 and the named encoding.md 6.0.1 exemption on the payload field.

requested_scope.description: Required immutable global Agent key/session ceiling, not a grant. Later key scopes, Realm grants and session requests MUST NOT exceed its actions, resource selectors or mandatory constraints. Participation is an independent action-time deny gate and cannot restore authority omitted here. Provisioning never materializes content grants from this field. Operation/service resources constrain the service surface; explicit content resource selectors only further narrow later grants.

controller_station_id.description: Authenticated controller account Station. Together with the session principal_id this selects the controller authority; PCR identifiers are not exposed.

agent_provision_outcome.description: Four-stage outcome. prepare returns awaiting_controller_event with an accepted inception commitment. An accepted ak.agent.provision moves it to awaiting_pcr_genesis. PCR acceptance moves it to awaiting_did_binding until the controller-authored continuous WebVH update publishes the exact Realm service entry. The Agent, pairing handle and list/get projection become visible only at complete.

did.description: Complete Agent DID whose registered adapter projection is agent_id; managed-Agent PCR genesis initial_resolution MUST commit this value and its verified method head.

initial_resolution.description: Exact verified accepted inception position. It is immutable across all provisioning outcomes and is copied byte-for-byte into managed-Agent PCR genesis.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id the controller derived locally as retype(event_id) of the managed Agent PCR genesis it froze, and declared in the provision payload. Until that genesis is accepted this is a claim, not a live Realm.

controller_realm_id.description: Authenticated controller PCR in which the provision Event must be authored. Present only while status is awaiting_controller_event.

allocation_handle.description: Service-signed opaque allocation binding returned only by prepare and presented unchanged by commit.

requested_scope_digest.description: Digest of the complete immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID accepted create-locked bootstrap history (entry 1); only this digest, not the complete scope, is public. The client MUST recompute it from its submitted scope, returned agent_id and authenticated controller DID.

agent_renew_pairing_request_body.description: Re-open bootstrap pairing or replace an agent runtime. The service issues a fresh one-time pairing_request_id + pairing_code; every previously issued pairing handle for the agent becomes permanently unresolvable. An Agent with no active accepted runtime-key authorization re-opens bootstrap pairing; an Agent holding an active authorized key (lifecycle active or paused) performs runtime replacement re-pairing. Lifecycle intent, existing keys and grants stay untouched until the new controller-signed authorization with an exact supersedes set is accepted atomically, and completion preserves lifecycle intent. deactivated rejects.

agent_renew_pairing_outcome.description: Fresh pairing handle for bootstrap or runtime-key replacement. Runtime pairing does not require a backup and does not recover active MLS state.

requested_scope_digest.description: Unchanged digest of the immutable requested_scope commitment in the Agent DID binding; the complete scope remains controller-private.

agent_pairing_bootstrap.description: One-time bootstrap material handed to a personal agent runtime after provisioning. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret.

agent_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for short agent pairing handoff links. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.self.agent.pause Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. The service submits these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and never synthesizes an Agent-authored Event. Its optional payload.reason MUST equal the request reason exactly (both absent or the same string).

Closed ak.self.agent.resume Event authored in the Agent PCR and executed/signed by the authenticated controller delegation. Sidecar desired membership is re-derived from accepted lifecycle and exact Realm membership after admission; the request carries no writable Sidecar roster or acknowledgement.

The single controller-authorized terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Event. Once accepted, lifecycle is an unavoidable AND gate that makes every subordinate runtime key, session, pairing handle, capability grant, KeyPackage, presence and future submission ineffective. Cleanup Events are not part of this request. Optional payload.reason MUST equal request reason.

provisioning_phase.description: Closed reconciliation phase. Clients derive localized explanatory text from this phase; no parallel reason string is carried.

control_frontier.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted accepted refs for Sidecar genesis, ownership, Agent lifecycle/runtime-key authorization, and exact Realm membership. It excludes action grants, participation selections, and MLS/key-readiness results.

current_controller_device_ready.description: True only when the authenticated controller session device is the accepted genesis creator device or has completed matching Welcome and KeyPackage consume evidence.

desired_agent_ids.description: Read-only projection derived at the accepted frontier: active, runtime-key-authorized Agent principals owned by the Sidecar controller and also active members of sidecar.realm_id. It is not caller-authored or reducer-stored and cannot be edited through Sidecar operations.

effective_agent_ids.description: Desired Agent principals that are members of the current accepted Sidecar MLS epoch and have completed target-device Welcome/KeyPackage consumption and key readiness. Reducer/service MUST enforce this set is a subset of desired_agent_ids. The controller is represented by sidecar.controller_id and is not duplicated in either Agent array.

version.description: Account Authority CAS version for this exact agent/scope selection.

expected_version.description: Value to echo verbatim into the next participation replace for this exact agent/scope selection.

next_replace_input.description: Verbatim prepare input for the next ak.self.agent.participation.resource.replace.v1 of this entry; member names match the replace request byte-for-byte per the service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline. A first-ever selection has no entry row and uses expected_version 0.

schemas/agent-provision.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Provision
schemas/agent-provision.schema.json.description: Controller-authored payload that creates one native personal Agent provisioning fact and atomically projects its accountability and controller-scoped selector bindings. The containing Event proof is the only signature; this payload carries no nested proof.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Agent PCR realm id this provision forward-declares. The controller freezes the managed Agent PCR ak.realm.create envelope locally, computes its event_id and writes retype(event_id, "realm") here; that genesis Event is not yet submitted when this payload is authored, and it MUST be submitted separately afterwards rather than alongside this Event. This is the named class C exemption ak.exemption.preimage_identity.agent_provision_principal_control_realm_id.v1 registered under encoding.md 6.0.1: the genesis preimage carries no reference to this Event, so the dependency stays one-way. Genesis admission reverse-looks-up this declaration; a service MUST NOT choose the value.

schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.title: Arkret Agent Requested Scope Disclosure
schemas/agent-requested-scope-disclosure.description: Controller-signed, verifier-bound private disclosure of a managed Agent's immutable requested_scope. This object is authorization evidence, not a grant. It MUST travel only over an authenticated confidential presentation/operation channel and MUST NOT be written to a public DID Document, durable Realm Event, public registry, pairing code, or notification. The verifier consumes request_id/challenge once, validates the short presentation window, verifies a current controller proof, recomputes the requested-scope commitment against the accepted-at Agent DID commitment, and then applies the Agent ceiling subset rules. After successful one-time admission, an implementation MAY retain the object only as encrypted verifier-private evidence keyed by the recomputed digest, verifier_id and audience.

request_id.description: Identifier of the signed ak.identity.presentation_request or an equivalent authenticated private challenge request. It is single-use at verifier_id.

requested_scope.description: Complete immutable Agent ceiling disclosed only to the bound verifier. It does not grant any action or resource.

verifier_id.description: Exact verifier named by the presentation request. A different verifier MUST NOT accept or forward this disclosure as its own evidence.

audience.description: Exact origin, service audience, or canonical operation audience requested by verifier_id.

challenge.description: Verifier-generated unpredictable challenge. The (verifier_id, request_id, challenge) tuple is single-use; replay MUST fail closed.

expires_at.description: Presentation admission expiry. expires_at MUST be later than issued_at and expires_at - issued_at MUST NOT exceed 300 seconds. It does not change the immutable ceiling; it only bounds disclosure delivery/replay.

proofs.description: At least one current controller proof. The proof verification method MUST belong to controller_id or one of its currently authorized devices. payload_digest is sha256(canonical_json(this object with proofs omitted)); detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.agent_requested_scope_disclosure_proof.v1', payload_digest, agent_id, controller_id, verifier_id, audience, challenge, verification_method, created_at}).

schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Selector Claim
schemas/agent-selector-claim.schema.json.description: Signed claim binding a controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug to an agent principal DID. It powers @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> compose-time resolution without making the agent carry a public handle.

controller_subject_id.description: Controller principal DID that owns the selector namespace.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped slug used as the right-hand side of @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>.

subject_id.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

issuer_id.description: DID that signs this selector claim. It is normally controller_subject; a delegated issuer MUST be authorized by controller_subject and bound in source_refs or proof evidence.

vouching_id.description: Optional service-only vouching role that served or vouched for this selector claim when distinct from issuer_id. The service subject-class requirement is validated independently of the field name.

visibility.description: Disclosure boundary for selector resolution. Restricted/private claims require audience and requester policy checks before returning subject.

audience.description: Audience binding for restricted selector disclosure, such as a Realm ID, verifier domain, or service DID.

claim_scope.description: Optional scope such as realm_id, organization_id, purpose, allowed_operations, or disclosure policy tags.

source_refs.description: Optional refs to accountability_grant, actor profile, provisioning, delegation, or revocation evidence.

schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Event Exchange Binding
schemas/agent-sidecar-event-exchange-bin.description: Closed typed binding that ties one native-Sidecar-scoped Message event to one source-routed exchange. It is legal only inside encrypted metadata plaintext of an event whose scope_ref.kind is sidecar. It is the only normative way to declare an explicit user-facing response; invalid or absent bindings are non-echo. See zh/models/sidecar.md.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity copied verbatim from the request binding. It is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT appear in shared events, plaintext metadata, publish output, push previews, notifications, public telemetry, account-data keys, or any public/shared surface.

role.description: Closed disposition. request: the controller's private request event itself. user_facing_response: an Agent response the controller MAY echo after validation. internal: exchange-scoped Agent collaboration/tool output that MUST NOT be echoed. Consumers MUST fail closed to non-echo on any value not listed here.

request_event_id.description: Accepted Event id of the private request event of the same exchange. Event id is the only canonical reference form; Message ids MUST NOT be used here.

completes_exchange.description: Optional coordinator completion request; legal only with role=user_facing_response. It does not itself make the exchange terminal. A controller device validates the actor against coordinator_assignment_event_id and, on success, authors a durable ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event with action=close.

coordinator_assignment_event_id.description: Request Event id for the initial coordinator assignment, or the accepted reassign_coordinator control Event id. Required only when completes_exchange=true.

request_context.description: Write-once exchange identity carried only on role=request. It is the single durable source of the projection's write-once fields: any controller device rebuilding the projection copies these values verbatim, so cross-device bit-identity is anchored to the accepted request event instead of device-local state. Forbidden on response/internal roles.

completion_policy.description: Closed v1 completion policy. Only the effective coordinator may ask the controller to close the exchange.

coordinator_agent_id.description: Initial coordinator. It MUST be one of addressed_agent_ids. It MAY be omitted only when addressed_agent_ids contains exactly one item, in which case that sole item is implied.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Control
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-control.s.description: Closed plaintext encrypted inside the payload of ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. Only the Sidecar controller may author this durable private-Strand Event. It is the sole source of coordinator reassignment and terminal exchange state.

basis_event_ids.description: Canonical UTF-8 byte-order sorted maximal causal heads of exchange facts observed when this control was authored. The outer Event refs MUST contain role=after for every id, and the request Event must be causally covered.

response_event_ids.description: Exact canonical set of validated user-facing response Event ids causally covered by basis_event_ids. Required for every terminal action, including an empty array.

failure_reason_code.description: Required only for action=fail. close/cancel derive empty-response failure codes controller_closed_empty/controller_cancelled.

coordinator_agent_id.description: New coordinator for action=reassign_coordinator. It MUST be addressed by the request and eligible at authoring time.

schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar Exchange Projection
schemas/agent-sidecar-exchange-projectio.description: Disposable controller-device-local cache for one source-routed native Sidecar exchange. Every field is a deterministic fold of accepted Sidecar-scoped Events. This object is not wire truth, is not Account Data, is never merged across devices, and may always be deleted and rebuilt.

source_event_id.description: Optional accepted Event id copied from the request context as the source Event for this exchange. This identifies one Event, not a frontier or trust anchor.

terminal_event_id.description: Controller-authored ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control Event that produced complete or failed.

exchange_id.description: Opaque controller-private idempotency identity; it is not a Sidecar locator and MUST NOT be copied into shared events.

folded_frontier.description: Local cache coverage. event_ids are the canonical sorted maximal causal heads of all contributing accepted exchange facts. event_set_digest commits to the canonical sorted complete contributing Event-id set. max_hlc is display/cache metadata only and never proves causal dominance.

schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..title: Arkret Agent Sidecar View State
schemas/agent-sidecar-view-state.schema..description: Controller-private encrypted account-data plaintext for one hosted Sidecar context. It changes only private presentation and never mutates either Strand, Track, access, read state, notifications, search, or event ownership.

schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.title: Arkret Agent Sidecar
schemas/agent-sidecar.schema.json.description: Controller-owned private AI workspace bound one-to-one to (realm_id, controller_id). Agent Sidecar is a first-class native protocol scope, not a Circle profile, backing Circle, or editable membership container. See spec/v1/zh/models/sidecar.md.

encryption_profile.description: Agent Sidecar is always protected by an independent MLS group; plaintext fallback is invalid.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence Operations
schemas/agent-signer-evidence-operations.description: Authenticated, anti-enumeration operation shapes for producing and resolving portable Native Agent signer evidence.

principal_id.description: Controller principal whose Account Authority lifecycle gate is being attested.

agent_authority_id.description: Native Agent PCR authority service assembling signer evidence. It MUST equal both the authenticated S2S caller and service_id in the controller principal's current AcceptedAtServiceBinding.

agent_authority_resolution.description: Current signed route and method-native control evidence for the Agent PCR authority. The Account Authority verifies this carrier before using its RFC 9421 keyid; a did_core_id, URL, bearer token or self-asserted public key is never a key source.

controller_account_gate_attestation_issu.description: Closed S2S request for the Account Authority-owned controller lifecycle gate. Agent state, account_id and raw account cell material are deliberately absent.
Byte-stable issuance outcome. The embedded attestation is the only Account Authority material admitted into AgentSignerEvidence.

query_outcome.description: Each success item is the complete content-addressed Native Agent signer-resolution root, including exact AgentSignerEvidence and all four recursive ref/digest pairs. Before returning success, the issuer atomically stores the byte-exact root and every recursively referenced dependency in the governance-dependency CAS. Clients never construct this wrapper from a bare AgentSignerEvidence.

schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.title: Arkret Agent Signer Evidence
schemas/agent-signer-evidence.schema.jso.description: Closed portable evidence for one Native Agent signer. Current admission and historical Event verification are structurally disjoint. Historical validity is fixed by a destination-signed admission receipt; it is never reconstructed from a later current snapshot.

admission_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of exactly {agent_authority_snapshot, controller_account_gate_attestation}. It never includes itself, a receipt or an outer attestation.

snapshot_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of core only.

seal_lineages.description: Complete duplicate-free predecessor closure needed to connect the key and Agent-status witness Seals to frontier_seal_id. Every Seal is in principal_control_realm_id.

agent_snapshot_lease.description: Authority signature over domain ak.agent_authority_snapshot.v1 and every sibling field except proof.jws. Current admission checks the lease at verifier-now; historical verification checks it at the receipt accepted_at.

basis_digest.description: Digest of the Account Authority-private binding/status projection selected by basis. The portable object never carries a service-local account_id or raw account cell.

controller_account_gate_attestation.description: Privacy-minimal Account Authority gate. The authority signs domain ak.controller_account_gate.v1 and every field except proof.jws. account_id and raw account cell material are forbidden by the closed schema.

current_observation.description: Fresh request binding for new admission. All basis digests and Seal ids must match admission_evidence exactly; this object never appears in historical evidence.

event_admission_receipt.description: Receiver-signed immutable record that the exact Event and the origin-frozen producer signer-evidence root were durably accepted. producer_accepted_at is copied from the verified station_admission proof. Event digest already commits to seal_ref or seal_basis, so no ambiguous receipt Seal id is repeated. The proof domain is ak.agent_signer_admission_receipt.v1 and covers every field except proof.jws.

core_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete top-level evidence with outer_attestation omitted.

outer_attestation.description: Anti-malleability assembly signature. It binds the tagged mode, request or receipt, admission evidence and optional transparency without replacing underlying authority proofs.

historical_outer_attestation.description: Immutable historical assembly attestation. Verifiers resolve the Authority method at attested_at; unlike the current branch it has no verifier-now TTL.

authorization.description: Key authorization only. Parent Agent/account gates never rewrite this interval and no cross-Realm valid-until scalar exists.

key_cell_value.description: Canonical resolved OR-set entries sorted by tag bytes. Raw or implementation-private JSON is not a valid state value.

realm_create_event_id.description: Accepted managed Agent PCR genesis ak.realm.create that materialized the first active status. This evidence object is assembled after both Events are accepted and never enters either digest preimage.

agent_provision_event_id.description: Accepted ak.agent.provision in the controller PCR whose payload.principal_control_realm_id equals retype(realm_create_event_id). The genesis create carries no reference to it, so a verifier resolves it by that reverse look-up.

schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.title: Arkret Agent Signing Key Binding
schemas/agent-signing-key-binding.schema.description: Controller-authored minimal public binding between one Native Agent signing verification method, its raw Ed25519 key, and the accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event. The authorize Event payload commits the digest of this object's binding core before agent_key_authorize_event_id and controller_proof are appended; those two fields are materialized only after the Event identity is known, avoiding self-reference. Private pairing, scope, PoP, attestation, and capability material MUST NOT appear in this object.

agent_key_id.description: Exact payload.key_id of the bound ak.agent.key.authorize Event; used with agent_id to derive the authoritative agent-key cell subject.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of public_key.key after base64url decoding to exactly 32 bytes, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest; verification_method and alg are not in this digest domain.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Complete identity of the already accepted authorize Event. This field is excluded from the binding core committed by that Event payload and is appended only after Event identity verification.

expires_at.description: Present iff the authorization itself declares expires_at. JSON null is forbidden.

key.description: Base64url without padding of exactly 32 Ed25519 public-key bytes.

schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.title: Arkret Applet Edge Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-edge-operations.schema.js.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Applet edge and bridge operations.

applet_transaction_request_body.description: Body for ak.edge.applet.command.transaction.v1. Transport-layer requirements are mandatory but not body fields: RFC 9421 Signature/Signature-Input, Source-Service-ID, Destination-Service-ID, Content-Digest, Idempotency-Key, received_at audit metadata, and a persisted delivery_authentication_record. See zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 7.3.1.

applet_id.description: Exact active Applet registration selected for signature and epoch verification; service_id alone is not unique.

source_id.description: Must exactly match the Source-Service-ID header and the signed source-service-id component. It identifies the source service only; each Event still requires independent actor/applet/capability signature verification.

signals.description: Optional encrypted Signal Extension envelopes. Exact applet payload types and targets remain inside ciphertext.

status.description: Closed transaction result: all items accepted, a mixed result, or all items rejected.

schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.title: Arkret Applet Ghost Actor Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-ghost-operations.schema.j.description: Closed preview, commit, and outcome DTOs for receiver-side Applet-managed Ghost provisioning. The commit carrier is exactly the signed authoring request plus its role-neutral managed-actor bundle.

schemas/applet-install-authoring.schema..title: Arkret Applet Managed-Actor Authoring DTOs
schemas/applet-install-authoring.schema..description: The single closed Station preview to Applet authoring carrier for install_bot and provision_ghost. No legacy install-only operation, branch-specific bundle aliases, or derived request identifier exists.

schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.title: Arkret Applet Install Operation DTOs
schemas/applet-install-operations.schema.description: Closed request/response DTOs for ak.self.applet.install.command.preview.v1, ak.self.applet.command.install.v1, and ak.self.applet.command.revoke.v1. The InstallPlan body itself is defined in applet-install-plan.schema.json.

reuse_existing_managed_actor.description: Immutable anchors of the one existing Bot authority winner for this applet and target Station. The receiver recomputes every field from accepted local state.

capability_revoke_events.description: Exactly one caller-signed ak.capability.revoke initial submission for every active grant in the recomputed plan.

membership_state_events.description: Caller-signed membership removals in the plan, or an empty array when the install owns no managed membership.

proof.description: Required when revoke_mode includes delegated session revocation in production. The proof signs the canonical ak.gate.account.command.revoke_session.v1 transcript reconstructed from the active applet install selector.

schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet InstallPlan
schemas/applet-install-plan.schema.json.description: Canonical plan returned by ak.self.applet.install.command.preview.v1 and recomputed by ak.self.applet.command.install.v1 before commit. plan_digest is calculated over the canonical InstallPlan object with plan_digest omitted.

applet_managed_actor_provision_payload.description: Immutable service-authored authority for one Applet-managed Bot or Ghost principal. It precedes and is cross-bound to the principal's applet_managed_control PCR genesis; it is not the actor's mutable resolution head.

method_history_evidence.description: Complete did:webvh inception/current log and witness evidence independently verified at provision acceptance. Applet-managed principals are long-lived rotatable high-risk authorities, so v1 rejects did:web snapshots and did:key expansions; service attestation and core projection never replace WebVH chain verification.

schemas/applet-package.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Package
schemas/applet-package.schema.json.description: Controller-signed package used to install an Applet. The package is a distribution object, not Realm history truth and not a grant. The Station authorization capability derives ak.applet.registration and capability grants during ak.applet.install.

package_id.description: Distribution identifier only. Not a grant subject.

proof.description: Controller DID detached proof over the canonical package or derived registration object. proof.payload_digest MUST equal package_digest (proof over canonical package) or the derived registration object digest. Empty object is invalid.

detached_proof.description: Controller-DID detached-JWS proof shape, aligned with event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof (the generic non-Event signed-object proof). Non-Event objects bind their canonical payload via payload_digest; Event proofs MUST instead use event_digest and event_proof.

webhook_auth.description: HTTP message signature verification policy for transaction push. key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used to verify the app/bridge->arkret inbound HTTP message signature. Verifiers MUST take its bare controller did, validate it with the registered method adapter, and require project(did) to equal service_id (did_core_id); direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. The key is bound to the effective registration_epoch. accepted_signature_algorithms pins the acceptable RFC 9421 signature algorithms.

key_ref.description: DID URL under an Applet service did whose registered adapter projection equals service_id. For app/bridge->arkret inbound transaction push, Signature-Input keyid MUST equal this value. Node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service did/key binding selected by the Source-Service-ID did_core_id, not this field.

endpoint_policy.description: Supported Applet API endpoints and their auth requirement.

limits.description: Service-side resource hints derived into the registration manifest.

ghost_policy.description: Ghost Actor support and accountability template. enabled defaults to false semantics; an explicit boolean is required.

delegation_policy.description: Delegated native-user acting request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

e2ee_policy.description: MLS join request. Defaults to false; enabled MUST be explicit.

widget.description: Optional Applet widget declaration. When present, it MUST validate ak.schema.applet_widget_declaration.v1.

schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.title: Arkret Applet Registration Epoch Transcript
schemas/applet-registration-epoch-transc.description: Closed, normalized security transcript hashed to produce an Applet registration_epoch. The hash input is the UTF-8 domain separator arkret-applet-registration-epoch-v1\n followed by the JCS bytes of this object.

did.description: Complete service DID whose adapter projection MUST equal derived_registration.service_id.

schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.title: Applet Widget Declaration
schemas/applet-widget-declaration.schema.description: Closed declaration for an Applet UI widget origin, CSP, scoped token capability scope, and consent gate.

widget_origin.description: Canonical HTTPS Web Origin only: lowercase scheme and host plus an optional valid non-default port. Userinfo, path (including a trailing slash), query, fragment, explicit :443, and out-of-range ports are forbidden.

csp.description: Content-Security-Policy that the host client MUST enforce for the widget document.

token_scope.description: Maximum capability scope for the short-lived widget token.

schemas/applet.schema.json.title: Arkret Applet Protocol Object
schemas/applet.schema.json.description: Schema-registry object for applet protocol metadata snapshots. Event payloads for ak.applet.* MUST use the typed payload definitions in event-payload.schema.json; this object is not a loose transport envelope and is closed at the top level except for x_* extensions.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet identifier. Service identity is carried separately in service_id.

service_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the service that hosts the applet runtime; current resolution is supplied by its authenticated service definition.

schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.title: Arkret Audit Release Attestation
schemas/audit-release-attestation.schema.description: Structured remote attestation for an audit applet release service under ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1. This is the wire form behind audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware: a verifier MUST be able to validate release-service measurement, attestation chain trust root, attestation key freshness, operator identity, Realm/Circle binding, and audit release policy digest without trusting prose declarations. The attestation binds the controlled output path for ak.audit.release; it does not add the applet to MLS and does not grant signal plaintext access. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6.

realm_id.description: Realm this attestation evidence is valid for. Verifier MUST require realm_id to match the MLS Welcome / Event Envelope Realm being joined or audited; identical audit_policy_version_digest values across Realms do not make evidence portable.

audit_actor_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the audit release service / applet actor whose controlled output path this evidence attests. MUST match the approved_recipient_audit_actor_id derived from the accepted ak.audit.session.authorize record, or the service actor accepted by the active ak.audit.applet_binding.

service_id.description: Stable operating service did_core_id hosting the audit applet or release service. MUST match the service_id in the active ak.audit.applet_binding / ak.audit.release chain.

family.description: Attestation family. 'software_test_only' is for conformance fixtures and MUST be rejected by deployments declaring attested_hardware assurance.

measurement.description: What is actually running inside the enclave / HSM / equivalent controlled output boundary. Verifiers compare this measurement to the measurement allowed by the active audit applet binding and release policy.

code_digest.description: Hash of the audit release service binary / image / policy bundle that the enclave loads. MUST be reproducible (signed by vendor build pipeline).

policy_version.description: Release service's compiled-in policy version (e.g. semantic version or git tag). MUST appear in the Realm/Circle audit binding's allowed release-service policy versions at issued_at.

report_data.description: Optional REPORTDATA-equivalent that binds the attestation to the release service public key or output-encryption key. Lowercase hex encoding of a 32–64 byte byte-string (pattern enforces an even hex length: each byte is exactly two hex characters; total 64–128 hex characters). Receivers MUST validate this binding when present.

attestation_chains.description: Ordered attestation evidence chain: leaf attestation (signed by the enclave) → intermediate (e.g. PCK certificate, AK certificate) → root (vendor attestation root certificate). Each item is base64url-encoded DER / CBOR per platform format. Verifier MUST validate signature chain and trust the root against the Realm-declared trust root list.

attestation_key.description: The attestation public key (extracted from the leaf of attestation_chain). ak.audit.release proofs and RYW receipt validation MUST be cryptographically bound to this attested output path when audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware.

verification_method.description: DID URL the receiving verifier uses to resolve attestation_key. MUST live under audit_actor_id's DID Document or a DID Document explicitly delegated by the active audit binding. Fragment characters are constrained to the ASCII set `[A-Za-z0-9._:-]` (a strict subset of RFC 3986 unreserved, excluding `~`, plus `:`) for stable byte-comparable key ids; see the Arkret verification-method DID URL profile in identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2. DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

validity.description: Validity window of THIS evidence. Verifier MUST reject evidence outside the window. For evidence presented under audit_assurance_class=attested_hardware (ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1), the verifier MUST reject evidence whose window (expires_at - not_before) exceeds 90 days; Realm/service policy MAY cap it lower. Evidence with a longer window MUST be treated as an elevated-risk signal and rejected by profile policy rather than silently accepted.

revocation.description: How the verifier should check whether attestation_chain leaves / intermediates have been revoked. Required when platform supports revocation (sgx_pccs CRL, tdx PCS, etc.).

operator_principal_id.description: DID of the controlling organization actually operating this enclave / HSM. This intentionally keeps the _did suffix because it is raw external DID material being compared against service_id and Realm policy, not a protocol actor_id/principal_id alias. MUST match what the Realm policy lists as the allowed audit operator. Distinct from service_id when the operating organization is different from the technical service DID (e.g. service hosted by organization A on behalf of organization B).

audit_purpose.description: Why this audit applet release service may output audit material. MUST match the active binding/session purpose; mismatch → audit_purpose_mismatch.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Same definition as ak.audit.ryw_receipt.audit_policy_version_digest — fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id, trust_domain, audit_binding, release_policy, release_window_policy, activation_frontier_digest, first_auditable_epoch} at the Realm policy frontier at issued_at. Lets verifier O(1) check that the policy classification this evidence was issued under matches the current binding/session state, cannot be reused across Realms, and cannot retroactively expand eligibility for already encrypted messages. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile. See encoding.md §2 (canonical JSON) and audited-e2ee.md §6.

proofs.description: Detached signature(s) over the canonical evidence bytes (all fields except `proofs`), signed by operator-controlled keys distinct from the enclave attestation key. Two-key separation: the enclave attests its own measurement; the operator separately attests that this enclave is the one they intend to deploy.

schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Audit RYW Receipt
schemas/audit-ryw-receipt.schema.json.description: Read-Your-Writes receipt issued by an Events API node, witness, or peer Station confirming that a ak.audit.release or other audit envelope has reached accepted state. Required by ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 and ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 before an audit applet release service may output wrapped material or plaintext evidence (see zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §6). The audit_assurance_class field MUST match the active Audit Applet Binding; mismatch fail closed.

trust_domain.description: Deployment trust domain for the Realm at the receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST require this to match the current receive context and the enclosing audit Event Realm context before using audit_policy_version_digest.

realm_operator_organization_id.description: Stable ID of the Realm operator's ultimate controlling organization at this receipt frontier. Verifiers MUST derive and verify it from the Realm service/operator DID control chain; it is not a self-attested label. For federation_witness_attested, every witness controlling_organization_id MUST be distinct from this value and from any organization under the same ultimate controller.

witness_id.description: Stable service ID of the witness that produced this receipt.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the key the witness used to sign (e.g. did:web:...#key-1). Federation-grade verification requires this value to be distinct from every other witness verification_method.

controlling_organization_id.description: Stable ID of the organization that controls the witness. This value is not self-attested: verifiers MUST resolve the DID projected from witness_id and confirm its controller / service ownership chain projects to controlling_organization_id. Federation-grade verification requires all witnesses' controlling_organization_id values to be pairwise distinct and not equal to the audit actor's controlling organization or realm_operator_organization, including common ultimate controllers.

attested_at.description: Time at which this witness attested. Receivers MAY use the latest attested_at across witnesses as the effective receipt timestamp.

witnesses.description: Externally verifiable list of witnesses attesting that audit_event_id reached accepted state. Its suite-bearing digest is decoded from audit_event_id. Verifiers derive the attestation class from this list, the accepted Realm audit policy and the verified operator control chain; producers do not declare a class on wire.

witness_attestation.description: Witness attestation block. The receipt's independence is externally verifiable from the witnesses[] list rather than self-claimed via a single enum. See zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1 / §4.1.1.

audit_assurance_class.description: Audit assurance class propagated from the active Audit Applet Binding. attested_hardware = ak.profile.attested_audit.e2ee.v1 (TEE/HSM/enclave controlled release required). disclosed_policy = ak.profile.disclosed_audit.e2ee.v1 (process-only disclosure, NOT cryptographically enforced). Release services MUST propagate the binding-declared value verbatim; receivers MUST fail closed when this field disagrees with the binding/policy state at the receipt's frontier.

audit_policy_version_digest.description: Canonical hash of the Realm-bound audit release policy tuple from the receipt frontier. Computed as fixed sha256 over canonical JSON {realm_id: <id>, trust_domain: <trust_domain>, audit_binding: <object>, release_policy: <object>, release_window_policy: <object>, activation_frontier_digest: <hash>, first_auditable_epoch: <n>}. Lets verifiers atomically check that the receipt's claim matches the active binding/policy at this frontier without replaying events and prevents cross-Realm reuse or retroactive expansion of identical policy text. MUST match the receipt frontier's policy state and ak.audit.release.eligibility_proof; mismatch MUST fail closed (audit_receipt_invalidated). Required field — missing receipts MUST be rejected to prevent silent policy drift. This field is intentionally not hash-agile in v1; a future algorithm change requires a new schema/profile.

recovery_reason_code.description: Optional machine-readable code, set only when this RYW receipt covers a ak.audit.accessed Event emitted via the Late Key Recovery path (see zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.3.5 and zh/crypto-media/audited-e2ee.md §4.1). Payload value, not an error-code-registry reason_code. Used by audit projections to distinguish late-key-triggered accesses from first-access reads. When absent, the receipt covers a normal (first-access) ak.audit.accessed Event.

schemas/authenticated-signer-resolution-.title: Arkret Authenticated Signer Resolution Evidence
schemas/authenticated-signer-resolution-.description: Content-addressed immutable signer-key resolution material retained for historical verification. The evidence ref is derived from the SHA-256 digest of the complete RFC 8785 JCS object; callers never substitute a current resolver result.

signer_evidence_ref.description: ak:signer_evidence:sha256:<hex>, where hex is SHA-256(RFC8785-JCS(complete evidence object)).

service_signer_evidence.description: The signed ServiceResolutionRecord, method-native history evidence and normalized DID document are retained together. signer_id equals record.service_id and verification_method is authorized by the retained normalized document at the signed record history position. Durable historical signer evidence permits only did:key or a complete did:webvh history; did:web is forbidden because a mutable web document cannot close historical verification. Record route expiry is checked at admission time but does not retroactively invalidate retained evidence. Complete canonical evidence is at most 1 MiB.

normalized_did_document.description: Exact normalized DID document whose digest and history position are authenticated by public_resolution.method_history_evidence.

principal_signer_evidence.description: attester_signer_evidence_ref/digest resolves to a service-kind leaf that historically verifies the Station projection attestation. Current route or DID expiry is not a retrospective validity input.

native_agent_signer_evidence.description: The four required ref/digest pairs resolve the Agent Authority, controller, Account Authority and receiver historical signer leaves selected by the exact methods in agent_signer_evidence. Each ref content digest equals its paired digest. Current route or DID expiry is not a retrospective validity input.

schemas/authority-set-policy.schema.json.title: Arkret Authority Set Policy
schemas/authority-set-policy.schema.json.description: Canonical, basis-resolvable authority policy bound by AuthoritySetRef. authority_set_digest is SHA-256(JCS(the complete object)).

schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Authorization Operation DTOs
schemas/authz-operations.schema.json.description: Closed response DTOs for authorization query operations that need operation-specific list envelopes.

schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret AvailabilityReceipt
schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.description: Content-addressed signed holder commitment that exact Event bytes remain available until retention_expires_at. Its content address is the Realm-suite digest of this complete object, including signature.

bytes_digest.description: Realm-suite digest of UTF8('ak.availability_event_bytes.v1') || 0x00 || JCS(the complete accepted EventEnvelope with only unsigned removed). event_id, actor_kind and all accepted producer/station proofs remain in the preimage.

schemas/availability-receipt.schema.json.$comment: The signature-free core is {realm_id,event_id,bytes_digest,holder_id,retention_expires_at,holder_signer_evidence_ref,holder_signer_evidence_digest}. signature.payload_digest is the Realm-suite digest of RFC 8785 JCS(core). The full receipt content address is computed from this complete signed object and is carried only by selectors, Seal commitments and storage keys.

schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Blob Operation DTOs
schemas/blob-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for blob service operations whose wire shape is not the full blob metadata resource.

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete issuer verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the receipt must pin one already accepted service key binding.

content.description: The binary blob content part in multipart/form-data. This field is not JCS-canonicalized as JSON; content_digest covers the bytes.

key_ref.$comment: Closed MLS group-binding object owned by this encrypted_attachment definition; not an opaque string.

oneOf.description: Reference to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit event.

group_state_ref.description: v1 MLS group state lookup hint. MUST point to accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit / equivalent group state proof. Does NOT replace MLS transcript verification.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, single ciphertext_digest
streaming chunked AEAD form (STREAM / OAE2): per-segment AEAD, per-object random nonce_prefix

not.$comment: content hashes use content_digest with an algorithm prefix

realm_id.description: Owning Realm for authorization, asset privacy policy enforcement, retention and GC. MAY be omitted only for global / cross-Realm service blobs (e.g. avatar previews) explicitly authorized by the Blob Service deployment policy.

schemas/bottom.schema.json.title: Arkret Bottom Diagnostics
schemas/bottom.schema.json.description: Structured diagnostic for cell join values that resolve to bottom (⊥). Surfaced on /account/subscribe, /events, and state query responses when a cell's effective Lattice value is undefined under the current CBA query basis. See spec/v1/zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md §5.1.

kind.description: Why the join produced bottom. 'conflict' = concurrent cas_register / fsm divergence on safety-critical cell. 'invalid_transition' = fsm op violates allowed_transitions. 'missing_dependency' = event ref to absent / failed prior event. 'unauthorized' = event issuer lacks capability for the op (verifier-side). 'notary_split' = multiple Seal leaves diverge on next-seal authority. 'schema_error' = lattice op or value violates declared cell schema.

cell_ids.description: Cell ids participating in the bottom diagnostic. Multi-cell when a multi-cell Control Move atomically failed across linked cells.

event_ids.description: Reducer-input event ids whose effects (or precondition checks) produced this bottom. Empty allowed when the cell's bottom is structural (e.g. notary cell schema_error) and not tied to a specific event.

seal_view.description: Seal leaves and control frontier under which this bottom was observed. Diagnostics MUST pin this so the receiver can reproduce the join without ambiguity.

state_root.description: Control-plane state_root at observation time (recompute from Seal leaves). Optional when the diagnostic is emitted before state_root is computable.

heads.description: When kind=conflict and the cell's lattice exposes multiple candidate heads (mv_register, or_set with conflicting tag values), the candidate values. Implementations MUST NOT pick a winner from this array; it is for UI / audit only.

details.description: Free-form structured details specific to the diagnostic kind. Producers SHOULD use stable keys per kind (e.g. invalid_transition: from/to/expected_transitions; schema_error: schema_id/violation_path). Receivers MAY display but MUST NOT use for authorization decisions.

escalated_at.description: When the cell first crossed Realm.bottom_escalation_after_ms. Absent when within the grace window. Implementations SHOULD raise an out-of-band notification to admins / recovery governance once set.

schemas/calendar-event.schema.json.title: Arkret Calendar Event Profile Fields
schemas/calendar-event.schema.json.description: Schedule subtree carried at Strand metadata.fields.calendar and activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. Both directions of that binding are enforced by strand.schema.json. All intervals are half-open [start, end). Timed events carry RFC 8984 LocalDateTime wall-clock anchors resolved through timezone plus tzdb_version; this schema never carries an absolute instant.

start.description: Inclusive lower bound of the event interval, and the recurrence anchor. Narrowed to local_date when all_day is true and to local_date_time when it is false.

end.description: Exclusive upper bound of the event interval, in the same shape as start. MUST be strictly later than start in both branches; a single all-day event spells end as the following date. JSON Schema cannot express the cross-field comparison, so reducers and profiles enforce it with schema_violation.

timezone.description: Canonical IANA Zone name in the release named by tzdb_version. Producers MUST resolve Link aliases to their canonical Zone before signing per calendar-timezone-registry.json; this pattern only constrains shape.

tzdb_version.description: IANA TZDB release tag (for example 2026a) whose rules resolve timezone and every derived instant. Signed with the schedule so receivers never silently substitute their locally installed release.

all_day.description: True selects the date branch of start/end/recurrence.until; false selects the whole-second LocalDateTime branch.

status.description: Whole-event schedule status. Required with no implicit default; distinct from the generic Strand stage and state axes. cancelled rejects new RSVPs and is schedule-relevant for notification.

call_id.description: Soft reference to an Arkret call session. It never widens access: an unresolvable or invisible call_id MUST NOT leak call state.

attendees.description: The single canonical schedule roster. Membership and invite projections are producer inputs only, never a second projection truth source. actor_id uniqueness is enforced by the reducer; at most one organizer is enforced here by maxContains.

allOf.$comment: All-day branch: start, end and recurrence.until are Gregorian dates.
Timed branch: start, end and recurrence.until are whole-second LocalDateTime values.

recurrence.description: RFC 8984 RecurrenceRule snake_case subset. Omitted interval means 1, omitted first_day_of_week means mo, rscale is Gregorian and skip is omit; the JSCalendar @type discriminator is implied by this schema and MUST NOT appear on the wire. Unlisted RecurrenceRule members, excluded rules, overrides, RDATE and EXDATE are rejected rather than ignored.

until.description: Inclusive termination bound compared against the occurrence local start with <=. Narrowed to the same branch as start/end by all_day, and MUST NOT be earlier than the base start.

allOf.$comment: nth_of_period selects an occurrence within a month or year and is meaningless for daily/weekly recurrence.
by_month_day filters a month position and cannot combine with weekly recurrence.
by_set_position selects from a candidate set and requires at least one candidate-producing by_* rule.

role.description: Attendance role. Omitted means required. organizer is display and scheduling semantics only and grants no capability.

display_name_snapshot.description: Identity-revealing display snapshot. It MUST be encrypted together with the rest of the schedule whenever Strand metadata is encrypted.

schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.title: Arkret Call Recording Artifact
schemas/call-recording-artifact.schema.j.description: Canonical metadata for a call recording artifact after it has entered the Arkret blob pipeline. It binds the blob, recording start event, MLS exporter recording key context, retention policy and deletion audit surface without introducing a ak:recording or ak:artifact storage key.

content_digest.description: Digest published by the Arkret blob pipeline for the stored recording object.

ciphertext_digest.description: Digest of encrypted recording bytes. This MUST match encryption.ciphertext_digest and the referenced encrypted blob metadata.

produced_by.description: Media service DID or recorder service DID that produced the encrypted recording bytes.

recording_initiator_capability_ref.description: Capability grant reference proving the recording was initiated by an actor holding ak.call.record.

deletion_audit.description: Present only after a delete attempt is scheduled, completed, or blocked. The referenced erasure receipt remains the durable audit proof.

call_recording_retention.description: Retention contract for a recording or transcript capture artifact. retention_expires_at is the earliest deletion time; deletion_trigger declares the only accepted purge cause; audit_lock blocks all purge paths until an audit-grade release is accepted; consent_confirmed records the required second client-side capture confirmation.

retention_expires_at.description: Earliest time the artifact MAY be purged. Absent = governed by retention_policy_id. MUST NOT be in the past at write time.

audit_lock.description: When true the artifact is under audit / legal hold; purge MUST be rejected with legal_hold_active until the lock is released by an audit-grade action.

consent_confirmed.description: Records that the second client-side confirmation required before recording or transcript capture was obtained.

trigger_event_id.description: Durable event that caused this delete attempt, when the trigger is event-backed.

erasure_receipt_ref.description: ak.audit.erasure_receipt event, ak.schema.erasure_receipt.v1 object, or digest proving the deletion outcome.

schemas/call-signal-plaintext.schema.jso.title: Arkret Call Signal Plaintext
schemas/call-signal-plaintext.schema.jso.description: Closed top-level plaintext object carried inside a SignalEnvelope encrypted_payload for ak.call.signal. The signal_kind-specific data object is validated by the corresponding normative branch in zh/crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref); arbitrary forward gaps are accepted. It is independent of seq, the per-call anti-rollback sequence monotonic over (realm_id, call_id, actor_id, device_id).

data.description: Signal-kind-specific payload. Producers and consumers MUST additionally validate the closed field rules for the selected signal_kind in webrtc-signaling.md; this extension point is encrypted end-to-end and is not interpreted by the Signal service.

issuer_id.description: Exact issuing actor. Its closed ActorId shape already contains the account or hosted-principal routing authority when one exists; no parallel station sidecar is permitted.

items.description: Canonical action vocabulary. MUST be of the form ak.<segment>.<segment>... matching capabilities.md §5. Bare names without the ak. prefix are not permitted; consult capabilities.md before introducing new action names. Wildcards within a segment are not permitted in this schema; the resource selector controls scope, not action expansion.

constraints.description: Constraints applied to this grant. Re-grant control MUST be expressed via constraint_kind='authority_control' and max_authority_depth (see capabilities.md §10). A top-level 'delegable' field is forbidden and MUST be rejected as schema_violation. With no authority_control constraint the grant cannot be re-granted (equivalent to max_authority_depth=0).

issued_at.description: Grant issuance time — carries the 'creation time' semantics for a Capability Grant in place of the generic created_at (models/common-fields.md §3.2). Retention / audit / ordering queries MUST use issued_at / expires_at / revoked_at rather than falling back to created_at.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

updated_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp for the most recent grant lifecycle update. Ordinary grant body fields remain immutable; revocation still uses revoked_by/revoked_at.

issuer_authority_refs.description: The authority this grant was issued under. Every grant has one: a root controller’s grant anchors on the authority-root cell, and any further grant anchors on the grants its issuer already holds. The typed ref is the only distinction within the unified grant shape. Authorization is recomputed from these refs on every decision, so revoking an ancestor invalidates its descendants at read time without any cascading write.

oneOf.description: A grant the issuer holds. The issuer MUST be that grant's subject, and the ref MUST be active at evaluation time; its capability, resources and constraints all bound this child.

controller_epoch_at_issuance.description: The controller epoch under which this grant was issued. It proves the issuer controlled the root at issuance and nothing more: it is issuance audit, not a liveness version. Comparing it to the current epoch would make ak.realm.owner.transfer kill the whole authority tree.

authority_generation.description: The authority generation this grant is anchored to. Unlike the epoch this IS compared to the cell's current value: ak.realm.authority.reset advances it precisely so an entire authority tree stops resolving.

oneOf.description: The Realm authority-root cell. A rooted terminal: it never contributes an edge to the cycle check. realm_id is explicit rather than inherited from the envelope because ak.capability.derived can carry roots from another Realm.

authority_depth.description: Reducer-derived absolute distance from the authority root: a realm_root ref counts 0, so a root controller's grant is 1 and a member's re-grant is 2. Derived from the refs, never author-declared, so it cannot be misreported — which is what makes it safe to answer 'how far did this authority spread' with a single field instead of a recursive join. Taken at issuance and not recomputed on revocation; a later chain may be shorter than the recorded value, which is the conservative direction for a max_authority_depth decision.

authority_root_refs.description: Reducer-derived set of roots this grant ultimately descends from: the direct realm_root refs plus the union of every grant ref's own roots. Plural because multiple parents, and ak.capability.derived inheritance across a Realm link, can reach different roots or generations. Deduplicated on (realm_id, cell_ref, authority_generation) and sorted canonically by unsigned-byte order; controller_epoch_at_issuance is per-grant issuance audit and is deliberately not part of the identity key.

allOf.$comment: Lint condition (2) from capabilities.md §18.1: grants whose actions[] include moderator-role actions MUST carry a constraint with depends_on_moderation_state=true. Conditions (1) and (3) (subject condition selector referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue/cell) are reducer-side lint and not enforced here.

schemas/cba-proof-bundle.schema.json.title: Arkret CBA Proof Bundle
schemas/cba-proof-bundle.schema.json.description: Unsigned receiver-relative dependency container for exactly one target_seal_ref. Every embedded object MUST belong to the target Realm, be reachable from the target Seal dependency graph, appear in canonical id/digest bytewise order without duplicates, and be independently verified; the bundle itself is not authoritative. A bounded verifiable superset is allowed, but unrelated objects are a schema violation. inclusion_proofs and availability_proofs together MUST contain no more than 2048 items; this cross-property aggregate and the dependency path depth limit of 4096 are semantic validation rules in addition to each array's local JSON Schema bound.

control_moves.description: Control Move Event envelopes only. Semantic validation MUST reject DataEvent, Anchor Unit, actor-private, or unknown non-control Event shapes even when the generic Event Envelope schema is otherwise valid.

inclusion_proofs.description: Inclusion proofs. The combined item count of this array and availability_proofs MUST be no greater than 2048.

availability_proofs.description: Availability proofs. The combined item count of this array and inclusion_proofs MUST be no greater than 2048.

schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/circle-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Circle administration operations (ak.self.circle.*). Every write operation carries the caller-signed ak.circle.* Event and the service submits those exact bytes through ordinary Event admission; the durable Circle object model is circle.schema.json. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

circle_view.description: Circle projection row returned by create/get/lifecycle operations. Reducer-managed mls_group_id is present exactly for MLS-backed Circles; actor create payloads cannot carry it.

profile_ref.description: Create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it; profile-specific Circles expose it so clients can apply mandatory filtering.

member_count.description: Exact count of active Circle members. Present only when the caller is an active Circle member; directory-only previews MUST omit it and use the privacy-bucketed preview contract instead.

viewer_membership.description: The caller's own Circle membership state when one exists.

member_ids.description: Active Circle member ActorIds (strict subset of parent Realm.members). Empty after tombstone.

circle_create_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.create Event and nothing else. The Circle id is retype(create_event.event.event_id), so the service cannot name the Circle and MUST NOT synthesize the Event: every actor-supplied field lives in create_event.event.payload.object, and the parent Realm is create_event.event.realm_id. See spec/v1/zh/models/circle.md and spec/v1/zh/sync/service-http-binding.md.

create_event.description: Closed ak.circle.create Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. Admission requires the payload closed union and forbids id/mls_group_id. The reducer derives both identifiers. encryption_profile='none' is allowed only when the parent Realm content-encryption floor permits plaintext.

circle_member_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state Event and nothing else. The target actor and the membership value live in member_event.event.payload; the Circle is payload.circle_id and MUST equal the path circle_id. The service MUST NOT add a capability verdict to the payload it submits: circle_member_state_payload is closed, and the ak.circle.member.manage decision is the admission path's, evaluated against projected grants rather than asserted by the request.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that payload.circle_id names the path Circle. Moving another actor to join requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed by allowed_circle_ids, and the target MUST already be a joined parent-Realm member; knock requires join_rule=knock. A self-service join is gated on the Circle join_rule instead.

circle_member_delete_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.circle.member.state leave Event and nothing else.
