The path circle_id and actor_id MUST respectively equal member_event.event.payload.circle_id and payload.actor_id; member_event.event.realm_id MUST equal the path Circle's parent Realm. The service submits the exact signed Event through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT rebuild it or synthesize a leave Event.

member_event.description: Closed ak.circle.member.state Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller, with membership fixed to leave and expected_membership carrying the concrete current membership as the signed head_eq guard. Admission MUST bind the Event proof to the exact account-local lineage selected by the authenticated session; matching only the caller DID is insufficient. Removing another actor requires ak.circle.member.manage narrowed to the path Circle; self-service leave uses ak.circle.member.add.

note.description: Reducer-emitted reason code on Ignored / Rejected, or unsupported-feature note while MLS scope rotation is not wired end-to-end.

schemas/circle.schema.json.title: Arkret Circle
schemas/circle.schema.json.description: Circle — an intra-Realm scoped event/message boundary with its own membership, history_access and optional independent MLS group. Parent Realm membership supplies only the current-membership intersection gate; history_access is never dynamically inherited.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm. create-locked; Circle never re-binds to another Realm.

profile_ref.description: Optional create-locked Circle semantic profile discriminator. Ordinary Circles omit it. Profile-specific creation paths MUST persist their registered profile id. Agent Sidecar is a separate ak.schema.agent_sidecar.v1 object and MUST NOT be represented by this field.

directory_visibility.description: Who may see this Circle exists as a directory entry. 'members' means only Circle members see its title/display/member_count. 'realm_members' exposes directory metadata only and does NOT grant event or history access.

join_rule.description: How an actor becomes a Circle member. 'public' lets any active parent-Realm member self-join; it does not make the Circle globally discoverable. 'knock' requires the application/approval flow. 'invite' requires Circle admin add or invite.

history_access.description: Circle's own governance history range ratchet, initialized by Circle create. The only state-changing update is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; widening is permanently forbidden. It is never dynamically inherited from or capped by the parent Realm history_access, while current access still requires active parent-Realm membership. Standard MLS requires since_join.

content_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local content encryption floor. When omitted, the Circle inherits the parent Realm's content_encryption_floor. Effective floor = max(parent Realm content_encryption_floor, this field). May only tighten, never widen, the parent Realm floor, and the effective floor is a one-way ratchet: once e2ee_required has been accepted it MUST NOT be lowered back to allow_plaintext (reducer rejects with content_encryption_floor_downgrade). e2ee_required is only meaningful when encryption_profile='mls_rfc9420'; a Circle with encryption_profile='none' MUST keep allow_plaintext. See zh/models/circle.md §7.

metadata_encryption_floor.description: Optional Circle-local metadata encryption floor (binary, symmetric with content_encryption_floor: allow_plaintext | e2ee_required). When omitted, the Circle inherits parent Realm's metadata_encryption_floor. May only tighten, never widen, parent Realm floor; the effective floor is a one-way ratchet (reducer rejects a lowering write with metadata_encryption_floor_downgrade).

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the parent Realm ceiling.

encryption_profile.description: Circle content encryption profile. create-locked. 'none' means plaintext delivery/query/projection isolation only and is allowed only when the parent Realm policy floor allows plaintext. 'mls_rfc9420' means the Circle owns an independent MLS group and MUST NOT derive its keys from the Realm-default MLS group.

content_scheme.description: Create/Genesis-locked MLS content scheme. Required exactly for an MLS-backed Circle and immutable for the derived group lifetime.

mls_group_id.description: Reducer-derived base64url_no_pad(utf8(canonical CircleId)). Present only on the materialized MLS-backed Circle and forbidden in the actor-supplied create payload.

durability_policy.description: Create/Genesis-locked exporter durability policy. Required exactly for mls_exporter_aead_v1; absent otherwise.

state.description: Circle lifecycle state. v1 defines active, archived, and tombstoned only; Circle has no independent freeze or destroy state because parent Realm freeze/destroy applies at the Realm boundary.

short_name.description: Human-facing short name. Unique per (realm_id, short_name) case-insensitive — reducer-enforced. Circle naming has no Sidecar-reserved prefix because Sidecar is a separate native scope.

color_token.description: Color token from the spec-controlled palette. Clients MUST map token -> theme color (light/dark/high-contrast) consistently across devices; clients MUST NOT reassign tokens.

schemas/common-ids.schema.json.title: Arkret Common ID and Reference Definitions
schemas/common-ids.schema.json.description: Shared ID and reference pattern $defs referenced cross-file by multiple object schemas so a single form change propagates without inline drift. Defs-only: not an object or event schema. See zh/models/common-fields.md and artifacts/registry/id-kind-registry.json for the authoritative ID kind registry.

event_id.description: Complete Arkret Event cryptographic identity. The suffix is the canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of exactly 33 octets: one registered active digest-suite wire_code followed by all 32 octets of the Event digest. Regex validation is only lexical; receivers MUST decode, require 33 octets, canonical re-encode, and verify the suite code and full digest before use.

history_request_id.description: Globally unique history-request object identity; it is never scoped by response stream, requester, service or effective scope.

history_response_id.description: Globally unique history-response object identity; reuse under another request response stream is duplicate_conflict.

push_target_id.description: Canonical typed pairwise push pseudonym. The suffix is the unpadded Base64URL encoding of the complete 32-octet HMAC-SHA256 output for one (recipient_id, principal_id, device_id, push_route, salt_epoch_id) tuple. Receivers MUST decode exactly 32 octets and require canonical re-encoding; it is never a DID, object id, raw provider token, or stable cross-service correlation key.

account_status_record_id.description: Account Authority issuer-ledger record identity derived from the complete closed unsigned AccountStatusRecord core.

account_id.description: Complete protocol account identity. Equality is byte-for-byte equality of both canonical did_core_id components; neither component may be inferred from a DID Document, route, session audience, current service, handle, or local database key.

actor_id.description: Complete protocol identity for an Event author or Realm member. The discriminator is validated against accepted registration, Actor Profile and admission evidence; it never authorizes itself. No variant is equal to another variant and no comparison may fall back to a bare principal_id.

web_origin.description: Canonical HTTP(S) Web Origin: lowercase scheme/host plus an optional valid non-default effective port. Userinfo, path (including a trailing slash), query, fragment, explicit :80 on HTTP, and explicit :443 on HTTPS are forbidden.

did_core_id.description: Canonical stable DID-derived identity core. The lowercase DID method name follows ak:did_core:, and the remaining method-adapter-defined core is opaque to generic consumers. The did:web v1 adapter uses the complete canonical method-specific-id, never a digest or truncated host. Principal, actor and service identity equality is byte-for-byte equality of the complete did_core_id. A did_core_id is not a DID and cannot be resolved without a did or ServiceResolutionRecord.

did.description: Canonical bare DID used for registration, DID method resolution and owner-published current resolution. It contains no path, query or fragment and MUST project through the registered method adapter to exactly one did_core_id.

webvh_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identifier used at method-native registration, document and evidence boundaries. Role admission is enforced separately.

human_principal_did.description: Canonical bare DID for a v1 human principal anchor. The method set is derived from role_requirements.human_principal_anchor; capability checks for relocation, DID-root recovery and ongoing governance are separate.

managed_agent_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of a durable managed Agent. Its accepted bootstrap history is controller-authored and must contain a continuous inception followed by the create-locked PCR binding update.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet installation identity. Applet service authority is carried separately by service_id.

applet_managed_actor_did.description: Canonical bare did:webvh identity of an Applet-managed Bot or Ghost. Its inception is committed by the immutable Applet-managed actor provision Event and the cross-bound applet_managed_control PCR genesis.

did_key_did.description: Canonical bare did:key identifier used at method-native key and witness evidence boundaries. This is a registered method-specific Did subtype, not a business ActorId and not a DID URL.

tsp_vid.description: Closed Trust Spanning Protocol Verifiable Identifier. The explicit kind is required because a VID is not necessarily a DID and generic consumers must never guess its identifier system from string prefixes.

did_url.description: Arkret verification-method DID URL profile (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.2): lowercase method name, no query, required fragment, fragment limited to ASCII [A-Za-z0-9._:-]. Every verification_method-family field and every kid/key_ref a schema declares to be a DID URL MUST resolve to exactly this definition; values compare byte-for-byte with no URI normalization or percent-decoding.

schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Consent Cell Self-Management Operation DTOs
schemas/consent-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for holder-private consent cells. Only holders/controllers receive consent_cell_view; peer request submission returns an opaque outcome and never exposes cell state.

active_grant_dots.description: Currently-active grant dots (not yet observed/revoked, within validity window).

consent_grant_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.consent.grant Control Move and nothing else. consent_id, peer, consent_scope, not_before and expires_at all live in grant_event.event.payload; the holder is taken from the path. consent_id is producer-allocated, so the caller mints it: it is the cell subject (ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id>), and the or_set add dot is 'ak:event:<enclosing event_id>:<write_index>' (zh/identity/consent-model.md section 3.2). A service that wrote this element itself would be putting consent into replicated cell state that no Event in the log explains.

grant_event.description: Closed ak.consent.grant Event whose actor_id and authenticated holder are the path holder Principal Control Realm's current authority-root controller. authorization_ref MUST bind the current authority-root authorization. This root_control_only action supports neither separate managed-behalf execution nor grants: controller/agent consent_write delegations, general PCR writes, co-owner grants, automation, or payload approval evidence do not substitute. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event. Admission MUST verify the authority-root binding, event.realm_id, and path holder; otherwise it rejects unauthorized.

consent_revoke_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.consent.revoke Control Move and nothing else. Its payload.observed_dot_ids MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive, and the caller reads those dots back from consent_cell_view.active_grant_dots: an observe-remove OR-Set revoker has to name the exact dots or two concurrent revokes race, one removing the old dot and the other the new one while the UI reports success (zh/identity/consent-model.md section 3.2). A consent_scope=any cascade is no exception.

revoke_event.description: Closed ak.consent.revoke Event whose actor_id and authenticated holder are the path holder Principal Control Realm's current authority-root controller. authorization_ref MUST bind the current authority-root authorization. This root_control_only action supports neither separate managed-behalf execution nor a controller/agent consent_write delegation or general PCR/co-owner grant. Its payload.consent_id MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event.

consent_request_request_body.description: Body for opaque contact/consent request submission. The peer principal is the authenticated actor and is never caller-supplied. Holder existence is deliberately not a precondition visible to the caller.

consent_request_outcome.description: Constant anti-enumeration response. Missing holder, denial, rate-limit drop and quarantine acceptance all return this exact shape; no cell id, state, dots, timestamps or expiry are exposed.

schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Contact and Direct Conversation Operation DTOs
schemas/contact-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTO bundle for the Contact lifecycle: request, respond, reject, scope replacement, tombstone, the portable Contact round evidence bundle, acceptance receipts and the peer Contact carrier, plus the contact-list projection.

bilateral_continuity_checkpoint_core.description: Domain-neutral, root-anchored commitment to one contiguous prefix of a bilateral lineage. Sequence is monotonic; same sequence with a different checkpoint digest is a fork, never a winner election.

participant_ids.description: The two exact ActorIds, sorted by RFC 8785 canonical bytes.

root_basis.description: Portable uncheckpointed root Contact round evidence. It is retained so founder and root identity remain independently derivable after prefix compaction.

covered_through_contact_round_id.description: The exact terminal contact_round_id at the compacted-prefix boundary. The oldest remaining tail edge points here; bundle content digests are accumulated only in prefix_accumulator_root.

signatures.description: Exactly one signature by each registered participant authority key over the checkpoint core.

bilateral_continuity_checkpoint_proposal.description: One participant service's immutable proposal. It is never portable continuity evidence until the other service returns and durably commits the completed two-signature checkpoint.

uncompressed_tail_entries.description: Immediate predecessor first; at least the latest terminal round remains explicit, and the final edge must terminate exactly at checkpoint.core.covered_through_contact_round_id.

contact_continuity_checkpoint_request_bo.description: Holder-authorized command to compact the deterministic oldest terminal prefix. The caller never supplies the checkpoint core or boundary.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Station cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

subject_id.description: Principal DID whose private Contact projection receives this fact.

recipient_id.description: Stable Station service did_core_id that hosts subject_id and accepts this delivery. Together with subject_id this is the complete Contact participant authority key.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same recipient_id route during Contact delivery bootstrap. They are not part of the signed Contact Event, Contact projection, Realm member cell or authority state; they do not extend any token/receipt TTL or authorize delivery.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Absent only for a root Contact round. On recontact it is copied from every signed request fact and request acceptance receipt in this bundle and points to the immediately preceding terminal round. The bundle field is derived convenience, never independent authority.

continuity_checkpoint.description: Latest mutually signed compacted prefix for this lineage. Its presence changes the chain terminator from the root round to covered_through_contact_round_id; it never changes the root basis or participant authority pair.

head_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the signed current-head Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel head_digest is carried.

terminal.description: Signed current-head classification. true means head_event_ref is an accepted ak.contact.tombstone terminal head for this basis; false means the basis remains non-terminal. A historical predecessor in a recontact continuity chain requires true from both directional proofs.

request_receipt.description: Closed prepare input for answering one incoming Contact proposal, carried only by the ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 projection. It is the complete signed request_acceptance_receipt object, not narrowed to a reference, and the field name is byte-identical to the request_receipt field of the prepare branch of ak.self.contact.command.respond.v1 and ak.self.contact.command.reject.v1, so a client copies it verbatim; the prepare contract is unchanged and a client MUST NOT rename, rebuild or re-derive the receipt, and MUST NOT assemble one from request_event_ref, which is a projection summary. Unlike next_prepare_input this receipt is issued and signed by the PEER's source service rather than by the holder's own server, which is exactly why handing the object itself to the holder client has real cross-server verification value: the client verifies the issuer signature, the issuer service key at accepted_at and the receipt's binding to the exact request Event ref and digest on its own, instead of unconditionally believing its own server's retelling. Presence is fixed by contact_state: a pending_incoming row MUST carry it, and a pending_outgoing, accepted, rejected, expired or tombstoned row MUST NOT, because pending_outgoing is the holder's own outstanding proposal with no incoming request to answer and the other four have a consumed admission slot or a terminal round. A glare pair is therefore never receipt-bearing: the holder's own unconsumed outgoing request keeps the row pending_outgoing while glare evidence is incomplete, and the mechanically derived glare Contact round projects accepted, which matches the rule that the glare branch forbids respond and reject. Absence is the sole encoding of 'respond and reject are not authorable now'; no extra error code and no extra contact_state value expresses it. When the slot has moved on, prepare refuses with zero writes; the client MUST re-read this operation rather than cache, guess or replay a consumed receipt.

effective_scopes.description: Optional shorthand. When present, MUST equal bidirectional_scopes.

peer_host_id.description: Optional stable Station service did_core_id hosting the peer. Omitted for same-Station contacts.

peer_host_resolution.description: Required bootstrap material whenever peer_id is present. It MAY be refreshed without changing peer_id.

continuity_evidence.description: Latest mutually committed portable checkpoint plus its exact uncompressed tail. Its absence means no committed export exists; clients must not synthesize it from projection summaries.

contact_next_prepare_input.description: Closed successor cursor for the holder's own issuer-local Contact lineage, carried only by the ak.self.contact.read.list.v1 projection. The container name carries the tense: version is the version the NEXT Event carries, that is current head version plus one, hence the minimum of 2; predecessor_event_ref is the current lineage head Event ID, that is the predecessor the next Event must name, and never the predecessor of the current head. The three field names are byte-identical to the prepare-phase fields of ak.self.contact.command.scope_update.v1 and ak.self.contact.command.tombstone.v1 and MUST be copied verbatim; a client MUST NOT rename, recompute or derive them, and MUST NOT assemble a successor from request_event_ref, response_event_ref or tombstone_event_ref, which are projection summaries and not authoritative lineage heads. Presence is fixed by contact_state: an accepted row MUST carry it, and a pending_outgoing, pending_incoming, rejected, expired or tombstoned row MUST NOT, because the first two have no basis or lineage yet and the last three are terminal. Absence is the sole encoding of 'no successor is authorable now'; no extra error code or contact_state value expresses it. A stale cursor is refused by prepare with contact_lineage_conflict or contact_scope_stale; the client MUST re-read this operation and retry with the fresh values, and MUST NOT guess a head or retry the same triple.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Immediate previously accepted terminal Contact round for a recontact request. The Station MUST require an exact local terminal-round match when present and MUST require it when a terminal predecessor exists.

continuity_evidence.description: Portable mutually signed prefix checkpoint plus bounded tail. A caller supplies it when the current Station cannot reconstruct the complete lineage locally; the service verifies it and persists the same checkpoint/tail instead of guessing or skipping a predecessor.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Station cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.
External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Station cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.
External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Station cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

block_peer.description: Holder-private commit side effect. true adds the peer to invite receive policy denied_subjects; false only tombstones the Contact lineage. This field is reservation-bound and is not copied into the public Contact Event payload.

control_proposal_ack.description: External-authority receipt set for this Contact Control Move when the receiving Station cannot itself produce the complete current authority quorum.

direct_conversation_summary.description: Contact-list projection of an already materialized stable Direct Conversation. Coordinates and binding identity are immutable; state only says whether the same conversation is currently sendable. Creation progress is exposed only by direct_conversation_resolve_outcome; there is no durable creation operation, draft or reservation.

glare_concurrency_attestation.description: Source-signed evidence that the issuer had accepted both directional request receipts while neither request slot had yet been consumed by a normal response or rejection. Exactly one attestation from each pair member is required by the glare evidence bundle.

response_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted response Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel response_digest is carried.

outgoing_slot_absence_digest.description: Digest binding the responder's local CAS-point slot state showing no outgoing request existed when the normal response was accepted (see identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 4). Self-describing <alg>:<hex>. The canonical preimage for this digest is not yet stated in normative prose; see review/spec-open.

peer_contact_authoritative_mirror_receip.description: Only an accepted or duplicate mirror receipt proves that the immutable signed Contact fact is durably mirrored. A deferred receipt is never authority for proof refresh or glare finalization.

result_digest.description: H('ak.peer-contact.control-result.v1',{request_digest,result_kind,glare_concurrency_attestation?,current_proof?}) over the exact closed successful result.

peer_contact_control_receipt.description: The recipient signs every field except signature. This receipt is only for proof_refresh, glare_finalize or continuity_checkpoint and cannot stand in for a signed Event mirror receipt.

peer_contact_event_submit_outcome.description: Only the five signed Contact Event request kinds use this branch. The receipt event coordinates and result_kind must match the submitted Event exactly. Request/response may return a current proof; accepted or duplicate scope/tombstone must return one; reject and deferred never do.

signed_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the mirrored signed Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; request_digest remains the distinct digest of the peer submit request.

reject_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted reject Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel reject_digest is carried.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Present exactly when this accepted request starts a recontact after a prior accepted Contact round became terminal. It MUST equal the requester-signed ak.contact.requested payload field and is covered by receipt_digest/signature. It is distinct from slot_predecessor, which is the issuer-local request-slot CAS predecessor and can also follow a rejected proposal.

request_event_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted request Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel request_digest is carried.

schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.title: Arkret Poll Content Block
schemas/content-block-poll.schema.json.description: Canonical content-block schema for ak.content.poll and ak.content.poll.response.

poll_answer.description: One visible answer option. answer.id values MUST be unique within a poll; reducers and conformance vectors enforce that cross-item constraint.

poll_body.description: Poll configuration. max_selections is validated against responses by reducers because JSON Schema cannot compare a response to its referenced poll message.

schemas/control-proposal-decision.schema.title: Arkret Control Proposal Ack and Decision
schemas/control-proposal-decision.schema.description: Quorum-capable Control Proposal Acks and signed reject/defer decisions for CBA Control Moves. Deadlines provide bounded authority decisions, never acceptance or Seal finality.

authority_acks.description: Canonical ascending verification_method order. Distinct valid members, not array length, determine quorum.

proofs.description: Canonical ascending verification_method order. Every proof signs the same decision payload and the set independently satisfies the Control Proposal Ack authority quorum.

control_proposal_ack_issue_request.description: Typed authority input used by a local signer or the registered HTTP operation to issue one immutable authority Ack.

control_proposal_decision_submit_request.description: Standard authenticated carrier for a complete signed defer or signed reject. The receiver resolves the durable proposal and its canonical Ack before accepting any decision; request data cannot create or replace those facts.

control_proposal_decision_read_outcome.description: Authenticated observation of the durable proposal/Ack/decision/Seal state. This is a read projection; it cannot synthesize an Ack or clear a pending proposal.

proposal_authority_kind.description: Discriminates ordinary Ack-governed proposals from the narrow authority-authored self-principal PCR Ack-less exception. ak.device.revoke is always control_proposal_ack.

schemas/cursor.schema.json.title: Arkret Cursor
schemas/cursor.schema.json.description:
Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'after', 'before', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Arkret-Wait-For'). Wire form is always ak:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure.

Integrity contract (normative, see client-sync.md §12 and encoding.md §8 / §8.3.1): v1 core uses the stateful opaque-handle form only — body is {v, purpose, issued_at, expires_at, h} where 'h' is an unguessable server-side handle that the issuing server resolves to the bound (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) tuple. Server-side handle lookup IS the integrity check; there is no inline transcript binding to verify on the client side. Servers MUST reject unknown / expired / cross-binding handles with cursor_integrity_invalid.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync / list pagination. Used as 'after' on /account/subscribe, 'before' / 'after' in the JSON content of ak.self.events.read.scan.v1 and ak.peer.events.read.scan.v1 (including its service-to-service federation binding QUERY /_arkret/peer/events), and as response 'prev_cursor' (older direction) / 'next_cursor' (newer direction). prev_cursor / next_cursor carry absolute directional meaning regardless of how the request was issued — see api-conventions.md §7.0. 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Arkret-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). The handle binding (resolved server-side) carries positions for 'stream' or target for 'barrier'; the wire body does not.

issued_at.description: Cursor issuance instant in the canonical Arkret UTC millisecond profile.

expires_at.description: Cursor expiration instant. MUST be in the future when issued. TTL upper bounds (expires_at - issued_at): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days).

h.description: Server-side opaque handle. The issuing server MUST bind this handle to (principal_id, device_id, service_id, filter_digest, purpose, positions, target?, expiry) and MUST be able to revoke it. The handle MUST be unguessable (≥ 128 bits entropy after base64url decoding); minLength=22 enforces that floor mechanically (base64url packs 6 bits per character so 128/6 ≈ 21.33 → at least 22 chars of the [A-Za-z0-9_-] alphabet). Servers MUST reject any unknown / expired / cross-binding handle with `cursor_integrity_invalid`. Handle lookup IS the integrity check — there is no MAC or signature to verify inline. This is the moral equivalent of Matrix `next_batch` / MSC4186 `pos` and satisfies the integrity contract without crypto. Servers SHOULD keep the handle → binding map durable across process restarts (see client-sync.md §12.1): a memory-only table is still integrity-correct (unknown handles fail closed) but turns every restart into a fleet-wide forced full resync. For production-grade deployment profiles (small_team / organization / high_security_organization / sovereign_deployment / sovereign_enclave / isolated_sovereign_network) this durability plus TTL GC is a MUST per client-sync.md §12.1; only personal_node keeps it at SHOULD.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private auxiliary fields (e.g. `_compress` / `_kid` flags). Names MUST start with underscore. In v1 core there is no `_mac` / `_sig` integrity field — handle lookup IS the integrity check — so the underscore namespace is private to the issuing server. `_mac` and `_sig` themselves are explicitly excluded by the top-level `not` clause: a cursor body carrying either MUST be rejected (encoding.md §8.3).

device_message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender endpoint id, device_message_id), where the endpoint id is sender_device_id, sender_agent_id, or sender_id according to the closed sender branch.

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. For a device sender, pair it with sender_device_id and verify that pair against the accepted PCR device projection; for a Native Agent sender it equals sender_agent_id and the signer is anchored by sender_agent_verification_method plus sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. For the restricted Station service branch it MUST equal recipient_principal_id: the holder remains the message principal while sender_id identifies the internal materializer.

sender_device_id.description: Authoring human device. Exactly one sender endpoint branch is present: this field, the complete sender_agent_* triple, or sender_id. A Native Agent runtime has no device identity and MUST NOT be disguised as an ak:device (crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1); the restricted Station materializer likewise has a service identity rather than a fake device. Receivers use the selected endpoint field in the device-message deduplication key.

sender_agent_id.description: Native Agent principal that authored this message. Present exactly when the sender is an Agent runtime, together with sender_agent_verification_method and sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. It equals sender_principal_id; carrying it explicitly is what makes the endpoint branch decidable from the envelope alone, matching the consume / claim_envelope XORs of crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1.

sender_agent_verification_method.description: Verification method the Agent currently signs with. The device branch gets the equivalent from the accepted device projection; without this the receiver would hold an Agent principal id and no way to say which key speaks for it.

sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted Agent key authorization Event that anchors sender_agent_verification_method.

sender_id.description: Station service identity that internally materialized an actor-private update for the holder. This branch is restricted to actor_private_update_kind, sender_principal_id MUST equal recipient_principal_id, and the service id MUST equal the Station identity bound to the recipient's current authenticated self/to-device surface. It is not a bearer delegation and cannot be submitted through ak.self.device_messages.command.send.v1.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

allOf.$comment: Closed sender endpoint XOR: sender_device_id alone, the complete sender_agent_* triple alone, or sender_id alone. Half-filled and mixed branches are rejected.

Only the recipient Station's internal materializer may use the service branch, and only for the closed actor-private update kind set. Principal equality and authenticated service binding are semantic checks described by the normative prose.

actor_private_update_kind.description: Closed DeviceMessageEnvelope.kind set for actor-private sibling-device projection updates. These values are transport discriminators, not Event kinds and never enter shared Realm history.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device_id.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. It MUST be byte-identical to the hpke_key registered for from_device in the current accepted device projection. A responder MUST fail closed on any mismatch and MUST NOT accept an ephemeral key merely because it appeared in a bound SAS verification transcript; SAS authenticates device signing keys, not HPKE sealing keys.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device_id.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {device_message_id, kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned device_message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style device-pairing code bound into a same-principal authorization transcript. It is short-lived, one-time, and locked after ten failed submissions.

new_device_pubkey.description: Canonical PublicKey for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. kid MUST be the requesting ak:device:<uuidv7> id and the key material MUST be carried in key. The {kid, alg, public_key} spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected. The object is later consumed verbatim by ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

challenge_proof.description: Fresh requesting-device proof of possession over the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 transcript, which commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. The receiving authorized device MUST recompute the transcript from the values it displays to the user and verify the signature before treating the requesting device as pairable; it is later submitted verbatim to ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1.

target_attestation.description: Closed accepted_device possession attestation of the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms. It is the same schema and same domain the short-link path uses, because it binds only pairing_challenge_transcript_digest and each path already closes its own challenge transcript. The receiving authorized device MUST rebuild and verify it after the challenge proof, requiring device_id to equal new_device_pubkey.kid, device_public_key_did to decode to the same key as new_device_pubkey.key, and pairing_challenge_transcript_digest to equal the transcript digest it just recomputed; only then may it read hpke_key and algorithms from it and copy device_signature verbatim into the ak.device.authorize payload. It travels only on this out-of-band message and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.

schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.title: Arkret Device Pairing Short-Link DTOs
schemas/device-pairing.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for the server-mediated device-pairing short-link handoff (device-lifecycle.md §2.1.1). These endpoints are unauthenticated: staging mints an account-less pending record, and resolve/status exchange the short handle for pairing material without binding or granting anything until an authenticated device authorizes the pairing.

algorithm_list.description: Algorithm ids supported by the target device, sorted by UTF-8 bytewise order and deduplicated before they enter any transcript.

pairing_nonce.description: base64url CSPRNG nonce carrying at least 128 bits of entropy.

gate_audience_uri.description: Origin of the Account Authority gate surface (gate_account_base_url) this pairing request is bound to. Minted by the staging service; the challenge proof commits to it so a proof cannot be replayed against another Account Authority.

device_pairing_to_device_challenge_trans.description: Transcript inputs the authorizing device forwards for the to-device pairing path, where no server-staged record exists. The Account Authority rebuilds the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 signing input from these values plus its own gate_audience origin and the digest of the submitted new_device_pubkey; it MUST NOT accept a client-supplied gate_audience, because substituting its own origin is exactly what blocks cross-Account-Authority replay. See crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2.

transaction_id.description: Verification transaction id of the ak.key.verification.request that carried this pairing challenge.

expires_at.description: Expiry the proof committed to. The Account Authority MUST reject an elapsed expires_at before it verifies the signature.

device_pairing_challenge_proof.description: Proof of possession of the staged new_device_pubkey, bound to the server-minted pairing challenge. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1\n") || canonical_json({client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 2.1.2. The proof can only be generated after staging returns, because it commits to server-minted values that do not exist at stage time.

transcript.description: Names the exact signing transcript. ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 is the server-mediated short-link path and commits to {client_nonce, device_pairing_request_id, expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, server_nonce}. ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 is the to-device verification path and commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. A verifier MUST select the member set from this discriminator and MUST NOT accept a proof whose transcript name does not match the path it is verifying.

kid.description: MUST equal new_device_pubkey.kid. The proof is verified with the staged new_device_pubkey and with no other key. This is a device-local ak:device key id selecting the staged key (identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 2.3), not a DID URL; it is deliberately not named verification_method.

transcript_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical challenge transcript bytes. The verifier recomputes it from its own staged record and rejects a mismatch before checking the signature.

device_pairing_target_attestation.description: Closed possession attestation the target device produces for the accepted_device pairing path, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms: neither the staged record nor the bootstrap carries them, so the approving device reads them here after the signature verifies and copies them byte-for-byte into the ak.device.authorize payload. Signing input is UTF8("ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json({algorithms, authorization_binding_kind, device_id, device_key_algorithm, device_public_key_did, hpke_key, pairing_challenge_transcript_digest}); see crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.2.2. The object is closed over target-owned material plus this pairing challenge, so the target can build it before it knows which sibling will approve and what principal_id, authorized_by, not_before, expires_at or scopes that sibling will choose; those values are carried by the approving device Event proof instead. It travels only over the out-of-band channel (QR fragment or to-device message) and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface. It is never a wire field of ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1: every member is already recomputable there from the request payload and the Account Authority own challenge transcript.

device_public_key_did.description: Self-describing did:key form of the same Ed25519 key as new_device_pubkey.key. A verifier MUST reject an attestation whose device_public_key_did decodes to different key bytes than the staged or forwarded new_device_pubkey.

hpke_key.description: Target device X25519 HPKE public key. This attestation is its authority; a service MUST NOT supply or substitute it.

authorization_binding_kind.description: This transcript exists only for accepted_device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use their separate full possession objects, and a transcript from one binding kind MUST NOT be accepted for another.

pairing_challenge_transcript_digest.description: MUST equal device_pairing_challenge_proof.transcript_digest of this same pairing challenge. It is the single replay boundary of this attestation: path A commits through it to device_pairing_request_id, pairing_code, gate_audience, expires_at, server_nonce, client_nonce and new_device_pubkey_digest, and path B to transaction_id, request_canonical_digest, expires_at, gate_audience, pairing_code and new_device_pubkey_digest. A verifier MUST recompute the challenge transcript itself and reject a digest that does not match this pairing.

device_signature.description: Ed25519 signature by the private key of device_public_key_did over the canonical signing input above. The approving device MUST copy it byte-for-byte into device_authorize_payload.device_signature and into the pair_device request device_signature.

public_key.description: Canonical PublicKey shape shared with agent-operations. For a staged device the key material is carried in `key` and `kid` is the target `ak:device:<uuid>` id.

device_pairing_state.description: Lifecycle state of a staged device-pairing short-link record. A staged record starts pending_authorization, flips to authorized once an authenticated device completes ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1, and reports expired once its bounded TTL has elapsed.

device_pairing_stage_request_body.description: Unauthenticated stage request that mints a fresh account-less pending pairing record. It carries only the canonical public key and a client nonce: the challenge proof cannot exist yet, because it must commit to the request id, pairing code, expiry, gate audience and server nonce that this call mints. It also deliberately omits hpke_key and algorithms; those reach the approving device inside the signed device_pairing_target_attestation over the out-of-band channel, so the anonymous staging surface never accumulates long-term device key material or a device algorithm fingerprint. The record binds no principal and grants nothing until an authenticated device authorizes it.

device_pairing_stage_outcome.description: Result of staging a device-pairing short-link record. It returns the full server-minted challenge material the new device needs to build the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 proof. pairing_code is a short human-carryable secret; both device_pairing_request_id and pairing_code are the query credential for the resolve/status endpoints and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query string.

device_pairing_resolve_request_body.description: Body-only resolver input for device-pairing short-link handoff. The token is obtained from a URL fragment or equivalent out-of-band channel and MUST NOT be sent in URL path or query.

device_pairing_bootstrap.description: Pairing material handed to an already-authorized device after resolving a device-pairing short link. It carries the server-minted challenge material so the authorized device can recompute the ak.device-pairing.challenge.v1 transcript and verify the proof it received out of band from the new device. It does NOT carry the proof itself, nor the device_pairing_target_attestation, nor the hpke_key and algorithms that attestation signs: the staging surface is unauthenticated and never sees any of them, and mirroring signed values here would only create a second, non-authoritative copy. This is not a session grant, capability grant or long-term secret; the authorized device still drives ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.v1 to complete authorization.

device_pairing_status_request_body.description: Body-only poll for the authorization status of a staged device-pairing record. The device_pairing_request_id + pairing_code pair is the query credential and MUST be sent in the JSON body; a record miss and a pairing_code mismatch MUST be indistinguishable (both not_found).

device_pairing_status_outcome.description: Authorization status for a staged device-pairing record. While the record is still open, state is pending_authorization. Once an authenticated device has authorized this pairing, state is authorized and device_id plus authorized_event_ref are present. An open record whose bounded TTL has elapsed reports state expired.

authorized_event_ref.description: Accepted ak.device.authorize Event id. It is the entry point for the mandatory pre-assembly check in crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 5.4.1: before the target device assembles the identity locally it MUST fetch this Event and confirm byte-identical device_signature, byte-identical device_public_key_did, hpke_key and algorithms, and an expected principal_id, or fail closed.

schemas/device-revocation-state.schema.j.title: Arkret Durable Device Revocation State
schemas/device-revocation-state.schema.j.description: Reducer-owned durable state for an accepted ak.device.revoke Control Move. A revoke is never an Ack-less self-principal PCR Move: accepted Event, canonical ControlProposalAck and this record are committed atomically. The record binds the exact principal authority, device authorization and generation observed at admission; producers cannot author those derived selectors. revocation_pending blocks the five registered action classes on every deployment until the exact proposal is either covered by an accepted Seal or terminated by a valid signed_reject under the same Ack authority contract.

device_revocation_gate_record.description: Gate-relevant durable state for an exact device generation. Rejected records are audit history and are excluded; pending and revoked records remain visible together so sealing one proposal cannot hide another surviving pending proposal.

device_generation_ref.description: Reducer-derived PCR-local monotonic current device-generation selector. A producer MUST NOT self-report it and it MUST NOT equal or be derived from a DID versionId.

denied_actions.description: Closed canonical action-class list blocked by revocation_pending on every deployment.

target_device_authorize_event_id.description: Reducer-derived accepted ak.device.authorize Event targeted by this proposal.

accepted_at.description: Actual durable atomic-commit time assigned when the Event, canonical Ack, derived selectors and pending index commit. It is independent of, and MUST NOT be copied from, a pre-collected ControlProposalAck.received_at.

acceptance_seq.description: Monotonic sequence assigned by the origin Station in the same atomic commit as accepted_at and the pending index.

control_proposal_ack.description: Mandatory canonical Ack committed with the accepted revoke. ak.device.revoke is excluded from the authority-authored Ack-less exception. Ack.received_at records Ack issuance and is not the pending record's accepted_at.

terminal_decision.description: The only transition that clears this proposal's pending gate. Its proposal_digest and proposal_ack_digest MUST match this record, and its verified authority set MUST be the Ack authority set.

device_revocation_gate_check_request_bod.description: Authenticated S2S request from an Account Authority or another registered issuer to the exact origin Station. The exact authorization Event and PCR-local generation are derived from the origin's locked durable current device projection. expected selectors are issuer-verified, appear together or not at all, and MAY be omitted only for session_grant_issue or returning_session_grant_issue. returning_session_grant_issue and human session_grant_refresh require AcceptedDevicePossessionProof; registration/recovery session_grant_issue uses its already verified durable root/recovery evidence and forbids that proof. The intent digest identifies immutable prepared issuance or refresh bytes.

intent_digest.description: Digest of the complete immutable issue or refresh intent, including the exact grant id, jti, subject, device, audience, scope, holder binding, issued_at and expiry. Session-grant introspection is read-only issuer-ledger verification and never consumes this receipt.

accepted_device_possession_proof.description: Required only for returning_session_grant_issue and human session_grant_refresh. The origin verifies it with the accepted device key from the same locked durable projection used to decide current authorization. Registration/recovery session_grant_issue and Agent runtime issuers MUST omit it.

device_revocation_gate_decision_receipt.description: Origin-Station-signed durable linearization receipt. Under the same database lock/serializable transaction used to accept ak.device.revoke, the origin derives the current authorization Event and generation from its own durable projection, compares them with any expected binding in the request, and atomically records (action_class,intent_digest) at linearization_seq before signing. Derivation is a partial function: a device with no current accepted authorization has no derived selector and returns authority_mismatch; authorization_absent is deliberately not a separate decision. Only an allow carries the derived target_device_authorize_event_id and target_device_generation_ref, and that pair is the sole source for the issued grant's device_binding; the issuer MUST copy it verbatim and MUST NOT accept a binding from client input. No other decision discloses the derived binding, so a generation_mismatch cannot be turned into a silent re-issue at the new generation. Exact replay returns byte-identical output. An allow records that exact immutable issue/refresh intent as lawfully admitted before any later revocation_pending transition; a later pending transition blocks only intents linearized after it. The issuer MUST atomically commit the same immutable intent plus this receipt before expires_at and MUST NOT mint a new/different intent after pending. The receipt authorizes no different intent and cannot be refreshed or reused after expiry. An unauthorized caller, an account this service does not host, an unknown or not-currently-authorized device and a device outside the named account all return the same authority_mismatch. A malformed internal row that claims to be current/verified while omitting its authorization Event or generation is an integrity failure, not an authorization-absence decision. A block can name pending/revoked without disclosing any other private device state.

target_device_authorize_event_id.description: Origin-derived current device authorization Event. Present only for allow.

target_device_generation_ref.description: Origin-derived current device generation. Present only for allow.

accepted_device_possession_proof_digest.description: Present for human SessionGrant issue/refresh allow or block after proof validation; SHA-256 of the exact canonical AcceptedDevicePossessionProof. It cryptographically binds the gate decision to the proof verified under the locked current accepted-device key.

linearization_seq.description: Monotonic sequence from the origin Station's durable device-revocation log.

expires_at.description: Hard receipt-use deadline no later than 30 seconds after linearized_at. It is a freshness bound, not a cache TTL and not a revocation deadline.

blocking_proposal_digest.description: For revocation_pending, the lexicographically smallest proposal_digest among all surviving pending records for the exact device/generation at linearization_seq. This deterministic witness does not imply that no other pending record exists.

covering_seal_id.description: For revoked, the covering Seal of the revoked record with the smallest (acceptance_seq, proposal_digest) among all revoked records for the exact device/generation at linearization_seq.

proof.description: Origin Station signature with context ak.device_revocation_gate_decision_proof.v1. payload_digest MUST equal sha256(JCS(the complete receipt with proof omitted)); proof.verification_method MUST equal receipt.verification_method; proof.created_at MUST equal linearized_at; and the verification-method controller projected to Core MUST equal account_id.station_id.

schemas/did-binding-contracts.schema.jso.title: Arkret Verified DID Binding Contracts
schemas/did-binding-contracts.schema.jso.description: Canonical shapes behind identity/did-usage-and-verification.md section 5: the retained evidence receipt whose digest is the binding's evidence_digest, the resolver policy snapshot whose digest is the binding's policy_digest, the mechanically extracted evidence dependency record used for selective invalidation, the limited-trust pin record, and the freshness profile row every authority call site references. These objects are trust-domain-local: the contracts guarantee recomputability and change-sensitivity, not cross-deployment digest equality.

method_token.description: Canonical lowercase DID method token (W3C DID 1.0 method-name), e.g. key, web, webvh.

normalized_did_document_metadata.description: Closed Arkret metadata projection. primary_handle is a holder preference pointer only; it never creates a handle claim or authorization.

normalized_did_document_extension.description: One lossless extension property from the verified DID Document. Rows are sorted by name in unsigned UTF-8 byte order and duplicate names are rejected. A name that collides with a registered known member is invalid rather than shadowing that member.

normalized_did_verification_method.description: Canonical Arkret projection of one DID verification method. public_key_material is the lossless canonical JSON object containing the registered method-specific public-key members; extensions retains every other member. Rows are sorted by verification_method and duplicate or conflicting verification methods are rejected before projection.

normalized_did_service.description: Canonical Arkret projection of one DID service entry. uri preserves the W3C service id as a generic URI (not an Arkret stable object id); protocol_names is the sorted, duplicate-free projection of the W3C type set; endpoint retains its complete canonical JSON value. Arkret-defined names and endpoint shapes are closed by did-document-contract-registry.json.

normalized_did_document.description: The sole canonical normalized DID Document projection used by document_digest. It retains every v1-normative member, including also_known_as and metadata.primary_handle, and losslessly retains unknown extensions. contexts preserves source order because JSON-LD context order can affect interpretation; every other set-like array is sorted in unsigned UTF-8 order with duplicates rejected. Duplicate/conflicting source properties, ids, relationship entries, services, metadata keys, or extension names fail before digesting. document_digest is exactly sha256:lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(this object))); raw resolver bytes use raw_document_digest and no third DID-document digest name exists.

items.description: Canonical URI validated by the DID resolver before projection; this array may contain non-network schemes such as acct: and therefore is not a URL field.

normalized_did_relationship.description: Sorted duplicate-free relationship references. Every entry must identify a method present in verification_methods; embedded W3C methods are first hoisted into verification_methods and then referenced here.

evidence_receipt.description: Canonical evidence receipt. evidence_digest = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(evidence_receipt))). The receipt MUST be retained so an auditor can recompute the digest; a method without proofs degrades to an empty method_proofs array (a document-bound receipt), never to an implementation-invented placeholder. Unknown method or proof kinds fail closed.

document_digest.description: Digest of the resolver's verified normalized DID Document projection (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.1); never the raw response bytes (those use the differently named raw_document_digest).

method_proofs.description: Closed per-method proof rows; empty for proofless methods (did:key, bare did:web). v1 registers exactly one row kind (webvh_log); receiving any unregistered proof kind fails closed. Rows never reuse resolver response order: each row kind registers its own canonical sort and duplicate-rejection rules.

webvh_log_evidence.description: did:webvh method evidence row. witnesses are sorted by witness_did (UTF-8 byte order) with duplicates rejected; witness_proofs_digest commits to the canonical raw witness proof set so the receipt stays change-sensitive to any witness signature change.

history_head.description: The verified webvh log head (versionId / entry-hash form) this binding pinned.

witnesses.description: Sorted by witness_did, UTF-8 byte order; duplicates rejected. These rows double as the evidence dependency coordinates for selective invalidation.

resolver_policy_snapshot.description: Canonical resolver policy snapshot. policy_digest = "sha256:" + lowercase_hex(SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(policy_snapshot))). The snapshot MUST be retainable and rebuildable so auditors can recompute the digest and verify that any security-relevant configuration change necessarily changes it. Enum values MUST use the registered wire tokens below; language-native debug formats are forbidden. accepted_did_methods and trust_roots are sorted by UTF-8 byte order with duplicates rejected; strings receive no Unicode normalization.

policy_profile.description: Registered resolver policy profile id; the schema discriminator for profile_policy. v1 registers ak.did_resolver_policy_profile.base.v1 (empty closed profile_policy). A deployment introducing extra policy dimensions MUST register its own profile with an additionalProperties:false schema listing every configuration field that changes resolution, verification, network boundaries, size limits or degradation behavior as required. Unknown profiles, unknown fields, and missing registered fields all fail closed.

profile_policy.description: Profile-specific dimensions validated by the closed schema the policy_profile registers; the base profile requires exactly the empty object. Any change here changes the digest, so section 5 invalidation obligations are preserved for deployment-specific knobs.

evidence_dependencies.description: Structured dependency record mechanically extracted from the evidence receipt (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.6). It answers 'which bindings depend on witness X / log head H' — a mapping a digest cannot provide because digests are one-way. Proofless methods produce the empty record.

witness_dids.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

witness_controlling_organization_dids.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

history_heads.description: Sorted, deduplicated; empty for proofless methods.

limited_trust.description: Per-pin limited-trust record (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.5). Omitted entirely when both pins are present; when present, each state MUST be consistent with the actual presence of the corresponding pin field. method_unsupported is a legitimate terminal state (did:key has no history); not_surfaced marks a resolver that failed to surface evidence its method supports and is treated as a failure state, not a normal audit note.

freshness_profile.description: One registered freshness profile row (did-usage-and-verification.md section 5.4). Every DID authority call site references exactly one freshness_profile_id through its operation/action registration; natural-language tier guessing is forbidden. Deployments declare their rows in machine-readable form and the declared snapshot enters profile_policy of the resolver policy snapshot, so changing any number structurally invalidates existing bindings. Tier constraints (finite windows, ordering, stale behavior) are normative in section 5.4.

did_method_selector.description: did:<method>: prefixes this row applies to, or the single wildcard "*".

fresh_for_seconds.description: The single freshness threshold: refresh_after = verified_at + fresh_for_seconds, and the authority call's max_age MUST equal the same value — two separately maintained constants are forbidden.

schemas/did-webvh-witness-receipt.schema.title: Arkret did:webvh Witness Receipt
schemas/did-webvh-witness-receipt.schema.description: Arkret-layer, cacheable and auditable record that a named did:webvh witness was observed attesting a specific log version. It is deliberately a separate object family from ak.schema.identity_receipt.v1: that one records a role (writer / witness / replica) inside a DID registry consensus group and binds seq + head_event_digest, whereas this one binds a did:webvh method versionId and a witness did:key drawn from parameters.witness. Overloading one object with both meanings would leave half its required fields meaningless on either branch and force verifiers to guess which sense of the word witness applies. This receipt NEVER substitutes for method conformance: a verifier MUST still fetch and verify the standard did-witness.json proofs, the entry hash chain and the controller proof. See zh/identity/identity-did.md.

schema.description: Closed discriminator. ak.root.identity.receipts.read.list.v1 returns a tagged union of receipt families; this constant is what lets a verifier pick the did:webvh method-witness branch instead of the registry consensus branch without guessing.

subject_did.description: Subject DID. Restricted to did:webvh because the object binds method-native did:webvh state; other methods need their own receipt family rather than a widened pattern here.

version_id.description: The exact did:webvh versionId this attestation covers, verbatim from the log entry. Binding to versionId rather than to a digest of the document is what makes the receipt replayable against did-witness.json, whose proofs are themselves keyed by versionId.

log_head_digest.description: Optional digest of the log head the issuer held when observing. Present it when the issuer can commit to the whole log state; it lets a consumer detect a split view that a per-version binding alone would not reveal.

witness_did.description: The attesting witness, which MUST be one of the parameters.witness.witnesses[].id values in force at version_id. did:webvh 1.0 constrains witness identifiers to did:key, so a receipt naming any other form is describing something that is not a method witness.

witness_verification_method.description: The specific verification method inside witness_did whose signature appears in did-witness.json for version_id.

controlling_organization_did.description: The organization that controls this witness, as resolved by the issuer. Arkret deployment policy counts distinct controlling organizations, not distinct witness keys; without this field an operator running several witness keys would satisfy a two-distinct-organization requirement by itself. A verifier that cannot independently verify this binding MUST fail closed on high-risk paths rather than count the witness.

observed_at.description: When the issuer actually fetched or observed the witness proof. Freshness is evaluated against this instant, not against created_at: an issuer could otherwise re-sign a years-old observation and present it as current.

source_url.description: Optional origin the proof was read from (the DID's own did-witness.json or a declared mirror). Recorded so a consumer can tell a first-party read from a mirrored one when adjudicating conflicting receipts.

issuer_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Arkret service issuing this receipt. This is the trust root for the receipt itself, and is unrelated to the DID's own controller.

trust_domain.description: Optional trust domain the receipt is scoped to.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

expires_at.description: Required. An Arkret-layer cache record without an expiry becomes indistinguishable from a permanent assertion, which is precisely how stale witness evidence outlives the state it described. MUST be later than created_at, and a consumer MUST treat an expired receipt as absent rather than as weak evidence.

signature.description: Issuer detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.did_webvh_witness_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, issuer_id, did, version_id, witness_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid assertion method controlled by issuer_id. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

schemas/direct-conversation-operations.s.title: Arkret Direct Conversation Operations
schemas/direct-conversation-operations.s.description: Closed carriers for the Direct Conversation resolver and single-sided founding. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_coordinates.description: Permanent Direct Conversation coordinates. binding_event_ref appears only from found or suspended onward; it is absent while the pair is still provisional.

direct_conversation_founding_acceptance_.description: Source-signed evidence that the founder current Station atomically accepted exactly one Direct Conversation founding unit and closed its local unique slot. It creates no Realm, authorizes no Message and is not a global slot; a second receipt for the same pair and founder but a different unit is direct_conversation_pair_materialization_conflict evidence. proof signs the closed transcript H("ak.direct-conversation.founding-receipt.v1", this object without proof); the receiver recomputes that preimage from the receipt fields and never trusts a carried digest. proof.verification_method resolves to the issuer_id current service key at accepted_at and proof.created_at equals accepted_at.

founder_id.description: Exact founder ActorId. A bare principal DID is insufficient because the same principal hosted by two Stations denotes two distinct account authorities.

agent_provision_ref.description: Complete identity of the accepted Agent provision Event. Its digest is derived by decoding this suite-tagged full-digest EventId; no parallel agent_provision_digest is carried.

direct_conversation_founding_input.description: Verbatim authoring material for the founding unit the caller is now entitled to author, carried only by the creation_required outcome. Member names equal the DirectConversationFoundingUnitSubmission members byte for byte, so the caller copies them across without any renaming map (service-http-binding.md 2.2.2 echo-container discipline). The caller still authors and signs all four Events itself; this container never carries Event bytes, coordinates or a receipt. Material that the service cannot assemble or verify yields temporarily_unavailable instead of a creation_required outcome without it.

founding_authority_evidence.description: The human branch for a peer Contact founding and the controller_agent branch for an own-Agent founding; the service selects the branch that matches this pair and never returns both.

direct_conversation_resolve_outcome.description: Closed tagged outcome of ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve.v1. Evaluation order is fixed: temporarily_unavailable when the current basis or founder cannot be verified; then creation_blocked, creation_required or awaiting_founder while no Realm exists; then suspended for identity, materialization, terminal or gate conflicts; then provisional while no binding endorsement exists; found last. awaiting_founder never transfers authority by timeout, recovery policy, successor designation or permanent-unavailability inference; v1 defines no founder_unrecoverable state.

group_state_digest.description: Digest of the unique derived MLS group's exact current winning Genesis/Commit state. The ref and digest are supplied or omitted as one pair.
Digest of the exact current winning group-state Event, not a second group selector.
Present with group_state_ref whenever the unique derived group has an accepted current state.

direct_conversation_resolve_request.description: Closed query body for ak.self.direct_conversation.read.resolve.v1. Creation is never carried here: a Direct Conversation Realm is created only by the derived founder through the direct_conversation_genesis admission variant of ak.realm.create.

direct_conversation_send_blocker.description: Closed machine-readable blocker set surfaced by the Direct Conversation resolver. Every value MUST be server-verifiable: the service MUST be able to prove it from accepted authoritative state it may lawfully read, and it MUST NOT guess, decrypt or relay a client self-report. personal_blocked and history_key_unavailable are deliberately absent and MUST NOT be re-added: ak.account.blocklist is holder-private account data that a synchronizing service only ever sees encrypted to holder devices, and whether a historical MLS secret is installed is device-private key state, so a service that answered either one would have to break the encryption invariant or accept an unauthenticated claim as authority. They live in the client-local blocker set of ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 instead, and a reply carrying either value is a schema_violation the client MUST reject rather than tolerate. presence_offline and keypackage_empty stay here because the service does hold provable facts for them, but they MUST be returned only to an existing exact-pair participant of that very pair; every other caller MUST receive the same opaque failure as for a pair that does not exist, so neither value can be used to enumerate or probe a non-participant. Values never disclose peer presence to non-participants.

schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Directory Operation DTOs
schemas/directory-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for Directory discovery search, resolve, private contact discovery, handle lookup, agent selector lookup, and push webhook registration operations.

proof.description: Directory requester proof leaf. Reuses the generic non-Event detached-JWS wire shape while closing the audience, domain, and purpose choices for the directory read surface: audience MUST be the target Directory service_id returned by ak.find.directory.read.describe.v1, in single-valued did_core_id form (the did:<method>:<msi> form and array audiences are invalid for this object family), and domain / proof_purpose MUST be absent. Canonical binding, signer authority, and freshness rules are defined in discovery-directory.md section 9.0.1.
proof.$comment: Every request family that carries requester proofs declares its own proofs array inline so that each object family owns a distinct detached-proof node with its own registered context (discovery-directory.md section 9.0.1); a single shared proofs alias would put unrelated operations under one domain separation. The audience narrowing lives on this shared leaf so that all five directory request families are gated by one mechanical constraint.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the issuer key that signed this presentation; its controller MUST equal iss.

source_refs.description: Event ids this entry was derived from, so a consumer can go back to the truth source and verify it. Omit the member entirely when the entry has no Event provenance: an implementation MUST NOT synthesize an id for an Event it never authored, and MUST NOT send an empty array to stand in for one. minItems stays 1 so a present array cannot fake compliance.

verified_badge.description: Public organization verification badge suitable for directory preview rendering.

member_count.description: Public exact organization member count when the organization directory policy permits exact counts.
