realm_ids.description: Public Realm ids linked to this organization when the organization directory policy permits Realm fan-out preview.

realm_count.description: Count of public Realm ids linked to this organization.

directory_resolve_handle_request_body.description: Resolve a canonical handle. For restricted handle claims, requester / proofs / claim_presentations / audience / realm_id are authorization inputs; services MUST use indistinguishable denial for anonymous or unauthorized restricted, revoked, rate-limited, and not-found cases.

controller_handle.description: Canonical controller handle string without the @ sigil.

controller_subject_id.description: Controller principal DID resolved from controller_handle and verified against the selector claim.

subject_id.description: Native personal agent principal DID selected by (controller_subject, agent_slug).

directory_list_handles_for_subject_reque.description: List currently visible handle claims for a subject. The service MUST apply the same visibility, audience, requester proof, rate-limit, and indistinguishable-denial rules as resolve_handle; absence of a returned handle is not proof the subject has none.

psi_ristretto255_element.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 32-byte RFC 9497 ristretto255 element. Decoders MUST additionally reject non-canonical group encodings and the identity element.

psi_voprf_proof.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of one 64-byte RFC 9497 batched DLEQ proof (two 32-byte scalars).

psi_derived_prefix_16.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the v1 fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix.

psi_response_padding.description: ASCII SP padding. The origin serializes the complete response with RFC 8785 JCS as UTF-8, omits Content-Encoding and applies no content coding, and chooses this value so the HTTP entity body Content-Length exactly equals the phase bucket declared by ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

psi_padded_problem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details shape for private-contact-discovery Class B failures. padding is the only extension member. The selected type, title, and status triple is canonical and must match error-code-registry.json.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The closed PSI projection preserves the RFC literal member vocabulary; instance remains the RFC URI-reference member rather than an Arkret-owned identifier role.

psi_batch_id.description: Client-generated UUIDv7 typed batch id correlating the blind and match rounds of one logical PSI query. It is unique within the authenticated device credential and is bound to canonical request digests for replay-safe quota charging.

psi_blind_request_body.description: Round 1 of the §6.2 two-round OPRF set-membership PSI: the client submits blinded connection identifiers. PSI window quota is enforced here; denial is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard RFC 9457 Problem Details, never a 200 outcome.

ciphersuite.description: Exact RFC 9497 ciphersuite identifier. The ak.private_contact_discovery.v1 profile fixes the separate RFC protocol mode to modeVOPRF (0x01).

blinded_elements.description: Client-padded batch. Cardinality MUST equal ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.batch_item_count; real and dummy elements are indistinguishable to the provider.

psi_match_request_body.description: Round 2 of the §6.2 two-round PSI: the client submits one fixed 16-byte derived digest prefix for every element of the admitted blind batch, preserving cardinality and order. An admitted batch_id MUST NOT be quota-denied at this phase.

derived_prefixes.description: Each entry is the fixed 16-byte prefix of the corresponding unblinded VOPRF output digest. Cardinality and order MUST equal the admitted blind request.

directory_private_contact_discovery_requ.description: Two-round OPRF set-membership PSI request (zh/discovery/discovery-directory.md §6.2/§6.3); the phase field discriminates the round.

invite_consent_handoff_stub.description: Minimal invite/consent handoff stub allowed beside PSI match bits. It declares state or next-step guidance only; it MUST NOT carry a contact request token, reachability proof, profile, membership, or read grant.

state_digest.description: If present, MUST be salted per requester/session or replaced by an audience-bound opaque token per consent-model.md §6.2.

psi_blind_outcome.description: Round 1 success outcome: VOPRF evaluations over the fixed-size submitted batch plus one RFC 9497 batched proof. evaluated_elements MUST be same-length and same-order as the request's blinded_elements.

evaluation_proofs.description: Exactly one RFC 9497 batched VOPRF DLEQ proof covering the entire fixed-size evaluated_elements array. The client verifies it with the public key for this key_epoch from ServiceDescribe.private_contact_discovery.

derived_prefix_bytes.description: Fixed byte length of every round-2 derived_prefixes entry in the v1 profile.

psi_match_outcome.description: Round 2 success outcome: fixed-cardinality hit bitmap (dummy-padded to the provider-enforced batch_item_count). Per-target conditions (nonexistent, undiscoverable, per-target policy-denied, OPRF mismatch) are encoded as unmatched bits and MUST NOT surface as distinct fields, codes, or timing (§6.4 Class A).

handoff_stubs.description: Optional minimal invite/consent handoff stubs. If present, MUST have the same cardinality as hit_bitmap, with dummy stubs (e.g. state="unknown") at unmatched positions so the field shape does not reveal hits.

directory_private_contact_discovery_outc.description: Two-round PSI success outcomes, discriminated by phase. PSI quota denial is NOT an outcome shape: it is HTTP 429 psi_quota_exhausted in the standard RFC 9457 Problem Details at the blind phase, padded to the success-path size bucket and delay class (§6.4 Class B).

schemas/dnd-schedule.schema.json.title: Arkret DND Schedule Account Data
schemas/dnd-schedule.schema.json.description: Closed decrypted plaintext shape for ak.dnd_schedule. Period ordering, IANA canonical-name validation, overlap/adjacency rejection, and tzdb equality are semantic validation steps in addition to this schema.

timezone.description: Canonical case-sensitive IANA zone name; aliases and the token local are forbidden by semantic validation.

schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.title: Arkret Draft Sync Account Data
schemas/draft-sync.schema.json.description: Encrypted account-data plaintext shape for ak.profile.draft_sync.v1.

schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Encrypted Payload Envelope
schemas/encrypted-envelope.schema.json.description: Minimal ciphertext wire. purpose, effective scope and Event kind come from the frozen signed outer Event; mls_group_id is derived from that scope; content_scheme comes from the exact referenced winning group state. The canonical pre-encryption header is reconstructed and is not duplicated on wire.

routing_context.description: Present only for a registered reaction outer Event kind. The reaction kind and routing_window=floor(unix_ms(outer.created_at)/3600000) are derived inputs to AAD/KDF and never wire fields. All non-reaction kinds forbid routing_context.

standard_mls_encryption_context.description: The absence of counter is the structural standard-MLS branch. The referenced winning group state MUST have content_scheme=mls_rfc9420.

exporter_mls_encryption_context.description: The required full-width counter is the structural exporter branch. The referenced winning group state MUST have content_scheme=mls_exporter_aead_v1.

encryption_context.description: Closed branch selected by counter presence and cross-checked against the content_scheme frozen by the exact group_state_ref. No caller-supplied scheme selector exists.

schemas/erasure-receipt-operations.schem.title: Arkret Erasure Receipt Operations
schemas/erasure-receipt-operations.schem.description: Typed service-to-service submit, acceptance and retrieval carriers for hard-erasure receipts and their exact retained verification stubs.

erasure_receipt_package.description: Self-contained acceptance package. retained_stub is carried exactly once at package level and receipt.retained_stub MUST be absent. The receiver computes H('ak.erasure-receipt.v1', receipt) for addressing and acceptance; retained_stub_digest MUST equal SHA-256(RFC8785_JCS(retained_stub)).

erasure_receipt_submit_request_body.description: Canonical body of ak.peer.erasure_receipt.command.submit.v1. Idempotency-Key is a required signed HTTP header and is not duplicated in the body.

erasure_receipt_acceptance.description: Receiver-signed acceptance. proof signs H('ak.erasure-receipt-acceptance.v1', this object without proof). A duplicate reuses the original accepted_at and byte-identical acceptance object.

erasure_receipt_resource.description: Result of ak.peer.erasure_receipt.resource.get.v1. The package is byte-identical in semantic content to the accepted submit package; no later lookup may substitute another retained stub.

schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.title: Arkret Erasure Receipt
schemas/erasure-receipt.schema.json.description: Signed attestation that an issuer completed, partially completed, or blocked a hard-erasure request within a declared storage boundary. It proves the issuer's deletion action and retained verification stub, not disappearance of independent third-party copies.

trigger.description: Exact authoritative fact that created this physical-erasure execution. Account erasure uses the account_status_record branch; other Event-authorized erasure uses the event branch.

scope.description: Boundary in which deletion was attempted. This MUST be narrow enough for an auditor to tell which service/storage class made the claim.

retained_stub_digest.description: Hash of the retained verification stub after erasure: hash(canonical_json(retained_stub)). The stub verifies typed-reference structure, redundant digest consistency, receipt/stub binding, and linkage to retained external proof, Seal, redaction-authorization, and legal-hold evidence. It does not independently verify erased canonical Event bytes.

retained_stub.description: Optional in-band verification stub. When omitted, the issuer MUST expose the same canonical stub via its erasure receipt endpoint; retained_stub_digest still binds the exact bytes.

fanout_status.description: Cross-Station erasure receipt fanout aggregate status tracked by the issuing server (models/realm-and-space.md §2.6.2). 'pending' = peers still within erasure_propagation_window_ms and not all acknowledged; 'complete' = every peer that ever held this Realm's content returned a receipt; 'incomplete' = at least one peer failed to acknowledge within erasure_propagation_window_ms. The issuing server MUST surface 'incomplete' to audit/UI and MUST NOT silently swallow it. Absent on receipts that do not drive fanout tracking.

peer_receipts.description: Per-peer fanout acknowledgement records maintained by the issuing server: one entry per peer Station that ever held this Realm's content. Each entry records that peer's acknowledgement status and time, backing the aggregate fanout_status.

status.description: 'pending' = awaiting this peer's feedback receipt; 'acknowledged' = peer returned a receipt (regardless of its outcome); 'failed' = peer reported a non-completed feedback outcome (partially_completed / blocked_by_legal_hold); 'timed_out' = no feedback within erasure_propagation_window_ms.

receipt_id.description: The peer's own feedback receipt id, when received.

schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.title: Arkret Erasure Verification Stub
schemas/erasure-verification-stub.schema.description: Minimal retained verification stub bound by erasure-receipt.retained_stub_digest. It preserves event graph, proof, seal, redaction, legal-hold and receipt linkage evidence without retaining erased plaintext.

event_digest.description: Optional redundant digest for an Event subject. Its suite and all 32 digest octets MUST exactly match the suite wire code and digest carried by subject.subject_ref. If omitted, the suite and digest are recovered from the Event ID. This field and the Event ID preserve consistency evidence; neither independently verifies erased canonical Event bytes.

trigger.description: Exact closed trigger copied byte-for-byte from the receipt.

events.description: Canonical set projection of covered Events. Every item carries the canonical Event ID, whose 33-octet token losslessly encodes the suite and full digest, plus the verified Event kind. Items MUST be strictly increasing by the UTF-8 bytes of canonical_json(item); producers sort and deduplicate before signing, and receivers reject a non-canonical wire array before digest verification.

proofs.description: Detached receipt proofs sign canonical_json({context:'ak.receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest: receipt_digest, issuer, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag, not a wire field.

allOf.$comment: A PCR genesis receipt is a canonical set containing exactly one realm create and one founding device authorize item. Array position has no domain meaning.

A device re-anchor receipt is a canonical set containing exactly one reanchor and one replacement authorize item. Each typed item carries the canonical Event ID, from which its suite-bearing digest is derived; array position has no domain meaning.

device_reanchor_scope.description: Durable acceptance evidence for an account-local PCR-policy re-anchor unit. The authority pair plus monotonic device generation selects the create-once lineage maintained by the Station.

station_id.description: Account authority Station; together with principal_id it must equal the covered re-anchor Event authority pair.

previous_device_generation.description: MUST equal the covered ak.device.reanchor payload previous_device_generation.

new_device_generation.description: Accepted monotonic successor generation. It MUST equal the covered ak.device.reanchor payload new_device_generation and MUST be the immediate successor of previous_device_generation. It is a PCR-local ref and MUST NOT be derived from or rendered as a DID versionId.

pcr_genesis_scope.description: Durable acceptance evidence for the create-once PCR genesis unit. The covered typed Event IDs are calculated only after both Events are fully formed and never enter either Event preimage.

did_version_id.description: The exact method-native version identifier pinned by the identity-root control proof. It identifies verified DID control evidence and MUST NOT initialize or otherwise determine the PCR-local device generation.

log_head_digest.description: The exact verified DID history head digest accepted for this PCR genesis.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the active identity-root control key pinned by the control proof.

registration_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of RFC 8785 JCS of the complete accepted registration_did_evidence relayed to the Station.

schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Event Envelope
schemas/event-envelope.schema.json.description: Single canonical wire object for durable and actor-private Events. kind + schema-validated payload is the only producer-authored business fact; reducer cell targets and lattice operations are derived from the registered reducer contract and never supplied on wire. DataEvents carry seal_ref/auth_context; Control Moves carry seal_basis and optional preconditions. proof.event_digest hashes canonical producer bytes, including the complete actor_id, after removing proofs, unsigned, and the sole reducer-stamped top-level field actor_kind. Signed scope_ref is included in the digest and is independently checked against payload-derived security scope. Signal uses signal-envelope.schema.json; point-to-point device verification and secret distribution use device-message.schema.json.

kind.description: Standard ak.* Event kinds MUST appear in artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json. State convergence is defined by the registered pure reducer over kind + payload; producers do not submit cell writes.

scope_ref.description: Required producer-signed security scope. The closed union is ordinary existing realm, circle, or native sidecar scope plus the create-only realm_genesis exception. It enters proof.event_digest and E2EE AAD. Reducers independently derive the exact scope from schema-validated payload and accepted references; missing dependencies, nonexistent scope, realm_id mismatch, omitted sidecar_id, substituting circle for sidecar, or any unequal field is fail closed. Sidecar domain Event kinds remain Extension-owned; recognizing this native security shape does not make Kernel interpret the Sidecar reducer. Exact product targets remain inside recipient-visible ciphertext.

actor_id.description: Complete identity of the principal whose Realm/cell state the Event mutates and to whom the durable fact is attributed. Account and hosted-principal variants carry their Station namespace inside actor_id; a service variant carries the directly authoring service identity. When executed_by is absent, the proof signer maps to actor_id. When executed_by is present, actor_id remains the principal of record while the actual executor and proof signer map to executed_by.

executed_by.description: Optional complete identity of the actual executor for a delegated write. This covers both an agent/applet/service acting for a controller actor and a controller acting under explicit managed-principal delegation to write an Agent principal's control state. actor_id is always the principal of record; executed_by is the principal that issued and signed the wire write. When present, MUST appear together with authorization_ref. Applet delegated writes also MUST carry applet_id. Enters canonical event bytes, event digest, and E2EE AAD. Receivers MUST verify that the proof verification method and admission evidence map to the exact executed_by variant (not actor_id) and MUST NOT synthesize an actor_id signature.

authorization_ref.description: Optional. Required when executed_by is present. Prefer a materialized ak:grant:* id; an event id is allowed only when it points to the accepted grant/delegation event that produced the effective authorization; a DID-document delegation URL (did_delegation_ref) is allowed when the delegation is expressed in the principal DID document; realm_authority_root_ref designates this Realm's registered authority-root cell. Exactly two non-grant profile sources are admitted here: direct_conversation_participant_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference, and direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_ref, paired with one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_founding_unit Event reference for the pre-binding founding phase. An arbitrary Event/cell MUST NOT be treated as participant authority. When executed_by is present, authorization_ref binds the executor delegation instead and the DM profile source is evaluated as an independent conjunctive profile gate.

applet_id.description: Optional signed Applet provenance. Required by ak.profile.applet_* when the Event is introduced by an Applet, Ghost Actor, bridge, or delegated applet path. Enters canonical event bytes and therefore is covered by proof.event_digest. When present, authorization_ref MUST also be present and MUST bind this applet_id and registration_epoch per zh/extensions/applet-integration.md section 11.

external_ref.description: Optional signed external provenance reference for Applet / bridge-originated Events. It is covered by event_digest and MUST NOT be carried only in unsigned when used for loop prevention, audit, or external-message idempotency. Must not contain unauthorized external plaintext.

actor_kind.description: Reducer-stamped projection of the actor_id Actor Profile's actor_kind at write time (see zh/models/event-and-patch.md and zh/models/actor.md). Lets audit/forensic/offline readers classify the event without resolving Actor Profile. Does NOT include 'device': a device is not an actor principal and never appears as actor_id; device actions are attributed to the owning user/organization principal DID. MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied submit payload (schema_violation reason=actor_kind_reducer_managed); reducer stamps it during accept. Immutable once written and excluded from producer proof.event_digest.

hlc.description: Advisory hybrid logical clock. INCLUDED in canonical bytes for signing and event digest (so it is integrity-protected and cannot be rewritten by relays), but semantically advisory: used only as a deterministic tiebreaker for timeline display when two events are causally unreachable. MUST NOT influence authorization, lattice join, Control Move precondition comparison, or Seal finality. See encoding.md §7 and event-auth-state-resolution.md §3 rule 1.

prev_refs.description: Actor-chain causal predecessors as complete Event IDs. Each Event ID carries the digest suite code and all 32 digest octets and is committed by this Event's digest preimage. For semantic refs (authorized_by, after, state_witness, inclusion_proof, ...), use refs[].

refs.description: Semantic refs with role. did_recovery_anchor is reserved exclusively for ak.device.reanchor and is enforced bidirectionally below; all other common roles remain open extension tokens.

causal_refs.description: DataEvent semantic causal predecessors by event_digest. A DataEvent carrying payload.patch MUST provide at least one causal_ref and MUST identify exactly one accepted base-head digest for every target cell; the per-cell uniqueness and post-state reconstruction checks are reducer semantics. Other DataEvents may use this field for business causality. These refs are not global completeness proofs.

preconditions.description: Control Move only. Pre-state predicates that must hold under the seal_basis governance view; if any fails, the entire event fails. DataEvents MUST NOT carry preconditions.

seal_ref.description: DataEvent only. Accepted control-plane Seal id used as the authorization basis. Receivers verify identity/key/capability validity at this seal and apply revocation freshness rules.

auth_context.description: DataEvent only. Pins the signing key id and epoch used to verify authorization at seal_ref. The signing principal is the complete executed_by when present, otherwise the complete actor_id. Effective capabilities are derived from the accepted governance basis, never selected by the producer.

seal_basis.description: Control Move only. Signed governance basis for preconditions and reducer derivation. The canonical sorted Seal leaves are the sole producer commitment; receivers resolve and verify each Seal and deterministically recompute the covered control set and joined state. Seal roots remain on the Seal itself and are not copied into the Event.

unsigned.description: Local / transport-only metadata (server-derived hints, redaction reason, age). NOT covered by signature or event digest.

proofs.description: Producer proofs sign canonical Event bytes, including the complete actor_id and executed_by when present. After local admission, the origin Station named by the account or hosted-principal signer variant appends at most one station_admission proof that binds the exact producer proof it verified; a directly authoring service is its own service identity. proofs and unsigned remain excluded from event_digest; federation and backfill preserve the accepted Event byte-for-byte.

requirements.description: Schema, feature, and critical-extension requirements declared by this event. All sub-fields enter the canonical event bytes and the proof event_digest. Reducer selection is derived from the Realm reducer-profile control cell, never declared by an ordinary Event. Receivers MUST fail closed on any unknown critical entry.

schema.description: Schema profile ids this event depends on.

features.description: Features this event requires; receiver MUST fail closed if any is unknown.

critical_extensions.description: Critical extension declarations; each entry MUST have id, extension_scope, fail_closed=true.

allOf.$comment: Machine-closed accepted-Event producer signer-evidence rule. When an admission proof is present it owns historical producer-key validation and the producer proof omits its external evidence pair. A no-admission envelope is shared by caller submission and retained direct-history replay, so its pair requirement is enforced by the consuming operation/profile rather than inferred from this context-free schema.
A patch-bearing DataEvent is identified by its required seal_ref and payload.patch. It needs at least one causal base; exact per-target-cell matching remains a reducer check.
Signed Applet provenance invariants. external_ref is only meaningful when bound to a signed applet_id, and Applet-originated writes must cite the accepted authorization/delegation grant.

Closed direct-conversation participant authority reference. Direct participant writes cite the registered source token and one exact critical binding Event evidence ref. Delegated Agent writes use authorization_ref for the executor delegation and satisfy participant authority independently in the profile evaluator.

Closed direct-conversation bootstrap authority reference. Pre-binding founding-phase writes cite the registered bootstrap source token and one exact critical founding-unit Event evidence ref, because no binding Event exists yet to cite.
Known active non-reducer Event kinds MUST NOT carry CBA fields: preconditions/seal_ref/auth_context/seal_basis.

Conflict-recovery event detection: any precondition with op=head_in implies conflict recovery semantics. When triggered, refs[] MUST contain BOTH a state_witness and an inclusion_proof (event-auth-state-resolution.md §8.1). Schema-level enforcement; reducer-level verify re-checks.
MUST contain at least one state_witness ref
MUST contain at least one inclusion_proof ref
ak.redaction is the cross-object redaction kind. Its payload class excludes Message so that a Message can only reach state=redacted through the object-scoped ak.message.redact.
ak.device.reanchor is the only event allowed to carry did_recovery_anchor, and it must carry exactly one critical ref whose id has did:webvh versionId shape.
Count the reserved role independent of critical so one critical plus one non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

Any Event carrying did_inception is confined to the closed self-principal PCR-genesis shape and carries exactly one critical ref. A delegated Agent PCR create intentionally carries no did_inception; batch/reducer admission distinguishes self-principal genesis from delegated Agent genesis by comparing the complete actor_id, executed_by, authorization_ref, PCR binding and DID subject, which JSON Schema cannot express.
Count the reserved role independently so a critical ref plus a non-critical duplicate cannot pass.

A managed_agent_control Realm create without did_inception is syntactically reserved for delegated managed-principal genesis. Requiring the delegation pair prevents a self-principal caller from falling through to ordinary realm.create capability admission; the delegated_pcr_genesis verifier performs the actor/DID/service/realm comparisons that JSON Schema cannot express.

An applet_managed_control PCR genesis is reachable only through one immutable Applet-managed actor provision authority Event. The admission verifier cross-binds the provision payload and initial_resolution; this shape cannot fall through to generic realm.create authority.

Reject these top-level field names. The Event Envelope root is closed (additionalProperties=false); extension data belongs in payload or requirements.critical_extensions. The root field names type / auth_refs / target_ref / operation_id are dropped and MUST NOT appear at the root; use kind / refs[role=authorized_by] / payload.* fields / SDK-internal id instead (see operations-sync.md §5).

anyOf.$comment: auth_refs is dropped; it MUST NOT appear at the root, use refs[role=authorized_by]

allOf.$comment: zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0: ak.realm.create MUST omit realm_id and use the realm_genesis scope. Every Realm, including Collaboration, Direct Conversation, human PCR, and managed Agent PCR, derives realm_id = retype(event_id, "realm") from this create Event. The uniform omission leaves one receiver-derived genesis form and avoids the digest cycle. Every other kind MUST carry realm_id.

external_ref.description: Signed external provenance. Extension profiles define exact field vocabulary; common fields include protocol, network_id, instance_id, user_id, location_id, event_id, external_id, and url. Implementations MUST preserve all fields in canonical bytes and MUST NOT use unsigned.external_ref for security decisions.

canonical_event_timestamp.description: Canonical Event Envelope/proof timestamp. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits; whole-second shorthand, finer fractions, and numeric offsets are forbidden.

oneOf.description: Native controller-and-owned-Agents private scope. It is not a Circle and has no editable membership.

Genesis scope for ak.realm.create only. It carries no realm_id because the receiver derives every Realm id, including Collaboration, Direct Conversation, human PCR, and managed Agent PCR, as retype(event_id, "realm") from this create Event (zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5.0). The uniform omission also prevents the digest cycle.

profile_ref.description: Profile that defines this extension's semantics when schema_ref is not the exact governing profile.

parameters.description: Closed extension-specific parameter bag. Unknown top-level fields are forbidden; extension-defined data belongs here and is interpreted only after id/schema_ref support is sealed.

material_digest.description: Optional digest of out-of-band extension material when parameters would be too large for the event envelope.

event_ref.description: Complete Event reference carrying the suite wire_code and all 32 digest octets. It is suitable for authorization, equality, deduplication, Seal coverage, and exact replay after normal recomputation and acceptance checks.

did_delegation_ref.description: DID URL of a non-device controller/organization authority entry that designates executed_by for an operation profile. Principal device authorization never uses this DID-document branch: it resolves through accepted PCR evidence. Historical DID authority is resolved at the Event accepted-at basis.

realm_authority_root_ref.description: Designates the registered authority-root cell of the envelope's own realm_id. This is a closed constant, not a general cell_ref: only the singleton ak.component.realm.authority_root.v1 cell carries Realm owner authority, and widening it to an arbitrary cell_ref would let any projected cell be presented as an authorization source. Reducer MUST resolve it against that cell in the Event's authorization basis and verify controller_id == the authorizing principal plus the cell's authority_generation. Inside the ak.realm.create genesis batch the staged root value is used and the Event MUST descend from the same batch's create Event through prev_refs; outside that batch an accepted-Seal inclusion proof is required and a staged proof MUST be rejected. See zh/models/realm-and-space.md section 2.5 and zh/authz/capabilities.md section 3.2.

direct_conversation_participant_authorit.description: The daily profile-scoped non-grant authorization source accepted by Event.authorization_ref. It is meaningful solely in ak.profile.direct_conversation_realm.v1 and requires one critical refs[] role=direct_conversation_binding Event reference. The evaluator rederives the pair's unique immutable binding, exact-two participant membership, Realm/Strand/MLS cross-binding, lifecycle, both directional Contact heads/scopes and action-specific gates without consulting Consent; this constant never authorizes arbitrary Realm or third-party writes.

direct_conversation_bootstrap_authority_.description: Pre-binding profile-scoped non-grant authority for a Direct Conversation between accepted founding unit and first legal binding endorsement. It requires one critical founding-unit ref. provisional_history_send authorizes only founder actions in the one scope-derived group; exact_pair_founding_completion applies once that same group holds exact authorized pair leaves. Both retire after the first binding. Neither phase authorizes a second Genesis/group, policy, grant, a third participant, another Strand or ordinary membership writes.

membership_compensation_delegation_ref.description: Content-addressed accepted-at membership compensation delegation. It is valid only for ak.member.state leave/remove submitted with the matching closed Event submission transport-only membership_compensation_evidence carrier and registered single-use evaluator. This carrier is not an ak:sidecar: Agent Sidecar object and has no participant semantics.

semantic_ref.description: Closed typed locator union. State witnesses use a SealRef plus inline typed Merkle proof; grant/event roles use the exact provenance EventId. Signer-resolution evidence is carried exactly once by each producer/station proof's required signer_resolution_evidence_ref and signer_resolution_evidence_digest, never as a SemanticRef. Unknown critical roles fail closed.

proof.description: Generic detached-JWS proof shape reused by non-Event schemas (snapshot signature, snapshot witness attestations, identity receipts, handle claims, etc.). MUST NOT be used as the shape of Event Envelope `proofs[]` — Event proofs reference $defs/event_proof and bind canonical Event bytes via `event_digest`. Non-Event signed objects MUST define an object-family signing-context constant and include it in the canonical proof binding object with payload_digest; the context constant is not a wire field in this generic shape. drift detection: `payload_digest#event_proof` in forbidden-wire-fields.json is the hard-reject mirror of this rule. New non-Event signed objects MAY $ref this shape; new signed Event-shaped objects MUST instead $ref event_proof.

kind.description: Generic detached JWS proof over a canonical non-Event payload binding object that includes an object-family context constant.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the signing key for this non-Event detached proof. Same pattern as $defs/event_proof.verification_method; semantics are decoupled from Event proof (see $defs/event_proof for the Event-only shape).

payload_digest.description: Generic non-Event detached-proof hash. This $defs/proof shape is reused by non-Event schemas; Event.properties.proofs references $defs/event_proof and MUST use event_digest instead.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for non-Event proofs. handle-claim.schema.json requires binding_state=verified claims to carry at least one proofs[] entry with proof_purpose=holder_acceptance; without this optional field that requirement was unsatisfiable under additionalProperties:false. governance_authorization marks a resource-governance-key authorization (directory withdraw/takedown-appeal, discovery-directory.md 8.7.1). Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it load-bearing.

station_admission_proof.description: Origin Station admission proof over canonical_json({context:'ak.station_admission_proof.v1',event_digest,producer_proof_digest,producer_verification_method,producer_signing_key,producer_signer_resolution_evidence_ref?,producer_signer_resolution_evidence_digest?,signer_resolution_evidence_ref,signer_resolution_evidence_digest,accepted_at,verification_method}). The optional producer pair freezes the original producer evidence root when that signer regime has portable evidence; Native Agent federation requires it. The unprefixed signer pair continues to bind the Station proof's own service signer evidence.

verification_method.description: Station verification method whose controller projects to the station_id inside the Event signer account or hosted-principal ActorId. A directly authoring service proof instead projects to that service ActorId's service_id.

producer_proof_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the complete producer_event_proof object actually verified by the origin service.

producer_verification_method.description: Must equal the bound producer proof verification_method byte-for-byte.

producer_signing_key_did.description: Public signing key that verifies the exact producer proof at admission time.

producer_signer_resolution_evidence_dige.description: Must be present as a matching pair with producer_signer_resolution_evidence_ref. Native Agent admission requires the pair and it resolves to the exact frozen CurrentAdmission root.

signer_resolution_evidence_digest.description: Must equal the digest encoded by signer_resolution_evidence_ref and resolve to the exact Station verification method used by this proof.

kind.description: Actor, device or service signature over the registered producer-proof transcript. When the Event has no station_admission proof, signer_resolution_evidence_ref and signer_resolution_evidence_digest are required and included. When a valid admission proof exists, both fields are forbidden and that proof's producer_signing_key is the historical producer-key truth.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the Event-signing key. Generic verification extracts the canonical bare DID base under the active method adapter, validates that method history/key, projects the base DID to did_core_id, and compares it byte-for-byte with the principal component of executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise; a did_core_id is never concatenated into a DID URL. For principal device proofs the fragment MUST be the full device_id (`ak:device:<uuidv7>`), so receivers can resolve the complete actor_id plus device_id through the device directory. The sole exception is an Event whose selected admission variant is did_root_anchor: its closed verifier MUST instead require verification_method to equal an active controller-proof verification method from the one critical did_inception/did_recovery_anchor entry and verify the controller proof/update authority against that referenced did:webvh history; a root did:key controller is not rewritten to the principal actor_id. This exception cannot apply to any other Event.

signer_resolution_evidence_ref.description: Required only for the direct/DID-root/native producer regime without station_admission; forbidden otherwise.

proof_purpose.description: Optional role discriminator for handle-claim proofs. Generic proof consumers ignore it unless their object-family contract makes it required.

producer_event_proof.description: Producer Event proof. The signer maps to the complete executed_by when present or actor_id otherwise. Its event_digest covers canonical producer Event bytes including that complete identity and excluding proofs, unsigned and reducer-stamped actor_kind. The event-level proof-regime validator enforces exactly one branch: a valid station_admission proof means producer signer evidence fields are absent and the admission-bound producer_signing_key verifies this proof; without such admission both signer evidence fields are present and resolve to this exact verification_method.

event_proof.description: Closed Event proof union. Callers submit producer_event_proof only; the origin Station may append one station_admission proof after successful local admission.

schemas/event-payload.schema.json.title: Arkret Standard Event Payloads
schemas/event-payload.schema.json.description: Definitions bundle for common payload contracts used by registered ak.* Event.kind values. The root schema is intentionally generic and MUST NOT be used as a complete payload validator. Event validators MUST validate the full Event Envelope and dispatch by Event.kind to the matching $defs payload class using artifacts/registry/event-kind-registry.json.

not.$comment: The event-payload schema root is a definition-bundle diagnostic only. Standard payload validation MUST select one explicit kind-bound schema ref from the event kind registry.

account_blocklist_payload.description: Payload for ak.account.blocklist. Holder-private personal blocklist state; it never enters shared Realm state or federation payloads.

version.description: Monotonic whole-value CAS revision. The next accepted ak.account.blocklist payload MUST use current version + 1; ak.account_data.set for key ak.account.blocklist uses expected_revision against the same counter. Omitting an entry in the next revision removes it, and entries=[] clears the list.

entry_id.description: Blocklist entry identity. This is the registered ak:block:<uuidv7> typed id of id-kind-registry.json, not a document-local symbol: the wire form owns the ak: namespace, so common-fields.md 2.1 classifies it as typed_object_id and the terminal MUST pin that form.

mode.description: block denies a new holder-facing interaction on the selected surfaces and filters shared durable content only after canonical receive/store; mute keeps content visible but suppresses attention surfaces; hide keeps canonical content but omits it from default holder rendering/search. None of the modes revokes a Realm capability or rewrites shared history.

account_data_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.account_data.set. Writes one holder-private account-data key; the value may be plaintext inside an already private envelope, encrypted account-data material, or a tombstone. Every key is a compare-and-set whole-value register per zh/models/account-data.md §5: expected_revision is the revision the writer believes is current (0 to create), and the accepted revision is expected_revision + 1.

expected_revision.description: Compare-and-set precondition against the accepted per-key revision. A mismatch MUST be rejected with cas_conflict and MUST NOT be stored; the revision counter is a high-water mark that never goes backwards, so a stale offline retry cannot resurrect a superseded value.

body.description: Caller-supplied opaque account-data value. Any JSON value.

actor_profile_create_payload.description: Initial actor profile payload. The materialized resolution projection is reducer-managed from the PCR resolution cell and is forbidden on this authoring surface. id/updated_by/updated_at are likewise materialized fields, not create input.

actor_profile_update_payload.description: Actor Profile patch payload. resolution and every resolution.* descendant path are reducer-managed projections of the PCR resolution cell and are forbidden on this generic profile write surface.

agent_action_approve_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_approve. Controller approval binds the draft/action request, target, approved payload digest, expiry, and single-use nonce.

agent_action_reject_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_reject. Controller rejection terminates a draft/action request without shared Realm side effects.

agent_action_request_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.action_request. Actor-private request for controller approval before a shared Realm write is emitted.

agent_action_target.description: Minimal target descriptor for an actor-private agent draft or approval. It identifies the eventual shared write surface without disclosing private draft content.

agent_deactivate_payload.description: Payload for the single terminal ak.self.agent.deactivate Control Move. At the accepted Seal covering this Move, every verifier mechanically AND-gates all subordinate Agent runtime-key authorizations, sessions, pairing handles, capability grants, KeyPackages, presence and future submissions on lifecycle=active. Historical child Events remain auditable; explicit child revokes are not prerequisites and are reserved for targeted revocation while the Agent is non-terminal. The lifecycle state witness is sufficient transition evidence for every derived ineffective child.

previous_status.description: Controller lifecycle intent at deactivation time. Generic Agent status has only lifecycle, readiness and presence; pairing-poll runtime_state is operation-local and never appears here (key-management.md §3.6.1).

agent_draft_propose_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.draft.propose. Actor-private proposal that may materialize into controller-owned encrypted draft account data after policy checks.

agent_key_approval_evidence.description: Evidence that authorized this agent key. Durable grant/approval/proposal/policy evidence carries ref so it can be replayed at the event frontier; the short-lived pairing_request branch instead binds pairing_request_id, request_canonical_digest, and approved_by and MUST omit ref.

pairing_request_id.description: Optional profile-local, short-lived pairing artifact id. Required by the agent-key pairing acceptance flow and MUST equal the pairing_request_id in the accepted request; it is not a durable protocol object ref.

agent_key_authorize_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.authorize. Binds one concrete agent signing key to an accountable principal, explicit agent_key_scope, audience, validity window, approval evidence, and both the service-surface and content-capability ceilings that later agent_key_proof sessions must narrow from.

public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 of the decoded 32-byte Ed25519 public key behind verification_method, computed with agent_signing_public_key_digest. Native Agent authorization always commits this raw-key digest; it is distinct from the private runtime-request PublicKey DTO digest.

signing_key_binding_digest.description: sha256 over the canonical agent-signing binding core containing schema, agent_id, agent_key_id, verification_method, public_key, public_key_digest, issued_at, optional expires_at, and controller_id, but excluding agent_key_authorize_event_id and controller_proof. The complete accepted Event ID and controller proof are appended only when materializing the public ak.schema.agent_signing_key_binding.v1 object. Including this Event's not-yet-derived identity would create an impossible digest fixed point. A service MUST recompute the core digest before appending the verified accepted Event identity and MUST NOT substitute another disclosure.

expires_at.description: Optional: absent means the key authorization is non-expiring and governed solely by revocation (ak.agent.key.revoke / lifecycle cascade).

supersedes.description: Exact set of every active Agent-key authorization dot observed immediately before this controller-signed authorization is accepted during runtime re-pairing. Each entry binds both the key id and the authorization Event that introduced the active dot. The array MUST be omitted only for first pairing, when the authoritative active set is empty. Every replacement MUST set-equal the complete pre-accept active authorization set, including an old dot with the same key_id as the new authorization; a stale, partial, extra, or implicit map overwrite fails closed. Acceptance atomically removes these dots with reason superseded_by_repairing and adds this authorize dot, so no server-forged ak.agent.key.revoke Event is required.

revocation_check_ref.description: Optional freshness source for revocation checking. When expires_at is absent, authorization lifetime is governed by the canonical revocation chain and lifecycle cascade; this field may identify the freshness source used for that check.

runtime_attestation.description: Optional runtime / workload attestation captured at pairing approval time. v1 enum includes self_asserted as baseline; future profiles MAY register TEE / SLSA / SPIFFE attestation kinds. Implementations encountering an unknown kind MUST fail closed.

kind.description: v1 enum. Future profiles MAY extend via accepted attestation taxonomy.

attestation_digest.description: Optional digest of verifiable attestation material when kind is not self_asserted.

attestation_ref.description: Optional external verifiable attestation reference (TEE quote, SLSA provenance, etc.).

agent_key_id.description: Stable key identifier within the agent DID. Prefer the DID URL verification method id when available.

agent_key_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.agent.key.revoke. The or_set cell subject is (agent_id, key_id); future protocol proofs from this key fail closed once this event is covered by an accepted Seal. The authoring frontiers is the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the payload carries no frontier field.

agent_key_scope.description: Agent scope object with two uses. In POST /_arkret/self/agents requested_scope it is the required immutable global Agent ceiling; in ak.agent.key.authorize it is a per-key ceiling that MAY be narrower but MUST be an actions/resources/constraints subset of the provision ceiling. It is never a capability grant. actions may contain service operation ids and content action tokens; an omitted action can never be restored by a key, Realm grant or session. resources constrain the service surface and may optionally narrow later content resources, but never authorize content by themselves. Provisioning and pairing do not materialize capability grants from this object; effective authority is the intersection of provision ceiling, key ceiling, independent Realm-scoped grants, session request, membership and policy, with participation applied as an additional deny gate.

actions.description: Literal action ceiling. Every downstream key scope, grant or session action MUST appear here; action families, prefixes and subsumption do not widen it.

resources.description: Selector ceiling, not authorization. Each downstream selector must be covered by a parent selector. operation/service parents cover the same kind and matching explicit field and cannot carry content fields. The content-kind vocabulary is the ResourceSelector vocabulary except '*'; kind=realm covers every Realm-local content kind in the matching Realm and other content kinds cover only the same kind. Omitted parent realm_id is a cross-Realm ceiling wildcard and omitted exact ref is a same-kind/same-Realm wildcard. With no content selector, later Realm grants still choose concrete resources and no content wildcard is granted.

constraints.description: Global mandatory constraints. Every effective key/grant/session evaluation MUST retain and AND these constraints; downstream scopes may add stricter constraints but MUST NOT omit or relax provision constraints.

agent_pause_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.pause. The status cell is keyed by agent_id and moves from active to paused. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis; the reducer accepts the transition only under the accepted current control frontier.

agent_resume_payload.description: Payload for ak.self.agent.resume. Authorization is evaluated against the Control Move envelope seal_basis, and reducers re-check controller, agent, key, capability, Realm policy, and accountability grant against the accepted current control frontier before returning the agent to active. Sidecar desired membership is derived afterward and is not carried in this payload.

agent_sidecar_exchange_control_payload.description: Outer payload for ak.agent.sidecar.exchange.control. sidecar_id and source_context_ref route the Event inside a native Sidecar scope; encrypted_payload plaintext MUST validate as agent-sidecar-exchange-control.schema.json. Admission MUST require matching scope_ref.kind=sidecar and actor_id equal to the Sidecar controller.

agent_slug.description: Controller-scoped native personal agent selector slug used by @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug>. Not a global handle or authorization subject.

applet_bridge_error_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.bridge_error. Durable Realm-history Event recording a bridge / external-network failure. Field table: zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7. MUST bind realm_id, failed_transaction_ref, retriable, and visibility_scope; missing any required field MUST be rejected as schema_violation. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

failed_transaction_ref.description: Reference to the failed transaction / source Event. MUST NOT inline unauthorized external plaintext.

error_class.description: Closed error category for aggregation / alerting. See zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §7.

visibility_scope.description: Closed visibility scope enum for the error event. Clients MUST honor it and MUST NOT expose bridge-internal detail to unrelated members.

external_ref.description: External network reference (protocol / network id). MUST NOT contain unauthorized external plaintext.

message.description: Human-readable summary. MUST NOT leak unauthorized external plaintext.

retry_after_ms.description: Suggested retry delay; meaningful only when retriable=true.

applet_registration_payload.description: Payload for ak.applet.registration. Durable Realm-history Event registering an Applet (bridge / bot / Ghost Actor namespace). Field vocabulary: zh/extensions/applet-integration.md §4 and zh/extensions/applet-schema.md §1 (the authoritative machine schema is applet.schema.json, which documents the applet object snapshot; the wire Event payload is this closed class). An Applet's capability to enter a Realm MUST be granted by that Realm's owner / admin / Realm-policy-authorized administrator actor and checked by the Station authorization capability. The formal Event is signed by that installing administrator and admitted by the target Station; payload.proof is the exact controller-signed package proof and is not an Event proof.

applet_id.description: Stable canonical Applet identifier; service identity is carried separately in service_id.

service_id.description: DID of the service hosting the applet runtime.

controller_id.description: DID of the Applet controller / external system; signs the registration.

claimed_profiles.description: Canonical Applet implementation profiles copied from the accepted package. These durable claims are the authority source for profile-bound grant rules.

namespaces.description: Applet namespace claims (actors / realms / handles patterns). Namespace match alone never grants write capability.

webhook_auth.description: Transaction push HTTP signature policy copied from the Applet package. webhook_auth.key_ref is the Applet service DID URL used to verify the app/bridge->arkret inbound HTTP message signature and is bound to this registration_epoch; node->Applet pushes verify the Arkret source service DID from Source-Service-ID instead.

manifest.description: Closed package-derived manifest and the sole registration-epoch evidence carrier.

proof.description: Exact controller-DID detached package proof copied from the accepted Applet package. payload_digest binds the canonical package, while the enclosing formal registration Event has its own Event proof and Station admission proof.

audience_mention_node.description: Broadcast mention AST node carried in a Content Block `audience_mentions[]`. It is never expanded into `mention_node` entries in shared history; recipient expansion happens receiver-side under the ak.message.mention.broadcast, audience policy, max_recipients and quota gates in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3-§9.4.4.

audience.description: Canonical audience selector. @here maps to strand_engaged and is never presence-filtered; presence-filtered audiences require a separate declared profile.

audit_accessed_payload.description: Strict payload for ak.audit.accessed. It records a specific access or paired privacy-sensitive write. Reducers MUST reject business events that require an audit pair unless this payload identifies the same writer, target, and object/cell in the same ordered submit batch, equivalent control transaction, or an accepted pre-read event with RYW receipt.

late_recovery_original_event_id.description: Required when access_kind=e2ee_late_recovery; identifies the original encrypted event whose plaintext became available through late key recovery.

ryw_required.description: When true, plaintext release or privileged projection MUST wait for an accepted-history RYW receipt before disclosure.

audit_applet_binding_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.audit.applet_binding.create. binding_id, initial active status, creator, and creation time are derived from the accepted Event envelope. Policy fields are immutable; changing them creates a new binding so historical release eligibility cannot be silently expanded.

activation_frontier_digest.description: Accepted Seal coverage digest at which this binding/policy became member-visible. Release requests MUST NOT cover messages or epochs before this coverage point.

first_auditable_epoch.description: First MLS epoch eligible for this binding. Reducers MUST verify it is the epoch created by a ak.mls.commit covering activation_frontier_digest; earlier epochs are permanently ineligible.

retroactive_release.description: v1 audited E2EE never permits a later binding or policy expansion to make pre-activation messages auditable.

eligibility_basis.description: A message is eligible only if it was encrypted after a commit covering this binding/policy frontier.

max_lookback_ms.description: Optional maximum age, measured from session request/authorization time, for otherwise eligible material. Later policy changes may narrow this for future messages but MUST NOT expand already encrypted messages.

max_epoch_span.description: Optional cap on the number of sealed historical epochs a single session/release may cover.

allowed_target_kinds.description: Optional target class allow-list for targeted_evidence_release.

audit_applet_binding_state_payload.description: Lifecycle-only transition for an existing Audit Applet Binding. Scope and release policy cannot be edited by this Event; a policy change requires a new binding genesis.

audit_release_payload.description: Payload for ak.audit.release. A sealed audit release manifest for a bounded historical window. It appends to the control-plane ordered log ak.component.audit.release.v1 keyed by session_id only while the accepted session FSM head is notice. Same-basis close dominates and rejects the release. The payload records release metadata and wrapped material digests only; plaintext MUST NOT be inlined.

eligibility_proof.description: Proof summary that the requested release is inside the binding activation frontier, first_auditable_epoch, release_window_policy, and the targets' encryption-time eligibility snapshots.

activation_commit_ref.description: ak.mls.commit that covered the activation frontier and created first_auditable_epoch, when the release covers MLS epoch material.

policy_snapshot_digest.description: Digest of the binding/release window policy snapshot used when authorizing this release.

target_eligibility_digest.description: Digest of the deterministic per-target/per-epoch eligibility set proving no pre-activation material is included.

audit_session_contract.description: Shared payload class for ak.audit.session.request / authorize / notice / close. The session_state field is the target state of the control-plane FSM cell ak.component.audit.session.v1 keyed by session_id. Initial state is request; legal main-path transitions are request->authorize->notice->close, with request->close and authorize->close allowed for aborted sessions. Close is terminal; same-basis conflicting siblings produce Bottom.

approved_recipient_audit_actor_id.description: Audit subject approved to receive release material. Required on ak.audit.session.authorize. The accepted authorize record is the sole recipient source for ak.audit.release; the release payload does not echo this field.

approved_recipient_public_key_ref.description: Audit release recipient key approved by ak.audit.session.authorize. MUST resolve to approved_recipient_audit_actor_id's authorized audit-release key. The accepted authorize record is the sole key source for ak.audit.release; the release payload does not echo this field.

board_space_id.description: A Space with kind=board. Pattern matches any ak:space:; kind invariant enforced by reducer/profile.

call_participant.description: A single participant value added by ak.call.state.payload.roster_delta. See crypto-media/call-state.md §4/§4.1.

foci_preferred.description: Client-local ordered focus preference list used for the session_focus election (see crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1 and media-service-binding.md §5).

participant_id.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg.

participant_binding.description: Required for sfu/mcu roster joins; MUST be absent for a direct p2p/mesh leg. The containing call focus.mode selects the semantic branch.

call_recording_start_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.recording.start. recording_id is a stable opaque ASCII handle (1–128 bytes, [A-Za-z0-9._-]) that feeds the recording key exporter Context byte-for-byte and MUST NOT be normalized by receivers. capture_kind selects recording vs transcription so both lifecycles share one start event kind. See crypto-media/call-state.md §5 / §5.1.

recording_id.description: Stable opaque recording / transcript lifecycle handle. Canonical byte-for-byte; receivers MUST NOT normalize (case-fold, NFC/NFKC, trim, re-encode) because it is a cross-implementation key-derivation input.

capture_kind.description: Whether this start event opens a recording or a transcription segment. REQUIRED: it selects the target capture cell family (ak.component.call.recording.v1 vs ak.component.call.transcript.v1) in the registered cell contract, so it MUST NOT be inferred from a missing-field default.

visible_notice.description: Asserts the initiating client will display the capture-in-progress notice to all participants.

result.description: Initial immutable capture evidence. retention.consent_confirmed=true closes the pre-capture consent gate before the FSM enters a capturing state. This wire payload MUST NOT carry recording_start_event_id or transcript_start_event_id: the accepted Event identity is derived only after digesting this payload, and the reducer stamps that identity into the projected result cell.

call_create_payload.description: Genesis payload for ak.call.create. call_id is omitted and derived by retyping the accepted Event id. Signaling, media tokens, Morph bindings, and state deltas MUST reference only an already accepted create.

call_state_payload.description: Typed delta payload for ak.call.state. Every present field maps to one or two explicit registered cell effects; omitted axes produce no effect.

failure_reason_code.description: Machine reason for to="failed". Required when to="failed" and forbidden otherwise, so a failed call always carries a diagnostic and a non-failed transition cannot smuggle one.

result.description: Typed recording outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent recording result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

artifact.description: Canonical artifact metadata for recording_transition.to=ready. It binds the Arkret blob, recording exporter context, retention policy and deletion audit surface.

failure_message.description: Human-readable diagnostic for recording_state=failed. It MUST NOT contain recording plaintext or backend direct URLs.

result.description: Typed transcription outcome for a stopped, ready, or failed segment. It is written to the independent transcript result cell and never embedded in the FSM transition op.

call_summary_payload.description: Typed payload for ak.call.summary (durable end-of-call summary). Written once after a call reaches a terminal `state`; carries duration, peak participant count, and capture status so clients can render a durable call record without replaying ephemeral signaling. See crypto-media/call-state.md §7. started_at/ended_at/duration_ms are nullable: non-active terminal states (missed/cancelled/failed) MUST set them null per call-state.md §7.

final_state.description: The terminal call lifecycle state this summary closes over. MUST be one of the call_state_payload terminal states.

peak_participant_count.description: Highest concurrent participant count observed during the call.

distinct_participant_count.description: Number of distinct (actor_id, device_id) participants that joined at any point.

recording_state.description: Final recording_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state for the durable record. Absent = the call was not recorded.

transcript_state.description: Final transcript_state at call end, mirrored from ak.call.state. Absent = the call was not transcribed.

capability_grant_payload.description: Canonical ak.capability.grant genesis payload. Both top-level grant_id and grant.id are forbidden because the durable GrantId is derived by retyping this Event's event_id. authority_depth and authority_root_refs are reducer-derived and forbidden in this closed authoring shape. issuer_id and a concrete subject are already exact ActorIds; no parallel station sidecar is permitted. The Event envelope proof is the sole durable issuer signature.

capability_derived_payload.description: Reducer-authored cross-Realm capability derivation. Unlike capability genesis this references an existing Grant and therefore carries the already-derived grant_id and complete projected grant body. Exact issuer and concrete-subject identity is preserved inside ActorId and MUST NOT be replaced with a local reducer or receiving service identity.

capability_relinquish_payload.description: ak.capability.relinquish — subject-only release of the actor own grant. The authority is the target grant subject's signature, never a capability: a narrowly-scoped holder that was never granted ak.capability.revoke must still be able to give up what it holds. The reducer target guard accepts actor == target.subject and nothing else, so this can never become an unauthorized revocation. Descendants of the released grant fail through their issuer_authority_refs at read time.

circle_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the create branch of Circle schema. Reducer requires created_by/created_at to match the Event, enforces the parent Realm content-encryption floor, derives circle_id and for MLS derives mls_group_id. Actor-supplied id or mls_group_id is forbidden.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

circle_member_state_payload.description: Payload for ak.circle.member.state. Uses the same membership_state enum as ak.member.state (Realm), scoped to a Circle; reducer MUST verify member_id is a `join` member of the parent Realm before any transition to `join`, MUST gate `knock` on Circle join_rule=knock, and MUST reject self-unban/self-unremove paths.

expected_membership.description: Optional optimistic-concurrency guard, orthogonal to the membership transition guard. The three wire states are distinct: omission applies no CAS and leaves legality to the FSM guard, explicit null asserts the actor currently has no membership record in this Circle, and a concrete value asserts the current membership equals it. A failed assertion MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. See zh/models/circle.md §9.1.

circle_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.circle.update. Patch path MUST NOT contain realm_id, encryption_profile, content_scheme, mls_group_id, durability_policy, history_access, state, state_changed_at, created_by, or created_at; history_access changes use dedicated ak.circle.history_access. Reducer enforces create-locks and semantic policy checks.

circle_seal_commit_payload.description: Reducer-derived payload for ak.circle.seal_commit. Commits an opaque Circle sub-seal head digest into the parent Realm Seal stream at the profile-defined cadence.

consent_grant_payload.description: Holder-private consent grant. The actor (consenter) is the holder; payload.peer is the counterparty whose contact is consented to. Wire-equivalent to a Move whose effect is add(tag,value) on the cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (or_set lattice); ak.consent.revoke writes a remove on the same cell. Lives in the holder's Principal Control Realm (or holder-private actor stream); MUST NOT be written to a shared Collaboration Realm. Realm role taxonomy: zh/models/realm-and-space.md §2.7.

consent_id.description: Stable identifier; used as the cell_subject of the consent cell. ak.consent.revoke MUST reference the same consent_id.

peer_id.description: Counterparty DID (or pairwise DID) that this consent applies to.

consent_scope.description: What kind of contact is consented to. 'invite' = peer may send Realm / Strand invites; 'direct_message' = peer may initiate 1:1 message; 'voice_call' / 'video_call' = peer may initiate WebRTC call; 'presence' = peer may observe presence; 'any' = full consent across all consent scopes.

constraints.description: Optional consent-specific constraints (rate limits, time-of-day windows, device restrictions). v1 does not standardise constraint types beyond capability constraint vocabulary.

evidence_ref.description: Optional reference to claim disclosure, presentation response, or invite proof that triggered this consent (audit trail).

consent_revoke_payload.description: Revoke a previously granted consent. Wire-equivalent to a Control Move whose effect is remove(tag) on the consent cell ak:cell:ak.component.consent.grant.v1:<consent_id> (the same cell written by ak.consent.grant). Payload observed_dot_ids MUST match the Control Move effect's observed_dot_ids so schema validation and audit can see exactly what was removed.

consent_id.description: MUST equal the consent_id of the ak.consent.grant being revoked.

observed_dot_ids.description: Exact add dots being removed. A full revoke, including consent_scope=any cascade, MUST enumerate every active dot that becomes inactive; implicit cascade without dot enumeration is invalid.

contact_accepted_payload.description: Holder-signed normal Contact acceptance fact. This is version 1 of the issuer-local directional lineage. It grants only the explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Required by semantic admission when the accepted request is a recontact. It MUST equal the same field in the referenced request fact and its source-signed acceptance receipt. It is absent for a root Contact round.

contact_rejected_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal rejection of one exact accepted request. It establishes no Contact round and carries no Consent or Contact round evidence fields.

contact_requested_payload.description: Requester-signed directional Contact request fact. It is created before any acceptance receipt or basis exists, so neither may appear in this payload. It grants only the requester's explicit Contact scopes and neither reads nor writes Consent.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Required digest of the exact private introduction_evidence carried by the request branch of ak.peer.contacts.command.submit.v1. Raw evidence is not written into the contact fact log.

previous_terminal_contact_round_id.description: Requester-signed immediate predecessor link for recontact. It is required when this request follows a previously accepted terminal Contact round and forbidden for a root request. It is not the issuer-local request-slot predecessor.

contact_tombstoned_payload.description: Holder-signed terminal event for one issuer-local Contact lineage. The event kind itself supplies terminal semantics; the payload carries only the exact peer, basis and predecessor coordinates. It does not read, write or revoke Consent.

mentions.description: Structured direct mention AST nodes for this Content Block. This is the only carrier of a direct mention: authorization, notification routing and audit attribution read mention_node.subject_id exclusively (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.1-§9.4.2).

audience_mentions.description: Structured broadcast mention AST nodes for this Content Block (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3).

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Reject discriminator field name `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`. The discriminator is `kind`, the composite child array is `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes` (see schemas/message.schema.json and forbidden-wire-fields.json `blocks/content_block_composite`).

anyOf.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

content_block_long_text.description: ak.content.long_text: plain text whose full normalized UTF-8 body exceeds the 256 KiB inline boundary (or, by the narrow exception in zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4, whose Event would otherwise exceed the 1 MiB envelope limit). Exactly one of the plaintext branch (blob_ref + size_bytes + media_type) and the E2EE branch (attachment) applies. v1 core Content Block: no feature gate, no server-side opt-out.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

blob_ref.description: Hash-addressed Blob ref for the full normalized UTF-8 body. UUID blob refs are forbidden here because they carry no digest commitment.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 body bytes. The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4), not a schema minimum.

media_type.description: MUST match format. No parameters: charset is fixed to UTF-8 by this kind.

format.description: Closed set for long text. prosemirror_json is forbidden here; structured rich text needs its own Content Block.

body.description: Inline fallback. Authoritative bound is 4096 UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound.

attachment.description: Encrypted full-body Blob descriptor. MUST use scheme ak.blob.stream_aead.v1 with the matching _stream alg; whole-file AEAD is forbidden for long text.

blob_ref.description: Long text MUST use a hash-addressed Blob ref; the <suite>:<hex> part MUST equal attachment.ciphertext_digest and the Blob metadata content_digest.

size_bytes.description: Normalized full UTF-8 plaintext body bytes; encrypted_attachment.size_bytes is the plaintext count that segment_count = ceil(size_bytes / segment_bytes) is derived from (zh/crypto-media/media-and-blob.md section 3.1 / 3.3.1). The >256 KiB rule and the narrow Event-overflow exception are normative validator rules, not a schema minimum.

cross_object_redaction_payload.description: Payload for the cross-object ak.redaction. Shares the ak.component.object.redaction.v1 cell family with ak.message.redact but carries a target set that mechanically excludes Message: message_id is not a member and target_ref cannot spell ak:message:. target_ref is the single target carrier; its lexical space covers both object targets and ak:event: targets, so the cell subject is well defined without a coalesce.

cross_object_redaction_target_ref.description: Cross-object ak.redaction object target. Identical to object_ref except that ak:message: is removed from the typed-object alternation: Message is the only object with a registered object-scoped redact kind, so a Message MUST enter state=redacted through ak.message.redact and MUST NOT be the target of a cross-object ak.redaction (models/common-fields.md 5.2).

device_authorize_payload.description: Closed authorization record shared by registration genesis, PCR-policy recovery, and accepted-device pairing. registration_anchor and pcr_recovery use a candidate-device possession proof over the full authorization core; pcr_recovery is admitted only beside an accepted recovery session and monotonic PCR generation CAS. accepted_device uses the current accepted approving device. None of these branches derives human authority from current DID state.

hpke_key.description: Device HPKE public key used for secret/key envelope sealing. It is covered by the possession transcript and by the surrounding root anchor or accepted-device Event proof; services MUST NOT substitute it. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_attestation, which the approving device reads only after that attestation verifies.

algorithms.description: Canonical sorted unique algorithm ids supported by this device. Enters device trust binding transcript together with device_public_key_did and hpke_key. For accepted_device pairing its authority is the target device_pairing_target_attestation, not any service-supplied or staged copy.

authorized_by.description: Under registration_anchor this is the principal whose durable registration control evidence was accepted. Under pcr_recovery it is the same principal selected by the recovery session and account-local lineage. Under accepted_device it is the approving device id at the accepted generation.

authorization_binding_kind.description: registration_anchor is valid only in accepted PCR genesis; pcr_recovery only in a recovery unit authorized by the accepted PCR recovery policy; accepted_device requires an active approving device. No branch permits a same-core foreign PCR lineage.

device_signature.description: Required Ed25519 possession proof. registration_anchor uses ak.device_authorize_possession_proof.v1, pcr_recovery uses ak.device_authorize_recovery_possession_proof.v1, and accepted_device uses ak.device_authorize_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1. All transcripts bind authorization_binding_kind and cannot be substituted across branches.

recovery_session_id.description: Required by the pcr_recovery branch and omitted for registration_anchor and ordinary accepted_device pairing.

device_push_route_payload.description: Closed account-private push-route write. Active routes and revoked tombstones are mutually exclusive whole-value shapes and both carry the single server-revision CAS precondition. The account identity is one atomic AccountId; its Station is never repeated as a delivery field.

device_reanchor_payload.description: Closed account-local PCR recovery payload. The account authority is selected by principal_id plus station_id and one monotonic local device-generation CAS. PCR realm/frontier identifiers remain local recovery state and are not an external principal identity selector.

new_device_generation.description: Must be the immediate monotonic successor of previous_device_generation.

did_root_evidence_digest.description: Required only when recovery_authority_kind=did_root; proves the optional factor enabled by the frozen PCR policy.

replacement_authorize_payload_digest.description: canonical_digest of the replacement ak.device.authorize payload object, using the Realm live digest suite.

device_revoke_payload.description: Payload for ak.device.revoke.
