The revocation's control-plane authorization basis is the Control Move envelope seal_basis (covered by the canonical event bytes and proofs); its permanent cutoff is the accepted Seal covering this Move. First durable canonical acceptance atomically creates ak.schema.device_revocation_state.v1 revocation_pending for the exact reducer-derived current device authorization and generation. The payload carries no frontier or generation field, and producers cannot self-report derived pending selectors.

direct_conversation_authorization_basis.description: Canonical authorization basis for creating a Direct Conversation. accepted_contact carries exactly the accepted contact request/accept refs. managed_agent_controller carries exactly two unique accepted Event refs: the controller-authored ak.agent.provision Event, whose payload already binds the Agent, controller, delegation, accountability and selector facts, and the current active ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

direct_conversation_bound_payload.description: Participant endorsement of the settled Direct Conversation coordinates and the first exact-pair state in the scope's single immutable derived MLS group. It does not enforce uniqueness: at most one Realm can exist per pair because only the founder derived from the pair's root Contact round may author the founding unit. Written once and never retired. binding_digest is a receiver-derived off-wire semantic digest over the closed normalized binding object defined by contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.3 and MUST NOT be added to this payload.

pair_key.description: Canonical unordered pair key: SHA-256(UTF8(ak.direct-conversation.pair-key.v1 followed by LF) || JCS({participants:[p0,p1],trust_domain_id})) where p0/p1 are exact ActorIds sorted by their RFC 8785 JCS bytes. Receivers MUST recompute it exactly as contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 5.1 defines; handles, bare principal IDs and unresolved pairwise DIDs are forbidden inputs.

founding_unit_digest.description: Digest of the accepted four Event atomic founding unit this binding endorses.

initial_exact_pair_group_state_ref.description: The winning Add Commit Event that first establishes both exact participants in the scope's single immutable derived MLS group.

history_effective_scope.description: Effective scope admitted by v1 private history-key request/response, history-only backup and organization-recovery archive contracts. Sidecar is deliberately excluded: its profile fixes mls_rfc9420 and defines neither history_access nor a deliverable history_secret.

history_authorization_incarnation.description: Closed history-delivery authorization incarnation. Circle reactivation/Add must causally cover the exact current parent-Realm incarnation; independent Realm and Circle MLS epochs are never compared.

history_access_payload.description: Realm history-access FSM transition. The atomic create unit uses from=null exactly once and chooses either closed initial state. After create the only legal state-changing edge is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; widening and every other new transition are permanently rejected. Exact same-transition/same-basis replay is an idempotent duplicate/no-op.

circle_history_access_payload.description: Dedicated per-Circle history-access FSM transition. Circle create initializes from=null. The only post-create edge is all_history_for_current_members to since_join; exact replay is idempotent and widening is permanently rejected. Generic ak.circle.update patches cannot touch history_access.

identity_disclosure_policy_state_payload.description: Closed holder-private disclosure-policy payload. policy_id is the stable policy cell subject and value carries the sole v1 disclosure-policy document family.

request_digest.description: Canonical SHA-256 of the exact retained Presentation Request Event. The receipt does not copy request-owned verifier, organization, domain or challenge fields.

identity_disclosure_receipt_state_payloa.description: Closed holder-private disclosure-receipt log payload. holder_principal_id is the stable log subject and value carries the sole v1 receipt document family.

constraints.description: Claim-kind-specific constraint parameters. The selected claim schema, not this generic carrier, defines the parameter vocabulary.

discovery_profile_visibility.description: Explicit map from profile field name to its maximum directory disclosure class. Dynamic keys are confined to this declared map slot.

identity_presentation_request_state_payl.description: Identity presentation-request log payload. request_id is the stable presentation correlation subject.

identity_presentation_response_state_pay.description: Closed Presentation Response correlated to one exact retained request. Request-owned audience, challenge and domain are not copied into the response.

presentation.description: Proof-suite-specific presentation document. The selected proof profile defines and verifies its closed inner shape.

invitee_account_id.description: Exact directed invite account. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the genesis payload. Delivery resolves this AccountId's station_id outside durable Realm state.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

expires_at.description: Invite expiry timestamp. Directed v1 invite creates MUST carry it; reducers MUST NOT infer indefinite validity.

third_party_invite.description: Third-party invite genesis material. The Invite id is derived from this Event's event_id and MUST NOT be carried in the payload.

invitee_account_id.description: MUST equal the directed invite's stored exact account so invite.lifecycle and member.state move atomically.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable diagnostic for the terminal transition this Move carries. Required by zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5 for every non-pending state write. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes; reason stays free text for humans.

invitee_account_id.description: Required for a directed invite and forbidden by semantic admission for a 3PID placeholder.

target_state.description: Terminal invalidation of a pending invite, carried by an authorized writer's signed Control Move. send_failed and expired are observations the writer commits explicitly (third-party-invites.md 6.1); neither may be written by a local timer or delivery retry loop.

reason_code.description: Stable machine-readable diagnostic for the terminal transition this Move carries. Required by zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5 for every non-pending state write. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes; reason stays free text for humans.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account being bound by an ak.invite.claim payload. It MUST match the account carried by binding_proof and the subject proof author; neither component may be inferred.

token_commitment.description: Reducer-matched salted commitment for the pending ak.invite.third_party record. Raw invite tokens, URL fragments, SMS codes, or plaintext 3PID values MUST NOT appear on wire.

claim_nonce.description: One-time nonce scoped to (invite_id, token_commitment). Reducers MUST reject nonce replay while preserving non-enumerable external responses.

binding_proof.description: Verification-service proof for ak.invite.claim. Reducers verify signature over the ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1 transcript against the invite's verification_public_key and current Realm verification_id allowlist before accepting a claimed transition.

verification_id.description: Verification service DID. Realm reducers MUST re-check this DID against the current effective Realm allowlist and any service DID pinned by the original invite.

verification_method.description: DID URL with required key fragment. Method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0; matches the strict form used by $defs/verification_method elsewhere in this schema.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account being bound by the verification service. MUST equal the payload top-level subject_account_id.

realm_id.description: Realm bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the Event envelope realm_id.

claim_nonce.description: Nonce bound into the verification-service proof. MUST equal the payload top-level claim_nonce.

expires_at.description: Proof expiration. Reducers MUST reject expired proofs and MUST also enforce the invite cell expires_at.

signature.description: Signature over utf8("ak.invite.claim.binding_proof.v1\n") || canonical_json({audience, binding_proof: unsigned_binding_proof, claim_nonce, invite_digest, invite_id, realm_id, subject_account_id, token_commitment, verification_id}); unsigned_binding_proof is this object without signature.

subject_proof.description: Account holder proof over ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript. The transcript digest binds subject_account_id, invite_id, realm_id, token_commitment, claim_nonce, audience, verification_id, and binding_proof_digest of the complete signed binding_proof object.

verification_method.description: Current verification method of subject_account_id.principal_id; the admission context separately binds the exact station_id.

transcript_digest.description: Digest of the canonical ak.invite.claim.subject_proof.v1 transcript.

join_policy_component.$comment: Value shape of the join_policy component of realm_policy_bundle_payload; it has no separate Event kind and no separate cell family, and rides inside the ak.component.realm.policy_bundle.v1 cas_register value. Structural validation is JSON Schema; property-level gate_id uniqueness within gates[] cannot be expressed in pure JSON Schema 2020-12, so it is enforced by (a) reducer rejection with reason_code=join_policy_duplicate_gate_id and (b) tools/artifact_lint check_join_policy_gate_id_uniqueness over fixtures and Markdown examples. uniqueItems below catches whole-object duplicates as a baseline. See zh/governance/join-policy.md §3 / §3.1.

join_policy_gate_id.description: Stable gate identifier, unique within one join policy gates[]. Both the definition site and every reference site (gate_proofs[].gate_id, Answer.gate_id) MUST use this one definition so the two lexical spaces cannot drift. The pattern is the document_local_symbol floor of common-fields.md 2.1: it mechanically excludes the ak: namespace that typed_object_id and responsibility_did own exclusively, and it admits the runtime:<challenge_id> spelling used by challenge gate proofs. See zh/governance/join-policy.md 3.1.

key_backup_active_series_payload.description: Payload for ak.key_backup.active_series. The standalone ak.schema.key_backup_active_series.v1 schema carries the authoritative signed active-series record shape.

keypackage_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped MLS KeyPackage reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

member_identity_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.member.identity.update. Append-only replacement event for one Realm-scoped member display/subject projection segment. Service-visible metadata names the segment and the prior events it replaces; the segment body is plaintext or the original encrypted envelope and MUST contain the complete data for that segment. Handle lifecycle is excluded from this event and is governed by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims.

segment.description: v1 core defines a single full MemberIdentity segment. Narrower segments require a future schema/profile revision that extends this enum or defines a new payload schema; v1 receivers MUST reject unknown segment values.

replaces.description: Prior ak.member.identity.update events in the same (realm_id, actor_id, segment) that this event supersedes for current profile projection. Referenced events remain immutable history.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of the replaced event's full payload.identity_payload carrier wrapper ({member_identity: ...} or {encrypted_payload: ...}). Prevents replacing a different payload under a reused or confused event id.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard for the current effective set of this (realm_id, member_id, segment). When present, it MUST equal the writer-observed effective-set digest before applying this event: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON {realm_id, member_id, segment, effective_events:[{event_id, segment, payload_digest}]}, with effective_events sorted by (segment,event_id). It is distinct from the locally derived identity_payload carrier digest and from a roster member_display_state_digest.

member_id.description: Exact member identity. Account members use the AccountId-bearing account variant; non-account hosted principals and directly authoring services use their explicit ActorId variants.

gate_proofs.description: Join-policy gate proofs evaluated by governance/join-policy.md before accepting membership=join. maxItems aligns with the gates 1..16 bound in join_policy_component; see zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md.

reason.description: Bounded human-readable audit note. It never supplies membership authority or proves cascade provenance.

agent_controller_binding.description: Required by semantic admission for every Native Personal Agent join and every controller-membership-ended cleanup. Non-Agent membership MUST reject it.

membership_state.description: Canonical materialized membership state enum shared by ak.member.state (Realm) and ak.circle.member.state (Circle). Invite is a separate pending workflow and is never a member state. `knock` denotes a pending self-authored join request; see governance/join-policy.md §9 and models/circle.md §9.1.

subject_id.description: Authoritative mention target principal DID. For native personal agent selectors this is the agent principal DID, not the controller DID.

handle_at_time.description: Canonical handle snapshot at compose time. Audit / debug / search metadata only; renderers MUST resolve the current primary handle from subject_id instead (zh/identity/identity-handles.md §3.8.1-§3.8.2).

controller_subject_id.description: Audit metadata for @<controller-handle>/<agent_slug> inputs. MUST NOT replace subject_id for routing, authorization, or attribution.

controller_handle_at_time.description: Canonical controller handle snapshot from an agent selector input. Audit / debug / search metadata only.

mimi_message_provenance.description: External attribution for a message Event authored and signed by a MIMI facade service. This object never transfers the attributed sender's signing authority to the facade.

message_create_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.create. If content/encrypted_content contains an audience_mention AST node (for example @all or @here), reducer admission and notification dispatch MUST additionally enforce ak.message.mention.broadcast plus the audience policy / max_recipient / rate-limit rules in zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3. @here maps to audience="strand_engaged" and is not presence-filtered.

allOf.$comment: ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry revision_root. Reducer initializes revision_root := id on create; only ak.message.revise events may set it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `revision_root/message_create_payload`.

ak.message.create payload MUST NOT carry message_id. The materialized Message.id is obtained by retyping the creating Event.event_id's full 33-byte / 44-character token; a second identity would create a conflicting truth source. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9 and forbidden-wire-fields.json `message_id/message_create_payload`.

reply_to_id.description: Optional creation convenience: the message this one replies to. The reducer records it as the message's reply linkage (lifting it onto the message content) and surfaces it as a replies_to relation in the message projection; it does not require a separate canonical ak.relation event. The materialized Message object itself carries no reply_to scalar. See strand-and-message.md §9.1.

agent_context.description: Auditable authorization context required when a native Agent authors the message.

message_encrypted_content.description: MLS-protected Message ContentBlock bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_encrypted_metadata.description: MLS-protected Message metadata bound to its one canonical decrypted schema.

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

message_redact_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.redact, the object-scoped redact kind registered for Message. Message is the only object that enters state=redacted through its own kind rather than a cross-object ak.redaction, which is why message.schema.json materializes redaction_ref (models/common-fields.md 5.2). message_id is the single target carrier, so the ak.component.object.redaction.v1 cell subject is always the Message typed ID.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the redacted message's parent Strand. Optional: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

message_revise_payload.description: Payload for ak.message.revise. Revisions that introduce new direct mentions MAY generate mention notifications only when the implementation can compare against the previous accepted visible revision. Revisions that introduce an audience_mention AST node (including @all / @here mappings) MUST satisfy the same ak.message.mention.broadcast and policy gates as create.

track_name.description: Active track_name of the target Strand. Optional on revise/redact: when omitted, reducers MUST resolve from the existing message identified by message_id. When present, MUST equal that resolved track_name.

mimi_room_binding_payload.description: Payload for ak.mimi.room_binding. Writes the ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell whose subject is payload.mimi_room_uri (see event-kind-registry.json cell_subject). Authoritative field set: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §3. The binding is a projection of an Arkret Realm/Strand discussion track into a MIMI room; it is not canonical truth. Creation / update / revocation MUST hold ak.policy.manage, ak.realm.admin, or an equivalent interop capability. E2EE MIMI rooms MUST bind mls_group_id and pass the active MLS security_frontier_digest gate.

mimi_room_uri.description: Canonical MIMI room URI and the cell subject source for ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 (registry cell_subject.kind = uri). The closed canonical form and the full percent-encoding that turns it into a CellRef subject are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md section 4 and zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4; a non-canonical spelling MUST be rejected with schema_violation rather than normalized.

binding_scope.description: Arkret Realm + Strand scope this MIMI room projects. strand_id MUST point at an accepted Strand with discussion track enabled inside realm_id; the MIMI room timeline only projects that Strand's discussion track.

hub_provider_id.description: Service DID explicitly delegated by Realm policy, Organization DID, or participant DID to host the hub role.

mls_group_id.description: MLS group id. MUST be present for E2EE MIMI rooms.

policy_root.description: Digest of the Arkret policy component projection bound to this MIMI room binding.

status.description: Lifecycle state of the binding. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are defined in zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2. accepted bindings authorize projection; revoked bindings stop new MIMI writes; migrating stops new writes until a verified migration proof returns the binding to accepted or revoked.

effective_scope.description: Exact MLS scope of the failed Commit/Welcome. MUST match the referenced event governance binding and the canonical group-id derivation.

base_epoch.description: Expected previous MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.previous_epoch.

next_epoch.description: Committed next MLS epoch. MUST equal governance_binding.next_epoch.

commit_bytes_b64.description: Unpadded base64url RFC 9420 MLS Commit message. Receivers verify commit_digest before applying it.

mls_genesis_payload.$comment: Schema requires both effective_scope and governance_binding. Reducers/verifiers must additionally compare effective_scope with governance_binding.effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express deep cross-field equality. v1 Genesis has exactly one initial principal leaf: the creator. Creator coordinates are not payload fields: the creator principal is Event.actor_id and the creator device is projected from the fragment of the sole producer proof verification_method, so carrying creator_principal_id, creator_device_id, initial_keypackage_refs or another initial-member list is a schema_violation. Every non-creator joins through a later Add/Commit/Welcome.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the MLS group created at epoch 0. MUST match governance_binding.effective_scope.

group_info_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the exact RFC 9420 GroupInfo bytes. The embedded sha256 value MUST equal group_info_digest without the sha256: prefix.

group_info_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes obtained by base64url-decoding group_info_bytes_b64 from the standard group-state-material operation.

ratchet_tree_ref.description: Content-addressed reference to the exact RFC 9420 ratchet_tree extension bytes for epoch 0. The embedded sha256 value MUST equal ratchet_tree_digest without the sha256: prefix.

ratchet_tree_digest.description: SHA-256 of the raw bytes obtained by base64url-decoding ratchet_tree_bytes_b64 from the standard group-state-material operation.

frozen_public_key_b64u.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of exactly 32 raw X25519 public-key bytes. Decoding failure, padding, non-canonical re-encoding or any other length is schema_invalid.

organization_recovery_key_tuple.description: One logical Realm-authority organization recovery public-key tuple. hpke_suite is fixed to the v1 X25519/ChaCha20-Poly1305 profile. Resolving key_agreement_ref at admission must yield a current exact method whose raw key bytes equal frozen_public_key_b64u and whose controller projects to holder_principal_id. Resolving holder_signing_ref must yield a current signing method with the same controller. Custody topology and threshold policy are not wire fields.

holder_proof.description: Holder proof over RFC 8785 JCS of {realm_id,new_key_tuple,holder_trusted_basis}. proof.verification_method MUST equal new_key_tuple.holder_signing_ref byte-for-byte, resolve current, and its controller MUST project to new_key_tuple.holder_principal_id. The proof key is that exact method key. The proof is excluded from its own transcript.

organization_recovery_key_register_paylo.description: Closed Realm Control Move that registers the first active organization recovery key after Realm create is already activated. All duplicated acceptance fields must match byte-for-byte. holder_trusted_basis is the complete canonical holder-pinned accepted Seal antichain containing the Realm-create evidence, or a later holder-pinned basis that causally covers it. Registration is a CAS from no active tuple.

organization_recovery_key_rotate_payload.description: Closed CAS rotation of the unique active Realm recovery-key tuple. expected_previous_key_evidence_ref/Seal must equal the current effective tuple provenance. The new holder acceptance anchor must be that prior holder-trusted evidence Seal or a holder-pinned accepted successor. Historical tuples remain verifiable and archives are never rewritten.

frozen_public_key_b64u.description: Byte-for-byte equal to the registered tuple's canonical unpadded base64url of 32 X25519 public-key bytes.

holder_trusted_basis.description: Complete canonical accepted Seal antichain independently verified and pinned by the holder in the register/rotate acceptance transcript. Direct Seal traversal from this basis to the archive target must replay accepted_key_evidence_ref into the effective registered tuple; a source or service cannot manufacture, narrow or replace the basis.

organization_recovery_archive.description: Exactly one RRK archive for this exporter transition. transition_digest is the mls_transition_digest: commit_digest for Commit and the closed Genesis core digest excluding organization_recovery_archive, outer EventId and proofs. accepted_key_evidence_ref identifies the exact register/rotate Event; its reducer-effective tuple is proved by direct Seal replay from holder_trusted_basis to the archive target, never by a singular activation Seal field. HPKE info/AAD binds every public field above except enc/ciphertext and never the containing EventId.

realm_id.description: Parent Realm identifier. MUST equal effective_scope.realm_id.

circle_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='circle'. MUST equal effective_scope.circle_id.

sidecar_id.description: Present only when effective_scope.kind='sidecar'. MUST equal effective_scope.sidecar_id.

effective_scope.description: Tagged MLS governance scope. Realm-default groups use {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle groups use {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}; Sidecar groups use {kind:'sidecar', realm_id, sidecar_id}. This field, not Strand id or track, determines key and participant scope.

security_frontier_digest.description: Canonical digest of the closed key-access frontier for this MLS scope: effective membership; only participant device/Agent keys referenced by current or pending MLS leaves; MLS group membership; and encryption/history policy that changes current or historical key access. Capability, ordinary metadata, moderation, routing, contact and consent-only facts are excluded unless their accepted effect actually removes an MLS leaf. Producers do not supply an arbitrary event list; every verifier rederives the digest from accepted Seal state.

sidecar_binding.description: Required exactly for effective_scope.kind='sidecar'; forbidden for Realm and Circle MLS scopes.

binding_profile.description: Explicit operation-local profile that defines how this governance binding is interpreted. Full E2EE uses ak.profile.mls_governance_binding.full.v1; the only v1 downgrade profile is ak.profile.e2ee_relaxed.v1. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field is missing, unsupported, inconsistent with the effective Realm policy derived from mls_send_pause, or unsupported by ServiceDescribe. It is not a Realm active-profile declaration.

reducer_profile.description: Reducer profile used to derive the closed security_frontier_digest projection. Receivers MUST fail closed when this field does not equal the Realm reducer-profile cell at the binding's authenticated frontier.

mls_governance_binding.$comment: Schema requires tagged scope ID presence rules. Reducers/verifiers additionally compare realm_id and the circle_id/sidecar_id value against effective_scope; JSON Schema cannot express those cross-field string equalities.

keypackage_id.description: Arkret MLS-profile KeyPackage identity. This is the registered ak:mls:kp:<uuidv7> special form, not an opaque external identifier.

keypackage_digest.description: Canonical hash of the MLS KeyPackage bytes identified by keypackage_ref.

proposal_bytes_b64.description: Unpadded base64url encoding of the complete RFC 9420 MLS Proposal message. The bytes are always inline so restart and offline replay never depend on a process-local proposal store or an auxiliary object route.

proposal_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the decoded proposal_bytes_b64 bytes. Receivers MUST verify it before admitting the Proposal to an MLS proposal store.

target_actor_id.description: Complete accepted target membership identity, including its Station. The endpoint signing principal alone is not membership authority.

target_authorization_incarnation.description: Required only for add. Exact current Realm or Realm+Circle membership incarnation that this Add admits; the effective scope in governance_binding selects the matching branch. A winning Commit consuming this proposal is the unique replay-derived join_epoch source for that incarnation.

recipient_pairwise_verification_method.description: Exact did:key:<multibase>#<same-multibase> method for recipient_pairwise_actor_id; receivers MUST verify canonical Ed25519 multibase equality.

claim_ref.description: KeyPackage claim binding validated before Welcome decryption. Exactly one trust branch is present: PCR-authorized device, independently authorized Native Agent runtime, or Realm-local minimal-metadata pairwise did:key endpoint.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event for the claimed Native Agent runtime key.

claim_envelope.description: Closed requester device, Native-Agent, or Realm-local pairwise signature binding the claimed KeyPackage to this Welcome, Realm, exact claim_request_id challenge and Welcome digest before decrypting the Welcome. Device/Agent signer authority is established by accepted authorization Events and their in-envelope Station admission proofs; the pairwise signer is established by its exact did:key method and Realm-local actor. No signer-evidence sidecar is carried.

welcome_digest.description: Exactly sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the raw RFC 9420 Welcome bytes obtained by strictly decoding top-level ciphertext as canonical unpadded base64url>.

claim_receipt.description: Destination-signed receipt used for both same-service and remote claims. The receiving destination Station validates it against its durable claim ledger before accepting the Welcome.

ciphertext.description: Canonical unpadded base64url encoding of the complete RFC 9420 Welcome message. Receivers MUST decode successfully, reject padding and non-canonical encodings, and require re-encoding the decoded bytes to be byte-identical to this field.

moderation_decision_lift_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision.lift. Writes an or_set remove effect on the same ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell, removing exactly the dots enumerated in observed_dot_ids, which MUST belong to the decision identified by decision_ref. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5.2 (appeal verdict=overturn MUST pair a lift whose target equals decision_ref in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction).

target_ref.description: The moderated target whose ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell the lift mutates. Same cell subject as the original ak.moderation.decision.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the prior ak.moderation.decision Event whose sealed tag is being removed.

observed_dot_ids.description: Exact add dots being removed. Every dot's event_id segment MUST equal the complete EventId token of decision_ref, so a lift can only revoke the appealed decision; adds from other issuers stay active and keep folding by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review. A lift is a partial revocation, so or_set_remove_observed is forbidden here - it would remove every surviving add on the cell. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2 and zh/governance/content-moderation.md section 5.5.2.

moderation_decision_payload.description: Payload for ak.moderation.decision. A sealed moderation decision that writes an or_set add effect onto the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell whose subject is target_ref. Multiple active adds fold by hard_deny > quarantine > require_review > none. dismiss is valid only when target_ref identifies the report Event being closed and contributes none to the content verdict fold. Runtime allow and soft_deny remain out-of-band outcomes. The actor MUST independently hold the registered ak.moderation.decision capability.

target_ref.description: The moderated target (event / object). Canonical string of this ref is the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell subject.

decision.description: Sealed moderation-state decision verb. dismiss only resolves a report queue item and does not loosen the target content verdict. allow and soft_deny are out-of-band runtime outcomes.

issuer_id.description: Actor or service DID issuing the sealed moderation decision. Reducers use it as part of the or_set add tag and appeal separation-of-duties check.

request_canonical_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the moderated request or Event preview. Part of the moderation_state or_set add tag.

action.description: Optional finer-grained §5.3 moderation_policy action family entry that the decision verb maps to (content-moderation.md §8.1).

reason_code.description: Machine-readable diagnostic. Values that cross service or federation boundaries MUST be registered in error-code-registry.json reason_codes.

modify_decision_ref.description: Set when this decision is the new decision emitted atomically by an appeal verdict=modify (content-moderation.md §5.5.2); reducer verifies it matches the same-batch appeal event id.

effective_scope.description: Governance boundary for the report. Defaults to the Realm scope when absent; Circle-scoped targets MUST resolve to the target Circle and route only to scoped moderators/admins.

provenance.description: Admission discriminator (contract-registry admission_variants). Absent or "self": the reporter's own device authored the Event (self_authored_proof, actor == reporter). "mimi_facade": the Event is service-authored by the MIMI provider facade (service_attested); reporter carries the Arkret principal resolved under extensions/mimi-interop.md section 10/11, and source_provider is required.

source_provider_id.description: Origin MIMI provider's service DID for a facade-mapped report. Required exactly when provenance is "mimi_facade"; forbidden otherwise.

morph_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Morph object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

morph_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.stage.set. Mutates Morph.stage / Morph.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/morph.md §2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes.

morph_update_payload.description: Payload class for ak.morph.update. Patches ordinary Morph fields on the Morph identified by target_ref. morph_kind is create-locked by ak.morph.create and MUST NOT appear in patch; stage and stage_changed_at are single-sourced by ak.morph.stage.set.

notary_fault_censorship_payload.description: Notary censorship evidence: a signed control-plane receipt whose event digest is provably absent from the obliged Seal's control_event_set_root and that received neither signed-reject nor defer. Does NOT automatically disqualify the notary; adds an audit fault record. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.2.

receipt.description: The signed control-plane receipt issued under proposal_intake_sla_ms (event_digest, received_at, receipt_seq, issuer, signature).

seal_ref.description: The Seal that was obliged to include / signed-reject / defer the receipted Control Move.

non_membership_proof.description: Sorted-neighbor non-membership proof for the receipted event digest against seal_ref's control_event_set_root.

missing_rejection_or_defer_proof.description: Optional structured evidence that no signed-reject / defer covering the receipt exists in the obliged window.

notary_fault_equivocation_payload.description: Notary equivocation evidence: two Seals signed by signer_id that violate the slot rule (same (realm_id, notary_seq) with different canonical bytes, or notary_seq=k+1 not descending from the same signer's notary_seq=k). Admission is verification-only: the two conflicting notary signatures are the complete authorization; no capability grant is consulted. See authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.1.

object_lifecycle_payload.description: Generic lifecycle payload for Strand / Circle / Morph archive-restore-tombstone style events. The target object is single-sourced by target_ref; target_state may describe the intended lifecycle result but cannot replace the target object reference.

or_set_dot.description: Canonical OR-Set dot: "ak:event:" + event_id + ":" + write_index, where write_index is the 0-based index of the write in the event kind's registry cell_writes[]. See zh/models/event-and-patch.md section 2.4.2.

organization_discovery_state_payload.description: State payload for an Organization discovery declaration. organization_principal_id is the stable cell subject.

organization_moderation_policy_state_pay.description: Closed Organization moderation-policy state. A producer identifies the Organization by exactly one canonical DID or typed Organization id; the first present identifier is the registered coalesce subject. value carries the sole v1 Organization moderation-policy family.

participant_binding.description: Token issuer's signed commitment over (realm_id, call_id, focus_id, actor_id, device_id, participant_identity, expires_at) for a media participant. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md §3 and crypto-media/call-state.md §4.1. v1 uses the single scheme ak.media.participant_binding.v1.

issuer_kid.description: DID URL (with fragment) of the token issuer service signing key. MUST resolve to a service DID present in the current-epoch ak.realm.media_service.service_id.

data_classes.description: Closed machine-checkable classes of plaintext or reversible derived content this service may receive. Human-readable purposes do not replace this field.

policy_action_state_payload.description: Closed policy action-log payload. Exactly one policy_id or action_id is present and becomes the registered coalesce subject; value carries the sole v1 approval-action document family.

policy_rule_state_payload.description: Policy rule state payload. rule_id is the stable ak.component.policy.rule.v1 cell subject and MUST equal the rule_id of the PolicyRule this event asserts, whose closed shape is defined by policy.schema.json #/$defs/policy_rule (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5). The cell is an ordered_log, so each accepted event appends one revision rather than replacing the previous one.

rule_id.description: Rule identifier, same lexical form as policy.schema.json #/$defs/policy_rule rule_id.

policy_set_state_payload.description: Closed Policy definition state payload. policy_id is the stable policy cell subject. value.schema selects exactly one of the two v1 Policy document families directly in this schema; unknown families fail schema validation.

profile_realm_override_payload.description: Realm-scoped actor profile override payload for ak.profile.realm_override. target_ref is the Actor Profile being overridden; target_realm_id is the Realm where the override applies. resolution and every resolution.* descendant path are reducer-managed projections of the PCR resolution cell and are forbidden here for the same reason they are forbidden on the generic profile write surface; the object-specific forbidden path set is machine-indexed in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json.

reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext.description: Plaintext JSON encrypted into reaction_payload.encrypted_payload.ciphertext for ak.reaction.add / ak.reaction.remove in E2EE realms. The outer reaction_payload.key remains required and carries the service-visible routing tag; this plaintext carries the real reaction key and optional user content.

key.description: Canonical reaction key after client-side normalization: a single NFC Unicode emoji cluster or profile-registered short tag. This is the real reaction key, not the outer HMAC routing tag.

annotation.description: Optional user-visible annotation associated with the reaction.

remove_add_event_ids.description: Optional client-side convergence accelerator for ak.reaction.remove: add event ids that this remove intends to tombstone. MUST be omitted on ak.reaction.add. Service-side reducers still rely on the outer event actor_id, target_ref, key, and causal frontier.

reaction_payload.description: Reducer input for ak.reaction.add and ak.reaction.remove. The cell is a core OR-Set of reaction assertions and both kinds project one or_set_add; default-view membership is keyed on (actor_id, target_ref, key), and a remove tombstones every add from the same actor with the same key that is not strictly causally later than it, which includes the adds concurrent with it. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.8 for the authoritative Reaction model (target scope, OR-Set, authz, anti-abuse) and zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9 for the plaintext-vs-encrypted policy.

key.description: Reaction key. Plaintext scopes SHOULD use a single Unicode emoji cluster or registered short tag. End-to-end-encrypted scopes MUST carry the v1 keyed-HMAC routing tag here and carry the equivalent base64url tag in encrypted_payload.encryption_context.routing_context. The exact derivation is ExpandWithLabel(routing_root[N], "ak.reaction-routing-v1", JCS({effective_scope,target_ref,routing_window}), 32), followed by HMAC-SHA256 over NFC(canonical_emoji); routing_root[N] is the epoch history_secret for exporter mode or MLS-Exporter("ak.reaction-routing-root-v1", canonical_effective_scope_key_bytes(effective_scope), KDF.Nh) for standard mode. routing_window is derived from outer Event.created_at and does not require an hourly MLS Commit. See zh/crypto-media/encryption-and-audit.md §2.9. The canonical emoji travels only in encrypted_payload.

annotation.description: Optional free-form annotation (e.g. issue triage label). MUST be omitted when `encrypted_payload` is present; in E2EE realms the annotation MUST instead be carried inside `encrypted_payload`.

encrypted_payload.description: Encrypted carrier for the canonical reaction key and any annotation in E2EE realms. The decrypted plaintext JSON MUST validate as #/$defs/reaction_encrypted_payload_plaintext. When present, outer plaintext `key` MUST be the routing tag and `annotation` MUST be omitted; service-side OR-Set convergence still uses the outer routing key.

read_receipt_policy_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.read_receipt_policy. Closed object so typos cause schema_violation. The enclosing Event carries realm_id; payload does not duplicate it. minProperties=1 rejects an empty no-op policy. The sole compliance exception is child_privacy_tightening_against_required; history_access has no read-receipt compatibility branch. See zh/discovery/read-receipts.md §2.5.1.

child_privacy_tightening_against_require.description: Privacy-floor escape switch. When the parent policy sets disclosure='required' and this is true, a child Realm MAY tighten disclosure to 'optional' or 'disabled'; otherwise the reducer rejects with read_receipt_compliance_floor_violated. Absent means false.

alias.description: Canonical realm alias <localpart>:<domain> (zh/discovery/object-addressing.md §3.3). Sigil-free: the display forms #general:acme.example and general@acme.example MUST NOT reach the wire. <domain> is the issuing authority and MUST be an authority domain of this Realm's trust_domain; a foreign-domain claim MUST be rejected with reason realm_alias_authority_mismatch.

realm_alias_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.alias, the ONLY wire carrier of a Realm alias. A declaration writes the complete canonical alias; {tombstone:true} is a durable value tombstone that removes the alias from effective resolution without erasing the cell history. realm-genesis.schema.json and realm-profile.schema.json are closed and have no alias property, and ak.realm.create / ak.realm.profile payloads MUST NOT carry one.

realm_authority_reset_payload.description: ak.realm.authority.reset — advance the authority generation. Every grant anchored to the previous generation fails at read time without any cascading write. Destructive: this is not how a controller hands the Realm over, and it MUST carry an independent confirmation.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root cell value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite.

destructive_confirmation.description: Explicit confirmation token. A reset discards an entire authority tree, so it MUST NOT be reachable by replaying a transfer body.

realm_create_payload.description: Minimal identity and security-root payload for ak.realm.create. User-visible, mutable, policy and reducer-derived Realm state is carried only by registered bootstrap facets. Every genesis, including Principal Control Realm and managed Agent PCR, requires a canonical 32-octet genesis_salt.

realm_digest_suite_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.digest_suite_transition under ak.profile.hash_transition.v1. The containing Transition Seal commits the pre-transition governance view with previous_state_root and the post-transition view with state_root.

realm_notary_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.notary. The enclosing Control Move MUST CAS the current ak.component.notary.v1 head and the current notary authority MUST finalize the containing Seal.

realm_organization_payload.description: Organization-side endorsement or revocation for a Realm relationship. Reducer validation MUST require realm_id to match the top-level Event.realm_id, organization_id to identify an Organization principal in accepted registration state, the Realm-side writer to hold ak.realm.admin, and authorization to verify against current organization DID control evidence or a delegated service whose purpose covers this relationship and control_scopes. The stable organization_id is not itself resolvable DID material.

statement_id.description: Stable id of this organization statement. It is audit identity, not the reducer cell subject; the reducer cell subject is (organization_id, relationship).

realm_id.description: Realm the organization statement is bound to. MUST equal the enclosing Event.realm_id.

organization_id.description: Stable Organization principal identity that endorses, governs, sponsors, certifies, or revokes the Realm relationship. This did_core_id is bound to current Organization DID evidence through accepted registration/resolution state; it is not itself resolvable.

relationship.description: Relationship being asserted or revoked for this organization and Realm.

control_scopes.description: Machine-readable scopes covered by the organization's consent. A scope here is an endorsement boundary only; actual Realm control still requires the corresponding Realm policy, notary, capability, or service-binding event.

expires_at.description: Administrative review/renewal hint only. It does not auto-transition account status; a later AccountStatusRecord is required and remains subject to sequence and terminal rules.

realm_frontier_digest.description: Optional digest of the Realm control frontier the organization evaluated when issuing this statement.

organization_policy_ref.description: Optional DID-document delegation URL, policy object, governance decision, or attestation reference used to evaluate the statement.

authorization.description: Organization-side authorization proof. This is independent of the Realm-side ak.realm.admin authorization required to write the event into Realm history.

issuer_id.description: Stable Organization or delegated-service principal identity that issued this statement. The issuer_id is a did_core_id; verification_method and accepted registration/delegation state carry the DID evidence required to verify the issuer.

delegation_ref.description: Required when issuer_role is governance_service or account_authority. It MUST resolve to a live organization DID delegation whose purpose covers ak.realm.organization and the requested relationship/control_scopes.

executed_by.description: Optional exact ActorId of the human administrator or service actor that initiated the organization-side decision. This does not become the organization principal.

proof.description: Signature, threshold transcript, or governance-service attestation over the canonical organization statement binding statement_id, realm_id, organization_id, relationship, status, control_scopes, issued_at, validity window, and statement replacement/revocation fields.

realm_owner_transfer_payload.description: ak.realm.owner.transfer — rotate the controller binding of the Realm authority-root cell. It changes controller_id and increments controller_epoch only: authority_generation, the cell ref and every existing grant are untouched, so the whole authority tree issued by the previous controller stays valid. This is not a reparent — the root never moves.

expected_state_digest.description: JCS SHA-256 digest of the authority-root cell value this Event expects to replace. The reducer MUST compare-and-swap against it and reject a stale value rather than overwrite.

controller_id.description: Exact ActorId of the successor that becomes the root controller. Its control proof MUST bind this complete identity; a bare principal DID or parallel Station sidecar is insufficient.

patch.description: The authority-root member selected by the author. The reducer also increments controller_epoch from the CAS-frozen pre-state; every other member is preserved verbatim.

successor_acceptance.description: Independent acceptance proof from the successor. The current controller proof, this proof, the payload and expected_state_digest MUST all enter the same signing transcript. The successor controller_epoch is uniquely computed from the expected pre-state, so neither party signs a producer-supplied counter.

realm_policy_bundle_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.policy_bundle — the payload IS this flat closed object (not a state wrapper); event-envelope.schema.json dispatches the kind directly to this def. The closed property set is the complete set of Realm policy components that have no independent facet Event kind. Components that DO have their own kind and cell (ak.realm.join_rule, ak.realm.history_access, ak.realm.read_receipt_policy, ak.realm.asset_privacy_policy, ak.realm.media_service, ak.realm.plaintext_visible_services, ...) are written by those events and are already covered by policy_root's ak.component.realm.*policy* leaf filter; they MUST NOT be echoed here. ak.realm.policy is not a third inline carrier: it only selects an independently defined Policy object by policy_id.
realm_policy_bundle_payload.description: Enabled Realm policy component set, written wholesale into the ak.component.realm.policy_bundle.v1 cas_register cell: every revision restates the complete enabled component set and the Realm object's derived policy fields re-derive from the latest accepted bundle. policy_revision is strictly monotonic; the reducer rejects rollback or gaps, and policy_frontier_digest MUST cover policy_revision (see contract-registry event-kind row and models/realm-and-space.md section 2.3).

policy_revision.description: Strictly monotonic bundle revision; rollback or gaps are rejected.

federation_policy.description: The sole producer carrier of the effective Realm federation policy. High-assurance Realm reducers require closed, restricted, or quarantine and reject open.

mls_send_pause.description: Declaring advisory downgrades the MLS send pause from MUST to SHOULD and is the sole Realm policy carrier of effective_e2ee_relaxed; omitting the field in a later revision reverts to the strict full-binding default.

relaxed_window_max_ms.description: Policy-derived relaxed-mode removed-member decryption window. It is meaningful only when mls_send_pause=advisory. Omitting it means the 30000 ms default. The 300000 ms absolute ceiling is enforced by the reducer and independently by every receiver with reason_code relaxed_window_exceeds_ceiling, NOT by this schema.
relaxed_window_max_ms.$comment: Deliberately unbounded above; ak.vector.e2ee_relaxed.window_exceeds_ceiling.v1 requires 300001 to reach the reducer.

media_service_decrypts.description: Whether a media service listed in plaintext_visible_services may decrypt call media. Defaults to false when absent. It is one of three conditions that MUST all hold (ak.realm.media_service declaration + plaintext_visible_services grant + this toggle). Because it changes who may receive media keys, it enters the media scope security_frontier_digest; a generation that does not cover the current value cannot authorize media decryption. See crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 8.2.

handle_issuer_policies.description: Ordered Realm handle-issuer trust policy used by primary-handle resolution. Earlier entries have higher tie-break priority; every issuer is domain-scoped.

member_action.description: How this Realm disposes of a principal's membership when the account enters deactivated. Defaults to leave_self_initiated when the component is absent. Unrecognized values fail closed to retain_membership with a policy parse warning and MUST NOT silently fall back to the default. The single authority for the closed enum and its disposition semantics is identity/account-lifecycle.md section 7.1.

cell_lattices.description: Complete current client hint set for Realm-specific cell lattice diagnostics. Registered reducer contracts remain authoritative.

consent_required.description: When true, every invite into this Realm MUST pass the holder consent admission gate in identity/consent-model.md section 6.1 before the invite Control Move is submitted. It MUST NOT be read as permission for a cross-Realm CBA precondition.

allowed_third_party_invite_verification_.description: Complete current allow-set of service DIDs trusted to attest 3PID ownership for ak.invite.third_party / ak.invite.claim. The array is whole-value replacement state in this policy-bundle revision, not an incremental patch. Absence and [] both deny every third-party invite verification service. Removing a DID in a later policy_revision revokes it for every later claim re-check; no separate tombstone exists. Reducers MUST evaluate the current accepted bundle cell on a fresh basis before accepting ak.invite.claim.

leakage_class.description: Machine-readable search leakage class. ak.profile.search.blind_index.v1 uses deterministic_token; ak.profile.search.forward_private.v1 requires forward_private; access_hiding is reserved for explicit PIR/ORAM-backed profiles.

token_rotation_cadence_ms.description: Maximum intended interval between search token generations for profiles that rotate index keys or OPRF blinds.

realm_set_default_strand_payload.description: Payload for ak.realm.set_default_strand. Sets / changes the Realm's authoritative default discussion Strand pointer. Reducer projects strand_id into the Realm projection default_strand_id (single authoritative pointer; avoids multi-default dirty state). Reducer MUST verify strand_id references a projected, non-tombstoned Strand in this Realm; a dangling reference MUST be rejected with failed_precondition. The Strand projection is_default is a derived marker (strand_id == realm.default_strand_id), never independent storage. expected_default_strand_id compiles to a cell head_eq precondition for optimistic concurrency (CAS). Absent and explicit null are normalized to the same null value before comparison, so omission asserts head_eq null and is only valid while the cell is still in its initial no-default state; once a default is set the field MUST be present, otherwise the reducer MUST reject with failed_precondition and MUST NOT overwrite unconditionally.

expected_default_strand_id.description: Optimistic-concurrency guard compared as a whole value after absent and explicit null are normalized to null. The reducer accepts the write only if the Realm's current default_strand_id equals this value (null asserts no default is currently set). Omission therefore asserts head_eq null and MUST fail once a default exists. Mismatch MUST be rejected (failed_precondition).

realm_upgrade_state_payload.description: Realm reducer-profile upgrade payload. target_reducer_profile is the new value written to the Realm reducer-profile singleton control cell. The Event's standard head_eq precondition binds the current cell value.

target_reducer_profile.description: Registered reducer profile id this Realm upgrades to.

relation_create_payload.description: Relation creation. The payload carries the whole relation object under `relation`: the registered effect_projection is set value = payload.relation, and event-and-patch.md 2.4.2 permits a projection to move an existing root path wholesale but never to assemble one, so a flat {relation_id, kind, from_ref, to_ref} form has no derivable cell value.

relation_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.relation.tombstone. relation_id is the sole target carrier for the irreversible active -> tombstoned transition; target_ref and update-style patch fields are forbidden. When supplied, reason is retained on the Event and is not copied into the materialized Relation object.

relation_update_payload.description: Relation patch payload. effective_scope and every effective_scope.* descendant path are the reducer-materialized projection of the verified Event.scope_ref and are forbidden on this generic update surface (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed); the object-specific forbidden path set is machine-indexed in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. When present it MUST equal the writer-observed digest of the frozen pre-state this patch was computed against; a mismatch MUST fail closed. Registered as the apply_patch projection's expected_prestate source in contract-registry.json.

resource_discovery_state_payload.description: State payload for actor, applet, and handle discovery declarations. resource_id is the stable cell subject; value carries the schema-versioned discovery state.

rsvp_encrypted_response.description: Encrypted RSVP response envelope. The content_type is pinned so a receiver can route the ciphertext to exactly one decrypted schema; the plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response.

rsvp_entry.description: Complete RSVP cell value. The whole entry is the mv_register set value, so every head independently carries the schedule the responder observed plus the response itself.

schedule_basis_refs.description: Non-empty schedule revision frontier the responder actually observed, as event_digest values sorted in ascending canonical UTF-8 byte order. MUST be a subset of the envelope causal_refs[], which caps it at the same 128 entries. A frontier larger than 128 MUST fail closed with schedule_frontier_too_large rather than being truncated.

response.description: Plaintext response branch. Only admissible when the target Strand effective scope encryption floor permits plaintext and the receiving service declares the rsvp_response plaintext data class.

encrypted_response.description: Encrypted response branch; content_type is pinned to application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json and the decrypted plaintext MUST validate against rsvp_response. Required when the effective scope encryption floor is e2ee_required.

rsvp_response.description: RSVP response object. Used directly by rsvp_entry.response and as the decrypted plaintext of rsvp_entry.encrypted_response, whose content_type is application/vnd.arkret.calendar-rsvp-response+json. status and comment always share one encryption boundary; a plaintext status with an encrypted comment is not a valid shape.

comment.description: Optional responder comment. An empty response is expressed by omitting the field, never by an empty string.

event_ref.description: Calendar event Strand id; encoded as a ak:strand: typed id.

occurrence.description: JSON null for the whole series, or the canonical recurrence instance key: YYYY-MM-DD for all-day events and YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[Zone] for timed events. The date component MUST be a real proleptic-Gregorian date, not merely match the digit pattern. The producer MUST canonicalize before signing; receivers MUST reject non-canonical keys instead of rewriting them.

schema_define_state_payload.description: Schema definition payload. value is a JSON Schema 2020-12 document validated by the executable ak.validator.json_schema_2020_12_definition.v1 profile; value.$id is the stable definition cell subject.

sidecar_context_attach_payload.description: Controller-signed versioned attachment of a source Realm context to an existing native Sidecar. It creates no Strand or Relation protocol object.

sidecar_create_payload.description: Minimal native Sidecar genesis intent. sidecar_id is derived from the Event id; realm_id, controller_id, state and timestamps are reducer-derived from the accepted envelope and MUST NOT appear here.

participant_authority_digest.description: Digest of the exact Sidecar identity, controller, and the Realm-scoped desired Agent roster derived from accepted ownership, lifecycle, and Realm membership facts.

control_frontier.description: Sorted accepted refs that materialize Sidecar genesis, ownership, lifecycle, authorization, Realm participation and key readiness. No Circle membership or Sidecar selection Event may appear.

sovereign_did_policy_state_payload.description: Sovereign DID policy state payload. trust_domain is the deployment-scoped replay-boundary subject.

trust_root_ids.description: Stable did_core_id allowlist. A root is compared against project(candidate did); it is not itself resolvable and does not carry a verification method or endpoint. Verification still requires approved did/key binding/method evidence and fails closed when that evidence is unavailable.

space_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Space object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

space_object_tombstone_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.tombstone. Realm tombstone uses its separate Realm lifecycle payload; Space tombstone targets payload.space_id.

space_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.space.update. Patches Space metadata (title, rank, kind-specific fields) on the Space identified by space_id. Per operations-sync.md §7.3 / §9.3 and realm-and-space.md §3.3, ak.space.update only mutates the Space's own metadata; it MUST NOT PATCH top-level state (archive/restore go through ak.space.archive / ak.space.restore) and MUST NOT move Strands (ak.strand.move / ak.strand.reorder). Reducer rejects update on a non-active Space (reason=space_not_active) — see conformance-vectors.md §6.7.

space_state_transition_payload.description: Payload for ak.space.archive and ak.space.restore. The target Space is expressed on payload.space_id; top-level target_ref is a rejected field on Event envelopes.

state_conflict_recovery_payload.description: Control cell bottom recovery. zh/authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 9.5 resolves a bottom=reject cell that has joined to Bottom back to a single legal value. The authorization and the pre-conflict anchor are not payload fields: they are refs[] entries with role=recovery_capability and role=state_witness.

target_cell_id.description: The cell being recovered. It MUST be in Bottom when the reducer applies this Event; on any other cell state the write MUST be rejected. This is the only registered kind whose write target is resolved from the payload rather than from a literal cell_family in the registry, because a recovery addresses one cell of an arbitrary family.

resolved_value.description: The single legal value the cell resolves to. Section 9.5 requires the Move to declare it, so it is signed payload, never reducer-synthesized.

realm_media_service_payload.$comment: Payload for ak.realm.media_service. The media descriptor lives under payload.value (a state_payload envelope), never flattened onto payload. This def is closed on purpose: the descriptor is the trust root for media token issuance (service_id, ice_config_endpoint and every foci[].token_endpoint per zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.1), and it was previously typed only as the open state_payload, which let a deployment carry provider-specific token issuer configuration inside a signed Realm policy cell while a spec-shaped consumer read nothing at all. Issuer configuration -- signing key ids, token audiences, TTLs, backend API credentials -- is deployment configuration of the service named by foci[].token_endpoint. It MUST NOT be carried here: putting it in the cell would make an issuer key rotation require a Realm policy Event holding ak.realm.media_service or ak.policy.manage capability, and would publish issuer internals to every Realm member. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.

service_id.description: Media service principal. Every issued participant_binding.issuer_kid and service_signature.kid MUST project onto this DID (media-service-binding.md section 3).

ice_config_endpoint.description: ICE / TURN credential endpoint. Part of the section 2.1 integrity binding.

foci.description: Non-empty multi-focus list. A descriptor carrying a single flat sfu_endpoint, or no foci at all, MUST fail closed with media_service_foci_required; a server MUST NOT normalize or infer one in the realtime path.

media_service_focus.$comment: One backend focus. focus_id and focus_kind identify it; token_endpoint and connect_url are what a client actually needs to join, so both are required rather than optional -- a focus a client cannot exchange a token at, or cannot connect to, is not a usable focus and must fail schema validation instead of failing at join time. See zh/crypto-media/media-service-binding.md section 2.

focus_id.description: Stable focus id inside this Realm media service. It enters the signed canonical bytes and the session_focus election (call-state.md section 4.1).

focus_kind.description: Backend binding id. It sits on the kind axis rather than being spelled `type`, because the value set is an Arkret-owned closed registry and classification-field-registry.json reserves the type axis for fields inherited verbatim from an external standard. Only livekit and arkret_native have a normative binding in v1; a client meeting an unknown or unsupported focus_kind MUST fail closed with unknown_focus_type rather than hand the token to an arbitrary SDK.

token_endpoint.description: Token exchange endpoint (section 3). Shared abstraction across every backend; only backend_token differs. Part of the section 2.1 trust root, so a client MUST verify the exact cell value against the current accepted Seal view before anchoring it.

connect_url.description: Backend connection entry point; the concrete protocol is fixed by the type-specific binding appendix.

health_endpoint.description: Client pre-flight endpoint, usable only for ordering foci_preferred before a session_focus is committed. Once ak.component.call.focus.v1 carries a session_focus, a connect failure MUST surface as focus unavailable and MUST NOT silently switch focus.

cascade_group.description: Backend cluster this focus belongs to, for user-visible disclosure that a cross-region conference is cascaded inside the backend. The protocol does not standardize SFU-to-SFU cascading.

realm_policy_payload.description: Closed payload for ak.realm.policy. It selects one independently defined Policy object by id; inline Realm facets remain exclusively in ak.realm.policy_bundle or their dedicated facet Event kinds.

realm_discovery_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.discovery. Preview field selection is owned exclusively by ak.realm.preview_policy.

realm_schema_payload.description: Closed whole-value payload for ak.realm.schema. schema_refs contains schema ids only; Realm structural-role profiles are create-locked in genesis and policy/deployment profiles have their own carriers.

strand_create_payload.description: Create payload uses the full Strand object schema for wire validation. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

not.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived.

board_space_id.description: Board Space that owns the position edge; deduplication key (board_space_id, strand_id) MUST be unique among active edges.

from_space_id.description: Source List Space (optional; reducer infers from current active edge if omitted).

target_space_id.description: Target List Space after move. This is the ONLY payload-level field for the destination; the reducer compiles it into the cas_register cell value as 'list_space_id' on the cell at ak:cell:ak.component.strand.position.v1:<board_space_id>:<strand_id>. Writers MUST NOT put 'list_space_id' directly on the ak.strand.move payload (additionalProperties=false enforces this) — there is exactly one destination input field on the wire.

strand_patch_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.update. Patches ordinary Strand fields on the Strand identified by target_ref.

space_id.description: List Space within which the reorder happens.

strand_stage_set_payload.description: Payload class for ak.strand.stage.set. Mutates Strand.stage / Strand.stage_changed_at. Intentionally carries no reason field — see the shared stage-set contract in zh/models/common-fields.md §5.3 and zh/models/strand-and-message.md §3.2.

not.$comment: Stage-set guard shared by the concrete Strand and Morph payload classes. Reason-style fields are forbidden; rationale belongs in a discussion-track Message.

strand_watch_set_payload.description: Payload for ak.strand.watch.set. Writes the (strand_id, watcher_actor_id) watch cell. The new cell value is computed from payload.level + payload.level_public: when level is null the effect is set null (clear, equivalent to mentions_only); when level is a string the effect is set { level, level_public? }. Reducer invariants: (1) watcher_actor_id MUST equal envelope.actor_id unless writer holds ak.strand.watch.set.others; (2) when watcher_actor_id != envelope.actor_id (.others write), level MUST be one of {mentions_only, participating, all} and level_public MUST be omitted or false — writing muted or level_public=true on behalf of another actor MUST failed_precondition; (3) .others writes MUST carry refs[role=audit_pair] to a same-batch ak.audit.accessed event whose payload access_kind=watch_set_others identifies writer / target / cell / before-after heads. See models/strand-and-message.md §8.4.

level.description: Watch level. Required. null clears the cell (equivalent to mentions_only / no record); in that case level_public MUST be omitted.

level_public.description: Opt-in publication of the level value to non-self projection consumers. Default false. muted MUST NOT be exposed even with level_public=true. MUST be omitted when level is null.

expected_value.description: Compiles to cas_register head_eq precondition. Whole-value compare against the cell pre-state: either null (assert no prior record) or { level, level_public? } matching the prior cell value exactly. When omitted, reducers MUST treat it as head_eq null: only the initial write may pass; an existing cell MUST fail_precondition. Omission MUST NOT disable CAS or imply last-write-wins.

allOf.description: level_public MUST be omitted when level is null (clearing a cell does not carry a public-level setting).

track_name.description: Strand track key for Message payloads. Mirrors message.schema.json#/properties/track_name: v1 Message payloads are restricted to 'discussion'.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a concrete verification method. Bare DIDs are not valid where a key binding is required.

expected_state_digest.description: Optional optimistic concurrency guard. When present it MUST equal the writer-observed digest of the frozen pre-state this patch was computed against; a mismatch MUST fail closed. Registered as the apply_patch projection's expected_prestate source in contract-registry.json.

allOf.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id (event-kind-registry.json declares id_source=event_derived for ak.view.create), so carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived. `type` stays banned because the object kind comes from the typed-id prefix. Reusing view.schema.json also closes the payload: state_changed_at is reducer-derived and view.schema.json already forbids it on any View whose state is not tombstoned.

object.description: ak.view.create object snapshot: the full View object schema minus the id. Semantic validation MUST require payload.object.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.object.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

view_reconcile_payload.description: Payload for ak.view.reconcile. view_id is the ak.component.view.reconcile.v1 cell subject; definition is the whole View definition object being synced (zh/models/views.md section 3.2). Reconcile is neither ak.view.create's object snapshot nor ak.view.update's patch: it replaces the definition wholesale, so it MUST NOT be dispatched to the shared view_payload, whose definition branch does not even require view_id.

allOf.$comment: zh/models/common-fields.md: the object id is derived from this create Event's own event_id; carrying it in the payload is schema_violation reason object_id_not_event_derived. `type` stays banned because the object kind comes from the typed-id prefix. `effective_scope` is the reducer-materialized projection of the verified Event.scope_ref (zh/models/circle.md §6.2) and MUST NOT be actor-supplied: reason effective_scope_reducer_managed, machine-indexed in registry/reducer-managed-path-registry.json.

relation_create_object.description: Relation create input: the full Relation object schema minus the id, the banned `type` name, and the reducer-managed `effective_scope`. Reusing relation.schema.json makes the Relation create shape decidable by schema exactly like the Strand / Morph / Space create shapes, while relation.schema.json's own `fields` property keeps the free edge-metadata surface open. Semantic validation MUST require payload.relation.created_by to match the top-level actor_id and payload.relation.created_at to match the top-level created_at before acceptance.

schemas/events-subscribe-frame.schema.js.title: EventsSubscribeFrame
schemas/events-subscribe-frame.schema.js.description: Closed frame union emitted by ak.self.events.stream.subscribe.v1 over NDJSON or as the payload of an Arkret WebSocket channel frame.

registry_id.description: Versioned registry symbol for a dependency, payload schema, or conformance vector.

retrieval_url.description: Optional retrieval hint only. The registry_id plus digest, not this URL, identifies the referenced content.

schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.title: Arkret File Transfer Account Data
schemas/file-transfer.schema.json.description: Plaintext shape that MUST be encrypted before writing ak.profile.file_transfer.v1 account-data values.

content_digest.description: Digest of the stored blob bytes. For encrypted file transfer this is the ciphertext digest and MUST NOT be a plaintext file hash.

blob_size_bytes.description: Size of the stored blob bytes, usually ciphertext plus AEAD overhead.

media_type.description: Original file media type. This field lives inside encrypted account data; encrypted blob metadata SHOULD use application/octet-stream.

plaintext_size_bytes.description: Original file byte length before client-side encryption.

oneOf.$comment: whole-file AEAD form: single nonce, no stream segment parameters
streaming chunked AEAD form: nonce_prefix and fixed segment parameters, no whole-file nonce

content_key.description: Fresh per-transfer content key carried only inside encrypted account-data plaintext.

enc.description: HPKE KEM encapsulated key for the recipient device.

schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.title: Arkret Grant Constraint
schemas/grant-constraint.schema.json.$comment: Property ordering is grouped by constraint family to match capabilities.md §6 (the human-readable family map): discriminator/meta, then temporal, field_access, kind_restriction, scope_limitation, authority_control, quota, claim_based, confidentiality, then the moderation cache-invalidation hint. Canonical JSON re-sorts keys lexicographically so this ordering is presentation-only and does not affect the wire (see C13-07).

constraint_id.description: Optional stable identifier of this constraint within the grant; used for diagnostics and overrides.

constraint_kind.description: Constraint family discriminator. v1 collapses what were 15 types into 8 by absorbing narrowly-scoped types into their conceptual parent: edit_window → temporal; container_move → scope_limitation; rate_limiting + resource_limit → quota; approval_workflow + accountability + device_session → claim_based (with constraint_subkind); encryption_requirement + visibility_control → confidentiality (with constraint_subkind). Use the optional 'constraint_subkind' field to indicate the original specialization where evaluation logic differs.

evaluation_class.description: Cacheability/dependency hint for the authorization evaluator. stateless = pure function of (constraint, op, now); grant_local = depends on the grant object only; realm_state = depends on Realm frontier (membership, policy_version, etc.); external = depends on data outside the Realm causal frontier (claim revocation status, rate-limit history counts, async approval). Each constraint_kind has a canonical evaluation_class declared in constraint-schema.md §2.3; implementations MAY tighten (e.g. grant_local → stateless) but MUST NOT loosen (e.g. external as stateless). Auth evaluators SHOULD use this hint to gate fast-path caching.

constraint_subkind.description: Optional discriminator within a constraint_kind. Standard values: claim_based.{claim,approval,accountability}; quota.{rate,resource}; confidentiality.{encryption,visibility}; temporal.{window,edit_window,redact_window,session}; authority_control.{applet_authority}. Per constraint-schema.md §2.2, device/session binding is NOT an independent constraint_subkind: it is the claim_based constraint_subkind=claim sub-case expressed via an accepted PCR device issuer. Implementations MAY require constraint_subkind for these families and fail closed on unknown values.
