applies_to_actions.description: Optional restriction of a temporal constraint to specific capability actions (e.g. ['ak.message.revise.own', 'ak.message.redact.own']). Action mismatch is neutral in the effect fold: satisfied for effect=allow and not matched for deny/quarantine/require_review.

recurrence.description: Recurrence rule for temporal constraints. Used by constraint-schema.md §3.1.

expires_after.description: ISO 8601 duration; used by approval_workflow constraint instead of expires_after_ms.

condition.description: Conditional predicate for field_access and similar constraints. The `kind` value is a registered named condition from constraint-schema.md §4.1; unknown kinds MUST fail closed. Implementations MUST NOT introduce ad hoc string DSL predicates.

allowed_space_kinds.description: Allowed Space kinds (e.g. 'board', 'list', or profile-registered kinds like 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket'). Reducer/profile MUST validate kind value.

allowed_circle_ids.description: Limits Circle-scoped capability actions to the listed Circle ids. Used by ak.circle.manage / ak.circle.member.manage style grants; unconstrained Realm-wide Circle management grants are not a normal permission shape.

allowed_session_ids.description: Limits applet interop-session operations to the listed applet-defined session correlation ids.

blob_presign_scope.description: Scope limiter for ak.self.blob.command.presign.v1 grants: allowed purposes plus optional blob/realm restrictions.

allowed_data_labels.description: Data classification labels this grant may read, export, transform, or send to external endpoints.

allowed_endpoints.description: Allowed outbound endpoint origins or deployment-approved endpoint patterns for applet / agent / connector operations.

max_authority_depth.description: Maximum remaining authority hops. Bounded by the canonical authority-chain depth ceiling (4) defined in zh/conformance/scalability-constraints.md §3 and zh/authz/capabilities.md §10.2; reducers MUST reject grants declaring a larger value at accept time rather than only truncating during DFS.

applet_id.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the accepted Applet registration.

executed_by.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the concrete Applet service, bot, or provisioned ghost actor did_core_id that may execute the grant. Its proof verification_method remains a DID URL and MUST project to this value through the registered method adapter.

registration_epoch.description: authority_control(constraint_subkind=applet_authority) binding to the canonical Applet registration epoch.

blob_presign_max_ttl_seconds.description: Maximum TTL, in seconds, that this grant permits for ak.blob.presign. The service must clamp requested max_age_seconds to the smaller of this value and deployment policy.

max_artifact_bytes.description: Maximum artifact size in bytes for applet / agent / export operations.

max_operations.description: Maximum number of distinct accepted idempotency identities in one UTC epoch-aligned fixed period. Enforcement is a linearizable check-and-reserve at one logical quota authority shared by every node in the enforcing service; per-node duplicated budgets and overshoot are forbidden.

period.description: ISO 8601 duration. For quota constraints, a stricter conditional schema permits only a non-zero fixed-length week/day/hour/minute/second duration; year/month durations are forbidden so every authority derives the same UTC epoch-aligned window id.

burst.description: Optional token-bucket capacity at the same logical quota authority, capped by max_operations and refilled at max_operations/period. It never increases the fixed-window total budget.

constraint_scope.description: Closed v1 quota counting scope. Unknown values are schema violations and MUST fail closed. Quota counters are actor-bound; the enum selects the additional slicing dimension: actor only, actor+space, actor+realm, or actor across all nodes/regions of the enforcing service's global quota domain. global is not an implicit federation-wide counter. Every node in the service domain MUST share one logical linearizable quota authority.

required_claims.description: Conditional claim requirements. resource-selector-grammar.md §3.3 caps this array at 32 entries as a normative DoS guard; the schema enforces maxItems:32 so condition-selector grants cannot smuggle in unbounded claim objects.

subject_matches_actor.description: If true, the credential subject did_core_id MUST match the actor did_core_id after each proof's DID is independently validated and projected through its registered method adapter.

value_constraints.description: Per-field equality / membership constraints on credential claims.

min_encryption_level.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static floor: the minimum content-encryption mechanism the grant requires. Values mirror Realm/Circle encryption_profile. Pure static declaration evaluated as stateless unless cross-checked against the Realm's current encryption_profile (see constraint-schema.md §12).

plaintext_fallback_allowed.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant permits plaintext when the encryption floor cannot be met. See constraint-schema.md §12.

audit_trail_required.description: confidentiality(constraint_subkind=encryption) static flag: whether the grant requires an audit trail (e.g. active Audit Applet Binding). See constraint-schema.md §12.

depends_on_moderation_state.description: Cache-invalidation hint: when true, this grant's authorization decisions depend on the ak.component.moderation_state.v1 cell (see capabilities.md §18.1) and the grant's cache entry MUST be invalidated when that cell changes. Default false: ordinary grants (ak.strand.update / ak.message.create / organization membership grants) do NOT take a cache hit on every moderation decision. v1 capabilities.md §18.1 lists three conditions where MUST be explicitly true (moderator-role grants, condition-selector subjects referencing moderation state, constraints referencing moderation queue / cell). Schema-side enforcement of condition (2) is in capability-grant.schema.json via if/then on actions[]; conditions (1) and (3) are reducer-side lint. Cache invalidation hint outside the eight constraint families; it does not participate in allow/deny evaluation and is documented in capabilities.md §6 / constraint-schema.md.

allOf.$comment: constraint-schema.md §2.2 / §2.3: claim_based, confidentiality and quota families have NO valid no-constraint_subkind form — every row in the §2.3 evaluation_class table carries a constraint_subkind (claim/approval/accountability; encryption/visibility; rate/resource). Without this gate a {"constraint_kind":"claim_based","effect":"allow"} with no constraint_subkind passes schema validation, letting weak implementations cache an external (claim-revocation) constraint on the grant_local fast path (see C05-03 fail-open). temporal is intentionally excluded: a temporal constraint with no constraint_subkind is the valid ordinary time-window form.
Rate quotas need an explicit counting scope; otherwise SDKs cannot derive a stable counter key.
Applet delegated grants must carry the complete grant-local registration binding. effective_scope is represented by the enclosing capability grant resources[] selector and is not duplicated here.
Applet binding fields are reserved for the registered authority_control.applet_authority shape; partial or cross-family use is invalid.
quota constraint_subkind=rate is a complete hard-quota tuple; partial rate constraints are invalid.
burst is a modifier of a complete rate quota and cannot stand alone.
Cumulative resource quotas need an explicit counting scope; single-operation fields such as blob_max_bytes do not.
Cumulative resource-count quotas need an explicit counting scope.
Quota periods must have a fixed duration so all nodes derive the same UTC epoch-aligned window. Calendar years/months and zero/empty durations are not valid quota periods.
An edit window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=edit_window requires the edit duration field.
A redact window is only interoperable when its canonical action gate is explicit.
temporal constraint_subkind=redact_window requires the redact duration field.
redact_after_window_allowed modifies message_edit_window and is invalid without it.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators / contract-registry consumers disambiguate this claim from other DID-bearing envelopes.

handle_aliases.description: Interop aliases such as RFC 7565 acct:. Aliases are never canonical; verifiers MUST normalize to handle before cache lookup, proof comparison, or account selection.

subject_account_id.description: Exact account selected by this account handle. Both canonical components are proof-bound; a resolver MUST NOT infer or replace station_id.

issuer_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the handle authority. Bare hostnames are discovery inputs, never proof issuers; proof verification resolves a DID URL separately and requires its registered adapter projection to equal this issuer.

vouching_id.description: Optional service-only vouching role that signed, served, or vouched for this handle claim when distinct from issuer_id. The service subject-class requirement is validated independently of the field name.

claim_kind.description: Protocol-level kind of holder/principal handle claim. v1 intentionally does not allow the earlier draft service_handle value: service-readable names or resource labels need their own service/resource schema, while organization-assigned user/principal handles use organization_handle.

visibility.description: Default disclosure boundary for this handle claim.

audience.description: Audience binding for the claim. For handle claims used to address an invite, audience is the target Realm ID, the inviting service DID, or another verifier domain the proofs explicitly bind to. Verifier MUST reject claims whose audience does not match the current invocation context.

claim_scope.description: Optional claim_scope such as organization_id, realm_id, purpose, or allowed operations.

schemas/high-risk-authority-proof.schema.title: Arkret High-Risk Authority Proof Family
schemas/high-risk-authority-proof.schema.description: Shared authority proof family for service operations that key-management.md designates as high-risk material destruction or equivalent (first consumer: active-series key backup tail deletion, key-management.md section 7.8). Exactly one closed branch: principal_signing, device_quorum, or trusted_recovery_service, discriminated by `kind`. Every branch reuses the common detached-JWS leaf (event-envelope.schema.json#/$defs/proof) over the operation's single canonical delete-intent transcript; branches never restate the leaf fields. An ordinary current-device session proof is deliberately NOT a branch of this family — operations that accept it for low-risk paths must say so in their own normative text. This is one wire leaf with per-consumer domain separation: the transcript context is owned by the consuming operation, never by the leaf, so x-arkret-proof-contexts below enumerates every registered consumer context and proof-context-registry.json carries the matching consumer_operation on each row.

detached_proof.description: Common detached-JWS leaf. `payload_digest` MUST be the digest of the operation's canonical transcript, whose first member is the consuming operation's registered context (for key backup deletion: the delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1 under ak.key_backup_delete_proof.v1); `created_at` MUST fall inside the server-issued challenge window when the operation binds one. A signature made under another consumer's context MUST be rejected even when it verifies cryptographically.

principal_signing_proof.description: Principal-control-key proof. The proof's verification_method MUST be a principal-grade DID-control verification method whose controller DID is byte-identical to the transcript's principal_id, and that key MUST be a currently accepted principal control key at proof.created_at. Device keys, service keys and retired keys MUST be rejected.

proof.description: Detached-JWS leaf whose verification_method MUST resolve, at proof.created_at, to an authorized non-revoked device key of exactly this device_id under the transcript's principal_id. Every quorum member signs the same canonical transcript bytes.

device_quorum_proof.description: Device-quorum proof. The schema enforces only the minimum wire shape (threshold>=2, signatures.minItems=1). Verification is normative in the consuming operation's text: (a) every signature MUST verify over the same canonical transcript; (b) signatures MUST be deduplicated by device_id; (c) the count of valid deduplicated signatures MUST be >= threshold; (d) threshold MUST equal the currently accepted recovery policy device-quorum k — a smaller issuer-supplied threshold MUST be rejected as failed_precondition. A deployment whose policy k is below 2 cannot use this branch and must use principal_signing or trusted_recovery_service instead; a single current device proof is not a high-risk quorum.

threshold.description: The quorum threshold the issuer claims to satisfy. MUST equal the principal's currently accepted recovery_policy device-quorum k; receivers MUST cross-check per description rule (d).

signatures.description: minItems=1 is the schema floor only; receiver-side verification requires deduplicated valid signature count >= threshold per description rule (c).

trusted_recovery_service_proof.description: Trusted recovery service proof. The verification_method of `proof` MUST be controlled by service_id, and service_id MUST be authorized as a trusted recovery service by the recovery policy / DID delegation snapshotted into the referenced recovery session. The session MUST be unexpired, unconsumed for this purpose, and MUST have been established by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum — the service alone is never a sufficient factor.

recovery_session_id.description: Verified, unexpired, unconsumed recovery session authenticated by principal_signing, recovery unlock or device_quorum. A service-only session is not a second factor.

attestation_ref.description: Optional attestation object for service_id. If present, receivers MUST resolve it in the same trust_domain as the operation and reject cross-domain attestations.

schemas/history-key.schema.json.title: Arkret History Key Recovery
schemas/history-key.schema.json.description: Canonical private request delivery, capability-addressed response stream, proof and packed-range wire for exporter-scheme history recovery.

history_candidate_material_key.description: Global received-material identity. Origin is deliberately absent; equal bytes at the same scope/group/epoch deduplicate to one resident material instance.

history_candidate_material_record.description: Device-local resident received bytes. material_received_sequence is assigned once when this byte instance becomes resident and is immutable; adding origin attribution never refreshes it. Eviction removes this record but not bounded attribution tombstones, and refetch creates a new record with a new sequence. local_authoritative uses a separate record class.

origin_quota_domain.description: Stable quota identity. It equals the verified response source_sender_domain and does not change across response ids or retries.
Stable holder/key/effective-rotation quota tuple. accepted_key_evidence_ref is the rotation identity; archive/container retrieval coordinates are deliberately excluded.
Stable backup series/producer quota identity. Individual backup envelopes are retrieval coordinates only.

backup_origin_id.description: Use backup:<BackupId> when the envelope carries a canonical BackupId; otherwise backup:sha256:<hex of exact envelope bytes>. This is an origin identifier, never sender_domain.

history_candidate_origin_attribution.description: Independent origin ledger row keyed by (material_key,origin_domain,origin_ref), with a separate stable origin_quota_domain. origin_ref is only a retrieval coordinate and never selects quota identity. The fixed expiry is computed as immutable first_observed_at+2592000 seconds and is not stored. It never duplicates secret bytes or refreshes material_received_sequence.

event_candidate_binding.description: Independent Event binding keyed by (event_binding_key,candidate_digest,outcome). It contains no origin and must not be used to infer one or pin candidate bytes. The fixed expiry is computed as first_observed_at+2592000 seconds and is not stored.

requester_endpoint_authorization.description: Requester-signed exact endpoint authorization locator. The release service re-resolves this same current PCR device or Native Agent authorization at create and every first chunk enqueue; it never substitutes the current session endpoint. Minimal-metadata uses only its Realm-local pairwise endpoint actor and therefore carries no principal/device locator.

holder_trusted_basis.description: Holder-durable canonical accepted Seal antichain supplied in the accepted register/rotate holder-acceptance proof. The accepted_key_evidence_ref Event and its effective registered tuple are verified by replay from this basis; no singular activation Seal is carried.

realm_current_gate_projection.description: Closed Realm current-gate projection. source_authorization_incarnation is required by the registered member-source branch and forbidden by the organization-recovery-holder branch.

circle_current_gate_projection.description: Closed Circle current-gate projection. Each authorization incarnation is the closed Realm+Circle form and therefore binds the parent-Realm intersection. source_authorization_incarnation follows the same member/holder branch rule as Realm.

seal_view_locator.description: Honest-service locator for a complete canonical accepted non-quarantined Seal frontier and its closed current gate. open_set uses the full antichain, never a selected leaf. The enqueue CAS re-resolves this exact basis and projection and rejects any known successor or projection change.

account_status_view_locator.description: Account Authority issuer-ledger record locator/digest; never a Realm/CBA proof.

pcr_seal_basis.description: Complete accepted non-quarantined PCR Seal frontier; open_set never selects one leaf.

device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation; it is not an EventId or DID versionId.

source_relay_view_locator.description: Digest locator for the complete SourceRelayAttestation verified by the requester release service. Source account/device/Agent or holder authority coordinates remain solely inside the source local Station's signed relay attestation.

accepted_authority_view_vector.description: Closed typed locator/digest vector in an honest release-service decision receipt. It carries no portable multi-authority proof. Profiles and source kind occur only in the outer attestation.

epoch_range.description: Inclusive non-empty range; from_epoch <= to_epoch is mandatory semantic validation.

history_secret_range.description: Packed history_secret[from] || ... || history_secret[to]. The receiver resolves KDF.Nh from each exact winning transition reconstructed by the receipt-bound direct Seal replay and requires decoded length=(to-from+1)*KDF.Nh.

secret_range.description: Its inclusive range must equal the outer chunk covered_epoch_range byte-for-byte. Decoded packed length is the sum of exact per-epoch KDF.Nh values resolved from the corresponding activation transitions.

history_chunk_plaintext.description: The only HPKE plaintext for a history response chunk. Every opened secret globally deduplicates by HistoryCandidateMaterialKey, never origin, and gets a separate response_sender CandidateOriginAttribution; it never becomes local_authoritative. Success/failure EventCandidateBinding contains no origin and does not pin bytes. It contains history secrets only and cannot carry active MLS state, sender counters, snapshots, policy claims or source metadata.

response_capability_b64u.description: Canonical unpadded base64url of exactly 32 service-generated CSPRNG bytes.

history_response_capability_plaintext.description: The only plaintext admitted by SealedHistoryResponseCapability. HPKE seals the RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 bytes of this closed object; raw bytes, a bare base64url string and nested JSON text are forbidden.

history_secret_b64u.description: Unpadded base64url of the exact history_secret for archive.epoch. Its decoded length must equal KDF.Nh of the winning group transition proven for that epoch.

organization_recovery_archive_plaintext.description: The only RRK archive HPKE plaintext. An opened secret globally deduplicates by HistoryCandidateMaterialKey and gets a separate rrk_archive CandidateOriginAttribution; it never becomes local_authoritative. Success/failure EventCandidateBinding contains no origin and does not pin bytes. HPKE seals RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 of this object. It cannot carry active MLS state, counters, policy snapshots, holder claims or another epoch.

requester_authorization_incarnation.description: Exact closed current membership-incarnation set for this scope. Create admission verifies it and retry preserves it byte-for-byte.

trusted_history_base_basis.description: Requester-selected, independently verified and durable-pinned predecessor-free Realm bootstrap cut. v1 history recovery replays from this complete canonical Seal antichain; the service cannot replace it with a later checkpoint or a singular head. It is independent from trusted_current_basis.

trusted_current_basis.description: Requester-durable verified complete current scope-Realm Seal antichain used as an anti-rollback floor. It is independent from the predecessor-free traversal bootstrap base and T1 Account/PCR/Agent facts are not added to it.

requested_ranges.description: Canonical requested range set. Before signing, sort by (from_epoch,to_epoch), remove duplicates, and merge every overlapping or adjacent pair. A verifier rejects an array that is not strictly increasing, pairwise disjoint, and pairwise non-adjacent in that canonical form.

expires_at.description: Canonical request expiry. Accepted create admission requires byte-for-byte equality with receipt.expires_at, response-stream expiry and history_traversal_retention.traversal_intent.retention.expires_at.

history_key_request.description: The complete RFC 8785 canonical HistoryKeyRequest is capped at 65536 bytes by history-recovery-scalability-registry.json. This inner-object limit is distinct from the 1 MiB create-operation envelope limit.

release_id.description: The requester's authenticated current Station selected as the unique honest release service for this request response stream.

release_service_resolution_ref.description: Adapter-canonical service resolution reference; it is not an Arkret EventId.

release_service_resolution_record_digest.description: Digest of the complete signed ServiceResolutionRecord used at request acceptance.

history_traversal_retention.description: Member branch only. Its traversal_intent.request_digest, effective_scope, derived mls_group_id, authorization_incarnation, trusted_history_base_basis, trusted_current_basis, requested_ranges and request-expiring retention equal the accepted request/receipt fields byte-for-byte; target_basis is the release service's complete verified durable Seal frontier and dominates both signed bases.

expires_at.description: Byte-for-byte equal to request.expires_at, response-stream expiry and history_traversal_retention.traversal_intent.retention.expires_at.

history_governance_traversal_intent.description: Closed direct-Seal traversal intent. target_basis must dominate every trusted_current_basis and trusted_history_base_basis leaf; reverse traversal follows signed predecessor_refs until the exact base cut, consumes every base leaf, and admits no predecessor outside the cut. requested_ranges are canonical. RRK requires one singleton range.

history_governance_traversal_retention.description: Retention commitment for the exact target-to-base accepted Seal cut, base Seals and their delta, each interval Seal.delta Control Move canonical byte string, every AvailabilityReceipt, SemanticRef external evidence, AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence, method-native DID material and registry snapshot required by registered apply_seal replay. Base predecessors are outside the cut and are never fetched. The service atomically pins the complete closure before signing the request receipt or archive-replica acknowledgement. Member retention ends at request expiry; RRK retention equals archive lifetime. This is not a proof package, snapshot, checkpoint or authority result set.

self_history_traversal_access.description: Narrow self resolve authorization for the exact retained direct-traversal cut. The service derives the cut and allowed Control Move/apply_seal dependency set from the named durable receipt or accepted archive replica; callers cannot enumerate an allowed descriptor set.

peer_history_traversal_access.description: Authenticated peer resolve authorization only for a pending organization-recovery archive replica. Member request replicas distribute request bytes but never authorize or promise a governance closure; the release service obtains and pins that cut through ordinary Realm governance sync before signing the request receipt. Unknown, unauthorized, outside-cut and missing selectors have one response shape.

sealed_history_response_capability.description: Uses the single active history-response-capability HPKE registry profile; algorithm fields are forbidden.

history_key_request_replica.description: Private S2S immutable request fanout from the release service to either the Station selected by one exact current member identity and membership Event, or an exact RRK holder service whose archive tuple intersects requested ranges. destination_authorization is a closed union and must name destination_id.

rrk_holder_authority_observation.description: Current source-local RRK holder authority observation. archive_authorization_tuple_digest binds the immutable historical archive tuple; current_holder_signing_ref, accepted_key_evidence_ref and holder_trusted_basis prove current holder authority and are not required to equal the tuple's historical signing/evidence coordinates. Its registered digest is SHA-256(UTF8('ak.rrk-holder-authority-observation-v1') || 0x00 || JCS(complete object)).

source_relay_attestation.description: The source's authenticated local Station verifies current source AccountId/device, hosted ActorId, exact membership Event or RRK holder authority and signs this private relay receipt. The first accepted self send atomically stores the exact relay envelope/outbox keyed by (response_id,source_record_digest); relayed_at and proof are never regenerated on retry/restart, and the first accepted outcome is durably backfilled. Exact retry returns those byte-identical bytes without a duplicate status. For RRK the source proof uses current_holder_signing_ref; historical archive holder_signing_ref is provenance only.

history_key_source_relay.description: Private S2S immutable source record carrier to request_receipt.release_id. The destination verifies the relay service against the source ActorId and current membership or RRK authority before it performs the final T1 linearization and creates HistoryReleaseAttestation.

covered_epoch_range.description: The one inclusive continuous range covered by this exact chunk_response_id. Descriptor ranges are pairwise disjoint across descriptors; their canonical ordered union is the sole manifest and attempt coverage truth and must be a subset of the request's requested_ranges. No second manifest-level ranges array exists.

history_response_manifest.description: manifest_digest = H(UTF8('ak.history-response-manifest-v1') || 0x00 || JCS(the closed HistoryKeyResponseSigningInput whose content.kind is ak.history_key.response_manifest)). Descriptors are sorted by chunk_index and are the sole truth for response id and one continuous range. covered_epoch_range must be a canonical subset of the request ranges authorized by direct Seal traversal replay; no proof/package selection is carried. A chunk repeats only manifest_digest and chunk_index. The canonical manifest source record is at most 256 KiB. Its first accepted send receipt, or the byte-identical receipt returned by an exact retry, must be durable before any named chunk is submitted.

authorized_ranges.description: Canonical sorted, disjoint exact descriptor ranges that passed the current scope history-access ratchet, requester current incarnation and join/profile floor after complete direct Seal replay. It must equal the complete manifest descriptor range union; partial admission is forbidden.

history_manifest_admission.description: Deterministic service-authenticated T0 result written only after resolving the receipt-bound target-to-base Seal cut and replaying standard apply_seal in topological order. The traversal verifies notary authority, every predecessor edge, delta Control Move and registered dependency, target dominance, requester incarnation/join floor, the scope's current monotone history-access ratchet, every winning MLS transition and exact descriptor range. Any missing dependency, predecessor outside the exact cut, unconsumed base leaf, hidden branch, failed Seal/root/reducer check, profile/join failure or exact-range mismatch rejects the entire manifest with zero response record/admission write.

manifest_admission_digest.description: Must equal the already accepted manifest's deterministic HistoryManifestAdmission digest. Missing/mismatch is dependency_missing and writes no chunk record or attestation.

sealed_history_chunk.description: Minimal chunk wire. The exact accepted manifest descriptor and manifest_admission_digest reconstruct the continuous range and HPKE context. T0 is the receipt-bound direct Seal replay recorded by the accepted manifest admission; the chunk carries no independent proof, selector, segment or range-key duplicate. Source submit before that manifest admission is accepted is dependency_missing with zero pending state, zero response record and zero release attestation. The complete canonical chunk source record MUST be at most 2 MiB.

history_source_agent_observation_input.description: Closed non-wire canonical input for history_source_agent_observation_digest. It intentionally excludes source_signer_evidence_ref and source_signer_evidence_digest so a Native Agent can obtain CurrentAdmission evidence before authoring the complete signed response.

source_signer_evidence_digest.description: Must equal the digest encoded by source_signer_evidence_ref and resolve through the request-receipt governance-dependency surface to the exact historical source signer and verification method.

identity_link_signer_evidence_ref.description: Content-addressed Principal signer evidence for the IdentityLink proof verification_method at the link effective_at boundary.

minimal_metadata_mls_leaf_signer_evidenc.description: Content-addressed historical signer evidence for a minimal-metadata pairwise actor. The source proof always uses the independent Ed25519 response-signing method/key committed by the end-to-end encrypted IdentityLink; it never treats an MLS ciphersuite signature key as a generic PayloadProof key. The identity_link_signer_evidence pair resolves the exact Principal evidence used to verify the IdentityLink's own proof without consulting a live DID document. The receiver validates that proof, the response key, exact locally received identity-link and RFC MLS LeafNode canonical bytes, winning transition provenance, target Seal basis and authorization incarnation against its independently verified durable MLS state before accepting source_proof. Canonical evidence bytes are limited to 1 MiB.

history_key_response_send_request.description: The source wire carries request_digest and request_receipt_digest only, plus the content-addressed historical source signer-evidence locator required to verify source_proof. Source service resolves the exact already-verified local request replica/list record by those digests; destination release service resolves its own durable request/receipt, verifies and pins the exact signer evidence plus its transitive attester closure until request expiry, and exposes that closure through the request-receipt governance-dependency surface. Unknown or mismatched digest or evidence is dependency_missing with zero write. Repeating the full request receipt or signer evidence bytes in every manifest/chunk is forbidden.

manifest_admission_digest.description: Exact digest of the previously accepted all-or-nothing manifest T0 admission.

t0_pass.description: Copied from the accepted HistoryManifestAdmission; it is not a caller-supplied authorization boolean.

released_range.description: The exact continuous chunk range; byte-for-byte equal to the matching already admitted manifest descriptor. Its authorization is reconstructed from the receipt-bound direct Seal traversal and current monotone history-access state, not from a page or selection field.

expires_at.description: MUST be <= and normally byte-for-byte equal to request/response-stream expiry. The record is admitted only while unexpired; a receiver may install the immutable record after a later read if accepted_at was within this bound.

verifier_profile_id.description: Frozen verifier profile implemented locally and selected by this id.

history_release_attestation.description: Immutable honest-release-service T1 decision receipt from first durable chunk enqueue. The requester Station verifies its local recipient authority slots, the short-lived SourceRelayAttestation and relay-service binding, plus current scope membership. Source account/device/Agent or holder facts occur only in that source-local relay attestation and are not duplicated as remote views. The service validates every intent-bound observation is unexpired and has no known successor, then CAS-writes this locator vector and record in one local transaction. The vector is an audit coordinate, not a portable multi-authority proof.

record_digest.description: Must equal SHA-256(UTF8('ak.history-response-record-v1') || 0x00 || JCS({sequence,cursor,source_record,sent_at,release_service_signer_evidence_ref,release_service_signer_evidence_digest,manifest_admission?,release_attestation?})). A manifest has exactly manifest_admission; a chunk has exactly release_attestation. record_digest and service_proof are excluded.

release_attestation.description: Required only for a chunk. The service creates it in the same transaction as the first durable record enqueue after evaluating current T1 authority views. Exact retries return the original attestation.

manifest_admission.description: Required only for a manifest. The outer service proof authenticates the complete deterministic T0 admission.

release_service_signer_evidence_ref.description: Content-addressed Service-kind historical signer evidence used by this exact release-service proof.

release_service_signer_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the complete AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence::Service object named by release_service_signer_evidence_ref.

service_proof.description: The honest release-service proof signs the RFC 8785 JCS transcript of the entire closed record with only service_proof omitted. For a chunk this coverage includes the byte-identical complete release_attestation and its typed authority locator/digest vector; the attestation has no independent proof wire.

history_key_response_record.description: The recipient response stream retains this complete byte-identical source record and conditional attestation only until a valid durable high-water disposition acknowledges it. Ack before durable install/reject/lost handling is a client error. The ack transaction atomically removes the large record/attestation and releases active quota; only the compact source-facing HistoryKeyResponseSendReceipt ledger remains through request expiry for exact source retry.

release_service_signer_evidence_ref.description: Content-addressed Service-kind historical signer evidence used by this exact lost-record proof.

release_service_signer_evidence_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the complete AuthenticatedSignerResolutionEvidence::Service object named by release_service_signer_evidence_ref.

service_proof.description: Release-service signature over the closed lost descriptor with service_proof omitted.

history_key_response_lost_record.description: Signed descriptor for an unrecoverably lost accepted response record. It permits only a durable service_record_lost disposition and never counts as manifest or epoch coverage.

history_response_page_entry.description: One item in the single sequence-ordered response stream. Pagination, limit, cursor, ack token and high-water all use this merged order; records and lost descriptors are never paginated separately.

entries.description: Strictly sequence-ascending merged record/lost entries. The verifier extracts each tuple {sequence,kind,response_id,entry_digest}, where entry_digest is record_digest or the digest of the complete signed lost descriptor.

history_response_ack_entry.description: Must match one byte-identical page entry at the same sequence. service_record_lost is structurally impossible for a normal record; all other dispositions are structurally impossible for a lost descriptor. installed on a manifest installs only its descriptor/admission, never epoch coverage.

ack_token.description: Authenticated token whose semantic preimage binds the internally resolved request_id, the exact contiguous sequence interval, high_water_cursor and ordered tuples {sequence,kind,response_id,record_digest|lost_record_digest}.

entries.description: Canonical strictly sequence-ascending entries matching the list page/ack token. Every sequence through high_water_cursor must have exactly one durable disposition.

manifest_admission_digest.description: Exact accepted manifest admission digest. For a manifest this is the admission created in the same transaction; for a chunk it must equal the already accepted admission named by the chunk.

release_attestation_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact release attestation for a chunk; JSON null for a manifest, which never releases secret material.

receipt_digest.description: SHA-256(UTF8('ak.history-response-send-receipt-v1') || 0x00 || JCS(the closed receipt with receipt_digest and service_proof omitted)).

service_proof.description: First release-service proof over the closed receipt including receipt_digest and excluding service_proof. Exact duplicate returns these identical originally accepted bytes; transport never emits a separately signed duplicate variant.

history_key_response_send_receipt.description: Small immutable source-facing success receipt. It never echoes the recipient response record, release authority locators, source record, request receipt or ciphertext.

holder_trusted_basis.description: Holder-pinned canonical accepted Seal antichain from the accepted register/rotate tuple. Cursor and every returned archive bind it byte-for-byte.

organization_recovery_archive_list_query.description: Recipient-bound RRK archive read/list query. The authenticated holder identity is transport authority and is not caller-supplied here. from_epoch/to_epoch, when present, form one inclusive non-empty range. The service returns only rows whose exact historical key tuple names this recovery_key_id/key_agreement_ref and accepted key provenance Event, whose holder_trusted_basis matches byte-for-byte, and whose holder_principal_id matches current authority. Replay from holder_trusted_basis proves that accepted_key_evidence_ref is reducer-effective; no singular activation Seal selector exists. Cursor binds only the authenticated holder authority, exact query selectors and last ordering tuple. byte_limit below the registry minimum legal item size returns limit_exceeded rather than a zero-progress page.

archive_sequence.description: Strictly monotonic sequence assigned by holder_id on first durable acceptance of this immutable archive replica.

archive_replica_digest.description: Exact canonical digest of the holder's first durably accepted organization_recovery_archive_replica. The holder MUST copy this value into SelfHistoryTraversalAccess.archive_replica_digest; archive_digest, traversal_intent_digest and container_event_ref are not substitutes.

organization_recovery_archive_list_item.description: A content-addressed row. archive_replica_digest is the exact holder-accepted replica identity and the only access coordinate for the self traversal surfaces. history_traversal_retention uses organization_recovery_archive/archive_lifetime, starts from this tuple's holder_trusted_basis, has requested_ranges exactly [{from_epoch:archive.epoch,to_epoch:archive.epoch}], and replays to a target basis that proves both the accepted key tuple and this one winning archive transition. container_event_ref equals the winning transition Event. No proof page, package root or singular activation Seal is carried.

organization_recovery_archive_list_outco.description: Canonical-byte-paged recipient-bound projection. Rows are ordered by (archive_sequence numeric ascending, container_event_ref UTF-8 bytes); a delayed old epoch receives a new sequence and cannot be inserted behind a cursor. Cursor binds only the holder principal/service authority, exact query digest including accepted evidence Event and complete holder_trusted_basis, and the last ordering tuple. The direct Seal traversal closure has the same long-term retention/replication lifetime as its archive. The high-privilege holder may resolve every Control Move, Seal and registered apply_seal dependency required by that closure, including membership/policy/control metadata, but no unrelated DataEvent, generic timeline scan, membership grant or send authority. Unknown scope, absent rows, wrong holder authority and unauthorized or mismatched tuple all produce the same not_found response shape.

organization_recovery_archive_replica.description: Private immutable S2S archive replica to the exact holder_id frozen by the archive tuple. It binds one container Event, the accepted-key evidence Event, the distinct holder trusted basis and one archive-lifetime exact-one-epoch direct Seal traversal. Semantic uniqueness is (effective_scope,mls_group_id,epoch,container_event_ref,archive tuple digest). The full body digest is only the exact-retry key: changing replicated_at cannot allocate another sequence for the same semantic row. Archive bytes and the traversal's complete registered apply_seal dependency closure are retained and reconciled for the archive lifetime; v1 has no remote GC or renewal state.

archive_sequence.description: First durable holder acceptance assigns this monotonic sequence; duplicate retry returns the identical value.

schemas/http-problem-details.schema.json.title: Arkret HTTP Problem Details
schemas/http-problem-details.schema.json.description: Canonical RFC 9457 application/problem+json error response. The type URI is the stable machine discriminator and must resolve through error-code-registry.json. Unknown extension members are tolerated by consumers as required by RFC 9457; producers may emit only extensions registered for the selected type.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: RFC 9457 Problem Details for HTTP APIs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The complete object uses the RFC literal member vocabulary; instance is the standard URI-reference member rather than an Arkret wrapper role.

schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.title: Arkret Media ICE Config Result
schemas/ice-config-response.schema.json.description: Result shape for the WebRTC media service ICE config endpoint. Used by ak.profile.webrtc_media.v1; see crypto-media/webrtc-signaling.md §4.

realm_id.description: Echo of the request Realm id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-Realm replay.

call_id.description: Echo of the request call id. Bound into the signature to prevent cross-call replay.

actor_id.description: Stable actor did_core_id that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

device_id.description: Device that may use this ICE configuration. Bound into the signature.

ice_servers.description: STUN / TURN server entries the client may use during this call.

ttl_seconds.description: Validity window for the issued credentials in seconds. Clients MUST refresh before this expires; servers SHOULD pick a value <= 1 hour for normal calls.

refresh_lead_seconds.description: Minimum lead time before ttl expiry at which the client SHOULD initiate refresh. refresh_lead_seconds MUST be strictly less than ttl_seconds (servers MUST NOT issue refresh_lead_seconds >= ttl_seconds, otherwise the client would judge the credential stale at issuance and storm refresh). Defaults SHOULD be ttl_seconds / 4. The recommended floor (60s) applies only when ttl_seconds is large enough that floor < ttl_seconds still holds; for small ttl (e.g. the 60s minimum) the server MUST shrink refresh_lead_seconds below ttl_seconds (see webrtc-signaling.md §4.2). Required so all clients refresh at consistent cadence and servers can plan secret rotation grace windows.

issued_at.description: Server-issued timestamp (RFC 3339 UTC). Bound into the ICE config signature.

turn_required.description: When true, clients MUST disable host/srflx ICE candidates and only relay through TURN. Used by high-privacy Realms to prevent IP leakage.

next_retry_at.description: Set when the response is a soft failure (e.g. turn_credential_expired). Clients MUST NOT retry before this time.

signature.description: Detached signature by the media service DID over the canonical bytes of this response (excluding `signature`).

urls.description: STUN/TURN server URL(s). Schemes: stun:, stuns:, turn:, turns:.

username.description: TURN ephemeral credential username. v1: <expiry-unix>:<per-call-pseudonym>. MUST NOT contain principal DID, handle, email, or any cross-call stable identifier.

credential.description: TURN ephemeral credential password (HMAC-SHA256 of username with per-tenant turn shared secret in REST-style).

kid.description: DID URL of the concrete media-service verification method. Bare DID is not accepted because the response must pin one already accepted service key binding.

signature_algorithm.description: Signature algorithm. Values MUST be active alg entries supporting detached_jws in signature-alg-registry.json. Default v1 deployments use Ed25519; stronger or deployment-specific profiles MAY require another registered algorithm while preserving the exact signing input defined in webrtc-signaling.md §4.1.

sig.description: base64url-encoded detached signature over canonical response bytes.

schemas/identity-link.schema.json.title: Arkret Minimal-Metadata Identity Link
schemas/identity-link.schema.json.description: Encrypted application-message or MLS private-extension payload that binds a Realm-scoped pairwise actor did_core_id to the real principal did_core_id for ak.profile.mls.minimal_metadata_realm.v1. The binding is scoped to both realm_id and trust_domain so the same pairwise mapping cannot be replayed across deployments. This object is never written to public Realm history unless a separate disclosure policy explicitly permits it.

pairwise_actor_id.description: Realm-scoped pairwise actor did_core_id used byte-for-byte in Event.actor_id and the MLS BasicCredential identity. Its Event proof verificationMethod controller is a did:key did whose registered adapter projection MUST equal this value.

principal_id.description: Real principal DID that controls or has disclosed the pairwise DID.

trust_domain.description: Deployment-scope trust domain. Receiver MUST require this value to match the current Realm / service trust_domain before accepting a pairwise DID -> principal DID mapping.

strand_id.description: Optional application-message context marker for the Strand carrying the identity link. It does not create independent membership or key scope; key scope is determined by effective_scope.

track_name.description: Optional display-track context marker for application routing. Track names do not create independent membership, policy, or MLS key scope.

mls_group_id.description: Optional MLS group identifier (base64url RFC 9420 GroupID) for diagnostic / cross-implementation correlation. NOT used by the reducer for authorization — authoritative MLS group state lives in ak.mls.genesis / ak.mls.commit events. Provided here so audit projections can quickly correlate an identity-link with its MLS group without replaying the full epoch chain.

response_signing_verification_method.description: Pairwise DID URL used only for generic history response PayloadProof signatures. Its controller MUST project to pairwise_actor_id.

response_signing_algorithm.description: The v1 history response PayloadProof algorithm. This key is independent from the MLS ciphersuite LeafNode signature key.

response_signing_public_key_b64u.description: Raw 32-byte Ed25519 response-signing public key encoded as unpadded base64url.

response_signing_public_key_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the decoded response_signing_public_key_b64u bytes.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a key controlled by principal_id or by a disclosure proof accepted by Realm policy. Fragment is REQUIRED (this is a DID URL, not a bare DID). DID method-name normalized to lowercase per W3C DID 1.0.

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical input bytes: utf8('ak.identity-link-v1\n') || canonical_json(identity-link object with proof.payload_digest and proof.signature omitted). The signed object includes trust_domain and the independent history response-signing key binding.

schema.description: Canonical schema discriminator. Aligned with schema-registry.json; lets validators distinguish identity registry receipts from other receipt envelopes (e.g. audit-ryw-receipt, event-batch-receipt).

subject_did.description: Method-native bare DID whose registry log position is attested by this receipt. This field intentionally remains a DID because seq and head_event_digest identify that DID method history; it is not a stable Arkret business identity field.

registry_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the registry service issuing the receipt. The detached proof verification_method remains a DID URL and MUST project to this value through the registered method adapter.

witness_role.description: Issuer's role in the DID registry consensus group. Required so verifiers can apply role-specific freshness / quorum rules; an absent role would force the verifier to guess writer vs replica semantics.

audience.description: Optional audience binding (verifier DID, service DID, or domain). When present, verifiers MUST reject the receipt outside that audience context to prevent cross-protocol reuse.

signature.description: Registry detached proof. payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with signature omitted)). The detached JWS signs canonical_json({context:'ak.identity_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, registry_id, subject_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); context is a fixed signing-context domain tag and is not a wire field. signature.created_at MUST equal receipt.created_at. signature.verification_method MUST be a currently valid DID URL assertion method whose DID component is independently validated and projected to registry_id by the registered method adapter. Receipt audience and proof audience MUST either both be absent or be the same single string; array-valued proof audiences are invalid for this object family.

schemas/identity-resolution.schema.json.title: Arkret Identity Resolution
schemas/identity-resolution.schema.json.description: Canonical did_core_id/did resolution state, owner-published evidence and service-route bootstrap contracts. A did is a standard bare DID and a did_core_id is the stable Arkret business identity projected by a registered DID method adapter.

authenticated_service_resolution.description: Self-contained current service-resolution verification input. The receiver validates the signed record, complete method-native history material and normalized DID document before using any verification method. This is the public service bootstrap response; a bare current record or a resolver-produced history summary is insufficient to freeze a Realm notary signer.

normalized_did_document.description: Exact registered normalized DID Document projection whose canonical digest equals method_history_evidence.evidence.document_digest. Its did equals service_resolution_record.record.did and the record proof names an authorized assertion method in this document.

method_evidence_boundary.description: Inclusive adapter-defined history interval covered by this evidence. For a method without native history the from and to values are identical synthetic values for the one verified state.

webvh_method_history_evidence.description: Complete did:webvh log, proof and witness material routed to adapter did:webvh:1.0. log_entries is the gap-free native history from inception through boundary.to_version_id, not a resolver summary or a partial segment. witness_records is the complete did-witness.json record set required by every witness policy active in that interval and is empty only when no entry activates a witness policy. The receiver independently verifies SCID derivation, every versionId/hash-chain link, every controller proof, rotation authorization, all applicable witness thresholds, the exact boundary endpoints and canonical equality of the terminal state with normalized_did_document. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB; an over-limit service history is ineligible for this retained historical-signer/notary bootstrap and fails closed rather than returning partial evidence.

evidence.description: Closed canonical evidence receipt for exactly the inclusive boundary. method MUST be webvh and method_proofs MUST carry the matching webvh_log row; the public evidence evaluator checks its history_head against boundary.to_method_history_head. This receipt summarizes the independently reverified log_entries/witness_records but never replaces them.

log_entries.description: Exact ordered native did:webvh entry objects from inception through the selected terminal entry. The adapter applies the registered did:webvh parameter-name and proof rules and rejects gaps, duplicates, surplus entries after boundary.to_version_id, or a first entry other than inception.

witness_records.description: Exact native did-witness.json record objects needed by log_entries. Records are keyed uniquely by versionId; missing, duplicate, invalid or surplus records fail closed. The array is empty exactly when the verified log activates no witness policy.

did_web_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded current DID Document retrieval evidence routed to adapter did:web:1. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical document-bound evidence receipt. method MUST be web and method_proofs MUST be empty; document_digest and boundary synthetic head are cross-checked by the public evidence evaluator.

did_key_method_history_evidence.description: Bounded deterministic local expansion evidence routed to adapter did:key:1. The boundary endpoints MUST be identical synthetic values. Canonical encoded evidence MUST NOT exceed 1 MiB.

evidence.description: Closed canonical local-expansion evidence receipt. method MUST be key and method_proofs MUST be empty; the public evidence evaluator recomputes document_digest and the synthetic boundary directly from did.

method_history_evidence.description: Adapter-routed evidence. adapter_version and evidence_kind are a closed discriminator pair; unknown adapters or mismatched pairs fail closed.

resolution_commitment.description: Owner-committed current did and method-native history position. For a deterministic method, method_history_head and version_id use the adapter-defined deterministic canonical values; they are never omitted.

principal_resolution_update_payload.description: Payload for ak.identity.resolution.update in the actor's Principal Control Realm. Admission projects did to the envelope actor_id and performs a strict CAS against the signed resolution_projection head_eq precondition before accepting a method-valid successor.

principal_genesis_event.description: The accepted identity-control Realm genesis Event. It is resolution history head 0 and commits the initial resolution; its derived Realm id, actor, purpose and initial projection are cross-bound by the principal resolution evidence evaluator.

resolution_update_event.description: One accepted post-genesis resolution successor Event. Its exact resolution-cell head_eq precondition and predecessor fields are mandatory under Event dispatch.

principal_resolution_projection_attestat.description: Station assertion that resolution_projection is the current accepted value of this account's singleton resolution cell. It carries no PCR realm id, Event, receipt or Seal: the public consumer verifies the account pair, the projection and the bounded method history, not the account's internal control stream.

method_history_evidence_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the exact method_history_evidence object carried in the same response. It binds the attestation to the bounded adapter evidence so neither half can be swapped.

issued_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Hard freshness bound. A consumer performing a security-sensitive action MUST refetch at or after this instant; a cache never extends it.

principal_resolution_projection_attestat.description: Complete Station-signed projection attestation. The detached proof signs the canonical transcript above; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.issued_at.

public_principal_resolution.description: Complete public resolution response for one account selected by (principal_id, station_id). It is the only unauthenticated resolution surface and it MUST NOT carry principal_control_realm_id, PCR genesis Event, genesis receipt, resolution Events or accepted Seal; those are account-internal audit material served only by the authorized audit operation. A consumer verifies the service route for station_id, then the attestation proof, then project(did)=principal_id and the bounded method history; a set of bare unproven fields is not a valid response.

station_id.description: Station for this account authority. Together with principal_id it is the complete public selector and the complete external identity; no PCR-derived value participates in principal equality.

resolution_projection.description: Current accepted value of the singleton resolution cell. resolution_event_ref is an opaque head coordinate for staleness comparison; it is not a handle for fetching that Event through any public surface.

method_history_evidence.description: Bounded adapter-routed evidence for exactly the projected history position. It is required: without it the projection is an unverifiable server assertion.

principal_resolution_audit_request.description: Authorized request for account-internal resolution audit evidence. Authorization is the current holder session bound to the exact AccountId. Recovery actors first finish the existing recovery transaction and become the current holder; v1 does not create a second audit authorization path. Caller-declared intent is never authorization. Unknown account, wrong AccountId and unauthorized caller are externally indistinguishable and share the anti-enumeration outcome.

account_id.description: station_id MUST equal the serving Station DID. A different value is an unknown account, not a referral.

history_depth.description: Maximum number of post-genesis predecessor resolution Events to disclose, counted backwards from current_resolution_event. 0 discloses the current head only. A value outside the closed range is param_invalid; an implementation MUST NOT substitute a private cap.

after_resolution_event_ref.description: Known ancestor already held by the caller. The disclosed segment stops exclusively at it, so only the unknown suffix is returned. It MUST be the genesis Event or an accepted ak.identity.resolution.update in this account's current lineage; a ref outside that lineage is param_invalid with reason resolution_history_ancestor_unknown. Supplying it with history_depth 0 is param_invalid, because depth 0 discloses no predecessor and the cursor could not apply.

principal_resolution_audit_evidence.description: Account-internal resolution audit and recovery evidence for one account selected by (principal_id, station_id). It is served only by the authorized audit operation. PCR genesis, realm and Seal material support account-local audit and recovery; they MUST NOT be compared as external identity, MUST NOT be required to validate an ordinary federated Event carrying a Station admission proof, and MUST NOT be republished on any unauthenticated surface.

station_id.description: Station for this account authority. Together with principal_id it is the complete public selector; the remaining PCR material is recovery/audit evidence and does not change principal equality.

principal_control_realm_id.description: Realm id derived from principal_genesis_event under the registered PCR derivation rule; it is not a producer-selected alternate scope.

principal_genesis_receipt.description: Account-local signed pcr_genesis_unit receipt. It supports audit/recovery and is not an external account-local-lineage identifier.

predecessor_resolution_events.description: Post-genesis resolution update Events preceding current_resolution_event, ordered from the current event's immediate predecessor toward older events and contiguous with no gaps. The genesis Event is carried separately and MUST NOT be repeated here. The segment ends at whichever comes first: request history_depth items, the exclusive request after_resolution_event_ref ancestor, or head 0. A server MAY return a shorter contiguous segment than requested when a response bound applies, MUST NOT return more items than history_depth, and MUST NOT skip an intermediate Event.

history_complete.description: True exactly when the disclosed segment reaches its requested stop condition: head 0, or the exclusive after_resolution_event_ref ancestor. False means disclosure was truncated and next_audit_cursor is present. Omitted history is unknown rather than absent.

accepted_seal.description: Accepted Seal covering current_resolution_event. The verifier replays that exact Event through the registered reducer; v1 does not add a second resolution-specific state-cell Merkle proof carrier.

next_audit_cursor.description: Present exactly when history_complete is false. It equals the value.resolution_event_ref inside the exact head_eq precondition of the oldest supplied Event, which is that Event's guarded immediate predecessor and the next Event the caller has not seen. The caller continues the audit walk by requesting again with this ref already held; it never skips the omitted segment or reads a payload echo.

service_resolution_record_core.description: Signed first-hop service route material. It lets a consumer map a stable service did_core_id to a candidate did; it is not an endpoint authorization by itself.

service_kind.description: Registered ServiceDescribe role selected at this route. The describe request MUST use this value when the base URL hosts multiple roles.

resolution_event_ref.description: Adapter-canonical service control-state reference. It MUST equal the active adapter row's service_resolution_event_ref_rule for this did and method_history_head: did:webvh maps to did-webvh-entry-sha256, did:web maps to did-web-document-sha256, and did:key maps to did-key-did-sha256.

record_sequence.description: Exact signed-record sequence within one service did_core_id. The first record is 0; every accepted same-core successor is exactly the immediately previous record_sequence plus one. Gaps, reuse and rollback fail closed.

previous_record_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the immediately previous complete signed ServiceResolutionRecord, including proof, or null exactly when record_sequence is 0.

current_record_url.description: No-redirect HTTPS current-record URL. It MUST equal canonical base_url plus _arkret/open/services/{RFC3986-percent-encoded service_id}/resolution. A fetched successor's independently verified signed value becomes the next refresh URL; an old record or redirect cannot retarget it. Fetchers apply SSRF, DNS-rebinding, response-size and timeout controls and trust only verified record bytes.

base_url.description: Canonical first-hop HTTPS base: lowercase scheme and host, normalized path, no query or fragment, exactly one trailing slash. The consumer resolves _arkret/describe relative to this value without following cross-origin redirects and cross-checks the returned binding.

describe_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of {service_id, service_kind, service_resolution, http_json_base_url} projected from ServiceDescribe. Dynamic capabilities, limits, rate policy and x_* fields are intentionally excluded.

issued_at.description: MUST be <= refresh_after and strictly earlier than expires_at.

refresh_after.description: MUST satisfy issued_at <= refresh_after < expires_at. At or after this time a cache refreshes current_record_url before a security-sensitive use.

expires_at.description: MUST be later than refresh_after. An expired record is never routable; current_record_url may provide a verified successor with the same service_id.

service_resolution_record.description: Portable signed ServiceResolutionRecord. Its record digest is sha256:<lowercase-hex SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object including proof>. Separately, payload_digest is sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of record. The detached proof signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service_resolution_record_proof.v1', payload_digest, service_id, service_kind, did, method_history_head, version_id, resolution_event_ref, record_sequence, previous_record_digest, current_record_url, base_url, describe_digest, issued_at, refresh_after, expires_at, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}) under a service control key accepted at method_history_head; proof.created_at MUST equal record.issued_at. The verifier also enforces project(did)=service_id, the adapter-canonical history/version/event-ref mapping, record_sequence=0 iff previous_record_digest=null, exact plus-one same-core succession, and the timestamp ordering declared by the record fields.

service_route_handover_notice_core.description: Portable future-route sidecar bound to one current ServiceResolutionRecord. It never changes the current route, never consumes record_sequence and never authorizes Realm, device, KeyPackage, repair or other business payload bytes. The evaluator enforces issued_at <= not_before <= cutover_at < grace_until <= expires_at for scheduled notices; candidate_record_url is the mechanical no-redirect service-resolution path below canonical candidate_base_url. A receiver accepts the candidate only after it returns the exact same service_id/service_kind, record_sequence=from_record_sequence+1 and previous_record_digest=from_record_digest in a formally verified ServiceResolutionRecord followed by describe reverse binding.

handover_id.description: Service-local UUIDv7 identity. It is stable across every scheduled update and cancellation in one notice chain.

notice_revision.description: The first notice is revision 0. Every accepted update or cancellation is exactly predecessor revision plus one.

from_record_digest.description: Exact complete signed-record digest at the notice basis. It MUST equal the receiver's durable last-seen/current digest for from_record_sequence; a stale or unrelated basis is never accepted silently.

not_before.description: Before this instant only bounded public record/describe preflight is allowed and it cannot update route state or carry business bytes. Clock skew may delay local use but cannot advance it.

previous_notice_digest.description: Null exactly for notice_revision 0; otherwise the digest of the immediately previous complete signed notice.

service_route_handover_notice.description: Complete target-service-signed handover artifact. Its notice digest is SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object including proof. Publishing or mirroring it does not make candidate_base_url current and cannot replace a formally verified successor ServiceResolutionRecord.

service_resolution_artifact_key.description: Canonical durable-ledger key for one mirrored artifact family.

service_resolution_publish_request.description: Publishes exactly one target-signed record or notice into a Realm-scoped peer mirror. The authenticated Source-Service-ID, not an untrusted body field, supplies source_id. artifact_digest is over the exact complete selected artifact. The receiver validates current federation-peer authority, target visibility/delegation, target proof, basis, chain, freshness and bounds before any durable write.

service_resolution_publish_ack_core.description: Receiver-authored durable exact-digest acknowledgement. Transport idempotency is keyed by (source_id, realm_id, request_id) and binds request_digest: an exact retry returns the original ack and a different request digest is duplicate_conflict. Artifact integrity is independently keyed by (source_id, realm_id, artifact_key): the same artifact key with another artifact_digest is duplicate_conflict with zero overwrite, while a new request_id for identical artifact bytes may receive a new ack cross-bound to that request.

request_digest.description: SHA-256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete service_resolution_publish_request.

service_resolution_resolve_request.description: Realm-scoped anti-enumeration query for target-signed successor material. requester authority comes from the authenticated peer service and current Realm relationship. target_id must already be visible to requester through an effective joined-member ActorId routing projection or explicit service delegation. Unknown, unauthorized, invisible and not-held outcomes are externally indistinguishable.

service_resolution_resolve_outcome.description: Bounded continuous target-signed successor supply. successor_records begins exactly at known_record_sequence+1 with predecessor known_record_digest and remains plus-one/digest-contiguous. handover_notice, when present, is the single active non-expired target notice on the returned/current basis. has_more never permits accepting a gap. The canonical response is at most 256 KiB. The requester independently verifies every target proof, method history, time, chain and describe binding; same sequence with different valid target-signed digests is a route fork and enters quarantine, never a majority or reachability choice.

has_more.description: True only when more continuous target-signed records are held beyond the bounded response. The caller continues from the last verified record; it never skips the omitted segment.

service_resolution_last_seen_floor.description: Durable remote ServiceResolutionRecord anti-rollback floor, distinct from route cache and service_route_notice_state. It survives process restart and cache eviction. The record floor advances only after target proof, exact successor chain, method history, freshness and describe reverse binding all pass. Same record sequence with a different valid target-signed digest is a fork quarantine, not last-writer-wins.

service_route_notice_state.description: Durable accepted handover-notice state, independent from the ServiceResolutionRecord floor and TTL route cache. It survives restart and is retained until cancellation, formal successor completion or signed expiry. A scheduled entry is usable only while state=scheduled and now<expires_at, and only against the exact from_record floor. A cancelled entry remains durable evidence that the candidate must not be used. Same revision with another digest is a fork quarantine.

service_route_cache_entry.description: Replaceable TTL performance cache derived from one already verified durable floor. It is not authority and MAY disappear on restart. Cache freshness never permits accepting a sequence below service_resolution_last_seen_floor, extending signed expires_at, bypassing describe, or turning a notice candidate into a current route.

version_id.description: Native DID-method version coordinate copied from the exact verified signed ServiceResolutionRecord; cache replacement cannot infer or refresh it independently.

refresh_after.description: Signed record refresh trigger; it does not extend expires_at or authorize a future candidate.

expires_at.description: Signed ServiceResolutionRecord hard expiry. The cache is never routable at or after this instant.

cache_expires_at.description: Local TTL no later than the signed record expires_at. Implementations enforce cache_expires_at <= expires_at and refresh_after < expires_at.

route_mirror_hint.description: Transport-only hint for one route-mirror service. mirror_id is only a stable lookup identity and MUST be paired with independently verifiable service_resolution first-hop material; neither the did_core_id nor the carrier authorizes target-service routing or Realm access.

mirror_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the candidate route-mirror service. A bare did_core_id is never a route or authority.

service_resolution.description: Verifiable first-hop carrier for the mirror itself: either an inline signed current record or its current_record_url locator. A naked URL is forbidden. The target service route still requires Realm-scoped resolve authorization and target-signed material.

route_assistance.description: Optional short-TTL, transport-only route recovery hints for invite locator, invite delivery, or Contact bootstrap. At least one member is required. Effective usability is bounded by the earliest containing locator/invite/contact bootstrap expiry and each fetched record or signed notice expiry. This object MUST NOT enter Event canonical bytes, a Realm member cell, capability or authorization state. Its notice and mirror carriers never extend an outer token/receipt TTL and never authorize delivery, route switching or Realm access.

handover_notice.description: At most one complete target-signed active handover notice. It is only a candidate-discovery hint; the receiver still requires a basis-matching formal successor ServiceResolutionRecord and describe verification.

mirror_hints.description: At most four independently routable mirror hints. Each item carries the mirror did_core_id together with a service_resolution_carrier; bare URLs and bare core ids are not valid items.

current_record_url.description: Directly dereferenceable stable HTTPS URL for the current signed record. Redirects are not followed unless the redirected origin is independently authorized. Fetchers enforce SSRF, DNS-rebinding, size and timeout policy.

pinned_record_digest.description: Optional sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS of the complete signed record expected for the version that produced this carrier. It pins that version only; a later refresh may return a different digest after the fetched same-core successor independently verifies.

schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.title: Arkret InclusionList
schemas/inclusion-list.schema.json.description: FOCIL-style control-plane inclusion list. A non-proposer notary signer lists pending Control Move digests that passed its local verification; the next Seal MUST include, signed-reject, or prove batch pre-state verification failure for every listed digest, otherwise receivers MUST reject that Seal (authz/event-auth-state-resolution.md section 7.3). single_signer notary profiles cannot provide this mechanism. The list is an accountability object, not a Seal: it never advances governance state by itself.

signer_id.description: Notary signer issuing the list. MUST be an eligible non-proposer signer of the Realm's multi-signer notary profile at issue time.

list_seq.description: Per-signer monotonic inclusion-list sequence. Two different canonical lists from the same signer with the same (realm_id, list_seq) constitute equivocation evidence under the section 7.1 slot rule.

event_digests.description: Canonical ascending list of pending Control Move event digests that passed the issuer's local verification and hold a valid receipt.

expiry_seal_count.description: Number of subsequent Seals within which the obligation must be discharged. Default deployment value is 1 (the next Seal).

payload_digest.description: Hash of canonical InclusionList bytes with signature omitted.

schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.title: Arkret Invite Delivery Request
schemas/invite-delivery-request.schema.j.description: Private service-to-service request used by an inviter-side Station to deliver a Realm invite to the invitee-side Station. The request carries an explicit invite address and introduction evidence; raw locator tokens are never written into durable Realm events.

invite_event.description: The ak.invite.create EventEnvelope or equivalent accepted event view being delivered.

account_id.description: Exact invite recipient account. Delivery is sent only to account_id.station_id.

route_assistance.description: Optional transport-only hints for recovering the same Station route. This field is outside invite_event canonical bytes and MUST NOT be copied into durable Realm state; it does not extend invite/locator TTL, change AccountId, or authorize delivery.

consent_grant_ref.description: Event ref of the invitee-issued ak.consent.grant (scope invite or any) that authorizes the inviter to send Realm/Strand invites. High-trust evidence: it is material the invitee actively issued to the inviter, equivalent in trust to a locator_ref.

consent_id.description: Optional consent cell id locating the holder consent cell, to speed up receiver verification of the active grant dot.

handle.description: Canonical handle string the inviter used as the human-readable entry point.

handle_claim.description: Verified handle claim proving that handle resolves to invite_address.account_id. The receiver MUST verify exact AccountId equality, binding_state, proofs, expiry, issuer trust, visibility/audience policy, and that handle_claim.handle equals handle.

resolved_by.description: Optional stable Directory or issuer service did_core_id that supplied the handle resolution.

status.description: Generic receive status. It MUST NOT reveal whether the AccountId exists or whether policy quarantined/dropped the invite. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST be reported as deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Only a receiver policy disclosure level of outcome may add disclosed_outcome, and only with delivered|blocked.

disclosed_outcome.description: Optional graded-disclosure result, closed to delivered|blocked.
