Present ONLY when the subject's receive policy disclosure level for this introduction trust tier is 'outcome' and the subject did not block the issuer; omitted (opaque) otherwise. delivered: the invite reached the holder surface awaiting acceptance; blocked: rejected by block list or policy. A holder-quarantine outcome MUST NOT be disclosed: it reveals holder-private consent state (identity/consent-model.md 6.1.1) and MUST be reported as status='deferred' with no disclosed_outcome, in the same response and timing equivalence class as rate-limit silent drop, timeout drop, holder-not-found and holder policy deny.

schemas/invite-delivery.schema.json.title: Arkret Invite Delivery
schemas/invite-delivery.schema.json.description: Actor-private plaintext account-data cell value of ak.account.invite_delivery, the holder-private carrier that delivers directed-invite credential material to the invitee's devices on the notify branch (zh/sync/invite-addressing.md section 7). The cell is written by the recipient Station, so it cannot be a client-encrypted envelope; invite_token is a server-issued private locator that MUST NOT enter the Invite object or Realm history (zh/models/governance-objects.md section 5.3).

updated_at.description: Instant of the accepted CAS write that produced this value.

delivery_entries.description: Bounded register of delivered invite credentials, oldest first. At most one entry per invite_id; a redelivery of the same invite_id replaces the previous entry. Entries whose expires_at has passed are purged on the next write; overflow beyond 200 evicts the oldest entries.

invite_id.description: Invite ID derived from the accepted ak.invite.create Event; the deduplication key of this register.

inviter_id.description: did_core_id of the inviter as bound by the delivery verification chain.

invite_token.description: Opaque server-issued private invite locator token used by the invitee's accept path. Clients MUST treat it as an opaque string and MUST NOT persist it anywhere outside this cell or equivalent holder-private state.

received_at.description: Instant the recipient Station accepted this delivery into the cell.

expires_at.description: Expiry of the underlying invite credential; an entry with expires_at <= now is stale and MUST NOT be used to accept the invite.

schemas/invite-quarantine.schema.json.title: Arkret Invite Quarantine
schemas/invite-quarantine.schema.json.description: Closed plaintext account-data cell value of ak.account.invite_quarantine. The recipient Station is the sole CAS writer; the cell is a pending-review pointer inbox and grants no membership, contact, or consent authority.

updated_at.description: Instant of the accepted Station CAS write that produced this value.

quarantine_entries.description: Bounded pending-review entries, oldest first. Expired entries are purged before a write and overflow evicts the oldest entries.

last_invalidation.description: Optional diagnostic for the latest accepted consent-revoke invalidation. It is holder-private and never disclosed to the requester.

entry_digest.description: Recipient-service-local stable deduplication digest for this quarantined delivery.

source_peer_principal_id.description: Requester/inviter principal used by consent review and revoke invalidation.

introduction_kind.description: Introduction evidence kind presented by the requester.

invite_event_id.description: Optional accepted invite Event identity when present in the delivery carrier.

expires_at.description: Deployment-policy TTL. An expired entry is discarded and never converts to a grant.

schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.title: Arkret Invite and Contact Receive Policy
schemas/invite-receive-policy.schema.jso.description: Subject-private policy used by a Station to decide which invite delivery or first-contact request introduction evidence may notify the holder. This policy is not written into the target Realm durable event log or the public contact fact log.

subject_id.description: Stable principal did_core_id whose private invite receive policy this object configures. A human anchor may originate from the registered did:webvh, did:web or did:key adapter; the separate ak.profile.ephemeral_pairwise_principal.v1 did:key role remains Realm-local and has no account/PCR/device directory.

holder_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Allowlist of introduction evidence kinds that may reach holder notification or review.

explicit_address_behavior.description: Default behavior for explicit_address evidence. Deployments SHOULD default to quarantine or drop, not notify.

handle_claim_behavior.description: Default behavior for handle_claim evidence. Omitted means quarantine. A subject MAY set notify to allow verified handle-based requests to reach the holder, but the effective value is capped by receive_policy_constraints.

unknown_invites.description: Behavior for invite/contact delivery requests without compliant introduction_evidence.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Optional subject-private allowlist for canonical handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty or omitted means no subject-level domain restriction; deployment constraints may still restrict the effective set.

denied_handle_domains.description: Subject-private denylist for canonical handle domains. Matches are rejected before allowed_handle_domains is evaluated.

trusted_handle_issuer_ids.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of handle claim issuers accepted for handle_claim evidence.

trusted_directory_ids.description: Optional subject-private allowlist of Directory service DIDs accepted as resolved_by for handle_claim evidence.

denied_subject_ids.description: Per-subject block list (peer principal DIDs). Invite delivery whose inviter is in this list MUST be dropped, and disclosure MUST be forced to opaque regardless of the disclosure policy, to avoid leaking the block via a side channel.

disclosure.description: Graded disclosure policy. Controls whether the invite/contact delivery outcome reveals a real result (delivered/blocked) to the requester, by introduction trust tier. Holder quarantine is never disclosable at any tier: it maps to status=deferred with no disclosed_outcome. Omitted means the default: high_trust=outcome, discovery_trust=opaque, low_trust=opaque.

domain_name.description: Canonical IDNA A-label domain. Subdomains are not implied; list each accepted domain explicitly.

disclosure_level.description: opaque: only a generic accepted-for-processing status is returned, indistinguishable across exists/not-exists/policy outcomes. outcome: the real delivered|blocked result is disclosed to the inviter. Neither level ever discloses holder quarantine.

high_trust.description: Disclosure level for the high-trust introduction tier: consent_grant, locator_ref, shared_realm. Default outcome.

discovery_trust.description: Disclosure level for public or restricted discovery evidence: handle_claim. Default opaque.

low_trust.description: Disclosure level for the low-trust introduction tier: same_station, explicit_address, and missing/non-compliant evidence. Default opaque.

receive_policy_constraints.description: Deployment/admin upper bound applied to subject-private receive policies. The effective receive policy is the intersection of the subject policy and these constraints; constraints can only make a subject less reachable, never more reachable.

applies_to.description: Surfaces governed by this constraint object. Omitted means both invite_delivery and contact_request.

deployment_allowed_introduction_kinds.description: Maximum set of introduction evidence kinds this deployment permits. Omitted means no deployment-level kind cap.

handle_claim_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for handle_claim evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

explicit_address_max_behavior.description: Maximum behavior allowed for explicit_address evidence using the order drop < quarantine < notify.

disclosure_max.description: Deployment/admin upper bound on graded invite outcome disclosure. Each present tier caps the corresponding subject disclosure value using opaque < outcome; omitted tiers impose no additional deployment cap.

allowed_handle_domains.description: Deployment-level allowlist for handle domains accepted as handle_claim evidence. Empty means no handle domain is accepted.

introduction_evidence_digest.description: Digest of private invite delivery introduction_evidence. Raw locator tokens and receive-policy state MUST NOT appear in durable Realm events.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent invite state update.

third_party_invite.description: Wire-level 3PID/OOB invite binding. No plaintext email/phone/SMS code is allowed here. `oob_code_kind` distinguishes offline high-entropy token validation from server-side lookup short-code validation.

display_name_hint.description: Non-identifying UI hint only; MUST NOT contain plaintext 3PID.

token_commitment.description: Salted commitment to a high-entropy invite token. Required for offline_token mode.

token_salt_id.description: Opaque handle for the verification service's private salt record. The salt value itself MUST NOT appear on wire.

lookup_table_ref.description: Opaque verification-service lookup table reference for short-code mode. The raw short code MUST NOT appear on wire.

pepper_id.description: Server-private pepper generation identifier for lookup mode; the pepper value itself is never on wire.

oob_code_kind.description: offline_token means the out-of-band code is itself >=128-bit entropy and validated against token_commitment. lookup means the human-readable code is only an index into a server-private lookup table protected by rate limits and pepper/HMAC storage.

token_entropy_bits.description: Required for offline_token mode. Entropy estimate excluding separators.

verification_public_key.description: Ephemeral public key or DID verification method used by the verification service to sign claim results.

schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..title: Arkret Key Backup Active Series Record
schemas/key-backup-active-series.schema..description: Signed principal-control record selecting the canonical backup series for one (actor_id, backup_kind). This closes the rollback gap when multiple series exist after compromise rotation or migration. Receivers MUST verify this record before choosing a series from list results.

series_pointer_version.description: Strictly monotonic per (actor_id, backup_kind). The first record is 1 and every successor is previous+1; receivers reject rollback, gaps and same-version forks.

previous_series_ids.description: Retained old series used only for read-old-data or erasure transition. MUST NOT be treated as a primary recovery source.

frontier_ref.description: Principal Control Realm frontier and current identity-root device generation under which active_series_id was selected.

signature.description: base64url signature over RFC 8785 JCS(record without auth_data.signature). The closed record shape fixes the authenticated projection.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize Event anchoring the device that signed this active-series selection.

device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation. This is not a DID versionId and MUST equal the accepted current_device_generation_ref at the referenced frontier.

items.description: Every packed secret in a portable backup MUST have local_authoritative origin from direct export of locally verified MLS state. A received history-response or RRK-opened candidate is forbidden even after it successfully decrypts an Event.

schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.title: Arkret Key Backup Unlock Proof
schemas/key-backup-unlock-proof.schema.j.description: Proof presented before a recovery strand downloads or unlocks a key-backup envelope. It binds a backup read/decrypt action to one recovery_session_id, requesting device, backup object, selected series, ciphertext digest, and the proof transcript accepted by the recovery session.

proof_digest.description: Digest of the canonical recovery proof transcript that moved the session to verified.

challenge.description: Optional echo of the recovery-session challenge; when present it MUST match the session snapshot.

verification_method.description: DID URL for either the accepted requesting device key after authorization, or the recovery-session proof key before a recovery_public_key unlock.

signature.description: base64url signature over RFC 8785 JCS(unlock proof without auth_data.signature). The closed proof shape fixes the authenticated projection, including challenge exactly when present.

mixed_secret_storage.description: True only for the personal_node exception where one encrypted backup envelope contains both identity-signing material and E2EE / MLS history material. Non-personal deployment profiles MUST reject this flag. When true and recipient_method=passphrase_kdf, the stricter Argon2id floor below applies.

series_id.description: Stable identifier for one immutable chain of backup envelopes belonging to a single (actor_id, backup_kind). A pair MAY have multiple series during compromise rotation or migration; active series selection is outside this envelope and MUST come from the signed active-series record in identity/key-management.md §7.6. Receivers use (actor_id, backup_kind, series_id) to detect server-side rollback / withholding within the selected series.

series_seq.description: 0-based, strictly monotonically increasing sequence number within (actor_id, series_id). Genesis envelope of a series MUST set 0. Receivers MUST reject envelopes whose sequence does not strictly exceed the previously accepted sequence in the same series.

supersedes_id.description: backup_id of the immediate predecessor in the same series_id. MUST be absent for series_seq=0; MUST be present, non-null, and reference an existing predecessor for series_seq>0.

supersedes_digest.description: Required when supersedes is non-null. Hash of the canonical_json of the predecessor envelope (excluding auth_data.signature). Receivers MUST recompute and reject mismatches as `series_chain_broken`.

frontier_ref.description: Optional reference to the Principal Control Realm frontier and identity-root device generation at envelope creation time.

device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic device generation. This is not a DID versionId and MUST equal the accepted current_device_generation_ref at the referenced frontier.

recovery_policy_ref.description: Required whenever encryption.recipient_method is recovery_public_key, and optional as a signed recovery-strand hint otherwise. Binds the backup envelope to the active recovery policy version under which it was produced. Receivers MUST compare this tuple to the currently accepted recovery policy before using such an envelope; mismatch fails as recovery_policy_mismatch, but the field does not replace active-series, frontier, Realm/MLS authorization, or device-state checks. This is intentionally separate from frontier_ref: it binds the recovery authorization surface, not only the device trust generation or control-stream position.

recipient_key_ref.description: For recipient_method=recovery_public_key, this MUST resolve to a non-revoked recovery_key_agreements[].key_agreement_ref in the envelope's referenced accepted recovery policy, and the selected hpke_suite MUST appear in that entry's hpke_suites. DID Document-only key agreements are not an authorization source. A recovery_keys[].verification_method is a signing-key ref and MUST be rejected here.

hpke_suite.description: Registered active HPKE suite (KEM x KDF x AEAD per RFC 9180) selector; the value space is the active rows of artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Applies only to recipient_method=recovery_public_key. When absent it denotes the default-MUST row ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1. aead.name MUST equal the selected suite's AEAD. An unregistered or inactive suite MUST be rejected (unsupported_hpke_suite). Absent / ignored for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key).

aead_profile.description: Optional AEAD profile id that binds algorithm version, nonce length, tag length, key length, and AAD construction. Receivers that do not support the profile MUST fail closed instead of inferring semantics from name alone.

nonce.description: base64url AEAD nonce. Required for the symmetric methods (passphrase_kdf / secret_storage_key). For recipient_method=passphrase_kdf this MUST equal HMAC-SHA256(HKDF(derived_key, info='arkret-key-backup-aead-nonce-v1'), canonical_json({backup_id, actor_id, device_id, backup_kind, backup_version, created_at, aead.name, aead.aead_profile?, aead.nonce_salt}))[0:N_AEAD]; receivers recompute and reject mismatches. Absent for recovery_public_key (HPKE derives its nonce internally).

nonce_salt.description: Producer-generated base64url random salt (at least 128 bits before encoding) included in the passphrase_kdf nonce derivation transcript. Required when recipient_method=passphrase_kdf; not secret, signed as envelope metadata, and prevents nonce reuse from duplicate business metadata tuples.

enc.description: base64url HPKE KEM encapsulated key. Required for recipient_method=recovery_public_key; the KEM/KDF/AEAD are pinned by encryption.hpke_suite (default ak.hpke_x25519_aead_chacha20poly1305.v1) per artifacts/registry/hpke-suite-registry.json. Absent for the symmetric methods.

domain_separation.description: Signed key-backup domain separation inputs. The HKDF info and fixed AEAD/HPKE AAD base are derived exactly from the envelope by key-management.md §7.2; only the subdomain and genuine x_* AAD extensions are carried on the wire.

aead_aad_extensions.description: Optional producer-chosen AEAD/HPKE AAD extensions. Every member name MUST be x_*; implementations merge these members into the fixed derived AAD base before RFC 8785 canonicalization and MUST reject collisions.

secret_version.description: Monotonic version of the backed-up secret (e.g. mls_account_secret). Used by clients for deterministic preferred-backup selection and anti-rollback ordering (key-management.md §9.1). Present on versioned secret items; absent on share-style items such as recovery_key_share.

ranges.description: Public range index for one effective scope. Secret bytes exist only in encrypted plaintext HistorySecretRange items.

verification_method.description: DID URL identifying the device signing key.

signature_algorithm.description: Raw signature algorithm name; MUST be an active signature-alg-registry alg whose proof_kinds includes raw_detached_signature. Ed25519 is the v1 default; ML-DSA-65 is gated behind the PQ migration profile.

signature.description: base64url-encoded signature over RFC 8785 JCS(envelope without auth_data.signature). Every present closed envelope member, including optional and x_* members, is authenticated; no wire field list selects the projection.

device_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted current-generation ak.device.authorize Event anchoring the device signing this backup.

allOf.description: Every recovery_public_key envelope is bound to one accepted recovery-policy version. The recipient_key_ref resolves only within that policy's recovery_key_agreements array, and recovery_policy_ref is signed even when backup_kind is secret_storage or mls_history.

then.description: One mls_history object covers exactly one exporter effective scope and contains only a public range index. Decrypted plaintext carries packed HistorySecretRange values and can restore history decryption only, never active MLS authoring state.

schemas/key-transparency.schema.json.title: Arkret Key Transparency Evidence
schemas/key-transparency.schema.json.description: Canonical Arkret-specific evidence for ak.profile.key_transparency.v1 and high-security/sovereign log-backed witness requirements. This wire object is not an implementation of IETF KEYTRANS and MUST NOT be advertised as such; interop with draft-ietf-keytrans-protocol-05 requires a separately registered adapter/profile.

schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.title: Arkret MLS KeyPackage Operation DTOs
schemas/keypackage-operations.schema.jso.description: Closed request and response DTOs for self and peer MLS KeyPackage upload, claim, claim-status query, consume, and revoke operations. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

object_ref.description: Opaque content-addressed or service-scoped reference. Hash-shaped refs MUST use keypackage_digest for digest bytes.

keypackage_capability_id.description: Open registered identifier from keypackage-capability-registry.json. Unknown well-formed values are preserved but treated as unsupported.

keypackage_capability_list.description: UTF-8 byte-lexicographically sorted unique KeyPackage capability identifiers. Semantic registry membership and ordering are enforced after structural schema validation.

keypackage_id.description: Arkret MLS-profile KeyPackage identity. This is the registered ak:mls:kp:<uuidv7> special form, not an opaque external identifier.

keypackage.description: Base64url encoding of the canonical MLS KeyPackage bytes.

cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

last_resort.description: When true, this entry is a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10). It remains published across claims and never enters the single-use claimed or consumed states; rotation, expiry, or explicit revocation transitions it to revoked with a registered revocation_reason. This application-layer flag is covered by the required upload batch endpoint_signature. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

agent_id.description: Native-Agent KeyPackage branch only. MUST equal principal_id and the current AgentSignerEvidence agent identity. It is never encoded as an ak:device identifier.

agent_verification_method.description: Native-Agent runtime method that signed the exact KeyPackage; MUST match agent_key_authorize_event_id and the KeyPackage signature byte for byte.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted active ak.agent.key.authorize Event that binds a Native Agent runtime verification method to this KeyPackage. Mutually exclusive with device_authorize_event_id.

last_resort.description: When true, this claim record returns a reusable last-resort KeyPackage (RFC 9420 Section 10) because the single-use pool was empty. The package may be reused within the same intended_realm_id and is not transitioned to consumed; the holder MUST rotate it and trigger group updates on next online. Optional capability gated by ak.feature.mls_last_resort_keypackage.v1. See encryption-and-audit.md section 2.6.2.

keypackage_claim_record.description: Closed KeyPackage claim record. Human-device, Native-Agent, and Realm-local minimal-metadata pairwise branches are an exact XOR. In the pairwise branch principal_id is the Realm-local actor projected from the exact did:key method; no account, Device, PCR, Agent evidence, or mirrored actor field is carried.

pairwise_verification_method.description: Minimal-metadata branch only. principal_id MUST equal ak:did_core:key:<same multibase>; no durable Device or account identity is created.

endpoint_signature.description: Required authoritative batch signature over the complete typed upload request with only this top-level signature omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.upload.create.v1 domain. The selected human device, Native Agent runtime, or minimal-metadata pairwise did:key endpoint signs the same transcript.

keypackage_refs.description: Accepted KeyPackage refs in request order; batch upload may accept more than one entry.

requester_authorization.description: Closed human-device, Native-Agent, or Realm-local minimal-metadata pairwise detached authorization by the requesting participant. The pairwise branch signs with the exact did:key method projected by requester and carries no account-local authorization Event.

target_keypackage_ref.description: Optional exact ordinary KeyPackage selector for a normal same-group Direct Conversation Add/Welcome after accepted member rejoin. When present, the owner authority atomically claims exactly this current, unconsumed package or returns the same opaque claim_failed result as every other target-side failure; it is never a best-effort hint.

target_agent_id.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch only. MUST equal target_principal_id and the Agent identity in the returned claim record and current AgentSignerEvidence.

target_agent_verification_method.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch current runtime verification method.

target_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

target_pairwise_verification_method.description: Minimal-metadata exact-target branch. target_principal_id MUST be the Realm-local ak:did_core:key actor projected from this method.

peer_keypackages_claim_unsigned_request.description: Server-prepared immutable peer claim request fields before requester_authorization is attached. claim_request_id carries at least 128 bits of entropy and equals the Idempotency-Key value on the peer command.

target_keypackage_ref.description: Optional exact ordinary KeyPackage selector for a normal same-group Direct Conversation Add/Welcome after accepted member rejoin. When present, the owner authority atomically claims exactly this current, unconsumed package or returns the same opaque claim_failed result as every other target-side failure; it is never a best-effort hint.

target_agent_id.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch only. MUST equal target_principal_id and the Agent identity in the returned claim record and current AgentSignerEvidence.

target_agent_verification_method.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch current runtime verification method.

target_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Native-Agent exact-target branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event.

target_pairwise_verification_method.description: Minimal-metadata exact-target branch. target_principal_id MUST be the Realm-local ak:did_core:key actor projected from this method.

request.description: The exact participant-authorized unsigned request fields. Together with request_digest, this lets the destination bind a later Welcome and Direct Conversation binding to the durable claim without trusting source-service assertions.

peer_keypackage_claim_receipt.description: Destination-service-signed durable receipt. source_id and request are covered by the receipt signature; request_digest additionally binds the complete transport command, including participant authorization and portable signer evidence.

keypackage_claim_terminal_receipt.description: The KeyPackage owner service signs an immutable terminal ledger fact. never_claimed is issued only after the request can no longer succeed; expired/revoked identify every formerly claimed ordinary KeyPackage. This is the portable cleanup authority for a failed Direct Conversation attempt.

keypackages_claim_outcome.description: Privacy-preserving peer success response. It intentionally omits inventory counts and per-device failure information.

welcome_ref.description: Exact accepted ak.mls.welcome Event referenced by this durable receipt; this is not a Welcome byte carrier.

recipient_mls_durable_receipt.description: The exact recipient signer signs every field except signature only after durably storing and opening the Welcome. Closed XOR: human device, Native Agent, or Realm-local minimal-metadata pairwise did:key. In the pairwise branch recipient_principal_id is the pairwise actor and no account, Device, or Agent evidence appears.

keypackage_consume_receipt.description: Recipient Station signed durable consume acknowledgement. recipient_durable_receipt is the sole carrier of claim request, KeyPackage, Welcome, Realm, MLS group, epoch, and recipient service coordinates. The service-generated request_digest, claim_id, and consumed_at plus the complete nested durable receipt are covered by signature. For an ordinary KeyPackage it is issued only after the exact single-use claim transitions to consumed. For a reusable last-resort KeyPackage it terminally acknowledges only that exact claim audit while the KeyPackage row remains published. Same exact consume replays this receipt; any claim, coordinate, signer-branch or evidence mismatch conflicts.

recipient_durable_receipt.description: Sole consume authority and coordinate carrier. Its closed device, Native-Agent, or minimal-metadata pairwise signer branch authorizes the command and binds the owner, KeyPackage, Welcome, Realm, MLS group, epoch, and recipient service.

signature.description: Signature over the typed consume request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.consume.v1 domain.
Signature over the typed revoke request with this field omitted, using the ak.self.keys.keypackages.command.revoke.v1 domain.

schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Device Key Operation DTOs
schemas/keys-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request and response DTOs for ak.keys.{upload,query,claim} and ak.keys.backups.{put,list,delete}. Individual OpenAPI components reference the $defs entries in this bundle.

request_id.description: Client-generated idempotency id. The service keys the canonical request digest and terminal outcome by (principal_id, backup_id, request_id).

keys_backups_delete_proof.description: High-risk authority proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1. Exactly one of principal_signing, device_quorum or trusted_recovery_service; an ordinary current-device session proof is not accepted for active-series tail deletion.

did_key.description: Authoritative device signing key as an Ed25519 did:key (multibase base58btc, multicodec ed25519-pub). Mirrors ak.device.authorize.payload.device_public_key_did (device-lifecycle.md §5.2 / §5.4). To check SignalEnvelope and durable Event proofs, receivers resolve a verification_method DID URL under the verified principal did, validate its bare did through the registered adapter, require project(did) to equal the actor/principal did_core_id, and require its fragment to equal the full ak:device:<uuidv7> id. Constructing a verification method by appending a fragment to did_core_id is forbidden.

device_generation_state.description: Reducer-managed identity-root generation fence for the principal device directory.

current_device_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation; it is not and MUST NOT be derived from a DID versionId.

device_projection_attestation_core.description: Origin Station assertion that this exact device projection is the account's current accepted one. It is the whole verification closure of the cross-principal keys/query surface: the row carries no PCR genesis receipt, no device authorization chain and no accepted Seal, because that material is account-internal governance and is disclosed only through ak.self.identity.read.resolution_audit.v1 under exact current-holder authorization. Required device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref fields describe the closed shape of a returned usable row; they do not require an unauthorized device to have a partial projection. A device with no current accepted authorization is omitted or reported through the non-enumerating failure shape. attested_at is a monotone freshness marker and, with authorized_generation_ref, is the cache key of device-lifecycle.md section 8.3.

station_id.description: Origin Station of the account. The proof controller MUST project exactly onto this value; an attestation that verifies under any other key is not evidence about this device.

device_status.description: This surface attests usable devices only. A revoked, fenced or conflicted device is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so the attested status is constant rather than a disclosure channel.

attested_at.description: MUST be strictly earlier than expires_at and MUST equal proof.created_at.

expires_at.description: Hard freshness bound. A consumer performing a security-sensitive action MUST refetch at or after this instant; a cache never extends it.

device_projection_attestation.description: Complete origin-Station-signed device projection attestation. The detached proof signs the ak.device_projection_attestation_proof.v1 transcript; proof.created_at MUST equal attestation.attested_at.

query_device_record.description: Per-(principal_id, device_id) entry in keys_query_outcome. principal_id and device_id are the device_keys map keys, not row fields. Every returned row is complete and attested: the origin Station signs the exact projection, so a relationship-gated third party can verify the row without ever seeing PCR material. A device whose generation is fenced or conflicted, or which is revoked, is not degraded into a partial row -- it is omitted from device_keys or reported through the non-enumerating failures shape, so an incomplete row can never be mistaken for a usable one.

trust_algorithms.description: The canonical (UTF-8 bytewise sorted, deduplicated) algorithm ids echoed verbatim from ak.device.authorize.payload.algorithms; together with device_signing_key and hpke_key this is the material the §5.2 ak.device-trust-bind-v1 transcript covers. Distinct from the sibling `algorithms` prekey-bundle map.

device_projection_attestation.description: Origin-Station signature over the authoritative device projection. Consumers read device_signing_key, hpke_key, device_status, device_authorize_event_id and authorized_generation_ref from the verified attestation. A row whose attestation is missing or whose controller does not project onto station_id MUST NOT be used for E2EE, Signal verification or a KeyPackage claim.

encryption.description: Non-secret recipient metadata so the client can categorize a backup (recovery_public_key vs passphrase_kdf vs secret_storage_key) without downloading the ciphertext. The aead/kdf material is withheld from the list summary.

device_generations.description: Current identity-root generation fence by principal. Fenced/conflicted principals or mismatched device generations expose no usable signing/HPKE/prekey material.

keys_backups_unlock_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.unlock.v1. The unlock proof MUST validate as ak.schema.key_backup_unlock_proof.v1 and MUST be verified against the recovery session, caller, requesting device key, active-series record, and target envelope before the full ciphertext is returned (key-management.md §7.7.1 / §7.8). The path backup_id and proof.backup_id MUST match.

keys_backups_issue_delete_challenge_requ.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.command.issue_delete_challenge.v1. While an issued challenge for the same (principal_id, backup_id, request_id) is still valid, the service MUST return the same challenge; a different request_id mints a new challenge.

keys_backups_delete_challenge.description: Server-issued, durable, single-use delete challenge (TTL <= 300s). Every field is materialized by the service; the client echoes challenge_id in the DELETE body and every proof signs the canonical delete-intent transcript of key-management.md section 7.8.1, which embeds these exact values. Replay, expiry, path mismatch, or audience/service mismatch MUST fail closed.

challenge_id.description: Server-issued unique id of this challenge; echoed verbatim in the DELETE request body.

challenge.description: Server-issued CSPRNG challenge bytes (base64url, no padding).

nonce.description: Server-issued CSPRNG nonce bytes (base64url, no padding); distinct from challenge so the transcript binds two independent freshness values.

audience.description: The service base origin this challenge is valid against; MUST match the origin the DELETE request is sent to.

request_id.description: Echo of the issuance request_id this challenge was minted for.

keys_backups_delete_request_body.description: Request body for ak.self.keys.backups.resource.delete.v1. The service verifies the referenced challenge against the current caller/path/service, verifies the high-risk proof over the canonical delete-intent transcript, and consumes the challenge in the same transaction as the successful delete. A byte-identical network retry returns the stored terminal outcome without re-admitting the consumed challenge; the same request_id with a different canonical digest is a duplicate conflict.

challenge_id.description: Exact echo of the server-issued challenge_id being consumed.

backup_series_erase_request_body.description: Transaction-bound exact request for erasing every old backup object reserved by one SecurityRotationTransaction plan.

schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.title: Arkret Directory Subject Handle List
schemas/list-handles-for-subject-respons.description: Result body for ak.find.directory.read.list_handles_for_subject.v1. It lists currently visible handle claims for a disclosed holder/principal subject did_core_id in the caller's context. Every claim in claims[] MUST have claim.subject byte-for-byte equal to this response subject; proof DID URLs are compared only after adapter projection.

subject_id.description: Holder/principal did_core_id used as the reverse lookup key. This is not a Realm actor_id. Proof verification methods remain DID URLs and are projected to this value by the registered method adapter.

claims.description: Current context-visible signed handle claims. Each item MUST have subject equal to the top-level subject; mismatches MUST be dropped or fail the response closed.

primary_handle.description: Optional canonical primary handle selected from claims[] by identity-handles.md section 3.2.1 for the same context/as_of. The @ mention sigil is not part of this field.

as_of.description: As-of timestamp used to build the visible claim set and primary handle selection.

thumbnails.description: Bound thumbnail / preview descriptors. Producers SHOULD prefer this over preview_blob_ref for private or E2EE media.

schemas/media-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret Realtime Media Operation DTOs
schemas/media-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request DTOs for realtime media service operations. ak.self.media.read.ice_config.v1 responses use ice-config-response.schema.json.

schemas/member-identity.schema.json.title: Arkret Member Identity
schemas/member-identity.schema.json.description: Realm-scoped, actor-scoped full member_identity segment. It is carried by ak.member.identity.update in plaintext or inside encrypted-envelope.schema.json. Replacement events that name segment=member_identity MUST carry this complete object. This object discloses subject_actor_id and display_profile for Realm UI projection; handle lifecycle is intentionally excluded and is governed only by ak.schema.handle_claim.v1 issuer claims. Mention / reply / quote / actor attribution MUST use the exact ActorId, never a handle string or a bare principal DID.

actor_id.description: Effective member actor did_core_id in this Realm. MAY represent a Realm-scoped pairwise identity.

subject_actor_id.description: Exact durable subject represented by a Realm-scoped or pairwise actor. Account and hosted-principal subjects retain their station component; authorization and audit continue to use the Event actor and member state.

payload_digest.description: sha256 over RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of this MemberIdentity object with the top-level proof field excluded. The signature MUST cover the same canonical bytes.

schemas/message.schema.json.title: Arkret Message

anyOf.$comment: forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content
forbidden track key; canonical name is track_name
forbidden Message extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata

id.description: For ak.message.create, the reducer derives this value by retyping the creating Event.event_id's full 33-byte / 44-character token from ak:event: to ak:message:. It is not independently producer-chosen.

track_name.description: Strand track key for this Message. v1 Message objects are restricted to the Strand discussion track. Profiles that need another timeline kind MUST register a separate object/event profile instead of overloading Message.track_name.

effective_scope.description: Read-only immutable effective scope of this Message, materialized from the accepted Event.scope_ref after the receiver verifies it against the Strand's frozen pre-state (models/circle.md §6.1-§6.2). kind='realm' for Realm-default scope; kind='circle' when the Message's Strand was Circle-scoped at write time. A later Strand scope rebind MUST NOT reinterpret already-written Messages. This field MUST NOT appear in actor-supplied content payload (reason=effective_scope_reducer_managed).

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Message ContentBlock.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a message_metadata object.

state.description: Top-level lifecycle state for messages. Messages do not have a separate deleted/tombstone state; retention or moderation removal uses ak.message.redact and state=redacted so the message slot and audit metadata remain stable.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.message.redact Event. Aligns with the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

revision_root_id.description: First revision in this message's edit chain. The first revision MUST have revision_root == id. Maintained by ak.message.revise reducer.

redaction_ref.description: Required when state=redacted; references the accepted ak.message.redact Event id that produced this state. A cross-object ak.redaction can never be the source: its payload class excludes Message targets, so this reference is single-valued and unambiguous (models/common-fields.md 5.1 Message exemption). MUST be absent for other states.

updated_by.description: Reducer-derived actor that produced the most recent materialized message update, such as ak.message.revise or ak.message.redact.

mentions.description: Structured direct mention AST nodes for this Content Block. This is the only carrier of a direct mention: authorization, notification routing and audit attribution read mention_node.subject_id exclusively (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.1-§9.4.2).

audience_mentions.description: Structured broadcast mention AST nodes for this Content Block (zh/models/strand-and-message.md §9.4.3).

attachments.description: Profile-defined attachment hints. At most 32; canonical durable attachment relations SHOULD use Relation attached_to.

not.$comment: Mirror of event-payload.schema.json $defs.content_block: reject discriminator field `type` (canonical: `kind`), composite child array name `blocks` (canonical: `parts`), and byte-count field `size` (canonical: `size_bytes`). Keeps materialized Message and Event payload schemas in lockstep so that the materialized Message.content cannot smuggle through wire-forbidden field names.

anyOf.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

message_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Message metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

sidecar_exchange_binding.description: Agent Sidecar exchange binding. Legal only inside encrypted_metadata plaintext of an event whose signed scope_ref.kind is sidecar; forbidden in plaintext metadata and shared Realm/Circle events.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Message metadata fields. Reducer-owned lifecycle and revision fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

schemas/message.schema.json.$comment: Top-level uses unevaluatedProperties (not additionalProperties) because the top-level oneOf branches contribute evaluated properties; additionalProperties at the top level would not see those and could wrongly reject legitimate oneOf-branch fields (JSON Schema additionalProperties/oneOf pitfall).

schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.title: Arkret MIMI Interoperability
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.description: Provider directory, room binding, and content mapping receipt objects for ak.profile.mimi_interop.v1.
schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json.$comment: Intentionally relaxed interop-extension surface: this profile tracks evolving IETF MIMI Internet-Drafts (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §1), so additionalProperties is left open at the top level and on the mimi/binding_scope/payload subtrees to forward-carry draft fields without a breaking schema bump. Known fields are pinned; unknown draft fields are tolerated rather than rejected. The provider_directory security core (schema, service_id, proof) and the complete capability declaration are required, and proof is the shared closed detached-JWS shape, so the openness is limited to extension subtrees and cannot mask a missing or unverifiable signature. Unknown fields anywhere on this surface are security-inert (see zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §9.2): receivers MUST ignore them for all security decisions and MUST NOT let them affect authorization, identity binding, policy_root, MLS epoch/group state, routing, or any signature/digest transcript.

mimi_room_uri.description: Canonical MIMI room URI. It is the ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1 cell subject source, so it is a closed canonical form rather than a free URI: lowercase mimi:// scheme, host[:port] authority with no userinfo, lowercase A-label host, no leading-zero port, at least one non-empty path segment, no dot or dot-dot segment, no trailing slash, no query, no fragment, uppercase percent escapes, and no percent-encoding of unreserved octets (RFC 3986 section 6.2.2.2). A receiver MUST reject a non-canonical value with schema_violation and MUST NOT normalize it first, because two spellings of one room would otherwise each own a first accepted binding and the revoked terminal state could be bypassed by respelling. Cell subject encoding is the uri subject kind of zh/conformance/encoding.md section 4. The pattern below expresses the structural half of the canonical form; two rules it cannot express portably -- the default port 443 MUST NOT be written explicitly, and a percent escape MUST NOT encode an unreserved octet -- are normative all the same and are closed by ak.vector.encoding.cell_subject_uri.v1 plus the SDK typed validator, which every producer and receiver MUST apply in addition to this pattern. See zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md section 4.

provider_directory.$comment: The Arkret facade's outbound self-declaration (service_kind is a single-role const). The security core (schema discriminator, service_id, proof) and the complete capability declaration are all required so the signed unsigned projection (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1) covers everything a consumer routes or negotiates on. Top-level and mimi-subtree extension openness is retained for draft evolution, but unknown fields MUST NOT change endpoint derivation, capability negotiation, authorization, routing or signature verification, and never enter the v1 transcript.

supported_profiles.description: Sorted unique by UTF-8 byte order; the sorted array is what enters the signed projection.

endpoints.description: Sorted by endpoint_id; endpoint_id unique across rows. Effective URLs derive only via a standard URL parser under the verified HTTPS base_url with same-origin re-check and the section 3 SSRF policy (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1).

mls_cipher_suites.description: Generated from active canonical_id rows in mls-ciphersuite-registry.json.

proof.description: Detached JWS by a verification method whose bare controller did validates under the registered method adapter and projects exactly to service_id (did_core_id), over the canonical unsigned projection (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1). The projection's first member is the registered object-family context ak.mimi_provider_directory_proof.v1 (proof-context-registry.json); a signature made under any other context MUST be rejected even when it verifies cryptographically. Direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. payload_digest is the projection digest; the proof object itself never enters the projection. A digest or dev placeholder is not a signature.

endpoint_id.description: The feature this endpoint serves; the id set is the same closed feature enum, and each endpoint_id appears at most once.

relative_path.description: Normalized relative path: begins with '/', no scheme, authority, query, fragment, whitespace or backslash. Receivers MUST additionally reject '.' / '..' dot segments and percent-encoded '/', '\', '.' or '..' after decoding (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 3.1).

room_binding.description: MIMI room binding effect payload. In CBA/Lattice state, the cell subject is payload.mimi_room_uri for ak.component.mimi.room_binding.v1.

status.description: Room binding lifecycle status. Initial status MUST be proposed or accepted; legal transitions are proposed->accepted, proposed->revoked, accepted->migrating, accepted->revoked, migrating->accepted (verified migration proof), migrating->revoked. revoked is the only terminal state; illegal transitions are rejected with mimi_room_binding_status_transition_invalid. Normative state machine: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

migration_outcome.description: Outcome of a migrating->accepted transition: completed (new topology in effect) or rolled_back (original topology restored). MUST be present on a migrating->accepted Control Move so the result is auditable; MUST be absent on other transitions. Normative: zh/extensions/mimi-interop.md §4.2.

receipt_kind.description: Interop-audit object discriminator. This object is not an Event Envelope and this value is not an event kind.

schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.title: Arkret MIMI Operation DTOs
schemas/mimi-operations.schema.json.description: Closed request/response DTOs for MIMI provider interop operation bindings.

proof.$comment: Wire shape only. Every request/outcome family that carries actor proofs declares its own proofs array inline so that each object family owns a distinct detached-proof node with its own registered context (mimi-interop.md section 5.1); a single shared proofs alias would put unrelated MIMI operations under one domain separation.

verification_method.description: DID URL of a verification method authorized by the issuer's current DID Document (extensions/mimi-interop.md section 5.1).

kind.description: Semantic update kind and durable-effect discriminator. It MUST equal the kind inside the decoded opaque payload. ak.mimi.room_binding selects the caller-authored Event branch; every other value selects the receipt-only branch.

room_binding_event.description: Complete caller-authored and caller-signed ak.mimi.room_binding initial submission. It is required exactly when /update/kind is ak.mimi.room_binding. The facade MUST first verify that the decoded opaque payload carries the same semantic kind, then bind the Event's exact payload to the path room, target Realm and Strand, MLS group, and authenticated MIMI operation and submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission. It MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign the Event. Every other receipt-only branch MUST omit this field.

mimi_update_consent_request_body.description: Carries the caller-authored, caller-signed Arkret consent Control Move. The facade verifies the detached MIMI operation signature over the complete unsigned body, then submits consent_event unchanged through ordinary Event admission. decision=accept requires ak.consent.grant; decision=deny or revoke requires ak.consent.revoke. The facade MUST NOT synthesize, rebuild or co-sign the Event.

consent_event.description: Exact EventInitialSubmission whose event.actor_id, actor_id, authenticated holder, and private-correlation holder are the same current Principal Control Realm authority-root controller, and whose payload.consent_id equals consent_id. authorization_ref MUST bind that authority root. A grant payload peer/scope, or the active cell and observed dots resolved by a revoke payload, MUST match the correlation. The root_control_only consent action supports neither separate managed-behalf execution nor consent_write delegation to a controller/agent; general PCR/co-owner grants or payload approval evidence do not substitute.

schemas/mls-governance-proof-bundle.sche.title: Arkret MLS Governance Read
schemas/mls-governance-proof-bundle.sche.description: Near-current stateless group_security_frontier query and outcome only. Bulk/history recovery replays the retained accepted Seal cut through standard Event/Seal resolve and is not a proof profile. complete_control_state_v1, epoch-range activation proofs, opaque nodes, full-object embedding and shared proof dictionaries are forbidden.

actor_id.description: Full accepted membership ActorId. Same signing principal at different Stations identifies distinct leaves and authorization; never infer Station from a current local session.

proof_request_common.description: The exact RFC 8785 canonical request must not exceed 8 MiB. This aggregate bound includes local_mls_leaves and is enforced after Schema validation and before materialization.

local_mls_leaves.description: Exact occupied public RFC 9420 leaves from the caller's locally verified current or pending group state, in strictly increasing leaf_index order. The service rejects duplicate leaf_index or credential_ref and proves governance state against this every-and-only set; the receiver repeats the comparison against its own group state. This is query input and is never copied into the response.

proof_base_basis.description: Canonical complete verified accepted base antichain. The caller MUST also hold the crash-safe local predecessor joined verification checkpoint for this exact basis; the wire field is not a standalone trust source.

proof_target_basis.description: Canonical complete accepted target antichain. It dominates proof_base_basis: every base leaf is retained or is an ancestor of a target leaf. The service never substitutes a single arbitrary head.

byte_limit.description: Caller-selected canonical response-byte ceiling for one complete near-current frontier selector. The response must fit without truncation or cursor. If the exact base-to-target frontier projection cannot fit, the caller must obtain a closer independently verified basis or fail closed; it cannot split cells or accept a partial frontier.

base_group_state_ref.description: Required only for a successor transition and byte-identical to the already accepted winning Genesis/Commit Event for previous_epoch. It never names the transition being authored. Genesis (0 -> 0) has no prior MLS group-state Event, so this field is forbidden there; this avoids an EventId/governance-binding authoring cycle.

leaf_canonical_preimage_b64u.description: Unpadded base64url of the exact leaf_data bytes. For state_root this is RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 of {cell,state:{value}}. For control_event_set_root this is the raw digest bytes obtained by decoding the selected Event digest suite prefix.

leaf_digest.description: H(0x00 || decoded leaf_canonical_preimage_b64u) under the digest suite named by root_digest.

merkle_membership_witness.description: Closed RFC 6962 membership witness. The verifier resolves root_seal_ref, requires its signed root_field to equal root_digest, independently reconstructs the domain-specific canonical leaf bytes, requires leaf_index < leaf_count and consumes exactly the audit-path length implied by leaf_count. Siblings are ordered from the leaf level upward.

value_digest.description: Digest of the exact resolved cell value reconstructed from the content-addressed provenance Events; full value bytes are not embedded in the page.

provenance_event_refs.description: Canonical complete FSM/join-chain Event references. Their signed bytes are resolved outside the page and must match proof_material descriptors.

event_ids.description: Canonical every-and-only Event ids named by sparse frontier provenance entries and boundaries. Each id losslessly binds its suite-bearing full digest. This array is not a duplicate catalog of every Seal.delta Event in the base-to-target cut; those exact accepted Event selectors come from each resolved signed Seal.delta and are fetched separately for checkpoint replay.

seal_predecessor_edges.description: Canonical UTF-8 ordering by (seal_ref,predecessor_seal_ref). It contains every and only direct predecessor edge needed to verify the anchor-to-target closure, every activation cause and every predecessor root named by a first-coverage witness.

typed_proof_material.description: Complete every-and-only content-addressed selector set for one near-current stateless group_security_frontier response. seal_descriptors are canonical by seal_ref bytes, event_ids is the direct canonical EventId set, and predecessor edges are canonical by their tuple bytes; duplicates are forbidden. Sparse paths live only in typed witnesses. Full signed proof objects are resolved through standard Event/Seal resolve; each Event's recomputed digest must equal the suite and full digest losslessly encoded by event_id. Complete checkpoint replay additionally resolves the exact Event digest set signed in the resolved Seals' delta arrays; those Events are not duplicated into event_ids unless sparse provenance also names them.

frontier_range_witness.description: Included entries occupy every index in [start,end). Adjacent authenticated boundaries/state edges prove completeness, including an empty prefix.

state_root.description: The exact signed state_root of target_seal_ref. Every entry and boundary witness in this branch MUST use that same target Seal and root.

frontier_branch_projection.description: One independently signed target-branch projection. It never claims that a joined multi-leaf state root was signed by one Seal.

frontier_registry_digest.description: sha256(RFC 8785 JCS bytes of the exact mls-security-frontier-registry.json artifact used for this projection). The verifier compares it with its locally pinned artifact digest; the service cannot select registry semantics.

branches.description: Canonical UTF-8 order by target_seal_ref and every-and-only the query proof_target_basis leaves.

frontier_projection.description: Per-target-leaf signed projections. The verifier validates every branch independently, then uses complete accepted-Seal replay and the generated lattice registry to join the full target antichain before deriving one security_frontier_digest.

query_digest.description: SHA-256(UTF8('ak.mls-governance-proof-query-v1') || 0x00 || JCS(exact request)). The response does not repeat local_mls_leaves; the caller retains the request and requires this digest to match.

group_security_frontier_outcome.description: A deterministic, complete near-current response for the exact query_digest and its caller-retained group-binding selector and canonical base/target antichains. Bulk history authorization and activation are reconstructed by direct accepted-Seal traversal and are not fields or profiles of this response.

schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.title: Arkret Moderation Appeal
schemas/moderation-appeal.schema.json.description: Payload shapes for the four ak.moderation.appeal.* event kinds (submit / review / decision / close) that close the moderation appeal loop. Each kind writes the ak.component.moderation.appeal.v1 cell on a deterministic state machine: (none) → submitted → under_review → decided → closed; close from submitted/under_review is allowed only for appellant withdrawal (closer == appellant and close_reason=appellant_withdrawn). The decided state additionally records the decision (uphold / overturn / modify); overturn MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event referencing the original decision. Modify MUST atomically lift the original decision and add the replacement decision named by modify_decision_ref. Lifting a decision does not resurrect an irreversible redaction tombstone or destroyed content key. All payloads carry realm_id and reducers MUST require it to equal the enclosing Event.realm_id and the appealed decision's Realm. See zh/governance/content-moderation.md §5.5 (appeal strand). Capability: ak.moderation.appeal.submit (any member, low risk) for submit; ak.moderation.appeal.review (moderator) for review/decision/manual reviewer close after decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant.

decision_ref.description: Reference to the ak.moderation.decision event being appealed.

target_ref.description: The original moderation target (message, strand, member, blob, etc.) — same typed-id form as the appealed decision's target.

evidence_visibility.description: Who may decrypt / read the appeal evidence narrative. Default per Realm policy; SHOULD be reviewers_only for sensitive disputes. The visibility tag MUST enter projection / redaction decisions; it does NOT change wire encryption of the envelope, only the plaintext audience for evidence fields.

submit_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.submit — opens the appeal. Writes appeal cell (state=submitted). MUST be issued by an appellant who is the original moderation target's controller (member appealing their own ban / message removal) or by an authorized advocate listed in Realm policy. A Realm member appellant is admitted by baseline membership; a non-member advocate MUST be authorized by Realm policy / ak.moderation.appeal.submit capability.

appellant_id.description: Actor lodging the appeal. MUST be the original moderation target's controller or an authorized advocate.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference (typically blob_ref or in-line short string) to the appeal narrative / supporting argument. For E2EE Realms this is an encrypted reference.

evidence_refs.description: Optional supporting evidence (blob refs, prior message ids, witness DIDs).

review_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.review — reviewer takes the appeal under review. Transitions cell state submitted → under_review. Reviewer MUST hold ak.moderation.appeal.review capability; the same actor MUST NOT review their own moderation decision (separation of duties enforced by reducer).

decision_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.decision — reviewer's decision. Transitions cell state under_review → decided. Verdict semantics: uphold = original decision stands, no further action; overturn = original decision is lifted for future governance evaluation, this event MUST be paired in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction with a ak.moderation.decision.lift event whose target equals decision_ref (reducer rejects with appeal_overturn_missing_lift otherwise), and irreversible redaction/key-destruction effects are not resurrected; modify = original decision is atomically replaced, requiring both a same-batch lift of decision_ref and a new ak.moderation.decision whose event id is modify_decision_ref.

reason_text_ref.description: Reference to the decision rationale. MUST be present for audit trail; visibility follows evidence_visibility on the submit event.

modify_decision_ref.description: Required iff decision=modify. Points to the replacement ak.moderation.decision event in the same ordered submit batch or equivalent control transaction; that transaction MUST also contain a ak.moderation.decision.lift for the original appealed decision.

close_payload.description: ak.moderation.appeal.close — closes the appeal from decided, or from submitted/under_review only for appellant withdrawal. Reviewer close and a deployment's authorized close service use the review capability after the appeal is decided; appellant withdrawal is authorized by closer == appellant plus close_reason=appellant_withdrawn while state is submitted or under_review. close is a manual/authorized action: the protocol does not mandate any auto-close timer, timeout duration, or cool-off duration — deployment/Realm policy decides those. Idempotency only: the same (decision_ref, appellant) pair MUST NOT have two non-closed appeals concurrently; a fresh appeal_id is allowed once the prior appeal cell is closed.

closer_id.description: Actor or service closing the appeal (reviewer, appellant, or a deployment's authorized close service). Reducer authorizes the close via the normal capability gate (or closer == appellant for withdrawal); the protocol does not mandate any timer service DID or timeout window.

auto_closed.description: Informational marker: true iff the close was emitted by a deployment's automated close service rather than a human actor. The protocol attaches no special timer/window enforcement to this flag; deployment policy defines when (if ever) automated close fires.

close_reason.description: Machine-readable close cause. appellant_withdrawn is valid only when closer is the appellant and the appeal is still submitted or under_review; timer_expired is an optional label for a deployment's automated close (auto_closed=true) and carries no protocol-mandated timeout semantics.

schemas/moderation-evidence.schema.json.title: Arkret Moderation Evidence Objects
schemas/moderation-evidence.schema.json.description: Defs-only canonical objects shared by signed moderation reports, MIMI report mapping and durable franking-proof Events. This schema depends only on primitive/common schemas and does not reference an Event or operation request schema.

evidence_package.description: Canonical encrypted moderation evidence-package descriptor. target_refs names exactly the report target at admission; recipient_public_key_ref and encrypted_to MUST be byte-identical and resolve to an authorized moderator key for the report's exact effective scope. reporter_signature covers the descriptor and referenced ciphertext. The encrypted material MUST contain only reporter-visible evidence for target_refs and MUST NOT contain Realm/Circle history keys, MLS epoch/exporter secrets or unrelated plaintext.

franking_proof.description: Canonical receiving-service receipt used both inside a moderation report and as the complete payload of an ak.moderation.franking_proof durable Event. The local signature uses domain ak.franking_proof.signature.v1 and covers every member except signature. event_id names the encrypted Event whose receipt is proven; the enclosing proof Event has its own distinct Event.event_id.

event_id.description: Event ID of the encrypted Event whose receipt is proven; not the enclosing franking-proof Event ID.

verification_method.description: Exact receiving-service verification method used for signature. Its controller MUST project to received_by and the method MUST be authorized at received_at.

replay_nonce.description: Opaque anti-replay nonce generated by the receiving service and covered by the proof signature.

signature.description: Receiving service signature over the canonical franking-proof transcript.

franking_data_event_inclusion_proof.description: RFC 6962 audit path proving the proof Event digest is included in covering_seal.data_event_set_root.

franking_seal_observation_outcome.description: Authorization-gated, independently verifiable observation for one durable franking proof Event. The proof Event payload must equal the requested franking proof bytes and target_event must equal its payload.event_id.

report.description: Immutable payload projection from the accepted ak.self.moderation.report Event; never the service-operation request wrapper.

status.description: Authoritative moderation queue-item lifecycle. v1 is intentionally minimal: 'submitted' = report accepted and awaiting handling; 'resolved' = handling complete (terminal). The disposition (action taken vs no violation) lives on the separate ak.moderation.decision event; the appeal loop lives in the independent ak.moderation.appeal.* subsystem (§5.5). Additional intermediate states MAY be introduced in a later revision if a workflow phase needs them. See governance/content-moderation.md §3.3.

schemas/moderation-report.schema.json.title: Arkret Moderation Report Operation
schemas/moderation-report.schema.json.description: Closed signed-request DTO for ak.self.moderation.command.report.v1. Canonical evidence and franking-proof objects live in moderation-evidence.schema.json so Event payload validation does not depend back on an operation request schema.

moderation_report_event_submission.description: Direct-holder signed ak.self.moderation.report DataEvent. The self endpoint accepts only absent/self provenance and forbids delegated executor, Applet and MIMI-facade provenance. event.actor_id and payload.reporter MUST equal the authenticated session principal. event.realm_id, payload.realm_id, the signed scope_ref and the accepted target's derived governance scope MUST match exactly. A Realm-default report may omit payload.effective_scope; a Circle report MUST sign the exact Circle scope. The target MUST be accepted and visible to the reporter; absent, invisible and scope-mismatched targets all return the same not_found response. This DataEvent carries seal_ref and auth_context and MUST NOT carry seal_basis or preconditions. The service forwards exact signed bytes through ordinary Event admission and never authors, rebuilds, co-signs or adds guards.

moderation_report_request_body.description: Carries exactly one direct-holder signed moderation report Event and no unsigned report projection.

schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.title: Arkret Morph Customer Risk Example
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.description: Reference business-field schema for the morph.md customer_risk example. It constrains the fields object carried by a ak.schema.morph.v1 container.
schemas/morph-customer-risk.schema.json.$comment: Logical schema id is ak.schema.morph.customer_risk.v1 (dotted, used in schema_refs[]); the artifact file name uses hyphens (morph-customer-risk.schema.json). Do not derive the id from the file name.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Morph top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle that defines this Morph's effective scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies scope_circle_id.realm_id == Morph.realm_id and exact equality between the derived scope and Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope.

schema_refs.description: Authoritative structural schema set for Morph fields. Reducers MUST validate fields against exactly these refs; morph_kind and facets are not a replacement for schema_refs. Generic before-to-after transition validation is not provided by JSON Schema.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a morph_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a ContentBlock for Morph content.

state.description: Morph lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.morph.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=morph_not_active); ak.morph.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else morph_not_archived); ak.redaction targeting the morph MUST come from {'active','archived'} (else morph_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.morph.archive / ak.morph.restore / redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Morph business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle). A morph_kind profile MAY require it; generic mirror/data Morphs may omit it. If absent, the first ak.morph.stage.set initializes the axis to any registered value; later changes follow the normal transition rules. ak.morph.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected. Stage transitions do not carry a reason/note; explanations belong in a referenced Message. See models/common-fields.md §5.3.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.morph.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions MUST NOT update this field.

allOf.$comment: Mirror of message.schema.json's state=redacted branch: the content slot (content <-> encrypted_content) MUST be absent once redaction has cleared it, so 'redacted' is verifiable from the object alone instead of only from the event stream (zh/models/common-fields.md §5 redacted row, §5.2; zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.4).

morph_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Morph metadata. Morph business fields stay in the top-level fields object; metadata carries display-oriented fields such as title and summary. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields and Morph business fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

Reject discriminator field `type`, composite child array name `blocks`, and byte-count field `size`; canonical content blocks use `kind`, composite children use `parts`, and byte counts use `size_bytes`.

anyOf.$comment: byte counts use size_bytes

body.description: Inline text body. Authoritative bound is 256 KiB UTF-8 bytes enforced by a byte validator; maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. Longer bodies MUST use ak.content.long_text (zh/models/content-types.md section 4.1.4).

not.$comment: Strand track keys use track_name; track is forbidden.

id.description: Profile-local approval_request_id. It is an opaque_correlation value, so its lexical space is disjoint from the ak: typed-ID namespace: a value MUST NOT begin with ak:.

source_account_artifact.description: Closed account-private artifact source for notifications that are not derived from a durable Realm Event.

source_ref.description: Optional canonical-object reference for clients that want to render the notification target without resolving source_event_id. Reducers MUST treat source_event_id as authoritative; source_ref is a render-only hint.

strand_id.description: Optional Strand context for routing the notification.

track_name.description: Optional Strand track key on the source Strand.

preview.description: Render summary. Under E2EE / redaction / history-limited scopes this MUST be empty or an authorized redacted digest; sender/reducer-enforced. A notification projection MUST NOT widen the plaintext visibility of the source Message. See models/private-objects.md §3.4.

schemas/object-addressing.schema.json.title: Arkret Object Addressing
schemas/object-addressing.schema.json.description: Canonical target descriptors and signed authorization-token claims for object-address links.

address_link_kind.description: Closed URL-resolution classification. Signed authorization tokens use only invite or preview.

basis_ref.description: Authorization basis. Ordinary publication uses an accepted Seal or signed multi-leaf seal_basis. Only a caller-validated registered genesis unit may use the exact anchor_unit digest commitment.

authorization_rule_id.description: Exact authorization_rules[].rule_id selected for this lease. The selected rule MUST allow action and only proofs from that rule may satisfy its threshold.

authority_set_policy.description: Portable concrete policy bytes. authority_set_id MUST equal authority_set_ref.authority_set_id and SHA-256(JCS(this object)) MUST equal authority_set_ref.authority_set_digest. Verifiers MUST additionally rederive this policy from basis_ref and the submitted CBA closure.

lease_basis_ref.description: Accepted control-state basis shared by authorization leases and other basis-committed records. Ordinary publication uses an accepted Seal or signed multi-leaf seal_basis; only a caller-validated registered genesis unit may use the exact anchor_unit digest commitment.

ingress_receipt.description: Closed six-field multi-proof evidence that a policy-qualified ingress received one exact Event under the exact companion AuthorizationLease before expiry. Lease identity, basis, DID and authority-set policy are verified from that companion object rather than copied into this receipt. It proves timely ingress only, never reducer acceptance or finality.

qualified_ingress_did.description: Version-qualified DID of the ingress service at receipt issuance; its stable service id is projected when the receipt is verified with the exact companion lease.

ingress_frontier.description: Non-empty strictly lexicographically ordered causal frontier used for the four-way offline-ingress decision.

authority_set_ref.description: Immutable reference to the CBA authority-set policy resolved at basis_ref. authority_set_digest binds the canonical policy bytes so a mutable registry lookup cannot change quorum, delegation, or revocation semantics.

authority_set_policy.description: Canonical concrete policy. authority_set_digest is SHA-256(JCS(the complete object)).

schemas/patch.schema.json.title: Arkret Field Patch (ak.schema.patch.v1)
schemas/patch.schema.json.description: Canonical field-patch format embedded in event payloads (typically at payload.patch) for non-create updates. Its only protocol identifier is ak.schema.patch.v1. Grammar, parser responsibilities, redactable content-slot protection and reducer-managed-field protection are defined normatively in zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4; the machine-readable path set an $op="unset" MUST NOT remove is registry/redactable-field-registry.json, which this schema deliberately does not restate.

propertyNames.$comment: Canonical machine projection of zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.1. A path contains 1..16 dot-separated snake_case identifier segments, each 1..64 ASCII characters. Selector segments, quoted identifiers and numeric array indexes are not part of v1 and MUST be rejected with reason_code patch_path_invalid.
