organization_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the external Organization to be registered. Resolvability alone confers nothing; this request only opens a proof window.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID submitted for first registration. The registry MUST independently resolve and validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes will be delegated to. It is fixed at challenge time and signed over by the control proof, because a proof that binds only the organization and the version says nothing about who benefits from it: anyone who obtained such a proof could submit ensure naming themselves and receive the organization's administrative scopes. ensure MUST reject a request whose local_admin_subject differs from the one in the referenced challenge.

OrganizationRegistrationEnsureRequestBod.description: Register an external Organization identity with this deployment by submitting both its stable organization_id core and current published organization_did. Idempotent on organization_id: replaying the same registration returns the existing binding with created=false. This operation registers a reference and a local administrative binding; it does not host the DID's method history, does not make this deployment its controller, and does not create Realm state.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID whose method history and control proof are pinned by this request. MUST equal the organization_did bound into the referenced challenge and project to organization_id.

version_id.description: The exact resolved DID version the control proof was made against. Pinning the version is what makes the receipt auditable later: without it, a receipt asserts control at an unknown point in the DID's history.

local_admin_subject_id.description: The local principal the requested scopes are delegated to. MUST equal the value bound into the referenced challenge and signed over by control_proof; a mismatch means the proof was made for a different beneficiary and MUST be rejected with organization_registration_challenge_invalid.

requested_scopes.description: MUST be identical to the set carried by the referenced challenge; a mismatch means the proof was made for different authority than is being claimed.

handle_attestation.description: Optional supporting attestation only. An organization handle or domain claim may improve discovery and display, but MUST NOT substitute for DID control or quorum proof: whoever operates a domain is not thereby the controller of the organization's DID. Named attestation rather than evidence because it carries exactly one material family (common-fields.md R6).

subject_id.description: Stable organization did_core_id the handle is claimed for. MUST equal organization_id; the attestation proof's DID URL is independently projected to its issuer did_core_id.

status.description: The issuer's assertion at signing time. It is a floor, not a guarantee: a receiver MUST still consult the issuer's current revocation state before relying on the handle for display, because a self-asserted active is exactly what a revoked attestation would also carry.

OrganizationRegistrationOutcome.description: Result of every organization registration command and of the read surface. Identity, DID, generation and version are read from the signed registration_receipt. created is true exactly on a call that opened a new generation.

created.description: True exactly when this call opened a new generation: the first registration, a re-registration after revoke, or an ensure that changed local_admin_subject or the scope set. False for a byte-identical ensure retry that matches the consumed challenge's canonical_request_digest and stored outcome, and for every read, refresh and revoke. Reusing the challenge with a different digest is an error, not created=false.

OrganizationRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed record that this deployment accepted an external Organization DID binding. receipt_claims is exactly the object formed by removing registration_receipt_id and proof from the receipt; registration_receipt_id is ak:organization_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt_claims))>. proof.payload_digest hashes the complete receipt after registration_receipt_id is inserted and proof is removed, so neither digest is self-referential. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object. The receipt proves acceptance of one generation of one local binding and nothing else: it is not a Realm capability, not membership, not a notary designation, and not a service delegation.

registration_receipt_id.description: ak:organization_registration_receipt: plus lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt with registration_receipt_id and proof both omitted)).

organization_did.description: Published Organization DID whose pinned version and control proof were accepted for this receipt. Consumers MUST independently validate it and require project(organization_did)=organization_id.

registration_generation.description: Monotonic generation of the binding for this stable organization did_core_id, starting at 1. A same-core did refresh does not create a different organization identity; terminal registration states remain per generation.

control_proof_kind.description: Mirrors OrganizationControlProof.proof_kind so a later auditor can tell which commitment control_key_digest is over without re-fetching the original request.

control_key_digest.description: Under resolved_verification_method, the digest of the active control/update public key at version_id. Under governance_quorum, the digest of the canonical governance key set head that satisfied the threshold. It is never a next-key commitment and never private material.

status.description: Closed lifecycle. active: control evidence is current. stale: the pinned version no longer reflects current control (controller rotation) or the evidence has aged out; low-risk reads may continue but high-risk paths MUST fail closed until a successful refresh. revoked: terminal for this generation, whether withdrawn locally, atomically superseded by a new generation, or forced by deactivation of the external DID. A signed historical receipt can retain status=active as an immutable audit artifact, but it authorizes only while its generation is the registry current generation and that registry state is active.

expires_at.description: After this instant the binding MUST be treated as stale regardless of stored status. A receipt without a bounded life would let a single first-time proof authorise an organization relationship indefinitely.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.organization_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, issuer_id, registration_receipt_id, organization_id, organization_did, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers validate the registered organization's organization_did and project it to organization_id, then independently obtain the issuer service's verified resolution, require its service_did to project to issuer_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod.

OrganizationRegistrationRefreshRequestBo.description: Re-prove control at a newer resolved version and re-issue the receipt. Scopes are not re-negotiated here; a scope change is a new ensure. Refresh exists because a binding pinned to one version stops proving current control the moment the organization rotates its controller.

organization_did.description: Current published Organization DID at the refreshed version. MUST project to organization_id before the refreshed proof is accepted.

OrganizationRegistrationRevokeRequestBod.description: Withdraw the local binding. This is a local act with local effect only: it does not modify, deactivate or annotate the external DID's method history, which this deployment does not control.

reason_code.description: Closed reason set. superseded: replaced by a new binding for the same organization. withdrawn: the deployment or the organization ended the relationship.

OrganizationRegistrationScope.description: Closed set of local administrative scopes a registration may delegate. organization_profile_manage covers this deployment's local organization profile and display; organization_realm_endorse permits issuing ak.realm.organization statements on the organization's behalf; organization_service_delegate permits declaring organization-to-service delegations locally. The set is closed because an open scope vocabulary would let a deployment mint authority the organization never consented to. Holding a scope is a permission to act later, not an action: registration by itself creates no Realm, membership, notary, capability or service delegation.

actor_id.description: Optional actor scope for policy-check authorization, policy, and membership roots. Generic federation probes omit it.

PeerEventsResolveOutcome.description: Read-only federation Event dependency response. Every Event selector is fully accounted for by a matching Event or same-type missing bucket. Event proof signer evidence is resolved through the typed governance-dependency surface; Control-Move effectiveness is checked through the separate Seal frontier/resolve closure. This response never duplicates CBA proof bundles or covering/first-activation Seal evidence.

PeerEventsResolveRequestBody.description: Read-only federation Event dependency resolution request. At least one of event_ids or event_digests must be non-empty. Standalone Seal selectors belong only to ak.peer.seals.read.resolve.v1. All selectors are scoped to exactly one Realm and canonical-bytewise sorted/duplicate-free.

max_response_bytes.description: Caller response budget. The responder MUST also enforce its advertised max_body_bytes and the 8 MiB Kernel ceiling, using the smallest of the three.

history_traversal_access.description: Optional narrow direct-traversal access. event_ids/event_digests may select only Control Moves or registered apply_seal dependencies in the exact retained target-to-base cut; Seal refs remain on ak.peer.seals.read.resolve.v1. The authenticated peer and retained request/archive-replica basis are checked before lookup.

ProjectionAssignedToRelation.description: Read-model edge backing a Strand assigned_to Relation. relation_id is needed by clients to tombstone the assignment; actor_id mirrors the Relation to_ref.

kind.description: Space kind such as `board`, `list`, `folder`, or a profile-registered kind.

title.description: Derived display title from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.title; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

summary.description: Derived display summary from plaintext-visible Strand metadata.summary; null when metadata is encrypted or hidden from the service profile.

board_space_id.description: Derived board Space id from ak.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

list_space_id.description: Derived list Space id from ak.component.strand.position.v1; not canonical Strand object state.

rank.description: Derived rank within list_space_id from ak.component.strand.position.v1.

assigned_actor_ids.description: Derived current full ActorIds from visible active Relation(relation_kind=assigned_to, from_ref=strand_id), preserving Station identity. Empty or absent means the Strand is unassigned for this projection caller. This is read-model state, not canonical Strand object metadata.

assigned_to_relations.description: Read-only active assigned_to Relation edges backing assigned_actor_ids. Clients use relation_id to tombstone assignments.

is_default.description: DERIVED, not independent storage: true iff strand_id == the parent Realm projection's default_strand_id (the authoritative pointer written by ak.realm.set_default_strand). The projector computes this from Realm.default_strand_id; a stale/dangling pointer never resolves to is_default=true because the reducer rejects set_default_strand against a non-existent Strand. Clients identify the Realm's default discussion Strand deterministically from this flag (or equivalently from Realm.default_strand_id) and MUST NOT infer the default from any Strand-reuses-Realm-token or other implementation detail. See zh/models/strand-and-message.md (default-Strand discovery).

RealmActorFrontierView.description: Deterministic authoring frontier for exactly one (realm_id, actor_id) chain. frontier_event_ids is the complete sorted sibling set at next_actor_seq - 1.

frontier_event_ids.description: Bytewise UTF-8 sorted, duplicate-free complete accepted sibling set at the highest actor sequence.

RealmSealFrontierView.description: The serving service's verified durable current accepted Realm Seal frontier used for seal_basis and seal_ref authoring. current is this observation coordinate, not a claim about global wall-clock latest state. open_set returns the complete canonical non-quarantined leaf antichain; single_signer and threshold return exactly one leaf. Consumers resolve and verify every Seal and recompute the joined control view; no service-derived root hint is an authority.

seal_basis.description: Canonical bytewise-sorted, duplicate-free complete accepted Seal leaf antichain. This exact object can be copied into a newly authored Control Move only after resolving and verifying every leaf.

governance_health.description: Readiness projection derived only from verified Control Proposal Acks/decisions and accepted Seals. It is not a second control-plane truth source.

payload_digest.description: Optional digest commitment to the canonical payload object before masking.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional proof that the suite-bearing digest decoded from event_id is included in an Event set / Seal / range-completeness root visible to the caller.

reducer_input.description: Redacted views are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

event_id.description: Present only when the source event id is already visible to the caller; omitted when even the event id would distinguish target existence.

realm_id.description: The source Realm boundary visible to the caller. Target Realm identifiers hidden by reference-disclosure policy MUST NOT appear.

event_digest.description: Optional source-event commitment when the source event is known but its payload is locked.

reason_code.description: Reasons that would reveal target existence MUST be collapsed to not_found_or_unauthorized for unauthorized callers.

inclusion_proof.description: Optional non-disclosing proof commitment. MUST NOT contain hidden target refs or target Realm metadata.

reducer_input.description: Locked stubs are projection-only evidence and MUST NOT be fed into a reducer as Event Envelope input.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C DID Core 1.0, DID document core properties
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A raw DID document is emitted and resolved verbatim, so its property names belong to the DID Core lexicon; identity-did.md forbids re-spelling them as snake_case.
A DID document service entry keeps the DID Core lexicon for every member it declares, including the Arkret-defined serviceKind extension property that sits beside serviceEndpoint.
A verification method is resolved and verified verbatim from the DID document, so publicKeyMultibase keeps the DID Core spelling.

did.description: Complete service DID. It MUST equal inception_operation.state.id and the adapter projection MUST equal the resulting service_id.

idempotency_key.description: Bounded opaque caller-chosen correlation string used only to relate audit records for one ensure attempt. It is deliberately outside the ak: typed-ID namespace and MUST NOT be parsed by the typed-ID parser or treated as an object identity. Registration identity is the canonical (service_kind, public_base_url) key that Provider persistence enforces with UNIQUE(service_kind, public_base_url), and the single idempotency authority for this operation is the operation registry's idempotency_mechanism=object_id; this field never establishes a second one.

public_base_url.description: Canonical service base URL: lower-case scheme and host, no query or fragment, normalized path, and exactly one trailing slash. Production deployments MUST use https; explicit development deployments MAY use http.

ServiceRegistrationReceipt.description: Provider-signed stable service-registration receipt. registration_receipt_id is ak:service_registration_receipt:<lowercase hex SHA-256(canonical_json(receipt claims))>. service_id is the projected did_core_id and did is the verified DID. proof is a detached JWS over the ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1 binding object; consumers verify the provider through its own resolution evidence.

control_key_digest.description: Digest of the active control/update public key at version_id; this is not the next-key commitment or private recovery material.

proof.description: payload_digest = sha256(canonical_json(receipt with proof omitted)). detached_jws signs canonical_json({context:'ak.service_registration_receipt_proof.v1', payload_digest, provider_id, registration_receipt_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}); created_at MUST equal issued_at. Consumers resolve the provider did, require project(did)=provider_id, and verify verification_method as a signing-time assertionMethod of that did.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: W3C Verifiable Credential Data Integrity 1.0, proofs
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The proof is verified byte-for-byte against the external DID log, so every member keeps the Data Integrity spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, the DID log file
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: A DID log entry must round-trip byte-for-byte with the external log, so versionId and versionTime keep the did:webvh spelling.

x-arkret-external-literal-object.specification: did:webvh v1.0, did:webvh DID method parameters
x-arkret-external-literal-object.reason: The parameters object is hashed and verified as part of the external DID log entry, so scid, method, updateKeys and nextKeyHashes are mirrored verbatim.

updateKeys.description: Exactly one active service-controlled update key. On a rotation entry it MUST open the previous entry's sole nextKeyHashes commitment; spent keys MUST NOT be reused.

nextKeyHashes.description: Exactly one sha2-256 multihash/Base58BTC commitment to a next update key generated and durably held by the service. Missing or mismatched commitments fail closed as service_prerotation_invalid.

SessionGrantCredentialClass.description: Closed credential class. recovery_session is a <=15 minute, non-refreshable, DPoP-bound candidate-device grant restricted to the exact recovery operation set; recovery completion issues a distinct standard grant.

SessionGrantDeviceBinding.description: Authorization state committed into a standard device grant. An Account Authority MUST populate it verbatim from the allow receipt of ak.peer.device_revocations.command.check.v1, which is the only source of the origin-derived authorization Event and generation; it MUST NOT be taken from client input, a local cache or a private lookup. Stations compare it with the current active device generation on admission.

model_generation_ref.description: PCR-local monotonic generation. It MUST NOT equal or be derived from a DID versionId.

proof_jwt.description: RFC 9449 DPoP proof JWT over the session-grant issuance endpoint. For agent_key_proof issuance this proves possession of the holder key before the Account Authority returns the session grant.

SessionGrantIntrospectGrant.description: Non-secret grant metadata returned to the validating Station. Never includes the grant JWT, refresh token, or session private key.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service this grant is valid for.

session_public_key.description: Session signing key (JWK) for RFC 9421 PoP verification on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.2). Server-to-server only.

cnf_jkt.description: RFC 7638 JWK SHA-256 thumbprint of the holder (DPoP) key the grant is bound to (cnf.jkt); the Station uses it to verify the per-request DPoP proof on /_arkret/self/* (api-conventions §3.3). Server-to-server only.

holder_binding.description: Required closed accepted human-device, recovery candidate-device, or Agent-runtime holder binding.

device_binding.description: Exact origin-derived device authorization preimage taken from the revocation gate's allow receipt. Required only for standard human_device grants and forbidden for recovery candidate-device and Agent grants.

active.description: Whether the grant is currently valid for the requested audience. READ-ONLY: introspection never consumes the grant.

proof_required.description: Whether an additional S2S holder proof is required to confirm the grant active for this introspection request. Default Station grant+DPoP validation uses the request DPoP instead of this field.

one_time_use_consumed.description: Always false: introspection is read-only and never consumes single-use state (rotation is the refresh endpoint's job).

SessionGrantIntrospectRequestBody.description: Server-to-server session-grant introspection request. Exactly one of id / grant_jwt identifies the grant.

id.description: Grant id. Mutually exclusive with grant_jwt.

grant_jwt.description: The signed grant JWT to introspect. Mutually exclusive with id.

audience_id.description: Stable service did_core_id the caller is validating the grant for; a mismatch yields status audience_mismatch.

proof.description: Optional S2S holder confirmation signed by the session key bound into the grant. Stations validating /_arkret/self/* grant+DPoP requests do not require a client-carried introspection proof; they verify the request DPoP locally against the returned cnf_jkt.

proof_jwt.description: JWS over ak.session_grant.introspection_proof.v1 claims (session_grant_id, grant_jwt_digest, audience, challenge, issued_at, expires_at).

account_id.description: Exact protocol account bound to this grant. Both components are signed; clients and resource services MUST NOT reconstruct either component from local state.

session_grant.description: Short-lived bearer/session grant bound to the requested principal, device and audience.

session_grant_id.description: Stable id of the issued session grant. Returned for every grant (human and agent) so the client can reference, refresh, introspect or revoke this exact grant without re-parsing the opaque session_grant. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.session_grant_id.

session_public_key.description: JWK of the holder/session key the grant is bound to (the device holder key). The client needs this to perform RFC 9421 PoP and to derive the DPoP cnf.jkt for /_arkret/self/* requests (api-conventions.md §3.2 / §3.3); returning it at issue time avoids a mandatory introspect round-trip before the first self-path request. Equals the grant's bound session_public_key for both human and agent grants. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.session_public_key.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the Station or resource service the grant is valid for. MUST equal the grant's bound audience. Mirrors SessionGrantRefreshOutcome.audience.

scope_details.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Materialized narrow scope
actually granted to the agent runtime session. Service-surface scope is the
intersection of immutable provision requested_scope, accepted agent_key_scope,
session requested_scope and endpoint/resource policy; content actions are
additionally constrained by independent effective Realm capability grants,
participation, membership, history visibility and E2EE policy. Provision
mandatory constraints remain in force. Present iff the request was the
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"` branch; absent for human session grants.

participation_entries.description: `ak.profile.agent_participation_policy.v1` overlay (service-surface.md §10.1). Present when the agent session scope covers participation-aware scope. Each entry is isomorphic to agent_participation_entry ({target_scope, selection, version, next_replace_input:{expected_version}}), with next_replace_input.expected_version equal to version. The runtime uses it to avoid disabled actions; the target still evaluates current policy, capability and lifecycle at action time and does not trust a copied ceiling/effective value.

account_id.description: Exact AccountId inherited unchanged from the predecessor grant.

grant_jwt.description: Rotated grant: same subject/scope/audience, cnf.jkt unchanged, fresh minutes-to-hours expiry.

session_public_key.description: JWK the rotated grant is bound to (the device holder key).

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service; unchanged from the predecessor grant.

dpop_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the holder key (equals the grant's cnf.jkt).

previous_session_grant_id.description: The predecessor grant, atomically superseded by this successor on success.

AcceptedDevicePossessionProof.description: Accepted-device Ed25519 possession proof shared by human SessionGrant issue and refresh. The signature covers utf8('ak.session_grant_accepted_device_possession_proof.v1\n') followed by RFC 8785 JCS of this complete object with signature omitted. It is not a server challenge: freshness comes from the <=300 second signed window, the one-time account handoff or predecessor grant, the issuer request identity, and issuer-ledger exact replay. The origin Station MUST verify this proof with the durable current accepted-device key in the same linearization that evaluates current authorization.

account_handoff_grant_digest.description: SHA-256 digest of the exact opaque DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant presented in Authorization; the credential itself MUST NOT enter the proof or logs.

holder_jkt.description: RFC 7638 thumbprint of the DPoP holder key for the handoff or predecessor SessionGrant.

session_intent_digest.description: Digest of the complete canonical immutable issue or refresh intent.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

verification_method.description: DID URL of the accepted device key; its fragment MUST identify device_id and its bare did MUST project to principal_id.

signature.description: 64-byte raw Ed25519 signature encoded as canonical unpadded base64url.

AgentSessionRefreshProof.description: Current Agent runtime-key proof for SessionGrant rotation. It is a distinct branch from accepted human-device PoP and carries no client-generated challenge or polymorphic proof_kind.

expires_at.description: MUST be after issued_at and no more than 300 seconds later.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry human DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

grant_jwt.description: Near-expiry Agent DPoP-bound SessionGrant presented as Authorization: DPoP plus a matching DPoP proof.

audience_id.description: If present, MUST equal the predecessor grant audience.

SessionGrantRefreshRequestBody.description: Closed human-versus-Agent SessionGrant rotation union. Neither branch accepts a client-generated challenge or a generic proof_kind enum.

HumanSessionGrantRequest.description: Returning-human issuance from an already bound account. Authorization is the DPoP-bound account_handoff_grant plus matching per-request DPoP; the body deliberately carries neither a second holder signature nor requested_scope.

RecoverySessionGrantRequest.description: Fresh-device existing-principal recovery issuance. Authorization is the Bound AccountHandoff plus matching per-request DPoP. The Account Authority binds this request to its account/principal mapping and does not consume the handoff on success.

agent_key_authorization_ref.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Event ref of the accepted
`ak.agent.key.authorize` that authorized the runtime key. REQUIRED when
`proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST be omitted for human session grants.

agent_scope_request.description:
`ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. Narrowing hints for the
issued session scope. Service-surface requested_scope values are intersected
with the immutable provision requested_scope, accepted agent_key_scope and
endpoint/resource policy; content actions are additionally intersected with
independent effective Realm capability grants, participation, membership,
history visibility and E2EE policy. Provision mandatory constraints remain in
force at every layer. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; MUST
be omitted for human session grants. `track_names` is a request-side narrowing
field only — the materialized session grant MUST express track scope via the
canonical `allowed_tracks` constraint, not via a new `track_names` grant.

requested_scope_disclosure.description: Optional only for the agent_key_proof branch. A runtime includes this controller-signed private disclosure when the Account Authority does not yet hold verifier-private ceiling evidence established by pairing or an authenticated private evidence transfer. If absent, the authority MUST resolve an already verified disclosure keyed by the same agent_id, DID commitment digest, verifier and audience; a service-local Agent row alone is insufficient.

dpop_binding_proof.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DPoP proof JWT for the holder key that the issued session grant will bind to. REQUIRED when `proof.proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the Account Authority verifies the proof and materializes the resulting JWK thumbprint into the issued grant's `cnf.jkt` / session_public_key binding.

applet_authority.description: Applet-specific delegated session binding. When present, the session grant, proof digest, persistence row, introspection metadata, and revoke selector are bound to the same applet_id, effective_scope, and registration_epoch.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service issuing the challenge and receiving the session request.

verification_method.description: `ak.profile.agent_auth.v1` overlay. DID URL of the runtime signing key. REQUIRED when `proof_kind="agent_key_proof"`; the verifier MUST parse and adapter-validate its canonical bare did component, require project(did)=principal_id, and then validate the referenced key at the accepted method-history position. A did_core_id MUST NOT be used as a DID URL prefix or concatenated with a fragment. Projection mismatch returns `verification_method_principal_mismatch`. MUST be omitted for human proof kinds.

signature.description: Current Agent runtime-key signature over the canonical request transcript.

SessionGrantRequestBody.description: Closed returning-human, fresh-device recovery, or Agent issuance union. OIDC authorization codes are consumed only by account_handoff_request_body and never by this operation.

SignalSubmitOutcome.description: Result of ak.self.signal.command.send.v1. accepted=true means the service admitted the encrypted envelope into the short-lived signal rail. No Event ID, actor_seq, Seal coverage, or durable receipt is minted.

envelope_digest.description: Digest of the admitted complete encrypted envelope, used only for short-lived replay suppression and local correlation.

dispatched_recipient_count.description: Optional implementation hint for fanout recipients queued locally.

SignedSessionGrantClaims.description: Canonical signed claims carried by an ak.session.grant JWT. Except for the fixed kind and derived jti, the closed issuance preimage fields are copied from these claims. credential_class and holder_binding are signed and jointly determine the authorization profile; recovery_session is never refreshable or upgradable and recovery completion issues a distinct standard credential. Verifiers MUST RFC 8785-canonicalize the complete claim-derived preimage, recompute SHA-256, prepend the active sha256 suite wire code, derive ak:session_grant:<44-char-token>, and require byte equality with jti. Changing either binding therefore changes the ID.

issuance_nonce.description: Canonical unpadded Base64URL encoding of the issuer-generated 256-bit issuance nonce. Exact replay reuses the same nonce, issuance preimage, grant ID and JWT.

account_id.description: Exact AccountId bound into this signed grant and its derived session_grant_id.

session_public_key.description: A supported public JWK serialized as its exact RFC 8785 JCS UTF-8 string. Producers MUST parse and canonicalize input before signing; consumers MUST reject strings whose parsed JWK re-serialization is not byte-identical. Private JWK members are forbidden.

audience_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the resource service. HTTP origins are bound separately by DPoP htu and MUST NOT be used as the SessionGrant audience.

SnapshotBootstrap.description: Optional ak.self.events.read.scan.v1 acceleration hint for federation pull / backfill. snapshot_ref is an external pointer and MUST equal the Snapshot manifest id. Verifier MUST validate signature, state_digest, snapshot_frontier, chunk digests, created_by, created_at, and authority_binding before use (manifest fields are bound by the manifest signature transcript — see schemas/snapshot.schema.json).

snapshot_ref.description: External pointer to the Snapshot manifest; MUST equal schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/id.

created_by.description: Stable Arkret identity of the snapshot issuer; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

created_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp ending in 'Z' when the manifest was sealed; bound by the manifest signature transcript.

authority_binding.description: Snapshot issuer authority evidence bound by the manifest signature transcript; mirrors schemas/snapshot.schema.json#/properties/authority_binding.

SessionGrantReplayProblem.description: Closed union of the two replay error-detail shapes. The Problem Details code selects the matching subtype in OpenAPI.

SessionGrantReplayExpiredProblem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_expired. The named issuer-ledger record remains authoritative and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.

SessionGrantReplayTerminalProblem.description: Closed RFC 9457 Problem Details extension members for session_grant_replay_terminal. The state is an exact durable issuer-ledger terminal state and no replacement grant is created under the same request identity.

schemas/signal-envelope.schema.json.title: Arkret Signal Envelope
schemas/signal-envelope.schema.json.description: Encrypted-only broadcast signal envelope. Exact product payload type and target are inside encrypted_payload. This object is never a durable Event and never advances actor_seq, Seal coverage, state_root, or reducer state.

expires_at.description: Semantic validation requires sent_at < expires_at and a class-specific TTL no greater than 120s for setup, 60s for moderation, and 30s for session.

encrypted_payload.description: AEAD ciphertext. The immutable outer header digest is bound into AAD; exact payload kind, product target, and sender sequence exist only in plaintext after recipient decryption. The scheme names the construction, never the algorithm: aead_profile carries the algorithm and MUST equal the active MLS ciphersuite the group at key_ref.group_state_ref actually negotiated (zh/conformance/encoding.md section 10.1). Activating a further ciphersuite therefore reaches Signal with no wire change.

group_state_ref.description: Accepted ak.mls.genesis / winning ak.mls.commit for the scope's MLS group, or an equivalent group state proof hash. It is what fixes which ciphersuite aead_profile must equal.

purpose.description: AEAD purpose for this domain. It is a nonce-derivation and AAD input, so it keeps a Signal nonce from colliding with a content-encryption nonce under the same key and epoch.

aead_profile.description: canonical_id of an active row of artifacts/registry/mls-ciphersuite-registry.json. It MUST equal the ciphersuite the group at key_ref.group_state_ref actually negotiated; a reserved suite, an unregistered suite, or a mismatch MUST fail closed.

signal_proof.description: Detached device proof over canonical_json({context:'ak.signal_proof.v1', envelope_digest, sender_actor_id, sender_device_id, verification_method, created_at, domain?, audience?}). envelope_digest hashes the complete SignalEnvelope with proof removed; created_at MUST equal the outer sent_at.

verification_method.description: The DID URL bare DID component MUST project through its registered adapter to sender_actor_id and its fragment MUST equal sender_device_id; constructing it by appending to did_core_id is forbidden. This mapping is only the completeness condition of the directory lookup key and never stands in for device authorization: the verifier MUST resolve the authoritative verify key for (sender_actor_id, sender_device_id) from its own current accepted device directory, which is a state domain seal_ref does not select (zh/sync/signal.md section 1).

schemas/signal-message-stream.schema.jso.title: Arkret Message Stream Signal Plaintext
schemas/signal-message-stream.schema.jso.description: Closed decrypted plaintext payload profile for transient Message generation previews carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1. It is not a durable Event or Content Block.

payload_sequence.description: Sender-device sequence within the signed Signal scope. It is independent of the per-stream seq and participates in generic Signal replay handling.

message_id.description: Predeclared final Message identity, derived by retyping the complete 33-octet token of the planned ak.message.create Event.event_id.

preview_text.description: Authoritative limit is 16 KiB of valid UTF-8, enforced after decryption by a byte validator. maxLength is a not-wider code-point fast bound. LF, CR and TAB are allowed; other C0 controls and DEL are forbidden.

schemas/signal-presence.schema.json.title: Arkret Presence Signal Plaintext
schemas/signal-presence.schema.json.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.presence, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. Presence is never a durable Event; the exact kind, actor, state and activity time MUST stay inside the ciphertext. Realm scope and sender identity come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here; receivers MUST require actor_id == envelope sender_actor_id. See zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 3.3 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref). Multi-device presence accepts arbitrary forward gaps and only considers signals that advance the device/scope high-water.

actor_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the actor whose presence this is. MUST equal the enclosing envelope sender_actor_id.

state.description: Closed v1 presence state set. Unknown values MUST be dropped or rejected as schema_violation; receivers MUST NOT map them onto an approximate state. Invisibility is not a state value: it is expressed by ak.presence.visibility=nobody.

status_message.description: Optional NFC status text, at most 256 Unicode code points. U+0009 and U+000A are the only permitted control characters; all other C0/C1 controls are rejected. NFC normalization is enforced after decryption by the receiver.

last_active_at.description: Optional and omitted by default. Either an RFC 3339 UTC instant or a Unix-epoch-aligned ISO 8601 <start>/<end> interval bucket. The bucket duration MUST be at least PT60S and MUST match the Realm policy granularity; that bound and the epoch alignment cannot be expressed in JSON Schema and are enforced by the receiver, which MUST fail closed on malformed values.

ttl_ms.description: Plaintext presence lifetime. It MUST NOT widen the outer Signal TTL, whose session-class ceiling is 30 seconds (zh/sync/signal.md section 2); receivers treat the effective lifetime as the minimum of this value and the envelope expires_at.

schemas/signal-relay.schema.json.title: Arkret Signal Peer Relay Request
schemas/signal-relay.schema.json.description: Bounded single-hop peer relay request for encrypted SignalEnvelope values. The request is short-lived, best-effort, non-idempotent, and never creates durable Event, Seal, frontier, receipt, or delivery state.

realm_id.description: The only Realm represented by this request. Every signals[].realm_id and signals[].scope_ref.realm_id MUST equal this value.

signals.description: Original producer-signed encrypted envelopes. The source and destination services MUST NOT alter, re-sign, decrypt, or re-encrypt an item.

signal_relay_outcome.description: Opaque request-level takeover result. accepted=true does not reveal whether the Realm, scope, sender, recipient, binding, or local Signal rail exists, and does not promise delivery.

schemas/signal-stream-frame.schema.json.title: SignalStreamFrame
schemas/signal-stream-frame.schema.json.description: One frame emitted by ak.self.signal.stream.subscribe.v1. Signal data is encrypted-only and ephemeral. Control frames never create a cursor, replay position, delivery receipt, or durable acceptance.

schemas/signal-typing.schema.json.title: Arkret Typing Signal Plaintext
schemas/signal-typing.schema.json.description: Closed decrypted Signal plaintext payload profile for ak.typing, carried only inside ak.schema.signal_envelope.v1 with signal_class=session. The target Strand and the exact kind MUST stay inside the ciphertext and MUST NOT be exposed to Station transport or sync surfaces. Realm scope and sender identity come from the enclosing signed envelope and are not duplicated here. See zh/discovery/profiles-presence.md section 3.5 and zh/sync/signal.md section 1.1.

payload_sequence.description: Strictly increasing but non-contiguous u64 within (sender_device_id, canonical scope_ref). Receivers apply the high-water rule only after proof, scope, Seal/MLS basis, AAD and plaintext validation; arbitrary forward gaps are accepted and repeats or rollback are stale.

strand_id.description: Target Strand. It MUST lie inside the Realm/Circle security scope named by the signed outer scope_ref.

track_name.description: Optional. When present it MUST be discussion; when omitted the receiver resolves it as discussion.

typing.description: True while the sender is composing; senders SHOULD emit at most one update every 3 seconds and MUST send typing=false when composition stops.

ttl_ms.description: Optional plaintext indicator lifetime. It MUST NOT widen the outer Signal TTL, whose session-class ceiling is 30 seconds (zh/sync/signal.md section 2); clients clear the indicator once it expires.

snapshot_witness_attestation.description: One witness statement that the snapshot issuer held snapshot-sealing authority for this exact reduced state at manifest created_at. It is a distinct object family from the manifest itself: the witness signs the canonical SnapshotWitnessAttestation projection of snapshot-schema.md section 5.1 under context ak.snapshot_witness_attestation_proof.v1, which binds the snapshot identity, state, frontier, event-set commitment and authority state but excludes every signature and proof field, so a witness never signs a transcript containing its own or another witness's signature. The manifest-level ak.snapshot_proof.v1 context MUST NOT be reused here.

witness_id.description: Stable did_core_id of the witness. The proof verification_method stays a DID URL whose bare controller did is validated and projected to this value by the registered method adapter; direct DID/core-id string comparison is forbidden. Quorum counting is per witness_id, so several keys of one witness count once.

proof.description: Detached proof whose payload_digest is the SHA-256 typed digest of the JCS canonical SnapshotWitnessAttestation projection (snapshot-schema.md section 5.1). Verifiers MUST recompute the projection from the manifest and this row's witness_id and MUST reject any other transcript.

security_class.description: Snapshot verification class. high_assurance requires verification_hints with inclusion challenge and non-accepted-input digests.

state_digest.description: RFC 6962 domain-separated Merkle root of the canonical reducer-derived state at the snapshot frontier (Lattice cell values keyed by cell_family/cell_subject, plus reducer_profile / schema_profile_refs): leaf=H(0x00||leaf_data), node=H(0x01||left||right), odd tail promoted. This binds *what the state is*. Paired with event_set_commitment which binds *which events produced it*: a verifier replays the events covered by event_set_commitment under reducer_profile and MUST obtain the same state_digest. The two digests are independent and BOTH required — state_digest alone cannot detect missing-event tampering, event_set_commitment alone cannot detect reducer divergence.

frontier.$comment: This is a true frontier (boundary head event ids of the snapshot), not a cumulative covered-set enumeration. Seal coverage is recursive via predecessor_refs + delta.

event_set_commitment.description: Commitment to the set of events whose replay produces state_digest. merkle_event_set_v1 uses the same RFC 6962 domain-separated family as state_digest and Seal roots: leaf=H(0x00||leaf_data), node=H(0x01||left||right), odd tail promoted. Algorithm + root + covered_event_count name the canonical reduction; actor_seq_ranges may further bind per-actor sequences. Boundary Event IDs are carried once by top-level frontier.event_ids.

created_by.description: Complete ActorId of the snapshot issuer (account, hosted principal, service, Realm notary, or federation witness). The signature transcript binds this identity; its DID URL verification_method is independently validated against the selected ActorId branch.

created_at.description: Issuer-local timestamp when the snapshot manifest was sealed. RFC 3339 UTC, MUST end with 'Z'. Required because the snapshot signature transcript binds this field via x-canonical-bytes-include.

authority_binding.description: Evidence that created_by was authorized to seal this snapshot at created_at. Verifiers MUST reject the snapshot when this binding cannot be checked against Realm policy / witness quorum at or before created_at. authority_kind=witness_quorum additionally requires the typed witness_attestations list below; there is no untyped alternative carrier.

auth_state_digest.description: Hash of the authorization state used to verify snapshot issuer authority.

auth_frontier.description: Realm auth/policy frontier proving the signer authority at created_at.

witness_attestations.description: Typed witness quorum evidence. Rows MUST be sorted by witness_id in UTF-8 byte order and witness_id MUST be unique across rows. Each witness signs the signature-free SnapshotWitnessAttestation projection first; the issuer then signs the manifest containing this final ordered list. Quorum admission uses only the accepted Realm auth/policy state resolved from auth_frontier / auth_state_digest at manifest created_at.

signature.description: Detached proof over the JCS canonical snapshot manifest bytes with only the signature field omitted. The signed transcript therefore binds id, realm_id, reducer_profile, schema_profile_refs, state_digest, frontier, event_set_commitment, chunks (chunk_ref / digest / size_bytes), security_class, verification_hints, created_by, created_at, and authority_binding — including the final sorted authority_binding.witness_attestations list, so a rewritten, truncated or reordered witness set invalidates this signature. Because security_class is signed (and required), a high_assurance -> standard downgrade cannot be performed without invalidating the signature. This transcript uses context ak.snapshot_proof.v1; each witness attestation uses the separate ak.snapshot_witness_attestation_proof.v1 context and never signs this transcript, which is what keeps the two levels acyclic.

schemas/space.schema.json.title: Arkret Space
schemas/space.schema.json.description: A Space is a structural grouping object inside a Realm. Boards, lists, swimlanes, calendar buckets, document outline groups, etc. are all Spaces. Authorization-transparent: never carries its own membership/policy/E2EE group; its metadata may be placed in an existing Realm/Circle effective scope via scope_circle_id.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

realm_id.description: Home Realm that stores, syncs, and authorizes this Space object's own metadata. This is also the fallback default Realm for new resources under this Space when default_realm_id is absent.

default_realm_id.description: Optional default Realm for resources created under this Space. Omitted means this Space's own realm_id; ancestor defaults are not inherited. This field does not grant membership or decryption rights.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional Circle scope for this Space object's own metadata and scoped structural relation facts. Space still does not own a security boundary; it only places its metadata into an existing Circle scope. Omitted means Realm-default scope.

child_scope_policy.description: Reducer-enforced placement/encryption policy for child resources created in or moved into this Space.

parent_space_id.description: Optional parent in the structural hierarchy. Parent MAY live in a different Realm; such a link is navigation only and never propagates membership, capabilities, history, E2EE keys, retention, or federation policy.

kind.description: Space kind. v1 standard kinds include 'space', 'project', 'folder', 'board', and 'list'. Profile-defined kinds (e.g., 'swimlane', 'calendar_bucket', 'page_group') MAY be added via Realm schema/profile and MUST be registered. Unknown kind MUST schema_violation.

rank.description: Fractional-index rank within parent. See encoding.md §9.

schema_refs.description: Optional schema/profile references that further constrain this Space's contained Strand types, fields, or position invariants.

fields.description: Space kind-specific fields. For kind=list, wip_limit is an integer 1..100000 and wip_limit_enforcement is required with enum warn|reject|require_review whenever wip_limit is present; these are the sole write-policy source and MUST NOT be read from View. For kind=board, view_id may identify a default presentation. MUST NOT contain a 'rank' key (rank is a top-level Space field; see relation.md §2 for the symmetric Relation constraint and forbidden-wire-fields.json `fields.rank/space_payload`).

state.description: Space lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. State transitions are reducer-enforced per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.space.archive MUST come from state=='active' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_active); ak.space.restore MUST come from state=='archived' (else failed_precondition reason=space_not_archived); ak.space.tombstone MUST come from {'active','archived'} AND must have no live dependents (failed_precondition reason=space_already_terminal for terminal source, space_has_live_dependents for live refs). Same-state self-transitions (archive on archived, etc.) MUST fail; clients re-archive by restore-then-archive. Tombstoned is irreversible (MUST NOT be restored). The transition timestamp lives on the writing Move and on state_changed_at.

state_changed_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent state transition. Required when state != 'active'.

anyOf.$comment: forbidden Strand top-level field; canonical name is content
forbidden Strand top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.title or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Strand top-level metadata; canonical path is metadata.summary or encrypted_metadata
forbidden Strand top-level extension metadata; canonical path is metadata.fields or encrypted_metadata
forbidden encrypted content carrier; canonical name is encrypted_content

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

scope_circle_id.description: Optional reference to an intra-Realm Circle (see models/circle.md) that defines this Strand's effective scope. When set, ALL Strand tracks (synthesis, discussion, etc.) share that Circle's membership, history visibility, delivery/query/projection boundary, and encryption_profile. When unset, the Strand lives in Realm-default scope. The producer signs the corresponding Event.scope_ref; the receiver verifies that the Circle belongs to this Realm and that the derived scope equals Event.scope_ref before materializing the object's immutable effective_scope. Rebinding scope_circle_id is forbidden by default (failed_precondition reason=scope_rebind_forbidden). For 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion' scenarios use two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation (circle.md §7.2).

schema_refs.description: Optional authoritative schema set for profile-defined metadata.fields subtrees. Unlike Morph, a plain Strand carries no profile subtree and omits this field entirely; when present it MUST list at least one profile schema id. The container self-schema ak.schema.strand.v1 MUST NOT appear here. Every listed profile schema and its metadata.fields namespace MUST co-occur in both directions: the ref without the subtree and the subtree without the ref are both schema_violation, evaluated on the post-patch object. Writers MUST also bind the same schema id in the Event requirements.schema[] so replay validates against the write-time schema instead of the object's current schema_refs.
schema_refs.$comment: Bidirectional co-presence for concrete profiles is enforced in allOf below; see zh/models/strand-and-message.md.

agent_participation.description: Optional wrapped five-bit Agent ceiling. When present every bit is explicit and may only tighten the enclosing Circle or Realm ceiling.

encrypted_metadata.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is a strand_metadata object. Required instead of plaintext metadata when the effective metadata_encryption_floor is e2ee_required.

content.description: Strand description body. This is base Strand content and is independent of the synthesis and discussion tracks.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted envelope whose plaintext is the Strand description ContentBlock. Exclusive with content.

tracks.description: Active Strand collaboration surfaces, keyed by an active name in track-name-registry.json. The synthesis entry may carry its own content / encrypted_content; the discussion entry configures a Message timeline and may not carry either field. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE: the entire Strand shares a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md). At most one track entry may explicitly set is_primary=true; when none does, the reducer derives the primary track by the deterministic rules in models/strand-and-message.md §4.5. The map MUST contain at least one entry; propertyNames fails closed for names outside the registry-backed TrackName enum.

allOf.$comment: Discussion content is carried by Message timeline objects, never by the discussion track config.

state.description: Strand lifecycle state. 'active' is the default. Reducer enforces transitions per common-fields.md §5.1: ak.strand.archive MUST come from 'active' (else failed_precondition reason=strand_not_active); ak.strand.restore MUST come from 'archived' (else strand_not_archived); terminal state is reached only via a ak.redaction event targeting the strand (MUST come from {'active','archived'} else strand_already_terminal). Same-state self-transitions MUST fail. 'redacted' is the irreversible terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent state transition. MUST be set when state != 'active'; MUST be the created_at of the corresponding ak.strand.archive / ak.strand.restore / ak.redaction Event. Aligns with Space.state_changed_at and the common-fields rule in models/common-fields.md §3.

stage.description: Optional Strand business-progression stage. Orthogonal to top-level 'state' (physical lifecycle): archive does NOT change stage; stage=done does NOT auto-archive. ak.strand.create MAY omit stage; when present it must be one of the protocol-level enum values and has no protocol-level default. The only wire path that mutates stage after creation is the dedicated ak.strand.stage.set event; ak.strand.update patches on stage / stage_changed_at MUST be rejected (schema_violation, single-source). Stage transitions intentionally do NOT carry a reason / note field — the ak.strand.stage.set event log is the audit source, and human-readable explanations belong in a Message on the discussion track that references the event. A per-Realm workflow profile MAY narrow which transitions are legal beyond the core reducer hard invariants (terminal state freeze, non-active reject) defined in models/common-fields.md §5.3.3. See models/strand-and-message.md §3.2 for full semantics and models/common-fields.md §5.3 for the protocol-level enum / bucket mapping.

stage_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the most recent stage transition. MUST NOT appear without stage. MUST be ignored when present on wire; reducer overwrites with the triggering ak.strand.stage.set event's created_at. Same-value self-transitions (stage value unchanged) MUST NOT update this field.

allOf.$comment: The container self-schema is not a business schema and MUST NOT appear in schema_refs (same rule as morph.md).

Calendar profile activation, direction 1: the schema ref requires the metadata.fields.calendar subtree. Only decidable when plaintext metadata is present; encrypted_metadata Strands are checked by the producer before encryption and by authorized clients after decryption.
Calendar profile activation, direction 2: the metadata.fields.calendar subtree requires the schema ref.

Mirror of message.schema.json's state=redacted branch: both authored Strand slots — description (content <-> encrypted_content) and tracks.synthesis content (content <-> encrypted_content inside that track) — MUST be absent once redaction has cleared them, so 'redacted' is verifiable from the object alone instead of only from the event stream (zh/models/common-fields.md §5 redacted row, §5.2; zh/models/event-and-patch.md §4.2.4).

strand_metadata.description: Extensible user-readable Strand metadata. In MLS / E2EE realms this object is encrypted as encrypted_metadata unless the Realm explicitly opts into plaintext metadata.

not.$comment: Reducer-owned fields stay top-level and MUST NOT be mirrored inside metadata.

metadata_fields.description: Profile-defined Strand metadata fields. Reducer-owned fields are forbidden here to avoid dual sources of truth.

anyOf.$comment: profile activation impostor; the canonical activation axis is Strand.schema_refs
profile activation impostor; the canonical activation axis is Strand.schema_refs
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.start
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.end
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.timezone
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.all_day
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.recurrence
flat calendar schedule field is not v1 wire; the canonical path is metadata.fields.calendar.attendees

calendar.description: Calendar event schedule subtree activated by ak.schema.calendar_event.v1 in Strand.schema_refs. See zh/models/calendar-event.md.

track_name.description: Closed active TrackName set mirrored from registry/track-name-registry.json. The artifact gate requires exact set equality; an unregistered map key is a schema violation.

strand_track.description: Strand track entry. The stable name is the map key in Strand.tracks. The synthesis entry may carry its own narrative content / encrypted_content in addition to config; the discussion entry is config-only because its authored content is carried by Message objects. Tracks do NOT carry independent membership / permissions / history visibility / E2EE. The whole Strand has a single effective scope determined by Strand.scope_circle_id (see models/circle.md); there is no per-track security boundary. To represent 'wide synthesis + narrow discussion', create two Strands linked by a confidential_discussion_of Relation per models/circle.md §7.2.

enabled.description: Whether this track currently accepts new writes (synthesis edits / discussion messages). Default true when omitted. Setting enabled=false MUST cause the reducer to reject subsequent writes to this track with 'track_disabled' until enabled is set back to true. Disabling a track does NOT delete prior history; it freezes new writes only. UI MAY hide a disabled track or render it read-only.

metadata.description: Track-local UI metadata only. The reducer NEVER interprets its keys; it does not create membership, history visibility, access, or E2EE scope. Access-like keys are rejected at the wire layer to prevent a pseudo-access surface (tracks have no independent access — see models/strand-and-message.md §4.4).

not.$comment: Forbid access-like keys so strand_track.metadata cannot smuggle a pseudo-access surface; track access is always derived from the Strand effective scope, never from track metadata.

content.description: Track-owned ContentBlock. In the active v1 registry only tracks.synthesis may carry this field; tracks.discussion content is carried by Message objects.

encrypted_content.description: Encrypted counterpart of track-owned content. In the active v1 registry only tracks.synthesis may carry this field.

anyOf.$comment: track-local extension field is not v1 wire; the canonical name is metadata.
Track content plaintext and encrypted forms are mutually exclusive.

schemas/string-profiles.schema.json.title: Arkret String Profiles
schemas/string-profiles.schema.json.description: Shared coarse-grained JSON Schema shapes for Arkret v1 string profiles. Custom format validation and UTF-8 octet limits are normative and require the SDK validator; JSON Schema patterns do not implement PRECIS, IDNA, or UTS #39.

human_identifier_localpart.description: Canonical RFC 8265 UsernameCaseMapped-derived localpart. Maximum 128 Unicode code points in prepared form.

agent_slug.description: Canonical controller-scoped native personal Agent selector slug. Maximum 64 Unicode code points in prepared form.

canonical_domain.description: Lowercase UTS #46 Nontransitional A-label domain with at least two labels; normative validation includes STD3, Bidi, Joiner, hyphen, DNS-length, and round-trip checks.

canonical_handle.description: Canonical <prepared-localpart>:<lowercase-A-label-domain> handle or realm alias. The prepared localpart maximum is 128 Unicode code points; the domain maximum is 253 ASCII octets.

acct_uri.description: RFC 7565 acct URI with UTF-8 localpart octets percent-encoded using uppercase hex when required, canonical A-label host, and no port.

single_line_display_text.description: NFC multilingual single-line display text; mixed scripts, emoji, and symbols are allowed.

display_text_256.description: Single-line display text limited to 256 Unicode code points in prepared form.

display_text_512.description: Single-line display text limited to 512 Unicode code points in prepared form.

short_text.description: NFC multilingual short text. LF is allowed; CR, other C0/C1 controls, BOM, and bidi embedding/override controls are rejected.

audit_reason_text.description: Human-readable audit reason limited to 1024 Unicode code points. It is explanatory text only and never a machine-readable reason code or authorization source.

content_text.description: NFC multilingual content text; rendering contexts must escape markup and apply bidi isolation.

non_typed_identifier_floor.description: Lexical floor of every identifier value category that does NOT own the ak: namespace (opaque_correlation, document_local_symbol, external_system_identifier, registry_catalog_symbol, unregistered_object_identifier); see common-fields.md 2.1. The negative lookahead IS the floor: it mechanically proves the value cannot be an ak: typed id, which maxLength alone can never prove, while admitting every other value the field already accepted. It deliberately constrains nothing else - the per-field convergence direction (a registered typed kind, or a tighter opaque profile) is decided per object family, so a pattern-only floor composes with whatever profile the field already carries instead of pre-empting it.

schemas/time.schema.json.title: Arkret Time Primitives
schemas/time.schema.json.description: Defs-only shared time primitives. Arkret-owned absolute instants use the single fixed UTC millisecond spelling YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ. Duration, external-protocol NumericDate, local wall time, and algorithm-internal epoch values are different semantic types and do not reference this definition.

timestamp.description: Canonical Arkret-owned absolute instant. UTC Z form with exactly three millisecond digits. Whole seconds MUST use .000Z; offsets, missing/finer fractions, lowercase separators, leap seconds, and invalid Gregorian calendar dates are forbidden. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

local_date.description: Proleptic Gregorian calendar date with no time, offset, or zone. Not an absolute instant: it resolves to an instant only through an explicitly carried IANA time zone plus TZDB version. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

local_date_time.description: RFC 8984 LocalDateTime narrowed to whole seconds. Wall-clock time with no offset, no Z suffix, no bracketed zone, and no fractional seconds; it resolves to an instant only through an explicitly carried IANA time zone plus TZDB version. Producers MUST NOT spell whole seconds as .0 or .000. Shape validation by this pattern is supplemented by semantic date validation.

schemas/transport-binding.schema.json.title: TransportBinding
schemas/transport-binding.schema.json.description: Standalone entry point for the closed ServiceDescribe transport_bindings union. Operation coverage is supplied only by registered operation bundles.

id.description: Present on the materialised object. MUST be absent from the create Event payload: zh/models/common-fields.md derives it from the create Event's own event_id (retyped), so a payload-supplied id would be a second, forgeable truth.

visibility.description: View sharing visibility. Private views are actor-private account data; shared views are canonical Realm objects.

state.description: Required View lifecycle state. Shared View removal is an ak.view.update patch to tombstoned; tombstoned is terminal.

state_changed_at.description: Reducer-derived timestamp of the ak.view.update that transitioned state to tombstoned. Actor-supplied values MUST be rejected.

collection_grouping.description: Grouping / lane / time-bucket / matrix configuration; mirrors models/views.md §3.3. Conditional required-ness is enforced per mode.

item_order_by.description: Stable item ordering; mirrors models/views.md §3.2. Drag-ordered collections SHOULD sort by rank.

display_fields.description: Display columns (dot path + format); see models/views.md §3.2.

schemas/websocket-dpop-proof.schema.json.title: Arkret WebSocket DPoP-Shaped Authentication Proof
schemas/websocket-dpop-proof.schema.json.description: Decoded protected header and claims for challenge_dpop_session_v1. This is an Arkret application-level proof carried in an authenticate frame, not an RFC 9449 DPoP HTTP header. Its wss htu and ARKRET-WEBSOCKET-AUTH htm are accepted only in this proof context.

schemas/websocket-frame.schema.json.title: Arkret WebSocket Frame
schemas/websocket-frame.schema.json.description: Closed union of all application frames for ak.profile.binding.websocket.v1. Duplicate JSON member names and the advertised UTF-8 byte limit are enforced before JSON Schema validation.

code.description: Must resolve to a registered code in error-code-registry.json codes[]. This closed transport error body is not the HTTP RFC 9457 Problem Details.
